Through his interactions with Cale, Maet highlights the significance of understanding one's past and respecting the traditions that have shaped human culture.

Furthermore, Titan A.E. touches on the idea of hope and resilience in the face of adversity. The movie presents a bleak future where humanity is on the brink of extinction, but it also offers a message of hope and redemption through Cale's journey. The film's themes are ultimately centered around the human spirit's capacity to persevere and adapt in the face of overwhelming challenges.

Overall, Titan A.E. is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas through its narrative and characters. While it received mixed reviews upon its release, the movie has developed a cult following over the years, and its themes continue to resonate with audiences today.

original_title: Always Watching: A Marble Hornets Story
overview: A small town news team discovers a box of video tapes where a faceless figure dressed in a dark suit, haunts and torments a family...slowly driving them insane. Soon after, they realize that the "Operator" has begun to stalk them as well.
tagline: You shouldn't have looked.
title: Always Watching: A Marble Hornets Story
plot:
Always Watching: A Marble Hornets Story is a found-footage horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the blurred lines between reality and paranoia. The movie masterfully weaves together elements of mystery, suspense, and psychological terror to create a sense of unease and uncertainty in its audience.

At its core, Always Watching explores the theme of obsession, as the protagonist, Jay, becomes increasingly fixated on uncovering the truth behind the mysterious Marble Hornets series. As Jay's investigation deepens, he finds himself trapped in a web of conspiracy theories, cryptic messages, and eerie encounters that challenge his perception of reality.

The film also delves into the concept of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Jay's past experiences and emotional scars are skillfully woven throughout the narrative, adding depth to his character and making his descent into madness all the more believable and unsettling.

Furthermore, Always Watching touches on the theme of the power of storytelling and the ways in which narratives can shape our understanding of the world. The Marble Hornets series, which serves as a central plot device, is presented as a mysterious and possibly supernatural entity that seems to have a life of its own, blurring the lines between reality and fiction.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as Jay's grip on reality begins to slip, and he becomes convinced that he is being watched by an unseen force. The movie's use of found-footage and handheld camera work creates a sense of immediacy and intimacy, drawing the viewer into Jay's world and making them feel like they are experiencing the events firsthand.

Ultimately, Always Watching: A Marble Hornets Story is a thought-provoking exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, the power of storytelling, and the blurred lines between reality and paranoia.

overview: Calvin and his friends, who all live in an orphanage, find old shoes with the faded letters MJ connected to a powerline. One stormy night, they go to get the shoes when Calvin and the shoes are struck by lightning. Calvin now has unbelievable basketball powers and has the chance to play for the NBA.
tagline: Think like Mike, Achieve like Mike, Be Like Mike.
title: Like Mike
plot:
Like Mike is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores several themes that resonate with audiences of all ages. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of identity, self-discovery, and the transformative power of sports.

The story follows a young boy named Calvin, who discovers he has the ability to step into the shoes of his basketball idol, Michael Jordan, when he wears his lucky red sneakers. As Calvin navigates this newfound phenomenon, he must confront the challenges of being a teenager, including peer pressure, family expectations, and self-doubt.

Through Calvin's journey, the film highlights the importance of staying true to oneself while also embracing one's passions and talents. The movie showcases how sports can be a powerful catalyst for personal growth, teaching valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and the value of hard work.

Moreover, Like Mike explores the theme of family and the impact that loved ones have on our lives. Calvin's relationships with his parents and friends are put to the test as he navigates this extraordinary experience, ultimately learning to appreciate the people who matter most in his life.

The film also touches on the idea of fame and celebrity culture, as Calvin becomes an overnight sensation after his basketball skills are showcased on national television. However, instead of letting fame go to his head, Calvin remains humble and grounded, using his newfound platform to make a positive impact on those around him.

Overall, Like Mike is a feel-good movie that celebrates the power of sports, family, and self-discovery, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Two Jesuit priests travel to seventeenth century Japan which has, under the Tokugawa shogunate, banned Catholicism and almost all foreign contact.
tagline: Sometimes silence is the deadliest sound.
title: Silence
plot:
Silence is a 2016 American epic drama film directed by Martin Scorsese, based on the 1967 novel of the same name by Shusaku Endo. The film stars Andrew Garfield, Adam Driver, and Liam Neeson.

The story takes place in the late 17th century, during the Edo period in Japan. The plot follows two Jesuit priests, Father Ferdinand (Adam Driver) and Father Garrpe (Liam Neeson), who are sent to Japan by their superior, Father Valdés (John Iserey), to find their missing companion, Father Rodrigues (Andrew Garfield).

Father Rodrigues had been in Japan for 16 years, studying the local language and culture. He was last seen on a ship that sailed from Portugal, bound for Japan. The two priests are tasked with finding him and bringing back any information they can gather about his fate.

Upon their arrival in Japan, the priests are met with hostility by the Japanese authorities, who view Christianity as a threat to their country's traditions and way of life. The priests are forced to go into hiding, using disguises and assumed identities to avoid detection.

As they journey through rural Japan, the priests encounter various challenges, including poverty, hunger, and illness. They also meet with local villagers, who are often skeptical of their intentions but eventually warm up to them.

Meanwhile, Father Rodrigues is revealed to be alive, having been captured by Japanese authorities and subjected to torture and forced conversion. He has become a devout follower of the Shinto faith, and his experiences have left him traumatized and disillusioned with Christianity.

The priests are reunited with Father Rodrigues, who shares his story with them. However, their reunion is short-lived, as they soon discover that Rodrigues' experiences have changed him profoundly. He is no longer the man he once was, and his faith has been shaken to its core.

As the story unfolds, Scorsese explores themes of faith, doubt, and redemption. The priests are forced to confront the harsh realities of their mission in Japan, where they must navigate a complex web of cultural and religious differences.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a tragic conclusion, as Father Rodrigues is forced to make a choice between his faith and his life. The ending is both heartbreaking and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of faith and redemption in a world torn apart by conflict and uncertainty.

Overall, Silence is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of faith, doubt, and redemption in a richly detailed and atmospheric setting. Scorsese's direction is masterful, using long takes and sweeping cinematography to create a sense of scope and scale that is both breathtaking and humbling.

overview: Brad and Dusty must deal with their intrusive fathers during the holidays.
tagline: More Daddies. More Problems.
title: Daddy's Home 2
plot:
Daddy's Home 2 is a 2017 American Christmas comedy film directed by Sean Anders and John Morris, and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film. Brad Whitaker (Will Ferrell) and Dusty Mayron (Mark Wahlberg) are still co-parenting their children, but they're struggling to balance their own relationships with their wives, Sara (Linda Cardellini) and Megan (Catherine Keener), respectively.

As Christmas approaches, the Whitakers and the Mayrons decide to spend the holiday together as a blended family. However, things quickly become complicated when Brad's estranged father, Don Whitaker (Mel Gibson), shows up unexpectedly with his own son, Ryan (Wes Bentley). Don is a gruff, old-school man who clashes with Dusty and the rest of the family.

As the two families try to come together for Christmas, they face various challenges. Brad and Dusty struggle to assert their authority as co-parents, while Sara and Megan try to keep the peace between their husbands. Meanwhile, Don's presence sparks tension among the group, particularly with Dusty, who feels like he's being replaced by his father.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Don's past, which reveal a complex and troubled relationship with Brad. We also learn more about Ryan, who is struggling to find his place in the world after serving in the military.

Throughout the film, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they navigate their differences and try to come together for Christmas. In the end, the Whitakers and Mayrons learn to put aside their differences and work together as a blended family.

One of the standout aspects of Daddy's Home 2 is its exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, masculinity, and identity. The film tackles these issues with humor and heart, making it a relatable and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Daddy's Home 2 is a fun and lighthearted holiday film that explores the ups and downs of blended families. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and heartfelt moments, it's a great addition to any Christmas movie marathon.

overview: In Verona, bad blood between the Montague and Capulet families leads to much bitterness. Despite the hostility, Romeo Montague manages an invitation to a masked ball at the estate of the Capulets and meets Juliet, their daughter. The two are instantly smitten but dismayed to learn that their families are enemies. Romeo and Juliet figure out a way to pursue their romance, but Romeo is banished for his part in the slaying of Juliet's cousin, Tybalt.
tagline: The most dangerous love story ever told.
title: Romeo & Juliet
plot:
Romeo & Juliet is a 2013 film adaptation of William Shakespeare's tragedy, directed by Carlo Carlei from a screenplay by Julian Fellowes. Douglas Booth and Hailee Steinfeld play the young lovers, with Damian Lewis as Lord Capulet, Kodi Smit-McPhee as Benvolio, Ed Westwick as Tybalt, Stellan Skarsgård as the Prince and Paul Giamatti as Friar Laurence. It keeps the original story but only part of Shakespeare's dialogue, a choice many critics objected to. It opened in Britain and the United States on 11 October 2013.

In late medieval Verona, the rich Montague and Capulet families have been enemies for generations. After a brawl in the market, the Prince warns that anyone who breaks the peace again will pay with their life. Young Romeo Montague pines for Rosaline, a Capulet, and despite his cousin Benvolio's advice he slips into a Capulet feast with Benvolio and Mercutio hoping to see her. Instead he meets Juliet; they fall instantly in love, dance and kiss, and only afterwards learn from her Nurse that they belong to opposing houses.

That night Romeo enters the Capulet garden, hears Juliet declare her love from her balcony and climbs up to her, and they resolve to marry. Friar Laurence agrees to wed them in secret, hoping the match will heal the feud. Soon after the ceremony, Tybalt confronts Romeo and his friends and kills Mercutio, and Romeo kills Tybalt in revenge. The Prince banishes him. Romeo spends one night with Juliet before fleeing, and Lord Capulet orders his daughter to marry Count Paris, threatening to disown her if she refuses.

Desperate, Juliet turns to the Friar, who gives her a potion that will make her appear dead until Romeo can take her away to Mantua, and sends a letter explaining the plan. The letter never arrives, and Romeo hears from Benvolio that Juliet is dead. He buys poison, kills Paris at the tomb and drinks it beside Juliet, who wakes just as he dies in her arms. Refusing to leave with the Friar, she stabs herself with Romeo's dagger. At their funeral the families finally reconcile.

Critics found it unremarkable, with a 25% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating, and it grossed about $3 million, though its score was honoured by the International Film Music Critics Association.

overview: In his homeland of Alagaesia, a farm boy happens upon a dragon's egg -- a discovery that leads him on a predestined journey where he realized he's the one person who can defend his home against an evil king.
tagline: As darkness falls, the last dragon will choose its rider.
title: Eragon
plot:
Eragon is a fantasy adventure film directed by Stefen Fangmeier, based on the novel of the same name by Christopher Paolini. The movie was released in 2006 and produced by 20th Century Fox.

The main themes of Eragon (2006) include:

1. Coming of Age: The story follows Eragon, a young farm boy who discovers a dragon egg and becomes a Dragon Rider, a legendary group thought to be extinct. As he embarks on his journey, he learns about responsibility, courage, and the true meaning of being a hero.

2. Friendship and Loyalty: Eragon forms strong bonds with Saphira, his dragon companion, and Brom, a wise old warrior who becomes his mentor. These relationships are crucial in helping Eragon navigate the challenges he faces and grow as a person.

3. Good vs. Evil: The film explores the eternal struggle between good and evil, as embodied by the villainous King Galbatorix and his dark magic. Eragon's quest to defeat the king is driven by his desire to protect his homeland and the people he cares about.

4. Self-Discovery: Throughout the movie, Eragon grapples with his newfound identity as a Dragon Rider and the weight of his responsibilities. He must confront his own doubts and fears in order to become the hero he was meant to be.

5. Sacrifice and Redemption: The story features several characters who make sacrifices for the greater good, including Brom's ultimate sacrifice. This theme highlights the importance of putting others before oneself and finding redemption through selfless acts.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics but has since developed a loyal fan base. While it deviates from the original book in some ways, it captures the essence of Paolini's world and characters, making it an enjoyable watch for fans of fantasy and adventure films.

original_title: Red Shoes and the Seven Dwarfs
overview: Princes who have been turned into Dwarfs seek the red shoes of a lady in order to break the spell, although it will not be easy.
title: Red Shoes and the Seven Dwarfs
plot:
Red Shoes and the Seven Dwarfs, released in South Korea simply as Red Shoes, is a 2019 English-language South Korean computer-animated fantasy film produced by Locus Corporation. It reworks the Brothers Grimm tale "Snow White" and borrows its title from Hans Christian Andersen's "The Red Shoes". Chloë Grace Moretz voices the heroine and Sam Claflin the dwarf Merlin, with Gina Gershon as the witch Regina, Patrick Warburton and Jim Rash. It opened in South Korea on July 25, 2019, and in the United States in September 2020.

The Fearless Seven, a band of princes made up of Merlin, Arthur, Jack, Hans and the triplets Pino, Noki and Kio, rescue a fairy princess from a dragon, but mistake her green complexion for a witch's and attack her. She curses them to turn into small green dwarfs whenever anyone looks at them, a spell that only a kiss from the most beautiful woman in the world can lift. Later, King White marries the sorceress Regina and vanishes, and his daughter, Princess Snow White, a strong, full-figured young woman, comes looking for him. Ignoring his written warning, she takes a pair of magical red shoes grown from an apple tree, which turn her into a slender beauty.

Escaping Regina, who fails to recognise her, Snow crash-lands near the dwarfs' cottage. Calling herself Red Shoes, she enlists the smitten dwarfs to help find her father, and they all compete to win a kiss, especially Merlin and Arthur. A large wooden rabbit joins them, and Regina sends the vain Prince Average after them, later turning him and his guards into monstrous wooden bears. Snow and Merlin fall for each other, but their kiss fails to break his curse. When Merlin is swept away in a river, Snow removes the shoes to rescue him with her real strength, and Merlin, shamed by his shallowness, leaves her.

Merlin comes to value Snow for who she is. Regina captures her and forces her to eat an apple that transforms her into a tree producing new red shoes. The dwarfs and the wooden animals rescue Merlin and smash the Magic Mirror, and Merlin falls from the castle with Regina, who dies. The wooden creatures return to human form, revealing the rabbit to be King White, and Snow's kiss revives the dying Merlin and frees him from the curse for good.

The film received mixed reviews from critics, with only a handful of reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: The Scorpion King 4: Quest for Power
overview: When he is betrayed by a trusted friend, Mathayus must marshal all his strength and cunning to outwit a formidable opponent who will stop at nothing to unlock a supreme ancient power.
title: The Scorpion King 4: Quest for Power
plot:
The Scorpion King 4: Quest for Power is a 2015 direct-to-video sword-and-sorcery action adventure directed by Mike Elliott and the fourth installment in The Scorpion King series. Victor Webster returns as Mathayus, with Ellen Hollman, Will Kemp, Barry Bostwick, Lou Ferrigno, Rutger Hauer, Royce Gracie and Eve Torres in supporting roles. It was released on home media on January 6, 2015.

Mathayus and his partner Drazen infiltrate a palace to steal an artifact called the Urn of Kings for King Zakkour of Al-Moraad, but Drazen betrays him and escapes with the urn. Sent by Zakkour to the northern kingdom of Norvania to deliver a peace treaty, Mathayus discovers that Drazen is the son of its ruler, King Yannick, who shatters the urn to retrieve the Golden Key of Lord Alcaman, an ancient sorcerer who once ruled the known world. The inscription on the key holds the secret to his power. Mathayus allows himself to be arrested to get inside the castle and meets Valina Raskov, a fierce prisoner from the kingdom's original royal bloodline whom Drazen intends to execute publicly to cement his father's rule.

Yannick believes Mathayus's peace mission and releases him, but Drazen assassinates his father with scorpions and frames Mathayus. Before dying, Yannick passes the key to Mathayus, who escapes with Valina. The pair seek out her father, Sorrell, a scholar and inventor who has no wish to reclaim the throne. He deciphers the inscription, which points to a hidden palace containing Alcaman's crown, an artifact that will grant its wearer power over the world. Drazen seizes the key and leaves them to die in a burning house, but the heroes survive and follow him through a series of villages, temples and traps. In the final confrontation inside the mountain, Drazen is destroyed by the crown's power, and Mathayus uses it to save Sorrell. The heroes seal the key and crown away and declare Alcaman's power a myth. Sorrell is restored to the throne but passes the crown to Valina, who vows to build a kingdom founded on science and reason with just a little bit of magic, and Zakkour releases Mathayus to stay at her side.

The film continued the series' tradition of lighthearted fantasy adventure, mixing martial arts, humor and cameos from genre veterans. A fifth film, The Scorpion King: Book of Souls, followed in 2018 with Zach McGowan replacing Webster.

overview: Paris, Kingdom of France, August 18, 1572. To avoid the outbreak of a religious war, the Catholic princess Marguerite de Valois, sister of the feeble King Charles IX, marries the Huguenot King Henry III of Navarre.
tagline: She was the wife of a king… and the lover of a soldier.
title: Queen Margot
plot:
La Reine Margot, released in North America as Queen Margot, is a 1994 French historical romantic drama directed by Patrice Chéreau from a screenplay he wrote with Danièle Thompson, based on the 1845 novel by Alexandre Dumas. It stars Isabelle Adjani as Marguerite de Valois, known as Margot, Daniel Auteuil as Henri of Navarre, Jean-Hugues Anglade as King Charles IX, Vincent Perez as La Môle and Virna Lisi as Catherine de' Medici.

In 1572, France is torn by the bitter conflict between Catholics and Protestant Huguenots. The kingdom is nominally ruled by the unstable and sickly Charles IX, but real power lies with his mother, the scheming Catherine de' Medici. In a gesture meant to reconcile the factions, Catherine arranges for her Catholic daughter Margot to marry Henri de Bourbon, the Protestant King of Navarre. Only days after the wedding, however, Catherine's maneuvering helps unleash the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre, in which thousands of Protestants who had gathered in Paris for the celebrations are slaughtered in the streets.

Margot, who does not love her husband, begins a passionate affair with La Môle, a Protestant nobleman caught up in the violence. At the same time she forms a pragmatic alliance with Henri, who must survive in a court that wants him dead. Poisonings, betrayals and conspiracies multiply as Catherine plots to secure the throne for her favorite son, the Duke of Anjou. A book whose pages have been coated with arsenic, meant for Henri, instead falls into the hands of King Charles, leading to tragic consequences for the lovers and for the crown.

Chéreau's version is noted for its brutal violence, sensuality and visceral depiction of religious hatred, contrasting with earlier, more decorous costume dramas.

The film premiered in competition at the 1994 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Jury Prize and the Best Actress award for Lisi. It received twelve nominations at the César Awards and won five, including Best Actress for Adjani and supporting awards for Anglade and Lisi. It drew about two million admissions in France, and an abridged version was released internationally.

overview: Mary Smith, a young girl who lives with her great-aunt in the countryside, follows a mysterious cat into the nearby forest where she finds a strange flower and an old broom, none of which is as ordinary as it seems.
tagline: From a single lie, everything will change.
title: Mary and The Witch's Flower
plot:
Mary and the Witch's Flower is a 2017 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Hiromasa Yonebayashi, produced by Studio Ponoc. 

The main theme of the movie revolves around the idea of self-discovery and growth. The protagonist, Mary, is an orphan who finds herself in a new environment, where she must navigate her way through unfamiliar surroundings and people. As she explores this new world, she discovers her own strengths and weaknesses, learning to balance her desire for independence with her need for connection.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and belonging. Mary struggles to find her place within the community of witches, feeling like an outsider due to her lack of magical abilities. However, as she learns more about herself and her powers, she begins to discover a sense of belonging and purpose.

Another significant theme present in the movie is the importance of friendship and relationships. Mary forms strong bonds with her friends, particularly Kiki, who becomes a source of support and guidance for her. The film highlights the value of nurturing these relationships and learning from one another's strengths and weaknesses.

The movie also explores the idea of responsibility and growth through experience. As Mary navigates her new life as a witch, she faces various challenges that test her abilities and force her to make difficult decisions. Through these experiences, she learns valuable lessons about courage, perseverance, and self-reliance.

Overall, Mary and the Witch's Flower is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores themes of identity, belonging, friendship, responsibility, and growth, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Lucinda Price is sent to a reform academy under the assumption that she has killed a boy. There, she meets two mysterious boys, Cam and Daniel, to whom she feels drawn to both. But as the love triangle unfurls, it is Daniel that Luce cannot keep herself away from, and things begin to take a darker turn when she finds out his true identity.
tagline: Some angels are destined to fall.
title: Fallen
plot:
Fallen is a 2016 romantic fantasy drama directed by Scott Hicks and based on Lauren Kate's 2009 young adult novel of the same name, the first book in her Fallen series. Addison Timlin stars as Lucinda "Luce" Price, with Jeremy Irvine as Daniel Grigori, Harrison Gilbertson as Cam, Lola Kirke, Juliet Aubrey and Joely Richardson. The film opened in several countries, including Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore, in November 2016, but its American release was delayed until September 2017, when Relativity Media distributed it.

Luce is sent to Sword and Cross, a gloomy reform school for troubled teenagers, after she is blamed for the death of a boy named Trevor, who died in a fire after she kissed him. She remembers seeing strange shadows around them before the fire and fears that she is cursed. At her new school she meets an assortment of students: the charming Cam, who quickly shows an interest in her; the eccentric Arriane, who takes her under her wing; the hostile Molly; the friendly Penn; and the brooding Daniel Grigori, to whom she feels an immediate and inexplicable attraction despite his efforts to push her away. She also meets Miss Sophia, a teacher of religious studies.

The school psychiatrist tells Luce that she can leave if she agrees to take antipsychotic medication, but strange events keep happening around her, including a near-fatal accident with a falling statue of an angel. Torn between Cam's open flirtation and her mysterious connection to Daniel, Luce begins to research his past with Penn's help and discovers evidence suggesting that she and Daniel have met many times before, in different eras. She eventually learns that Daniel and several of her schoolmates are fallen angels and that she has been reincarnated repeatedly, each time falling in love with Daniel and dying before their love can be fulfilled. As a battle between heaven and hell draws closer to Sword and Cross, Luce must discover who she really is and whom she can trust.

The film was a critical and commercial failure. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 7 percent approval rating based on 14 reviews, with an average score of 3.2 out of 10. Several critics compared it unfavorably with earlier supernatural teen romances, and its long-delayed American release did little to attract an audience.

overview: Buenos Aires, Argentina. A luxurious van is parked on the sidewalk. A man enters with the purpose of stealing whatever he can find, but when he wants to leave, he cannot. The doors do not open, the control panel does not respond: the van has become an armored box and he is trapped like a mouse.
tagline: Welcome aboard
title: 4x4
plot:
4x4 is a 2019 Argentine crime thriller written by Mariano Cohn and Gastón Duprat and directed by Cohn, who conceived it after reading news reports of car thieves trapped inside vehicles. Peter Lanzani stars as the petty criminal Ciro and Dady Brieva as the car's owner, Dr. Enrique Ferrari, with Luis Brandoni as a retired police negotiator. Its premise recalls the 1998 Argentine film Captured. Buena Vista International released it in Argentina on 4 April 2019, where it had the year's best opening weekend for a local film.

In a Buenos Aires neighbourhood, Ciro breaks into a parked SUV, starts stripping out the stereo and other valuables and vandalises the interior. When he tries to leave, the doors will not open. The vehicle is reinforced, bulletproof, soundproof and tinted, so that nobody outside can see or hear him; a bullet he fires at the windscreen ricochets into his thigh, and his phone soon dies. As the hours pass he battles heat, thirst and an infected wound.

Then the car's phone rings. The caller is Ferrari, an obstetrician who has been the victim of repeated crimes and who has turned his car into a trap. He warns that the fuel tank is rigged with explosives and begins a long, taunting dialogue, revealing that he is a widower with a daughter and grandchild and is dying of cancer. When Ciro threatens his family, Ferrari blasts freezing air into the cabin, and rewards obedience with small mercies such as a hidden water hose or a chocolate bar. Ciro grows delirious, drinks his own urine and rails against a society he says belongs to the rich. Ferrari visits Ciro's wife and son, giving them money under a pretext, and confronts him with his violent criminal record.

After Ciro's dream of escape proves an illusion, Ferrari arrives to take him away, and a public stand-off erupts when police intervene. Retired negotiator Julio Amadeo is called in, while the neighbourhood divides between those who want Ciro punished and those who want him freed. Persuaded to give up, Ferrari instead climbs into his car and detonates the explosive, killing himself. Ciro is arrested and awaits trial, and the media nickname Ferrari the "Samurai Doctor" as the case sparks a debate about crime and insecurity. The film was not released in Spanish cinemas, going instead to television.

overview: In Greenwich Village in the early 1960s, gifted but volatile folk musician Llewyn Davis struggles with money, relationships, and his uncertain future.
title: Inside Llewyn Davis
plot:
Inside Llewyn Davis is a 2013 black comedy-drama written, directed, produced and edited by Joel and Ethan Coen. Oscar Isaac, in his breakthrough role, plays a struggling folk singer in Greenwich Village in 1961, with Carey Mulligan, Justin Timberlake, John Goodman, Garrett Hedlund, F. Murray Abraham and Adam Driver. Loosely inspired by Dave Van Ronk's memoir, it features folk songs performed live in full, with music produced by T Bone Burnett. It premiered at Cannes in May 2013, winning the Grand Prix.

In February 1961, Llewyn Davis's solo album is not selling, he has no money and sleeps on friends' couches. After a set at the Gaslight Café he is beaten in an alley by a stranger in a suit. Waking in the apartment of the Gorfeins, an academic couple, he accidentally lets their ginger cat out, and ends up carrying it around the city. Staying with the singers Jim and Jean Berkey, he learns that Jean is pregnant and may be carrying his child; she furiously demands that he pay for an abortion. His sister urges him to go back to the merchant marine.

To raise money he joins Jim and Al Cody in recording a silly novelty song about space travel, taking a $200 fee instead of royalties. At the clinic he discovers that a former girlfriend he had paid to have an abortion two years earlier had in fact kept the child. At dinner with the Gorfeins he lashes out when Mrs. Gorfein sings the harmony of his late partner Mike, who killed himself, and the cat he returned turns out to be the wrong one.

Llewyn rides to Chicago with the gruff jazz musician Roland Turner and the silent beat poet Johnny Five. When Johnny is arrested and Roland lies unconscious after an overdose, Llewyn abandons the car and the cat. In Chicago he plays for the impresario Bud Grossman, who is unmoved and suggests he join a trio, which he refuses. Hitchhiking home, he hits a cat on the road. Back in New York he cannot ship out because his sister threw away his seaman's licence, and he drunkenly heckles a performer at the Gaslight. The Gorfeins' real cat, Ulysses, has found its own way home. The story loops back to the opening night: as a young Bob Dylan takes the stage, Llewyn is beaten in the alley by the heckled singer's husband.

Widely acclaimed, the film holds 92% on Rotten Tomatoes and earned two Academy Award nominations.

original_title: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
overview: The sailor of legend is framed by the goddess Eris for the theft of the Book of Peace, and must travel to her realm at the end of the world to retrieve it and save the life of his childhood friend Prince Proteus.
title: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
plot:
Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas is a 2003 animated adventure comedy film produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of Sinbad, a sailor who gets caught up in a quest to retrieve the magical Golden Chalice.

The film begins with Sinbad (voiced by Brad Pitt), a charismatic and cunning sailor who has lost his way after being shipwrecked on a deserted island. He is rescued by a group of pirates led by Captain Cutler (voiced by John Cleese) and his daughter, Marina (voiced by Michelle Pfeiffer). Sinbad soon discovers that the Golden Chalice, which can grant any wish, has been stolen from the sea goddess, Eris (voiced by Catherine Zeta-Jones).

Eris tasks Sinbad with retrieving the chalice, but he is not the only one on the quest. The villainous Captain Cutler and his crew are also after the chalice, intending to use its power to gain control over the seas. Along the way, Sinbad meets a talking parrot named Pola (voiced by Leila Arcieri) who becomes his unlikely ally.

As Sinbad navigates through treacherous waters, he faces various obstacles and challenges, including fierce sea creatures and treacherous storms. He also discovers that Marina is not just a beautiful woman, but also a skilled warrior with her own motivations for retrieving the chalice.

Throughout the journey, Sinbad's character undergoes significant development as he learns to put aside his selfish desires and work towards a greater good. He forms an unlikely bond with Marina, who becomes a valuable partner in his quest.

The film features stunning animation, witty humor, and memorable characters. The voice cast delivers impressive performances, bringing depth and nuance to their respective roles. The movie's climax features an epic battle between Sinbad and Captain Cutler, with the fate of the seas hanging in the balance.

In the end, Sinbad successfully retrieves the Golden Chalice, but not before learning a valuable lesson about the importance of friendship and sacrifice. He returns to Eris' kingdom, where he is hailed as a hero and rewarded for his bravery. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with Sinbad and Marina sharing a romantic moment, hinting at a possible future together.

Overall, Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas is a thrilling adventure that combines humor, action, and romance. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's no wonder this film has become a beloved classic among animated movie fans.

overview: As the railroad builders advance unstoppably through the Arizona desert on their way to the sea, Jill arrives in the small town of Flagstone with the intention of starting a new life.
tagline: There were three men in her life. One to take her… one to love her —and one to kill her.
title: Once Upon a Time in the West
plot:
Once Upon a Time in the West is a classic Western film directed by Sergio Leone, released in 1968 by Paramount Pictures. The movie is set in the late 19th century and follows the story of Frank, a mysterious stranger who arrives in the small town of Red Rock, where he becomes embroiled in a conflict between a group of settlers and a ruthless outlaw named Harry Luck.

The film begins with Frank (Henry Fonda), a former Union soldier, arriving in Red Rock, where he meets a young woman named Jill McBain (Claudia Cardinale). Frank is immediately drawn to Jill, but their budding romance is complicated by the presence of Harry Luck (Charles Bronson), a notorious outlaw who has been terrorizing the town.

As Frank and Jill's relationship deepens, they become embroiled in a conflict between the settlers and Harry Luck, who is determined to take over the town's gold mine. The settlers, led by a man named Harmonica (Claude Debusschere), are determined to protect their land and way of life from Harry's tyranny.

Meanwhile, Frank discovers that Jill is actually the daughter of a wealthy rancher named Lattimo (Luigi Zanni) and that she has been hiding her true identity in order to escape her family's expectations. As tensions between the settlers and Harry's gang escalate, Frank finds himself drawn into a violent confrontation with the outlaws.

One of the most iconic scenes in the film is the "Harmonica" sequence, in which Harmonica plays a haunting melody on his harmonica while being pursued by Harry's gang. This scene has become an iconic moment in Western cinema and showcases Debusschere's impressive acting skills.

As the conflict between Frank and Harry reaches its climax, it becomes clear that Frank is not just a simple stranger, but a complex and troubled individual with a deep sense of justice. In a final confrontation, Frank faces off against Harry and his gang, leading to a violent and bloody showdown.

In the end, Frank emerges victorious, but not without scars. He rides off into the sunset with Jill by his side, leaving behind the violence and bloodshed of the conflict. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that Frank has finally found redemption and a sense of purpose in life.

Throughout the film, Leone's direction is masterful, using long takes and sweeping cinematography to create a sense of scope and scale. The score by Ennio Morricone is equally iconic, featuring a haunting theme that has become synonymous with Western cinema.

Overall, Once Upon a Time in the West is a classic Western film that explores themes of violence, redemption, and the search for identity. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and iconic scenes, it remains one of the greatest Westerns of all time.

overview: Six years ago NASA discovered the possibility of alien life within our solar system. A probe was launched to collect samples, but crashed upon re-entry over Central America. Soon after, new life forms began to appear and half of Mexico was quarantined as an infected zone. Today, the American and Mexican military still struggle to contain "the creatures," while a journalist agrees to escort a shaken tourist through the infected zone in Mexico to the safety of the U.S. border.
tagline: After Six Years, They're No Longer Aliens. They're Residents
title: Monsters
plot:
Monsters (2010) is a British science fiction film directed by Gareth Edwards. 

The movie revolves around two American scientists, Dr. Wood (Swoosie Kurtz) and her assistant, Amanda (Zoe Saldana), who are sent to Mexico to investigate the disappearance of several people in a small town. They soon discover that the missing individuals have been transformed into humanoid creatures with reptilian features.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, they meet Dr. Mitchell (Jason Flemyng) and his assistant, James (Sylvester McCoy), who are also investigating the strange occurrences. The two teams eventually team up to uncover the truth behind the transformations.

The main themes of Monsters include:

1. Isolation: The film explores the theme of isolation through the characters' experiences in the remote Mexican town. The isolated setting heightens the sense of unease and fear as the characters navigate the unknown.
2. Science vs. Nature: The movie delves into the consequences of scientific experimentation gone wrong, highlighting the dangers of playing with nature. The creatures are a result of human experimentation, and their existence serves as a warning about the risks of tampering with the natural world.
3. Human Connection: Despite the eerie atmosphere, the film emphasizes the importance of human connection and relationships. The characters form bonds with each other, which ultimately helps them survive the terrifying events unfolding around them.

The movie's slow-burning tension, atmospheric setting, and thought-provoking themes make it a compelling watch for fans of science fiction and horror.

overview: The impressionistic story of a Texas family in the 1950s. The film follows the life journey of the eldest son, Jack, through the innocence of childhood to his disillusioned adult years as he tries to reconcile a complicated relationship with his father. Jack finds himself a lost soul in the modern world, seeking answers to the origins and meaning of life while questioning the existence of faith.
tagline: Nothing stands still.
title: The Tree of Life
plot:
The Tree of Life is a 2011 American drama film written and directed by Terrence Malick. The movie is known for its philosophical and poetic exploration of life, existence, and the human condition.

The main themes of The Tree ofLife are:

1. **The Meaning of Life**: The film grapples with the question of why we exist and what gives our lives meaning. It explores the idea that life is a mystery that cannot be fully understood or explained.
2. **Family and Relationships**: The movie focuses on the O'Brien family, particularly the relationship between the father (played by Brad Pitt) and his three sons. It examines the complexities of family dynamics, love, loss, and the passing of time.
3. **Existentialism and the Human Condition**: The Tree of Life is a deeply philosophical film that explores existentialist ideas about human existence, mortality, and the search for meaning in an indifferent universe.
4. **Nature and the Universe**: The film features stunning visuals of nature, from the Texas landscape to the vastness of space. It uses these images to explore the interconnectedness of all things and the mystery of creation.
5. **Memory and Nostalgia**: The movie is structured around a series of fragmented memories, which are presented in a non-linear fashion. This structure reflects the way our memories can be distorted or incomplete, and how nostalgia can shape our understanding of ourselves and our experiences.

The film's narrative is also notable for its use of **poetic and symbolic language**, which adds to the sense of mystery and wonder. The Tree of Life has been praised for its beauty, depth, and emotional resonance, but it has also been criticized for its complexity and lack of traditional narrative structure.

Overall, The Tree of Life is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges viewers to consider the big questions about life, existence, and human experience.

original_title: Cirque du Freak: The Vampire's Assistant
overview: Darren Shan is a regular teenage kid. He and his friend Steve find out about a Freak Show coming to town and work hard at trying to find tickets. They do, and together they go to "Cirque du Freak" where they see many strange acts including a wolf-man and a bearded lady
tagline: Meet Darren. He's sixteen going on immortal.
title: Cirque du Freak: The Vampire's Assistant
plot:
Cirque du Freak: The Vampire's Assistant is a 2009 American vampire fantasy film directed by Paul Weitz, who wrote the screenplay with Brian Helgeland. It is loosely based on the first three books of Darren Shan's twelve-part young adult series The Saga of Darren Shan: Cirque du Freak, The Vampire's Assistant and Tunnels of Blood. Chris Massoglia stars as Darren Shan, with John C. Reilly as the vampire Larten Crepsley, Josh Hutcherson, Ken Watanabe, Salma Hayek, Willem Dafoe, Patrick Fugit and Michael Cerveris. Universal Pictures released it on 23 October 2009.

In an American town, high school student Darren Shan and his rebellious best friend Steve Leonard sneak out at night to see a traveling freak show, the Cirque du Freak. During the performance, Steve recognizes one of the performers, Larten Crepsley, as a vampire more than a century old, and goes looking for him afterward. Darren, meanwhile, is fascinated by Crepsley's performing spider, Madame Octa, and steals her. Hiding in Crepsley's dressing room, he overhears Steve begging to be made a vampire, a request that Crepsley refuses after tasting Steve's blood and declaring that it tastes of evil.

Darren escapes, and he soon encounters the mysterious Mr. Tiny and the brutish Murlough. When Madame Octa bites Steve, Darren makes a deal with Crepsley: in exchange for the antidote, he agrees to become a half-vampire and Crepsley's assistant. To protect his family, Darren fakes his own death and joins the Cirque, where he meets its remarkable performers, including the bearded lady Madame Truska, the snake boy Evra and Rebecca, a girl with a monkey's tail, with whom he begins a romance. Darren struggles with his refusal to drink human blood, while he learns that the peaceful vampires are on the brink of war with the Vampaneze, a faction of vampires who kill when they feed. Mr. Tiny, who secretly manipulates both sides, recruits a resentful Steve to the Vampaneze, setting the former friends on a collision course.

The film received poor reviews, with a 37 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus described it as an overstuffed, scattershot vampire film with poor characterization and an unwieldy mix of scares and laughs, and a Metacritic score of 43. It was a commercial failure, grossing $39.2 million against a $40 million budget, and planned sequels were never made.

overview: Two middle-aged men embark on a spiritual journey through Californian wine country. One is an unpublished novelist suffering from depression, and the other is only days away from walking down the aisle.
tagline: In search of wine. In search of women. In search of themselves.
title: Sideways
plot:
Sideways is a 2004 American comedy-drama film directed by Alexander Payne, written by Jim Taylor and Peter Hedges, and produced by Fox Searchlight Pictures.

The main themes of Sideways include:

1. **Friendship and camaraderie**: The movie explores the complex and evolving friendship between Miles (Paul Giamatti) and Jack (Thomas Haden Church), two middle-aged men who embark on a wine-tasting tour through California's Napa Valley. Their bond is tested as they navigate their personal struggles, relationships, and midlife crises.

2. **Midlife crisis and existentialism**: The film delves into the themes of aging, identity, and purpose. Miles, in particular, is struggling to come to terms with his own mortality, failed marriage, and stagnant career. His journey serves as a metaphor for the search for meaning and connection in life's twilight years.

3. **Love, loss, and relationships**: The movie also explores the complexities of love, heartbreak, and relationships. Miles' ex-wife, Brenda (Virginia Madsen), is struggling to move on from their failed marriage, while Jack's own romantic entanglements are revealed throughout the film.

4. **The American Dream and disillusionment**: Sideways critiques the idea of the "American Dream," which promises success, happiness, and fulfillment. The characters' experiences in Napa Valley serve as a commentary on the superficiality and materialism that can accompany this idealized lifestyle.

5. **Self-discovery and personal growth**: Ultimately, the film suggests that true growth and self-awareness come from confronting one's fears, insecurities, and limitations. Miles' journey is marked by moments of introspection, vulnerability, and acceptance, which ultimately lead to a deeper understanding of himself and his place in the world.

Sideways received widespread critical acclaim for its nuanced portrayal of complex themes, memorable characters, and Alexander Payne's masterful direction.

overview: Josie, Melody and Val are three small-town girl musicians determined to take their rock band out of their garage and straight to the top, while remaining true to their look, style and sound. They get a record deal which brings fame and fortune but soon realize they are pawns of two people who want to control the youth of America. They must clear their names, even if it means losing fame and fortune.
tagline: They were three small time girls, with big time dreams. Now, fate is giving the Pussycats, the chance of a lifetime.
title: Josie and the Pussycats
plot:
Josie and the Pussycats is a 2001 musical comedy film that explores several themes, primarily focusing on female empowerment, friendship, and self-discovery. The movie follows the story of Josie, Melody, and Valerie, three teenage girls who form a rock band called the Pussycats.

At its core, the film celebrates the power of female friendships and the importance of supporting one another in pursuing their passions. The main characters are strong-willed and independent individuals who refuse to be defined by societal expectations or stereotypes. They use their music as a means of self-expression and empowerment, taking control of their lives and forging their own paths.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, particularly for young women navigating the complexities of adolescence. Josie, Melody, and Valerie must balance their individual desires with the pressures of conformity and social norms. Through their experiences, they learn to stay true to themselves and find their unique voices.

Furthermore, the film critiques the music industry's objectification of women, as embodied by the villainous character, Wyatt Frame. The Pussycats' rise to fame serves as a commentary on the commodification of female talent and the exploitation of young artists for commercial gain.

Ultimately, Josie and the Pussycats is a heartwarming tale about embracing one's individuality, finding creative expression, and celebrating the bonds of sisterhood.

overview: When straight arrow FBI agent Roy Clayton heads up the investigation into a dangerous international conspiracy, all clues seem to lead back to former U.S. Special Operations officer Samir Horn.
tagline: The truth is complicated.
title: Traitor
plot:
Traitor is a 2008 spy thriller film that delves into the complexities of loyalty, deception, and redemption. The story revolves around Roy Clayton (played by Don Cheadle), a CIA operative who goes undercover to infiltrate an international terrorist organization.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes apparent that nothing is as it seems, and the lines between loyalty and betrayal are constantly blurred. The film expertly weaves together themes of identity, trust, and the moral gray areas that often accompany espionage work.

One of the primary concerns of Traitor is the exploration of the human cost of deception. Clayton's character is forced to navigate a web of lies and half-truths, which takes a toll on his personal relationships and sense of self. The film raises questions about the nature of loyalty and whether it can ever be truly earned or given.

The movie also touches on the theme of redemption, as Clayton grapples with the consequences of his actions and seeks to make amends for past mistakes. This narrative thread adds a layer of complexity to the story, highlighting the difficulties of escaping one's past and finding forgiveness in a world where trust is often a luxury.

Throughout Traitor, the tension between loyalty and deception creates a sense of unease, mirroring Clayton's inner turmoil as he struggles to distinguish between right and wrong. The film's exploration of these themes ultimately raises important questions about the nature of humanity and our capacity for both good and evil.

overview: A mysterious woman recruits bank teller Ludwig Dieter to lead a group of aspiring thieves on a top-secret heist during the early stages of the zombie apocalypse.
tagline: Before Vegas, one locksmith became a legend.
title: Army of Thieves
plot:
Army of Thieves is a 2021 heist film directed by Chris McKay and written by Chris McKay and Adam Sztykiel. The movie takes place in an alternate universe where the events of Deadpool 2 occurred, but with some key differences.

The story follows Dieter Deitz (played by Daniel Radcliffe), a young thief who works for a gang led by Lacey (played by Natasha Lyonne). However, after being betrayed and left for dead by his partner, Dieter sets out on a solo mission to steal the world's largest diamond, known as the "Heart of Europe," which is currently in transit from Berlin to Amsterdam.

Dieter's plan involves infiltrating the armored transport vehicle carrying the diamond, but he soon discovers that it's being escorted by an elite team of mercenaries led by the ruthless and cunning Lacey. As Dieter navigates the complex web of thieves and con artists, he must use his wits and cunning to stay one step ahead of his enemies.

Along the way, Dieter meets a mysterious woman named Kate (played by Lucy Fry), who claims to be an expert in safe-cracking and helps him on his mission. As they work together, Dieter begins to question his own morals and loyalties, particularly when he discovers that Lacey's true intentions for the diamond are far more sinister than he initially thought.

As the stakes grow higher, Dieter finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with Lacey and her team, with the fate of the diamond and the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Dieter must use all his skills and resources to outwit his enemies and claim the Heart of Europe for himself.

Throughout the movie, Radcliffe delivers a standout performance as Dieter, bringing a sense of vulnerability and humor to the role. The supporting cast is equally impressive, with Lyonne and Fry delivering memorable performances as the ruthless and cunning Lacey and Kate.

Overall, Army of Thieves is a fun and action-packed heist film that explores themes of loyalty, morality, and redemption. With its witty dialogue, clever plot twists, and standout performances, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: Film geek Josh is looking for the subject of his new documentary when a chance meeting puts the perfect star in his sights—Dylan, his school's most popular junior. But Dylan's hopes of using the film to become Blossom Queen don't quite match with Josh's goal to make a hard-hitting exposé about popularity. Will Josh shoot the film as planned, or show Dylan as the truly interesting person she is?
title: Geek Charming
plot:
Geek Charming is a 2011 American romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of high school relationships and social cliques. The movie delves into the theme of self-discovery, as the protagonist, Mac, navigates his way through adolescence and grapples with his own identity.

The film also touches on the idea of social hierarchy and the pressures that come with fitting in. The main characters are divided into distinct groups, each with their own set of expectations and stereotypes. This dichotomy serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of conformity, individuality, and the challenges of finding one's place within these societal structures.

Furthermore, Geek Charming examines the complexities of first love and relationships, highlighting the vulnerability and uncertainty that often accompany these experiences. The movie also explores the tension between tradition and innovation, as Mac struggles to reconcile his own desires with the expectations placed upon him by those around him.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced portrayal of high school life, capturing the messy, emotional, and often overwhelming nature of adolescence. Through its relatable characters and engaging storyline, Geek Charming offers a thoughtful exploration of the challenges and triumphs that come with growing up.

overview: Four sisters come of age in America in the aftermath of the Civil War.
tagline: Own your story
title: Little Women
plot:
Little Women is a 2019 American period drama written and directed by Greta Gerwig. It is the seventh film adaptation of Louisa May Alcott's 1868 novel and chronicles the lives of the four March sisters, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy, in Concord, Massachusetts, in the 19th century. The ensemble cast includes Saoirse Ronan as Jo, Emma Watson as Meg, Florence Pugh as Amy, Eliza Scanlen as Beth, Laura Dern as their mother Marmee, Timothée Chalamet as Laurie, and Tracy Letts, Bob Odenkirk, James Norton, Louis Garrel, Chris Cooper and Meryl Streep. Drawing on Alcott's other writings and her own life, Gerwig restructured the story using a nonlinear timeline.

The film opens in 1868, with Jo working as a teacher in New York and selling her stories to a newspaper editor, Mr. Dashwood. Her youngest sister Amy is in Paris with their wealthy Aunt March, studying painting and being courted by the rich Fred Vaughn, when she meets their childhood friend Laurie, who has fallen into an aimless and dissolute life. Jo is stung when Friedrich Bhaer, a German professor at her boarding house, criticizes her writing, and soon after she returns home to Concord when she learns that Beth's illness has worsened.

The story alternates between these adult years and the sisters' adolescence seven years earlier, during the American Civil War, when their father was away fighting and the family lived in reduced circumstances. In the earlier timeline, the girls befriend Laurie and his grandfather Mr. Laurence, put on plays, quarrel and support one another, and Marmee teaches them generosity toward neighbors poorer than themselves. Meg longs for pretty things but marries the modest tutor John Brooke for love, Jo rejects Laurie's marriage proposal because she wants independence and a writing career, Beth's frailty after a bout of scarlet fever haunts the family, and Amy pursues art and a practical marriage. In the end, Jo turns her family's story into a novel and negotiates with her publisher over both its ending and her rights to it.

Little Women received widespread acclaim for Gerwig's screenplay and direction, the performances, the costumes and Alexandre Desplat's score. It grossed more than $218 million worldwide. It received six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Actress for Ronan, Best Supporting Actress for Pugh and Best Adapted Screenplay, and won for Best Costume Design.

overview: David's comfortable world is turned upside down when his birth mother Melissa unexpectedly reaches out, longing to meet the eighteen year old son she's only held once.
tagline: Hope is at the heart of every journey.
title: Lifemark
plot:
Lifemark is a 2022 American Christian drama directed by Kevin Peeples, based on the true story of David Scotton, whose birth mother considered abortion before choosing adoption and who reconnected with her as a young adult. Kirk Cameron, Alex Kendrick and Raphael Ruggero star, with Dawn Long and Rebecca Rogers in supporting roles. Alex and Stephen Kendrick co-wrote the script with Peeples and served as executive producers; it was the brothers' first adaptation of a true story. The story had previously been told in the 2018 short documentary I Lived on Parker Avenue.

Melissa is a frightened, pregnant teenager who goes to a clinic to end her pregnancy. At the last moment, she tells the doctor that she cannot go through with it. She chooses to give birth to her son and arranges for him to be adopted, and the baby, named David, is raised by a loving couple, the Coltons, in Louisiana. Eighteen years later, David is a high school senior with a close relationship to his adoptive parents when Melissa reaches out to him through the adoption agency. The two connect through social media, and David must sort through his feelings about the mother who gave him up before deciding to meet her. Their reunion brings together both of his families, and David learns the full story of the choice that saved his life, while Melissa finds healing from the pain she has carried since his birth.

Scotton first told his story in a 2011 pro-life oratory contest at Jesuit High School in New Orleans, and Louisiana Right to Life funded the documentary, which he later presented across the country. Cameron, who had worked with the Kendricks on Fireproof, brought the project to them after seeing the documentary. Both Stephen Kendrick and Cameron have adopted children, and Cameron's wife was herself adopted, which they cited as motivation. The filmmakers used two sets of actors for the birth parents across the time jump and de-aging techniques for the adoptive parents. Development began in 2019, and Stephen Kendrick described its release after the Dobbs decision as providential timing.

After traditional distributors declined, the film was released through Fathom Events on September 9, 2022, and its one-week run was extended due to strong ticket sales. Rotten Tomatoes reports 83% positive reviews from six critics. Christian outlets praised Ruggero's performance, while World magazine felt it paled beside the documentary, and the National Catholic Register noted a lack of conflict.

overview: A miserable conman and his partner pose as Santa and his Little Helper to rob department stores on Christmas Eve. But they run into problems when the conman befriends a troubled kid.
tagline: He doesn't care if you're naughty or nice.
title: Bad Santa
plot:
Bad Santa is a dark comedy film released in 2003, directed by Terry Zwigoff and written by Glenn Ficarra and John Requa. The movie stars Billy Bob Thornton as Willie Soke, a con man who poses as a mall Santa Claus during the holiday season.

The story begins on Christmas Eve, where we meet Willie Soke (Billy Bob Thornton), a rough-around-the-edges, hard-drinking, and foul-mouthed individual who is forced to take a job as a mall Santa due to his financial struggles. Willie's plan is to scam the wealthy families that visit him by pretending to be a jolly old man, while secretly drinking and causing chaos.

Willie's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Thurman Merman (Brett Kelly), a 6-year-old boy who has been sent to the mall as part of his father's divorce proceedings. Thurman is a troubled child who has been shuffled between foster homes and is struggling to cope with his parents' separation.

As Willie spends more time with Thurman, he begins to develop a bond with the young boy, who reminds him of his own childhood struggles. Despite their differences, Willie takes Thurman under his wing and teaches him how to scam the wealthy families at the mall.

However, things take a turn when Willie's con artist past catches up with him, and he is forced to confront his own demons. Meanwhile, Thurman's father, Harry Merman (John C. Reilly), becomes suspicious of Willie's intentions and starts to investigate his background.

As Christmas Eve comes to an end, Willie and Thurman embark on a wild adventure that takes them from the mall to a seedy bar, where they encounter a group of shady characters. Along the way, Willie learns valuable lessons about the importance of family, friendship, and redemption.

The movie culminates in a heartwarming finale where Willie and Thurman share a heartfelt moment, and Willie finally finds a sense of belonging and purpose. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Willie and Thurman parting ways but promising to stay in touch.

Throughout the movie, Billy Bob Thornton delivers a tour-de-force performance as Willie Soke, bringing depth and nuance to a character that could have easily been one-dimensional. Brett Kelly shines as Thurman Merman, capturing the vulnerability and spirit of a child struggling to find his place in the world.

Overall, Bad Santa is a darkly comedic masterpiece that explores themes of redemption, family, and the power of human connection during the holiday season. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and heartwarming story, this movie has become a cult classic that continues to delight audiences to this day.

overview: Bill O'Neal infiltrates the Black Panthers on the orders of FBI Agent Mitchell and J. Edgar Hoover. As Black Panther Chairman Fred Hampton ascends—falling for a fellow revolutionary en route—a battle wages for O’Neal’s soul.
tagline: You can kill a revolutionary but you can't kill the revolution.
title: Judas and the Black Messiah
plot:
Judas and the Black Messiah is a 2021 American biographical drama film directed by Shaka King. The movie tells the story of Fred Hampton, a young black Panther Party leader who was assassinated in 1969.

The main themes of Judas and the Black Messiah include:

* The struggle for civil rights and social justice: The film highlights the Black Panther Party's efforts to address systemic racism and police brutality in the United States during the late 1960s.
* The complexities of leadership and power: Fred Hampton's character is portrayed as a charismatic leader who is both admired by his followers and feared by his enemies. The movie explores the challenges of balancing personal ambition with the demands of leadership.
* The corrupting influence of power: The film also examines how the FBI, led by Agent William O'Neill (played by Daniel Kaluuya), uses its power to manipulate and destroy Hampton's movement from within.
* The importance of community and solidarity: Throughout the movie, Hampton's relationships with his comrades and allies are depicted as crucial to his success and survival. The film emphasizes the value of building strong networks and alliances in the face of adversity.

The title "Judas and the Black Messiah" refers to the biblical story of Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus Christ for 30 pieces of silver. In this context, the title suggests that William O'Neill is the "Judas" figure, who betrays Hampton's trust and ultimately leads to his downfall.

Overall, Judas and the Black Messiah is a powerful and thought-provoking film that sheds light on a pivotal moment in American history and the ongoing struggle for racial justice.

overview: Hours after the tragic death of their youngest brother in unexplained circumstances, three siblings have their lives thrown into chaos.
title: Athena
plot:
Athena is a 2022 French action drama directed by Romain Gavras, who co-wrote it with Ladj Ly and Elias Belkeddar. Dali Benssalah, Sami Slimane, Anthony Bajon, Ouassini Embarek and Alexis Manenti star. Known for its long, elaborate single-take sequences, the film depicts an uprising in a French housing estate after the death of a teenage boy. It premiered in competition for the Golden Lion at the 79th Venice International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released on Netflix later that month.

Abdel, a French soldier of Algerian descent who has served in Mali, holds a press conference outside a police station after the death of his 13-year-old brother Idir, who was apparently beaten to death by men in police uniforms in an incident captured on video. As Abdel appeals for calm, his younger brother Karim and a group of young men throw a Molotov cocktail, storm the station and steal weapons, equipment and a police van. They retreat to Athena, the sprawling housing estate on the outskirts of Paris where the brothers grew up, and turn it into a fortress, barricading themselves and the residents inside.

Riot police are sent to retake the estate, and the young rebels fight back with fireworks and improvised weapons, while the area's residents are evacuated. Caught between the two sides are Abdel, who tries desperately to restore order and protect his family; their older half-brother Moktar, a drug dealer who wants only to move his merchandise out of the estate; Karim, who demands the names of the officers responsible for Idir's death; and Jérôme, a young riot police officer who becomes trapped inside the complex. As the night goes on and the violence intensifies, Abdel's loyalties are tested, rumors circulate that far-right extremists may have been behind the killing, and the siege becomes a tragedy that engulfs the entire family.

Athena received mostly positive reviews. Critics widely praised Gavras's direction, the virtuoso long takes, the cinematography and the sound design, comparing its staging to Greek tragedy, but some found its characters thinly drawn and its treatment of political issues superficial, and the film provoked debate in France about its depiction of the banlieues.

overview: Dueling high school debate champs who are at odds on just about everything forge ahead with ambitious plans to get into the colleges of their dreams.
tagline: Two rivals have met their match
title: Candy Jar
plot: Dueling high school debate champs who are at odds on just about everything forge ahead with ambitious plans to get into the colleges of their dreams.

overview: A renowned professor is forced to reassess her life when she is diagnosed with terminal ovarian cancer.
tagline: It appears to be a matter of life and death.
title: Wit
plot:
Wit is a 2001 drama film that revolves around the life of Vivian Bell, a brilliant and ambitious English professor who struggles with ovarian cancer. The movie delves into the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and mortality.

At its core, Wit explores the theme of resilience in the face of adversity. Vivian's unwavering determination to live life on her own terms despite being diagnosed with a terminal illness is both inspiring and heartbreaking. Her unapologetic attitude towards death serves as a catalyst for self-discovery, forcing her to reevaluate her priorities and relationships.

The film also examines the intricacies of human connection, particularly in the context of romantic love. Vivian's complicated past and present relationships serve as a backdrop for exploring the complexities of intimacy, vulnerability, and trust. Her interactions with those around her, including her colleagues and loved ones, reveal the fragility and beauty of human relationships.

Furthermore, Wit touches on the theme of identity and legacy. As Vivian navigates her mortality, she grapples with the idea of leaving a lasting impact on the world. Her struggles to come to terms with her own mortality serve as a poignant reminder that our time is limited, and it's up to us to make the most of it.

Ultimately, Wit presents a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. The film's thoughtful pacing and nuanced performances create a cinematic experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: This documentary follows a team of local archaeologists excavating never before explored passageways, shafts, and tombs, piecing together the secrets of Egypt’s most significant find in almost 50 years in Saqqara.
title: Secrets of the Saqqara Tomb
plot:
Secrets of the Saqqara Tomb is a 2020 British documentary film directed by James Tovell and produced by At Land Productions and Lion Television. It follows a team of Egyptian archaeologists as they excavate a tomb dating to the 25th century BC in the vast Saqqara necropolis outside Cairo, a burial that had remained sealed and untouched for some 4,400 years. The Egyptologist Salima Ikram is among those who appear on screen. Netflix released the film on October 28, 2020.

The documentary centers on a local excavation team led by the Egyptologist Mohammad Mohammad Youssef, as they explore a series of passageways, burial shafts and chambers that had never been entered in modern times. The tomb belongs to Wahtye, a high-ranking priest who served during the Fifth Dynasty of Egypt's Old Kingdom, and to members of his family. Its walls are decorated with vividly colored reliefs and painted scenes, preserved in remarkable condition, along with dozens of carved statues of the priest and his relatives. The discovery was hailed as one of the most significant Egyptian finds in nearly half a century.

As the excavation progresses, the cameras follow the team through the painstaking work of clearing the shafts, often descending deep underground in difficult and dangerous conditions. The archaeologists recover a rich collection of artifacts, including personal possessions, statues, pottery and the mummified remains of members of the priest's family, as well as an unexpected find of a mummified lion cub. The documentary interweaves the progress of the dig with an investigation into who Wahtye was, how he and his family lived and died, and what their tomb reveals about religious beliefs and daily life in ancient Egypt. Specialists examine the human remains to learn about the family's health and causes of death, and the team tries to determine whether the people buried in the shafts are indeed Wahtye and his relatives.

The film emphasizes the role of Egyptian archaeologists in uncovering their own country's history, and it captures the excitement and tension of the moment when sealed chambers and sarcophagi are opened for the first time. The discovery of the tomb was announced publicly by Egyptian antiquities officials in late 2018 and drew international attention, and the documentary offers an extended behind-the-scenes account of the excavation that followed.

overview: Contemporary Moscow. A talented gambler gathers a team of people with supernatural powers to win big at a casino. But they find a much stronger mystical rival.
title: Beyond the Edge
plot:
Beyond the Edge is a 2018 South African drama film directed by Michael John Barton. The movie follows the story of a young boy named Sibusiso, who runs away from his troubled home life and finds himself at the edge of a vast savannah.

The main themes of Beyond the Edge revolve around the struggles of growing up in poverty-stricken communities, family dynamics, and the search for identity. The film explores how Sibusiso's journey is shaped by his experiences with loss, abandonment, and the harsh realities of life on the outskirts of society.

Throughout the movie, Barton delves into themes such as:

1. **Resilience and Survival**: Sibusiso's determination to survive in a world that seems determined to crush him serves as a testament to the human spirit's capacity for resilience.
2. **Family and Belonging**: The film highlights the complexities of family relationships and the struggle to find one's place within them, particularly in the face of neglect and abandonment.
3. **Identity Formation**: As Sibusiso navigates his new surroundings, he begins to forge a sense of self, separate from the traumas of his past, and discovers what it means to be alive.

The movie features stunning cinematography that captures the vast expanse of the African savannah, serving as a backdrop for Sibusiso's emotional journey. Overall, Beyond the Edge is a powerful exploration of the human condition, tackling tough themes with sensitivity and nuance.

overview: Dorothy wakes up in post-tornado Kansas, only to be whisked back to Oz to try to save her old friends the Scarecrow, the Lion, the Tin Man and Glinda from a devious new villain, the Jester. Wiser the owl, Marshal Mallow, China Princess and Tugg the tugboat join Dorothy on her latest magical journey through the colorful landscape of Oz to restore order and happiness to Emerald City.
tagline: There's trouble in OZ...
title: Legends of Oz: Dorothy's Return
plot:
Legends of Oz: Dorothy's Return is an animated musical fantasy film that explores the idea of self-discovery and empowerment through Dorothy's journey. The movie delves into the complexities of growing up, as Dorothy navigates her way back to Kansas while confronting the harsh realities of adulthood.

One of the primary themes of the film is the struggle for independence. As Dorothy faces various challenges on her path, she must learn to rely on herself and trust her own instincts, rather than relying solely on others for guidance. This theme is beautifully illustrated through her interactions with Glinda, who serves as a mentor figure, but also pushes Dorothy to take control of her own destiny.

The movie also touches upon the idea of identity and self-discovery. As Dorothy encounters new characters and experiences different worlds, she begins to question her own sense of purpose and belonging. This introspection is a crucial aspect of her growth, as she learns to reconcile her past life in Kansas with her newfound understanding of herself.

Furthermore, Legends of Oz: Dorothy's Return explores the concept of home and what it truly means to belong. Throughout her journey, Dorothy grapples with the idea of returning to her familiar surroundings, only to discover that home is not just a physical place, but also a sense of belonging and connection with others.

The film's themes are woven together through its vibrant animation, memorable characters, and catchy musical numbers, creating a rich and immersive cinematic experience. Overall, Legends of Oz: Dorothy's Return is a heartwarming tale of self-discovery, empowerment, and the importance of finding one's own path in life.

overview: A family man convicted of killing an intruder must cope with life afterward in the violent penal system.
tagline: No rule. No hope. No way out.
title: Felon
plot:
Felon is a 2008 American drama film directed by Tiller Russell. The movie revolves around a man who has just been released from prison after serving a 20-year sentence for a crime he committed as a teenager.

The main theme of Felon explores the struggles of reintegration into society, particularly for individuals with felony convictions. The protagonist's journey is marked by his attempts to find employment and rebuild his life, but he faces numerous challenges, including racism, prejudice, and societal stigma.

Throughout the film, Russell sheds light on the harsh realities faced by people with felony records, who often struggle to find stable housing, employment, and access to basic necessities like healthcare. The movie also touches upon the theme of redemption, as the protagonist seeks to make amends for his past mistakes and start anew.

The film's narrative is character-driven, delving into the complexities of human emotions, relationships, and personal growth. It raises questions about the nature of justice, rehabilitation, and the cyclical nature of violence and trauma. Ultimately, Felon presents a poignant portrayal of the struggles faced by individuals with felony convictions, highlighting the need for compassion, understanding, and support in their journey towards redemption.

overview: 14 years after making a film about his journey across the USA, Borat risks life and limb when he returns to the United States with his young daughter, and reveals more about the culture, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the political elections.
tagline: Delivery of prodigious bribe to American regime for make benefit once glorious nation of Kazakhstan.
title: Borat Subsequent Moviefilm
plot:
Borat Subsequent Moviefilm is a satirical comedy film directed by Jason Woliner and written by Jay Roach, Sacha Baron Cohen, Anthony Hines, Dan Mazer, Eric Saindon, Jena Friedman, Lee Kern, and Aneru Ujapho. The film is the sequel to the 2006 film Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan.

The movie takes place five years after the events of the first film.
