But one morning, he wakes up to find his face is gone. All the years of acquiescence have cost him the one thing he can't replace: his identity. Now he's a blank, outside as well as in, an anonymous, featureless phantom. Bent on exacting revenge, he explodes. He isn't going to follow the rules anymore.
tagline: Meet the new face of terror.
title: Bruiser
plot:
Bruiser is a 2000 psychological thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows a hitman, played by Jason Flemyng, who suffers from dissociative identity disorder, which causes him to switch between different personas.

The main theme of Bruiser revolves around the exploration of the human psyche, specifically the concept of identity and how it can be fragmented and distorted. The film's protagonist is a complex character with multiple personalities, each with its own distinct traits and motivations. This fragmentation serves as a metaphor for the chaos and disorder that can exist within an individual's mind.

The movie also touches on the theme of violence and its effects on the human psyche. The hitman's profession is portrayed as a means to cope with his inner demons, but it ultimately leads to further emotional turmoil and disintegration. This highlights the cyclical nature of violence and how it can perpetuate itself, even in those who attempt to escape or overcome it.

Furthermore, Bruiser explores the idea of control and agency in a world that often seems to be beyond an individual's grasp. The protagonist's multiple personalities serve as a means of coping with the unpredictability of his life, but this also raises questions about the nature of free will and whether individuals can truly exert control over their circumstances.

Overall, Bruiser is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human psychology, exploring themes of identity, violence, and the search for control in a chaotic world.

overview: An angel under the thumb of a ruthless gangster is saved by a trumpet player down on his luck.
tagline: Love Is Stronger Than Death.
title: Passion Play
plot:
Passion Play is a 2011 American fantasy drama film written and directed by Mitch Glazer, in his feature directorial debut, and executive produced by Rebecca Wang. Mickey Rourke stars as a down-and-out jazz trumpeter, with Megan Fox as a carnival performer born with wings, Bill Murray as a gangster, and Rhys Ifans, Kelly Lynch and Robert Wisdom in supporting roles. Filmed from December 2009, it premiered at the 2010 Toronto International Film Festival, where its poor reception led to talk of a direct-to-video release.

Nate Poole is a washed-up jazz musician and recovering heroin addict whose luck has run out. After a gig one night he is attacked, tied up and driven into the desert by a hitman. Just as he is about to be executed, his would-be killer is shot dead by a group of Native Americans, who leave Nate unharmed. Wandering through the desert, he reaches a travelling carnival and freak show, full of fire eaters and sword swallowers, and asks to use a telephone.

There he becomes fascinated by Lily Luster, a beautiful young woman with real wings who is exhibited as one of the sideshow's attractions. Lily is aloof at first, but begins to see the kindly Nate as a possible escape from her life. When the carnival owner, Sam Adamo, tries to kill Nate, Lily saves him by stealing a truck, and the two run away to the city, where they begin a tentative romance.

Fearing for his life, Nate goes to see Happy Shannon, the wealthy gangster who ordered his death after Nate slept with Happy's wife, whom Happy also had killed. Nate offers him most of the profits from putting Lily on display, but Happy only believes in her wings after seeing her from a distance. He then takes Lily for himself, promising to leave Nate alive as long as she stays with him. Nate realises that he loves her and tries in vain to free her. Adamo, discovering where Lily is, breaks in to take her back and is shot dead by Happy.

When Nate learns that Happy is showing Lily in a glass case at a theatre, he smashes the case and the two flee to the roof, pursued by Happy's men. Lily doubts she can fly, so Nate leaps from the building and she jumps after him, catching him in mid-air. As they fly over the desert, Nate glimpses his own body lying where the hitman had taken him, suggesting that everything since had been his dying dream.

The film was savaged by critics, holding a 3% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Living with her snobby family on the brink of bankruptcy, Anne Elliot is an unconforming woman with modern sensibilities. When Frederick Wentworth - the dashing one she once sent away - crashes back into her life, Anne must choose between putting the past behind her or listening to her heart when it comes to second chances.
title: Persuasion
plot:
Persuasion is a 2022 American historical romance based on Jane Austen's 1817 novel of the same name. Directed by Carrie Cracknell from a screenplay by Ron Bass and Alice Victoria Winslow, it stars Dakota Johnson as Anne Elliot, Cosmo Jarvis as Captain Frederick Wentworth and Henry Golding as William Elliot, with Richard E. Grant as Sir Walter Elliot, Nikki Amuka-Bird as Lady Russell and Mia McKenna-Bruce as Mary.

Eight years before the story begins, Anne Elliot broke off her engagement to Frederick Wentworth, a young naval officer without wealth or connections, after being persuaded by her family and by Lady Russell, a family friend who has been like a mother to her, that the match was imprudent. Still unmarried years later, Anne lives with her vain and spendthrift father, Sir Walter, whose debts force him to rent out the family estate, Kellynch Hall, to Admiral Croft. While her father and her sister Elizabeth move to Bath, Anne is sent to stay with her self-absorbed younger sister Mary.

Anne soon learns that Admiral Croft's wife is Wentworth's sister, and that Wentworth, now a wealthy and celebrated captain, has returned to shore after years at sea. Their reunion is awkward and painful, especially as Mary's sister-in-law Louisa Musgrove sets her sights on him. On a seaside trip to Lyme, Anne meets Wentworth's naval friends and attracts the attention of her charming cousin William Elliot, the heir to her father's estate. As old feelings resurface and misunderstandings multiply, Anne must decide whether to trust her own heart and whether a second chance at love is possible.

The adaptation takes a deliberately modern approach, with Anne breaking the fourth wall to address the audience directly and contemporary dialogue and humor, a choice that divided viewers and critics.

Persuasion opened in select theaters in the United States on July 8, 2022, a week before its streaming release on Netflix on July 15. Reviews were largely negative: it has about 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it chaotically anachronistic, and a Metacritic score of 42.

overview: In 18th century France, the Chevalier de Fronsac and his Native American friend Mani are sent by the King to the Gevaudan province to investigate the killings of hundreds by a mysterious beast.
title: Brotherhood of the Wolf
plot:
Brotherhood of the Wolf is a 2001 French epic historical drama film directed by Jacques Audiard, produced by Canal+, and written by Tonino Benacquista. The movie is set in 18th-century France during the reign of King Louis XV.

The story revolves around Vicente Franco (played by Mads Mikkelsen), a young nobleman who seeks revenge against the aristocrats who wronged him. After being betrayed and left for dead, Vicente returns from his travels with a mysterious wolf-like creature that he claims to have encountered in the forest. He believes this creature is the key to his revenge.

As Vicente navigates the complexities of court politics and social hierarchy, he becomes embroiled in a plot by the Duke de Richelieu (played by Romain Duris) to overthrow King Louis XV. The Duke seeks to gain power and control over France, while Vicente sees an opportunity to use his newfound creature to exact revenge on those who wronged him.

Throughout the film, Audiard explores themes of identity, class, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Vicente's encounters with the wolf-like creature serve as a metaphor for his own inner turmoil and struggle to find his place in society.

As the story unfolds, Vicente becomes increasingly obsessed with his quest for revenge, leading him down a path of violence and destruction. The Duke, on the other hand, is driven by ambition and a desire for power, which ultimately leads to his downfall.

The film's climax features an intense confrontation between Vicente and the Duke, with the wolf-like creature playing a pivotal role in the outcome. In the end, Vicente emerges victorious, but not without scars both physical and emotional.

One of the standout aspects of Brotherhood of the Wolf is its visually stunning depiction of 18th-century France. The film's cinematography, costume design, and production values all contribute to a richly detailed and immersive world that draws the viewer in.

Overall, Brotherhood of the Wolf is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, class, and revenge. With its stunning visuals and strong performances, it is a must-see for fans of historical dramas and epic storytelling.

overview: A young boy wins a tour through the most magnificent chocolate factory in the world, led by the world's most unusual candy maker.
tagline: Prepare for a taste of adventure.
title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
plot:
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory is a 2005 musical fantasy film directed by Tim Burton and written by John August, based on Roald Dahl's 1964 children's novel. Johnny Depp stars as the eccentric candy maker Willy Wonka and Freddie Highmore as Charlie Bucket, alongside David Kelly, Helena Bonham Carter, Noah Taylor, Missi Pyle, James Fox, Deep Roy and Christopher Lee. It is the second film adaptation of the book, after Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory (1971), and the Dahl estate gave Warner Bros. a high degree of creative input during its long development.

Charlie is a kind boy who lives in poverty with his parents and four bedridden grandparents in a crooked little house in the shadow of Wonka's enormous chocolate factory. Years earlier, Wonka closed the factory to the public because of industrial espionage by rival confectioners, firing all his workers, including Charlie's Grandpa Joe. Charlie's father has recently lost his job at a toothpaste factory. One day Wonka announces that he has hidden five Golden Tickets in Wonka Bars around the world; the finders will receive a tour of the factory and a lifetime supply of chocolate, and one will win a special extra prize.

The first four tickets are found by the gluttonous Augustus Gloop, the spoiled Veruca Salt, the aggressively competitive gum-chewer Violet Beauregarde and the know-it-all video game addict Mike Teavee. After two failed attempts, Charlie finds the last ticket with money he picks up from the snowy street and chooses Grandpa Joe to accompany him. Inside the factory, Wonka leads the children and their parents through a series of fantastical rooms, staffed by the tiny Oompa-Loompas, played by Deep Roy, who sing a mocking song each time one of the badly behaved children falls victim to temptation and is removed from the tour. Flashbacks reveal Wonka's lonely childhood with his strict dentist father, played by Christopher Lee, which explains his strange relationship with family and the choice he offers the last child remaining.

The film received generally positive reviews, with praise for its visuals, Danny Elfman's score and its fidelity to Dahl's story, while Depp's unusual interpretation of Wonka divided critics. It grossed about $475 million worldwide, becoming one of the highest-grossing films of 2005, and earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Costume Design.

original_title: 東京喰種 トーキョーグール
overview: A Tokyo college student is attacked by a ghoul, a super-powered human who feeds on human flesh. He survives, but has become part ghoul and becomes a fugitive on the run.
tagline: Humans are no longer at the top of the food chain
title: Tokyo Ghoul
plot:
Tokyo Ghoul is a 2017 Japanese dark fantasy action film directed by Kentarō Hagiwara and based on Sui Ishida's manga of the same name. Masataka Kubota stars as the college student Ken Kaneki and Fumika Shimizu as the waitress Tōka Kirishima, with Nobuyuki Suzuki, Yo Oizumi and Yū Aoi. After a premiere at Anime Expo in Los Angeles in July 2017, it was released in Japan by Shochiku on July 29, 2017, while Funimation handled its North American release.

The story takes place in a version of Tokyo where ghouls, beings who look human but can only survive by eating human flesh, live hidden among ordinary people while being hunted by a government agency. Kaneki, a shy, bookish student, is thrilled when the elegant Rize Kamishiro agrees to a date, but at the end of the evening she reveals herself to be a ghoul and attacks him. He survives only because an accident kills Rize, and he wakes in hospital to learn that surgeons transplanted her organs into his body.

The operation has turned him into a half-ghoul. Ordinary food now disgusts him and he is tormented by a hunger for human flesh that he refuses to satisfy. He finds unexpected refuge at Anteiku, a coffee shop run by the gentle Yoshimura that quietly shelters ghouls who wish to live peacefully. There he meets the abrasive Tōka, who works at the café and reluctantly helps him learn to survive, and he struggles to keep his new nature hidden from his human friend Hide.

Meanwhile two investigators of the Commission of Counter Ghoul, the ruthless veteran Kureo Mado and his younger partner Kōtarō Amon, are tracking the ghouls of the ward. Their hunt claims the mother of the young ghoul girl Hinami, whom Anteiku has been protecting, drawing Kaneki and Tōka into open conflict with the investigators. Torn between the human and ghoul worlds, Kaneki finally embraces his powers to protect his new friends, while trying to show his enemies that coexistence between the two species might be possible.

The film grossed about 1.1 billion yen in Japan and received generally positive reviews, with 82% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and was followed by a sequel, Tokyo Ghoul S, in 2019.

overview: Bucum Jackson (Cube) is a bounty hunter with a lot of attitude and no interest in taking on a partner. Working at Martinez Bail Bonds, Jackson has unorthodox methods of tracking down low-life criminals, but they work, and one day he hopes to become his own boss and open up his own private investigation firm. Reggie Wright (Epps) is a slippery con artist who is avoiding the law, and Jackson. During a cat and mouse chase, the two stumble on a multi-million dollar diamond heist. Hiding from Jackson, Wright finds himself in the thieves' getaway van and ends up having to escape from them after they discover their booty is fake, much to the displeasure of their ruthless boss (Flanagan). When Wright meets up with his girlfriend (Mendes), he discovers that his recently purchased lottery ticket is the sole winner of $60 million. Unfortunately, his wallet, which held the ticket, was left in the thieves' van, so he persuades Jackson to help him get it back.
tagline: Money can make people do funny things.
title: All About the Benjamins
plot:
All About the Benjamins is a crime comedy film that revolves around two con artists, Pimpin' Pete and Reggie Warrington, who get caught up in a complex web of deceit and double-crosses. The movie explores themes of loyalty, trust, and the blurred lines between right and wrong.

At its core, All About the Benjamins is a story about the consequences of one's actions and the importance of maintaining relationships in the face of adversity. As Pimpin' Pete and Reggie navigate their way through a series of misadventures, they are forced to confront their own morals and values, leading to a deeper understanding of what it means to be loyal and trustworthy.

The film also touches on the theme of identity, as both characters struggle with their own sense of self-worth and purpose. Through their experiences, they learn to redefine themselves and find new meaning in their lives.

Ultimately, All About the Benjamins is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and wit to explore complex themes and ideas. While it may not be a deeply profound or thought-provoking movie, it offers an engaging and enjoyable viewing experience that leaves audiences with a sense of satisfaction and closure.

overview: An everyday man has only three and a half days and limited resources to discover why he was imprisoned in a nondescript room for 20 years without any explanation.
tagline: Ask not why you were imprisoned. Ask why you were set free.
title: Oldboy
plot:
Oldboy is a 2013 American neo-noir action thriller directed by Spike Lee and written by Mark Protosevich, a remake of the 2003 South Korean film by Park Chan-wook, which was itself loosely based on a Japanese manga. It stars Josh Brolin as Joe Doucett, Elizabeth Olsen as Marie Sebastian and Sharlto Copley as the mysterious Adrian Pryce, with Samuel L. Jackson in a supporting role.

In 1993, Joe Doucett is a hard-drinking, abrasive advertising executive whose life is falling apart. After a night of heavy drinking following the loss of a major client, he blacks out and wakes up locked in a windowless room resembling a cheap hotel. His unseen captors feed him and supply him with alcohol, but never explain why he is being held. Through the television he learns that his ex-wife has been raped and murdered, that he is the prime suspect and that their young daughter Mia has been adopted.

Over the next twenty years, Joe stops drinking, trains his body and plans for revenge, compiling a list of everyone who might have wanted to imprison him and writing letters to the daughter he hopes to meet one day. Then, without warning, he is drugged and released, waking up outside with money and a cell phone. With the help of his old friend Chucky, a bar owner, and Marie, a young nurse moved by his story, Joe sets out to find the people responsible. A taunting voice on the phone, calling himself the Stranger, challenges him to discover who imprisoned him and why, promising proof of his innocence in his ex-wife's murder if he succeeds. Joe's brutal search leads him back through his own past and toward a revelation more devastating than his imprisonment.

Lee's version retains the original's famous corridor fight with a hammer while altering many story details, while the version released was a producers' re-edit that left Lee and Brolin unhappy.

Oldboy was released in the United States by FilmDistrict on November 27, 2013, and was a commercial failure, earning about 885,000 dollars in its first five days, one of the weakest Thanksgiving openings on record. Reviews were negative, with 39 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49, and many critics felt it did not measure up to the original.

overview: On the run in the year 1987, Bumblebee finds refuge in a junkyard in a small Californian beach town. Charlie, on the cusp of turning 18 and trying to find her place in the world, discovers Bumblebee, battle-scarred and broken.  When Charlie revives him, she quickly learns this is no ordinary yellow VW bug.
tagline: Every hero has a beginning.
title: Bumblebee
plot:
Bumblebee is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Travis Knight and produced by Paramount Pictures. The movie takes place in 1987, during the height of the Transformers franchise's popularity.

The story begins with Charlie Watson (Hailee Steinfeld), a high school student who lives on the outskirts of a small town in California. Charlie is struggling to cope with her mother's death in a car accident and her father's absence due to his work as an oil rig worker. She spends most of her time alone, tinkering with cars and daydreaming about adventure.

One night, while out running from her troubles, Charlie stumbles upon a damaged Chevrolet Camaro that has crash-landed on the outskirts of town. As she approaches the car, it transforms into Bumblebee, an Autobot scout sent to Earth to protect its secrets from the Decepticons.

Initially, Charlie is frightened by the giant robot, but as she observes Bumblebee's behavior, she realizes that it is not a threat. Instead, she begins to form a bond with the Autobot, and they start to communicate through a series of beeps and chirps.

As Charlie spends more time with Bumblebee, she learns about its mission to find its long-lost friend, Jazz (Josh Duhamel), who has been captured by the Decepticons. The Autobots have sent Bumblebee to rescue Jazz, but it needs Charlie's help to navigate the human world and evade the Decepticon forces.

The plot thickens as Charlie becomes embroiled in a series of events that put her life at risk. She is pursued by the Decepticons, led by Shatter (Angus Macfadyen), who will stop at nothing to capture Bumblebee and exploit its advanced technology.

As Charlie and Bumblebee work together, they develop a strong bond, with Charlie learning about the Autobot's values of loyalty, friendship, and sacrifice. In return, Bumblebee learns about human emotions and experiences, which helps it to better understand its mission.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Charlie, Bumblebee, and the Decepticons. With the help of her father, who has been hiding a secret of his own, Charlie is able to outsmart the Decepticons and help Bumblebee rescue Jazz.

In the end, Charlie says goodbye to Bumblebee as it departs to continue its mission, but not before they share a heartfelt moment that leaves Charlie with a newfound sense of purpose and belonging. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest times, there is always the possibility for connection and redemption.

Overall, Bumblebee is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its blend of humor, adventure, and sci-fi excitement, it has become a beloved entry in the Transformers franchise.

overview: College student Danielle must cover her tracks when she unexpectedly runs into her sugar daddy at a shiva - with her parents, ex-girlfriend and family friends also in attendance.
title: Shiva Baby
plot:
Shiva Baby is a 2021 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Emma Seligman. The movie follows the story of Danielle, a young Jewish woman who attends her family's Purim party, where she reconnects with two men from her past: Max, her ex-boyfriend, and Josh, a colleague.

The main theme of Shiva Baby revolves around identity, particularly in regards to one's cultural heritage. The film explores the complexities of navigating multiple identities, including Jewishness, femininity, and adulthood. Danielle struggles to reconcile her desire for independence with her family's expectations, as well as her own sense of self-worth.

The movie also delves into themes of loneliness, relationships, and the search for meaning in one's life. Through Danielle's interactions with Max and Josh, the film highlights the complexities of human connection and the ways in which people can both hurt and heal each other.

Furthermore, Shiva Baby touches on the idea of performance and presentation, particularly in regards to cultural identity. The film shows how individuals often put on a mask or persona to navigate social situations, and how this can lead to feelings of disconnection and inauthenticity.

Overall, Shiva Baby is a nuanced exploration of the human experience, tackling themes that are both deeply personal and universally relatable.

overview: When a Hollywood star mysteriously disappears in the middle of filming, the studio sends their fixer to get him back.
tagline: Lights. Camera. Abduction.
title: Hail, Caesar!
plot:
Hail, Caesar! is a 2016 American comedy film directed by Joel Coen and Ethan Coen, written by the Coen brothers, and produced by Universal Pictures.

The movie is set in 1950s Hollywood during the Golden Age of cinema. The story revolves around Eddie Mannix (Josh Brolin), a fixer for a major film studio, who must navigate the complexities of the industry while dealing with personal struggles.

The main themes of Hail, Caesar! include:

1. **The Illusion of Hollywood Glamour**: The film satirizes the glamour and superficiality of old Hollywood, highlighting the dark underbelly of the industry's excesses and corruption.
2. **Identity and Performance**: The movie explores the theme of identity through the characters' performances on screen and their struggles with their own identities off-screen. Burt Gurney (George Clooney), a washed-up actor, is a prime example of this theme.
3. **Power Dynamics and Corruption**: Hail, Caesar! critiques the power structures within the film industry, particularly the relationships between studio executives, actors, and writers. The character of Hobie Doyle (Josh Lucas) serves as a commentary on the exploitation of talent by those in power.
4. **The American Dream**: The movie pokes fun at the idea of the American Dream, which is often associated with Hollywood's promise of success and fame. Eddie Mannix's journey represents a more nuanced understanding of what it means to achieve success and happiness.

Throughout the film, the Coen brothers use humor, satire, and clever storytelling to explore these themes, creating a rich and engaging narrative that both celebrates and critiques the Golden Age of cinema.

overview: The making of a horror movie takes on a terrifying reality for students at the most prestigious film school in the country. At Alpine University, someone is determined to win the best film award at any cost - even if it means eliminating the competition. No one is safe and everyone is a suspect.
tagline: Legends Never Die.
title: Urban Legends: Final Cut
plot:
Urban Legends: Final Cut is a 2000 American horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and fiction. The movie primarily revolves around the theme of the power of storytelling, particularly in the context of urban legends.

The narrative explores how stories can be manipulated and distorted to create a sense of fear and unease among an audience. This is exemplified through the character of Allison, who becomes increasingly enthralled with the urban legend about "Death" and begins to weave it into her own reality. As the story progresses, it becomes clear that Allison's perception of reality is being shaped by the very stories she's consuming.

The film also touches on the theme of voyeurism, as characters become obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the urban legends. This fixation can lead individuals down a dark path, where they begin to lose sight of what's real and what's just a product of their own imagination.

Furthermore, Urban Legends: Final Cut critiques the notion that stories can be used to control or manipulate others. The character of Allison, in particular, becomes trapped in her own web of deceit, using the urban legend as a means to exert power over those around her.

Overall, the movie presents a thought-provoking exploration of how stories can shape our perceptions and understanding of reality, highlighting the dangers of becoming too enthralled with the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: A three-person crew on a mission to Mars faces an impossible choice when an unplanned passenger jeopardizes the lives of everyone on board.
tagline: Millions of miles from home, survival comes with sacrifice.
title: Stowaway
plot:
Stowaway is a 2021 science fiction thriller directed by Joe Penna, who co-wrote it with Ryan Morrison. A German and American co-production, it stars Anna Kendrick as the ship's doctor Zoe Levenson, Toni Collette as commander Marina Barnett, Daniel Dae Kim as the biologist David Kim and Shamier Anderson as the stowaway Michael Adams. Netflix, which acquired the rights in December 2020, premiered it on April 22, 2021, in most territories, with a later release in German-speaking countries.

Barnett, Kim and Levenson launch aboard the spacecraft MTS-42 on a two-year mission to a Martian colony. Once in transit, the ship generates artificial gravity by rotating against the spent upper stage of its rocket, linked by long tethers. Soon after launch, Barnett discovers Michael Adams, a launch support engineer, unconscious and injured inside a panel, where he had been trapped by accident. As he falls free, he wrecks the CO2 scrubbing system essential to the crew's survival.

Emergency lithium hydroxide canisters cannot cope with four people, and David's algae experiment, rushed into action as an oxygen source, only partly survives. Mission control can offer no rescue, and the only option, a dangerous climb up the tethers to recover liquid oxygen from the upper stage, is judged too risky. Barnett and David begin to accept that Michael must die, but Zoe persuades them to wait. David eventually tells Michael the truth and offers him a lethal injection, which Michael almost uses before Zoe stops him. When the rest of the algae dies, David agrees to join Zoe on the climb.

The two make the spacewalk and improvise a way to fill two oxygen cylinders, but a solar storm forces them to retreat with only one, which is then lost. They realise that someone must go back out through the lethal radiation to retrieve the cylinder left behind. Barnett must stay to pilot the ship, and since Michael is untrained and both he and David have families, Zoe insists on going. She recovers the oxygen and saves the others, but succumbs to radiation, spending her last moments gazing at the distant red point of Mars.

The film received generally positive reviews, with 76% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though critics noted pacing problems.

overview: A traumatised veteran, unafraid of violence, tracks down missing girls for a living. When a job spins out of control, his nightmares overtake him as a conspiracy is uncovered leading to what may be his death trip or his awakening.
tagline: Bring the hammer.
title: You Were Never Really Here
plot:
You Were Never Really Here is a 2017 psychological thriller film directed by Lynne Ramsay, based on the novel of the same name by Jonathan Lethem. The movie stars Joaquin Phoenix as Joe, a former Marine and hitman who suffers from PTSD.

The story begins with Joe (Phoenix) being hired by a wealthy client to kidnap her young daughter, Leah (Aria Mia Loberti), who has been kidnapped by a human trafficking ring. As Joe delves deeper into the case, he becomes increasingly entangled in a web of corruption and deceit that threatens to destroy him.

As Joe navigates the dark underbelly of New York City's elite, he is haunted by his own demons and struggles to form connections with those around him. His relationships with his colleagues, including his handler (Ed Harris) and his fellow hitman (Jeffrey Wright), are strained and superficial, reflecting Joe's emotional numbness.

Throughout the film, Ramsay employs a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth in time to reveal fragments of Joe's past and present. We see glimpses of Joe's traumatic experiences during the Iraq War, as well as his complicated relationships with his family members, particularly his sister (Judy Greer).

As Joe becomes more entrenched in the case, he begins to uncover a sinister plot involving human trafficking, corruption, and government complicity. The further he delves into the mystery, the more he realizes that he is trapped in a world of violence and exploitation.

The film's climax features a tense and violent confrontation between Joe and the traffickers, which ultimately leads to a tragic and devastating conclusion. Without giving away too many spoilers, it can be said that Joe's actions are motivated by a desire to protect Leah, but also by his own sense of guilt and responsibility for not being able to prevent her kidnapping.

Throughout the film, Phoenix delivers a tour-de-force performance as Joe, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and troubled character. His portrayal is both captivating and heartbreaking, conveying the full range of emotions that Joe experiences throughout the story.

Overall, You Were Never Really Here is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores themes of trauma, exploitation, and the human cost of violence. With its non-linear narrative structure and outstanding performances, the film is a masterclass in storytelling and character development.

overview: A passionate holiday romance leads to an obsessive relationship when an Australian photojournalist wakes one morning in a Berlin apartment and is unable to leave.
title: Berlin Syndrome
plot:
Berlin Syndrome is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of captivity and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film follows Claire, a young woman who finds herself trapped in a seemingly idyllic relationship with her boyfriend, Luke, in Berlin.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Claire's world is not as perfect as it initially seems. She begins to experience strange and unsettling occurrences, which lead her to question her own sanity and the true nature of her captivity. The film expertly weaves together themes of control, manipulation, and the darker aspects of human relationships.

One of the primary concerns of Berlin Syndrome is the way in which women can be trapped by those who claim to love them. Claire's situation serves as a commentary on the societal pressures that can lead women to settle for unhealthy relationships, often due to fear or insecurity. The film also explores the theme of gaslighting, where Luke manipulates Claire's perception of reality, making her doubt her own memories and experiences.

The movie also touches on the idea of escapism and the human desire to break free from constraints. Claire's situation serves as a metaphor for the ways in which we can become trapped by our own fears and insecurities. As she navigates her way through this complex web of emotions, Claire must confront the darker aspects of herself and the world around her.

Overall, Berlin Syndrome is a gripping thriller that explores the complexities of human relationships, control, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film's tense atmosphere and thought-provoking themes make it a compelling watch for fans of psychological thrillers.

overview: A homicide detective teams up with a criminal profiler to catch a serial killer whose crimes are inspired by the children's game, Hangman.
tagline: There will be one winner.
title: Hangman
plot:
Hangman is a 2017 American crime thriller directed by Johnny Martin and written by Charles Huttinger and Michael Caissie. It stars Al Pacino as retired homicide detective Ray Archer and Karl Urban as Detective Will Ruiney, with Brittany Snow as journalist Christi Davies, Sarah Shahi as Captain Lisa Watson and Joe Anderson as the killer. The story follows two detectives hunting a serial killer who stages his murders after the children's word-guessing game Hangman.

In Monroe, Georgia, Detective Ray Archer confronts the driver of a hit-and-run van and notices a gothic pendant hanging from its mirror. A year later, Christi Davies, a reporter who has been allowed to shadow the police for a story, accompanies Detective Ruiney to a gruesome crime scene: a teacher has been hanged outside her school with a letter carved into her chest. Inside a classroom the killer has staged a game of Hangman between two mannequins and carved the badge numbers of Ruiney and Archer into a desk, making it clear that the detectives have been chosen as his opponents.

Although retired, Archer joins the investigation, and the two detectives, with Davies in tow, follow a trail of clues that leads them through the victim's private life and to a church where the killer strikes again. Each body is marked with a new letter, and the detectives realize that the murderer intends to keep killing, with a new letter for each victim, until the game's puzzle is complete. Racing against the clock, they must decipher the hidden word, uncover the killer's identity and his connection to their own pasts, and protect the people close to them, especially Ruiney, who is still haunted by the unsolved murder of his wife.

The film draws on the conventions of serial-killer thrillers, combining a police procedural with a puzzle-based mystery.

Hangman was released in the United States on December 22, 2017. It received overwhelmingly negative reviews, with an approval rating of 5 percent on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31, and critics found its plot contrived despite the presence of Pacino.

overview: Black police officer Russell Stevens applies for a special anti-drug squad which targets the highest boss of cocaine delivery to LA—the Colombian foreign minister's nephew. Russell works his way up from the bottom undercover, until he reaches the boss.
tagline: There's a thin line between catching a criminal... and becoming one.
title: Deep Cover
plot:
Deep Cover is a crime drama film that delves into the complexities of identity, loyalty, and deception. The story revolves around a deep-cover FBI agent who infiltrates a gang to gather evidence against them, but as he becomes more entrenched in their world, his own moral compass begins to blur.

At its core, Deep Cover explores the theme of identity fragmentation, where an individual's sense of self is torn apart by conflicting loyalties and allegiances. The protagonist's dual existence as both a lawman and a gangster raises questions about the nature of truth and how it can be distorted or manipulated for personal gain.

The film also touches on the idea of loyalty and betrayal, highlighting the difficulties of navigating complex relationships within a world where trust is a luxury few can afford. As the protagonist becomes more embroiled in the gang's activities, he must confront the consequences of his own actions and the true cost of his deception.

Furthermore, Deep Cover critiques the systemic failures that enable organized crime to thrive, particularly in urban communities where poverty, racism, and social inequality create fertile ground for exploitation. The film offers a nuanced portrayal of the cyclical nature of violence and the devastating impact it has on individuals and society as a whole.

Ultimately, Deep Cover presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of their own nature and the world around them.

original_title: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
overview: After an abrupt and violent encounter with a French warship inflicts severe damage upon his ship, a captain of the British Royal Navy begins a chase over two oceans to capture or destroy the enemy, though he must weigh his commitment to duty and ferocious pursuit of glory against the safety of his devoted crew, including the ship's thoughtful surgeon, his best friend.
tagline: The courage to do the impossible lies in the hearts of men.
title: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
plot:
Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World is a 2003 historical naval adventure film directed by Peter Weir, starring Russell Crowe as Captain Jack Aubrey and Paul Bettany as Dr. Stephen Maturin.

The story begins during the Napoleonic Wars, in 1812, when Captain Jack Aubrey, a British Royal Navy officer, is tasked with commanding the HMS Surprise, a 38-gun fifth-rate frigate. Aubrey's mission is to intercept and capture French merchant ships carrying supplies to Napoleon's army in Europe.

Aubrey's trusted friend and ship's surgeon, Dr. Stephen Maturin, joins him on this voyage. Maturin is a complex character with a mysterious past, who has been struggling with his own demons. Throughout the film, their friendship and professional partnership are put to the test as they face numerous challenges at sea.

As the HMS Surprise sets sail from Plymouth, England, Aubrey and Maturin encounter various obstacles, including treacherous weather conditions, hostile French privateers, and a mutinous crew. The ship's captain, Tom Pullings, is struggling with his own personal demons, which puts the entire crew in danger.

The plot thickens when the HMS Surprise intercepts a French merchant ship carrying supplies to Napoleon's army. Aubrey and Maturin engage in a fierce battle with the French privateers, resulting in the capture of several ships and the death of many French sailors.

As the HMS Surprise continues its mission, Aubrey and Maturin develop a deeper understanding of each other's strengths and weaknesses. They also face personal challenges, including Aubrey's struggles with his own identity as a naval officer and Maturin's ongoing battle with his demons.

The film's climax takes place in the Strait of Magellan, where the HMS Surprise is pursued by a French ship. In a thrilling sea battle, Aubrey and Maturin work together to outmaneuver their pursuers and emerge victorious.

In the end, the HMS Surprise returns to England as a hero, having successfully completed its mission. Aubrey and Maturin's friendship has been tested and proven stronger than ever, and they look forward to future adventures together.

Throughout the film, Weir explores themes of loyalty, duty, and personal identity, set against the backdrop of one of history's most tumultuous periods. The film's attention to historical detail and its engaging characters make it a compelling watch for fans of naval adventure films.

Overall, Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World is a gripping and entertaining film that showcases Weir's mastery of storytelling and his ability to bring complex characters to life on screen.

overview: Ben Stiller, Jack Black and Robert Downey Jr. lead an ensemble cast in 'Tropic Thunder,' an action comedy about a group of self-absorbed actors who set out to make the most expensive war film. After ballooning costs force the studio to cancel the movie, the frustrated director refuses to stop shooting, leading his cast into the jungles of Southeast Asia, where they encounter real bad guys.
tagline: Get Some.
title: Tropic Thunder
plot:
Tropic Thunder is a satirical action comedy film directed by Ben Stiller, released in 2008 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of four self-absorbed actors who drop into the jungle to film a war movie.

The film begins with Tugg Speedman (Ben Stiller), a washed-up action hero struggling to revive his career. He is joined by Kirk Lazarus (Robert Downey Jr.), a method actor who undergoes a drastic transformation to play a black Australian soldier in the war movie. The two are accompanied by Jeff Portnoy (Jack Black), a comedic actor known for his outrageous performances, and Damien Cockburn (Steve Coogan), a British actor who is more serious about his craft.

The four actors embark on a disastrous journey into the jungle to film their war movie, which they hope will revitalize their careers. However, things quickly take a turn for the worse as they are dropped off in the middle of nowhere with limited supplies and no clear direction from their director, Les Grossman (Tom Cruise).

As the actors struggle to survive and complete their scenes, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and each other's egos. The group soon realizes that they are not prepared for the harsh conditions of the jungle and that their inexperience will put them in grave danger.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities and flaws are on full display. Tugg Speedman is shown to be a self-centered actor who only cares about his own career, while Kirk Lazarus is revealed to be a shallow and pretentious actor who uses his transformation as an excuse for his lack of talent. Jeff Portnoy, on the other hand, is depicted as a lovable but immature actor who often provides comic relief.

As the story unfolds, the actors are forced to confront their own mortality and the reality of their situation. They must work together to survive and complete their scenes, which leads to some unexpected moments of camaraderie and growth.

In the end, the actors manage to escape the jungle with their lives, but not without some serious consequences. The film ends on a bittersweet note, as the actors reflect on what they have learned from their experience in the jungle.

Overall, Tropic Thunder is a hilarious and satirical take on the Hollywood film industry, with plenty of laughs and memorable moments along the way. The film's cast delivers standout performances, and Ben Stiller's direction brings the story to life with humor and heart.

overview: Feeling isolated from that unwelcoming community, June and Jennifer Gibbons turn inward and reject communication with everyone but each other, retreating into their own fantasy world of artistic inspiration and adolescent desires.
tagline: Imagination will set you free.
title: The Silent Twins
plot:
The Silent Twins is a 2022 British-Polish biographical drama directed by Agnieszka Smoczyńska in her English-language debut, from a screenplay by Andrea Seigel adapted from Marjorie Wallace's 1986 book of the same name. It tells the true story of June and Jennifer Gibbons, identical twins who communicated with almost no one but each other. Letitia Wright, also an executive producer, plays June and Tamara Lawrance plays Jennifer, with Leah Mondesir-Simmonds and Eva-Arianna Baxter as the girls in childhood, Nadine Marshall and Treva Etienne as their parents, Jack Bandeira as Wayne, Michael Smiley, and Jodhi May as Wallace.

Born in 1963 to Barbadian immigrants, the twins grow up as the only Black family in Haverfordwest, in Wales, where they are bullied and ostracized. As children they make a pact to speak to no one else, including their own parents and siblings, and they withdraw into a private world in their bedroom, playing elaborate games and later writing poems, diaries and novels; June even self-publishes one, Pepsi-Cola Addict. Their fantasies are rendered in stop-motion puppet animation, and their volatile bond swings between devotion, rivalry and fights. Obsessed with understanding romance, the teenagers venture out and fall in with Wayne, a young American, and his circle, experimenting with drugs and sex.

Their frustration and hunger for experience end in a spree of shoplifting, burglary and arson in 1981. Convicted, the nineteen-year-olds are sent indefinitely to Broadmoor, a high-security psychiatric hospital, where they remain for eleven years and where the journalist Wallace, who had followed their trial, begins visiting them and listening to their side of the story. There they face a choice between separating to survive or dying together, and the film ends with Jennifer's sudden death in 1993, shortly after the sisters leave the hospital, which June came to see as a sacrifice that set her free.

The film was shot in Poland and premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2022 Cannes Film Festival on May 24. Focus Features released it in the United States on September 16, 2022, and Universal Pictures in the United Kingdom that December. Reviews were generally positive, with about 69 percent of critics on Rotten Tomatoes recommending it. The Guardian called it an absorbing, well-acted drama, disturbing but tender, while RogerEbert.com admired its visual creativity but found its episodic storytelling emotionally distant.

overview: Madea's back - hallelujer! And she's not putting up with any nonsense as family drama erupts at her great-grandson's college graduation celebration.
tagline: It's a family affair.
title: Tyler Perry's A Madea Homecoming
plot:
A Madea Homecoming is a 2022 American comedy film written, produced, and directed by Tyler Perry. The movie marks the return of Mabel "Madea" Simmons, played by Tyler Perry, after her last appearance in A Madea Family Funeral (2019).

The story begins with Mabel, now an elderly woman, who has been living a peaceful life in her Atlanta home. However, her tranquility is disrupted when she receives news that her estranged daughter, April, and her son-in-law, Brian, are coming to visit her for the first time in years.

As Madea prepares for their arrival, she reflects on her complicated past with April, who has been struggling to care for her own family. Madea's harsh words and tough love have often led to tension between them, but as they spend more time together, it becomes clear that April is at a breaking point due to the stress of caring for her husband, Brian, who suffers from dementia.

As the story unfolds, Madea takes it upon herself to help April and Brian navigate their challenges. She uses her signature blend of humor, wisdom, and tough love to guide them towards a more positive path. Along the way, she also confronts her own demons and grapples with the consequences of her past actions.

Throughout the film, Perry's signature style is on full display, as he tackles themes such as family dynamics, mental health, and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships. The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Tika Sumpter, Lynn Whitfield, and Brian Tyree Henry, among others.

As Madea's influence begins to bear fruit, April starts to find her footing again, and the two begin to rebuild their relationship. Meanwhile, Brian's condition worsens, leading to a poignant confrontation between Madea and her own mortality.

The film builds towards a heartwarming conclusion, as Madea finds a way to reconcile with her past and make amends with those she loves. In the end, Madea comes to terms with her own legacy and the impact she's had on those around her.

A Madea Homecoming is a testament to Tyler Perry's ability to craft stories that are both entertaining and emotionally resonant. The film is a loving tribute to the enduring power of family and the importance of forgiveness and redemption.

overview: Recruited to assist Montreal police in their desperate search for a serial killer who assumes the identities of his victims, FBI profiler Illeana Scott knows it's only a matter of time before the killer strikes again. Her most promising lead is a museum employee who might be the killer's only eyewitness.
tagline: He would kill to be you.
title: Taking Lives
plot:
Taking Lives is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the cat-and-mouse game between a profiler and an assassin. The film's main theme revolves around the blurred lines between good and evil, as it explores the motivations and backstories of its complex characters.

The movie sheds light on the idea that people are not inherently good or evil, but rather a mix of both, shaped by their experiences and circumstances. The protagonist, Isabel Lacey (Angelina Jolie), is a profiler who uses her skills to track down serial killers, while the assassin, Cassie Holmes (Morgan Freeman), is driven by a desire for revenge against those she perceives as responsible for her past traumas.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and how it can be both a source of strength and weakness. Isabel's troubled past and her struggles to connect with others serve as a reminder that even the most skilled and intelligent individuals can be haunted by their demons. Cassie, on the other hand, uses her alias and persona to create a sense of detachment and control, highlighting the tension between her true self and the persona she presents to the world.

Furthermore, Taking Lives explores the idea of obsession and how it can consume both the profiler and the assassin. Isabel's fixation on catching Cassie becomes an all-consuming force that drives her to take risks and push herself to the limit, while Cassie's pursuit of revenge becomes an all-encompassing goal that defines her existence.

Overall, Taking Lives is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, exploring themes of identity, obsession, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

overview: Gloria finds a power she never knew she had when she is drawn into a dangerous world of cross-border crime. Surviving will require all of her cunning, inventiveness, and strength.
tagline: Who would you become to save your family?
title: Miss Bala
plot:
Miss Bala is a 2019 American action thriller film directed by Catherine Hardwicke and written by Chris Morgan. The movie stars Gina Rodriguez, Luis Gerardo Sánchez, and Ismael Cruz Córdoba.

The main themes of Miss Bala revolve around the exploitation of women, particularly those from marginalized communities, and the consequences of patriarchal societies. The film tells the story of Jessica "Jess" Morales (Gina Rodriguez), a young woman who becomes embroiled in a human trafficking ring after her sister is kidnapped by a powerful cartel leader.

Throughout the movie, the themes of female empowerment, survival, and resistance are prominent. Jess's journey from victim to survivor serves as a powerful metaphor for the struggles faced by women in patriarchal societies. The film also explores the consequences of systemic inequality and the ways in which women are often exploited and marginalized by those in power.

The movie critiques the way in which women are objectified and commodified, particularly in the context of human trafficking. It highlights the ways in which women are forced into prostitution and other forms of exploitation, and the devastating impact this has on their lives and well-being.

Ultimately, Miss Bala is a powerful commentary on the need for social change and the importance of supporting survivors of human trafficking. The film's themes of female empowerment and resistance serve as a beacon of hope in the face of oppression, inspiring viewers to take action and make a difference in the world.

The movie received widespread critical acclaim for its thought-provoking themes, strong performances, and timely commentary on social issues.

overview: Puppy mayhem turns the lives of newlywed Chihuahua parents Papi and Chloe upside down when their rambunctious, mischievous puppies present one challenge after another. But when their human owners end up in trouble, the tiny pups will stop at nothing to save them - because in good times and hard times, the family always sticks together. So Papi, Chloe and the puppies embark on a heroic adventure, proving once again that big heroes come in small packages.
tagline: The family just got bigger
title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2
plot:
Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2 is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores several key themes. At its core, the movie is about the power of friendship and loyalty. The story follows Chloe, a pampered Chihuahua who finds herself separated from her owner and must navigate an unfamiliar world to find her way back home.

Throughout the film, Chloe forms strong bonds with a group of street-smart dogs, including a wise-cracking mutt named Duke, who becomes her unlikely ally. As they face various challenges together, Chloe learns valuable lessons about perseverance, adaptability, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

The movie also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery. Chloe's journey is not just about finding her way back home but also about discovering her own strengths and weaknesses. Along the way, she encounters a range of characters who teach her valuable lessons about courage, kindness, and the value of following one's heart.

Furthermore, Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2 explores themes of belonging and acceptance. Chloe's experiences on the streets are marked by both loneliness and connection, highlighting the complexities of finding one's place in the world. The film suggests that true belonging can be found through shared experiences and relationships with others, rather than solely through material possessions or social status.

Overall, Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2 is a lighthearted yet meaningful film that celebrates the importance of friendship, self-discovery, and embracing one's unique qualities.

overview: A volcanic eruption in Iceland sends a glacier towards North America, causing everything in it's path to freeze. A family man struggles to escape the onslaught of the coming ice age.
tagline: A World Frozen Over ... A Family Torn Apart.
title: 2012: Ice Age
plot:
2012: Ice Age is a 2011 American science fiction disaster film directed by Travis Fort and written by Paul Sinor and Victoria Dadi. Produced by David Michael Latt for The Asylum, the independent studio known for low-budget "mockbusters", it is the third and final installment of the company's 2012 trilogy, following 2012: Doomsday (2008) and 2012: Supernova (2009), all riding on the release of Roland Emmerich's 2012. Patrick Labyorteaux stars as the scientist Bill Hart, with Julie McCullough as his wife Teri, Nick Afanasiev as their son Nelson and Katie Wilson as their daughter Julia.

In Maine, Bill drops Julia at the airport for her flight back to New York City, where she studies. Soon afterwards his colleague Dr. Divya, flying over Iceland, warns him that violent volcanic eruptions have broken loose an enormous mass of glacial ice hundreds of kilometers wide, which is now hurtling across the Atlantic toward North America; Divya is killed moments later. Bill picks up Teri at the office of the senator she works for, and the family sets out for New York to rescue Julia as the advancing ice brings a summer blizzard, closes airports and flattens Boston, while Air Force jets fail to break it apart.

The journey becomes a struggle for survival in temperatures of forty below. After crashing into an abandoned car, the Harts find a van, only to lose it to Gary, a desperate man heading for California who threatens them with a gun and later drowns when the van plunges through a frozen river. Sheltering in a house, they free Gerald, a man pinned beneath a fallen shelf, and in gratitude he lends them his light aircraft. Meanwhile Julia and her friend Logan try to escape the freezing city on foot through the subway and the Lincoln Tunnel. From the air the Harts witness a second failed attempt to stop the ice, then make an emergency landing when the plane leaks fuel. Tracking Julia's phone, they find her and Logan and take refuge at the Statue of Liberty, from where they watch the military finally destroy the glacier with a nuclear weapon, leaving New York buried in snow but saved.

Shot on a budget estimated at about $250,000 at The Asylum's Los Angeles studio and other locations including the Lacy Street Production Center and a movie ranch in Agua Dulce, the film premiered in the United States on 28 June 2011 and was later released direct to video in other countries, including France in 2012.

overview: The sequel to Monster Hunt. Set in a world where monsters and humans co-exist, the franchise tells the story of Wuba, a baby monster born to be king. Wuba becomes the central figure in stopping an all-out monster civil war.
title: Monster Hunt 2
plot:
Monster Hunt 2 is an action-comedy film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and the struggle to balance personal ambitions with familial responsibilities.

The movie delves into the theme of identity, particularly in the context of the protagonist, Leilou's, journey. As she navigates her dual identities as a human and a monster, she must confront the challenges of self-discovery and acceptance. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for her growth and understanding of what it means to be true to oneself.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of loyalty and the importance of relationships in our lives. The bond between Leilou and her family members is put to the test as they face various challenges and obstacles together. This highlights the significance of having a supportive network of loved ones and the sacrifices that must be made for their well-being.

The movie also explores the idea of tradition and cultural heritage, particularly in the context of the monster world. The film's depiction of the intricate social hierarchy and customs within this world serves as a commentary on the importance of preserving cultural traditions while also embracing change and progress.

Overall, Monster Hunt 2 is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and tradition in a richly imagined monster world.

overview: An undocumented immigrant finds a human heart in one of the toilets of the west London hotel where he works with other undocumented immigrants.
tagline: Every dream has its price.
title: Dirty Pretty Things
plot:
Dirty Pretty Things is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human nature, morality, and the consequences of one's actions. The movie takes place in a world where people from different walks of life are brought together by circumstance, forcing them to confront their own demons and make difficult choices.

At its core, Dirty Pretty Things is a story about the struggle for identity and belonging. The characters, each with their own unique backstory and motivations, find themselves entangled in a web of relationships that challenge their sense of self-worth. As they navigate this complex landscape, they are forced to confront the darker aspects of human nature, including exploitation, manipulation, and violence.

The film also explores themes of morality and the gray areas that exist between right and wrong. The characters are often faced with difficult decisions that require them to weigh their own desires against the needs of others. This moral ambiguity is a hallmark of the movie, leaving the audience to ponder the consequences of each character's actions.

Furthermore, Dirty Pretty Things touches on issues of class, privilege, and social inequality. The film highlights the stark contrasts between the wealthy elite and those struggling to survive in the margins of society. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the systemic injustices that perpetuate inequality and the ways in which individuals are often forced to navigate these oppressive systems.

Ultimately, Dirty Pretty Things is a thought-provoking exploration of human nature, morality, and the complexities of relationships. The film's nuanced characters and morally ambiguous themes make for a gripping narrative that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: 1930s Hollywood is reevaluated through the eyes of scathing social critic and alcoholic screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz as he races to finish the screenplay of Citizen Kane.
title: Mank
plot:
Mank is a 2020 American biographical drama film directed by David Fincher, written by Eric Roth, and produced by Netflix International Pictures.

The main themes of Mank include:

1. **Obsession with storytelling**: The film explores the obsessive nature of screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz as he works on writing the screenplay for Orson Welles' Citizen Kane. Mank's fixation on creating a masterpiece is evident in his relentless pursuit of perfection, often at the cost of his personal relationships and well-being.

2. **The struggle for creative control**: The movie highlights the tension between Mank and Orson Welles, as they navigate their complicated relationship and competing visions for Citizen Kane. This theme speaks to the challenges faced by creatives in asserting their artistic vision in a collaborative environment.

3. **The corrupting influence of power and fame**: As Mank's star rises with the success of Citizen Kane, he becomes increasingly consumed by his own ego and desire for recognition. The film suggests that the pursuit of fame and power can lead individuals down a path of moral compromise and self-destruction.

4. **The impact of personal demons on creative work**: Throughout the film, Mank's personal struggles with addiction, depression, and relationships are woven into the narrative, illustrating how these issues can both inspire and hinder artistic expression.

5. **The tension between art and commerce**: The movie touches on the commercial pressures that come with creating a successful film, particularly in the context of the Hollywood studio system. Mank's struggle to balance his artistic vision with the demands of the studio serves as a commentary on the challenges faced by creatives in navigating the business side of the industry.

Overall, Mank is a thought-provoking exploration of the creative process, the human condition, and the complexities of artistic expression.

overview: French nuclear tests irradiate an iguana into a giant monster that viciously attacks freighter ships in the Pacific Ocean. A team of experts, including Niko Tatopoulos, conclude that the oversized reptile is the culprit. Before long, the giant lizard is loose in Manhattan as the US military races to destroy the monster before it reproduces and it's spawn takes over the world.
tagline: Size does matter.
title: Godzilla
plot:
Godzilla is a 1998 American monster film directed by Roland Emmerich, who co-wrote it with producer Dean Devlin as an American reboot of Toho's Godzilla franchise. Matthew Broderick stars as the biologist Nick Tatopoulos and Jean Reno as a French secret agent, with Maria Pitillo, Hank Azaria, Kevin Dunn, Michael Lerner and Harry Shearer. The film is dedicated to Godzilla co-creator Tomoyuki Tanaka. TriStar Pictures released it on May 20, 1998, in a then-record 3,310 theatres in North America.

Fallout from French nuclear tests in Polynesia mutates an iguana nest. Years later a huge creature sinks a Japanese fishing ship, and a traumatised survivor, questioned by a mysterious Frenchman, can only repeat "Gojira". Nick Tatopoulos, studying earthworms at Chernobyl, is drafted by the US government to analyse the trail of destruction and concludes that the animal is a radiation-born mutant, not a dinosaur. The creature then comes ashore in Manhattan, flattening streets as the city is evacuated.

The army lures it out with a mountain of fish but fails to kill it. Nick discovers that the animal reproduces asexually and is about to lay eggs. He reunites with his former girlfriend Audrey Timmonds, an ambitious junior reporter, who steals a classified tape from him; her boss, Charles Caiman, claims the story and names the monster Godzilla. Nick is dismissed from the operation and recruited by Philippe Roaché, an agent of the French secret service trying to cover up France's role. Audrey and her cameraman Victor "Animal" Palotti tag along.

After a second strike, Godzilla is attacked by submarines in the Hudson and believed dead. Nick's group locates its nest inside Madison Square Garden, where hundreds of offspring hatch and attack. They broadcast a warning from the arena, escaping just before air strikes destroy it. Godzilla, still alive and enraged by the loss of its young, pursues them across Manhattan until it becomes tangled in the cables of the Brooklyn Bridge and is killed by missiles. Audrey quits her job, and Philippe departs with Animal's footage. In the ruins, one surviving egg hatches.

The film earned about 379 million dollars worldwide but was widely panned, with a 20% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and won Golden Raspberry Awards including Worst Remake or Sequel.

overview: Coffee And Cigarettes is a collection of eleven films from cult director Jim Jarmusch. Each film hosts star studded cast of extremely unique individuals who all share the common activities of conversing while drinking coffee and smoking cigarettes.
title: Coffee and Cigarettes
plot:
"Coffee and Cigarettes" is a 2003 film written and directed by Jim Jarmusch, not Smokescreen Inc.

The main themes of "Coffee and Cigarettes" are:

1. **Friendship and camaraderie**: The film explores the relationships between various characters, including musicians, actors, and writers, as they engage in conversations over coffee and cigarettes.
2. **Existentialism and meaninglessness**: Many characters discuss the search for meaning and purpose in life, often with humorous and irreverent results.
3. **Cultural identity and nostalgia**: The film features a diverse cast of characters from different musical genres, including Tom Waits, Iggy Pop, and Bill Murray, among others. This diversity reflects Jarmusch's interest in exploring cultural differences and the passing of time.
4. **The power of conversation**: Throughout the film, conversations between characters reveal their personalities, values, and experiences, highlighting the importance of human connection and communication.

These themes are woven throughout the film, which consists of a series of vignettes featuring various characters engaging in conversations over coffee and cigarettes at a New York City diner.

original_title: Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle
overview: When Curious George is offered a special space mission, Ted (The Man in the Yellow Hat) can't deny his little friend this exciting journey, especially after Curious George completes the training. But when he crash-lands in Africa, a worried Ted goes searching, expecting the worst, only to have it turn out to be the best.
title: Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle
plot:
Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle is a 2015 American traditionally animated family adventure film directed by Phil Weinstein and written by Chuck Tately, based on the Curious George books by Margret and H. A. Rey. Produced by Imagine Entertainment, Universal 1440 Entertainment and WGBH, with music by Heitor Pereira, it is the third film in the franchise and the second to skip theaters. Frank Welker and Jeff Bennett return as the voices of George and his friend Ted, the Man with the Yellow Hat, joined by John Goodman as Hal Houston, Angela Bassett as Dr. Kulinda and Alexander Polinsky as Andrew.

After a hectic kite chase in the park, George and Ted are approached by Houston, an official of a space agency, who offers George a once-in-a-lifetime mission. As part of a project to stop the floods devastating a region of Central Africa, George is to fly into orbit, retrieve a device called the Regional Dam Synchronizer from a broken satellite, and bring it back so that it can be installed on a dam, where its antenna will coordinate the other dams in the area. Ted is reluctant at first, but agrees after George's pleading, on the condition that he complete the astronaut training, which he does.

The first part of the mission goes smoothly, and George retrieves the device, but during the return his curiosity sends the capsule's systems haywire and it plunges toward Earth. George ejects and lands somewhere in the African jungle, while the capsule disappears with the device still on board. Houston, his assistant Andrew and Ted travel to Africa, where search teams scour an area hundreds of miles wide; eventually Ted sets out on his own, cut off from contact with Houston. Back in the land of his birth, George meets Dr. Kulinda, a veterinarian who runs an animal preserve. The friends must find each other, recover the device and install it before a huge storm bearing down on the region can ravage the jungle, and in the end they complete the mission in time.

The film was released on DVD by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on 23 June 2015 and later aired on PBS Kids. It was the last film in the series to use traditional animation. Reviewers praised its fast, suspenseful yet gentle storytelling, bright visuals and lack of a conventional villain, with the storm serving as the main threat, as well as songs such as "Ordinary Superman".

overview: One year after the events of "Kickboxer: Vengeance", Kurt Sloan has vowed never to return to Thailand. However, while gearing up for a MMA title shot, he finds himself sedated and forced back into Thailand, this time in prison. He is there because the ones responsible want him to face a 6'8" 400 lbs. beast named Mongkut and in return for the fight, Kurt will get two million dollars and his freedom back. Kurt at first refuses, in which a bounty is placed on his head as a way to force him to face Mongkut. Kurt soon learns he will have no other choice and will undergo his most rigorous training yet under some unexpected mentors in order to face Mongkut in hopes to regain his freedom.
tagline: It's time to fight back
title: Kickboxer: Retaliation
plot:
Kickboxer: Retaliation is a 2018 martial arts film directed by Yuen Woo-ping and written by Eric Bress, J. Mackye Gruber, and Chris Mancini. The movie serves as the third installment in the Kickboxer film series.

The main themes of Kickboxer: Retaliation revolve around revenge, redemption, and self-discovery. The protagonist, Jay Kuan (played by Muay Thai fighter Tony Jaa), is a former kickboxer who seeks vengeance against his brother's killers after their family is brutally murdered in Thailand.

Throughout the film, Jay's journey is marked by intense physical confrontations, emotional turmoil, and a quest for justice. As he navigates the dark world of organized crime and corruption, Jay must confront his own demons and learn to let go of his anger in order to find redemption.

The movie also explores themes of cultural identity, as Jay struggles to reconcile his Thai heritage with his American upbringing. His experiences serve as a metaphor for the immigrant experience, highlighting the challenges faced by individuals who navigate multiple cultures and identities.

Ultimately, Kickboxer: Retaliation is a story about the human capacity for forgiveness, healing, and transformation. Through its intense action sequences and emotional character development, the film offers a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of the human condition.

overview: In the 22nd century, a paraplegic Marine is dispatched to the moon Pandora on a unique mission, but becomes torn between following orders and protecting an alien civilization.
tagline: Enter the world of Pandora.
title: Avatar
plot:
Avatar (2009) is a science fiction epic film directed by James Cameron, set in the mid-22nd century on the planet Pandora, inhabited by the Na'vi people. The story follows Jake Sully, a paraplegic marine who is recruited to participate in the Avatar Program, which allows humans to control genetically engineered Na'vi bodies called "avatars."

Jake's twin brother, also a marine, had previously participated in the program and was killed during a clash with the Na'vi. The program's goal is to convince the Na'vi to leave their homes so that a mining corporation can extract valuable minerals from Pandora.

Upon arrival on Pandora, Jake is fitted with an avatar body and begins his training as an avatar driver. He soon becomes immersed in Na'vi culture and forms a bond with Neytiri, a Na'vi warrior who teaches him about the natural world and the spiritual connection between humans and nature.

As Jake becomes more deeply involved with the Na'vi, he begins to question the true intentions of the human corporation and the motivations of his own brother's death. He also starts to experience strange visions and sensations that suggest a deeper connection to the natural world.

The conflict escalates when the human corporation threatens to destroy the Na'vi's sacred Tree of Souls, which is connected to their spiritual energy source. Jake must choose between his loyalty to humanity and his growing allegiance to the Na'vi people.

The film culminates in an epic battle between the humans and the Na'vi, with Jake ultimately siding with the Na'vi and helping them defeat the human forces. The movie ends with Jake permanently transferring his consciousness into his avatar body, allowing him to live among the Na'vi as one of their own.

Throughout the film, Cameron explores themes of colonialism, imperialism, and the clash between technology and nature. The film's stunning visuals and groundbreaking use of motion capture technology brought the world of Pandora to life in a way that was both breathtaking and thought-provoking.

Overall, Avatar is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of human actions on the natural world.

overview: Benny and Claire, a down-on-their-luck couple, find a discarded Chitauri weapon referred to as 'Item 47'.
tagline: The Avengers won the battle, but a few items were left behind.
title: Marvel One-Shot: Item 47
plot:
Marvel One-Shot: Item 47 is a 2012 superhero short film that explores the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The story revolves around Darcy Lewis, a quirky and resourceful character who finds herself at the center of a high-stakes adventure.

At its core, Marvel One-Shot: Item 47 delves into the theme of responsibility and the unintended consequences of one's actions. When Darcy stumbles upon an alien artifact known as the "Item 47," she inadvertently unleashes a powerful energy that wreaks havoc on New York City. As she navigates this chaotic situation, she must confront the reality of her own agency and the impact of her decisions.

The film also touches on the idea of obsession and the blurred lines between fascination and fixation. Darcy's initial excitement about the Item 47 gradually gives way to a desperate attempt to control its power, highlighting the dangers of becoming too invested in something that ultimately surpasses human understanding.

Furthermore, Marvel One-Shot: Item 47 explores the theme of female empowerment and self-discovery. As Darcy navigates this treacherous situation, she discovers hidden strengths and resourcefulness within herself, ultimately emerging as a capable and determined individual.

Throughout the film, the tone is lighthearted and humorous, with a touch of action-packed excitement. However, beneath its entertaining surface, Marvel One-Shot: Item 47 poses thought-provoking questions about the human condition, encouraging viewers to consider the consequences of their actions and the importance of self-awareness.

overview: Set in the underworld of debt-collecting, homegrown hustler Peg Dahl will do anything to escape Buffalo, NY.
tagline: You can't always take what you want
title: Buffaloed
plot:
Buffaloed is a 2020 American sports comedy-drama film directed by Bob Saget. The movie revolves around a former high school basketball star who returns to his hometown and becomes involved in a local crime syndicate, leading to a series of events that test his loyalty and morals.

The main theme of Buffaloed explores the consequences of chasing material wealth and status, particularly for those who have lost their way in life. The protagonist's journey is marked by a struggle between his desire for financial security and his sense of identity, as he navigates the complexities of small-town politics and organized crime.

Throughout the film, the director uses humor and satire to critique the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of rural America. The movie also touches on themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the power of community, highlighting the ways in which people can come together to support one another despite their differences.

Ultimately, Buffaloed presents a nuanced portrayal of small-town life, revealing the intricate web of relationships and motivations that underpin these communities. By exploring the complexities of human nature, the film offers a thought-provoking commentary on the American Dream and the consequences of our choices.
