3. Self-Discovery: Through her experiences with Leo, Alex undergoes a journey of self-discovery. She learns to let go of her past and take risks, embracing the present moment and new possibilities.
4. Love Across Borders: The film celebrates the idea of love transcending geographical boundaries. Despite being from different countries, Alex and Leo find common ground and fall in love, proving that true connection can conquer distance.

Overall, Love in the Villa is a lighthearted, feel-good romantic comedy that explores themes of cultural exchange, self-discovery, and the power of love to bridge gaps between people.

overview: A young woman thinks she’s found a path to internet stardom when she starts making YouTube videos with a charismatic stranger  – until the dark side of viral celebrity threatens to ruin them both.
tagline: Like him. Or not.
title: Mainstream
plot:
Mainstream is a 2020 American comedy-drama directed by Gia Coppola, who co-wrote the screenplay with Tom Stuart. Andrew Garfield, Maya Hawke and Nat Wolff star, with Johnny Knoxville and Jason Schwartzman in supporting roles. A satire of internet celebrity and social media, the film premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2020 and was released by IFC Films in May 2021.

Frankie is a young woman in West Hollywood who has dropped out of school to pursue her artistic ambitions, but she is stuck working at a bar with her friend Jake and posting videos to a YouTube channel that few people watch. One day at a shopping mall she films Link, an eccentric young man working as a costumed mascot. When she claims she was recording a painting behind him rather than him, Link grabs the painting and delivers a rambling, passionate speech urging passersby to look up from their phones and pay attention to art. Frankie uploads the footage, and it quickly becomes her most popular video.

Frankie runs into Link again and befriends him. He is manic, charismatic and loudly opposed to the establishment and to social media. He agrees to appear in more of her videos on the condition that she quits her job, and she persuades Jake to join them as a writer. Together they create an online persona for Link called "No One Special," a provocateur who mocks the vapid culture of social media influencers, and his anarchic content quickly makes him an online star. But as his fame and followers grow, Link becomes increasingly egotistical, cruel and unpredictable, embracing the very culture he claimed to despise, and his stunts become more outrageous and offensive. Frankie, who has developed feelings for him, and Jake, who resents being sidelined, must confront what they have helped create as Link's behavior spirals toward a public disaster.

The film received generally negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 42 percent rating, with a consensus stating that it makes a vain attempt to satirize viral fame and settles for obvious commentary that feels dated, and it has a Metacritic score of 36. Garfield's committed, manic performance was frequently singled out as the most memorable element of the film.

overview: Five medical students, hoping to understand the mystery of what lies beyond life, embark on a dangerous experiment. When their hearts are stopped for a short period of time, they have a near-death experience…
tagline: You haven't lived until you've died
title: Flatliners
plot:
Flatliners (2017) is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human consciousness and the blurred lines between life and death. The film explores the theme of mortality, questioning what it truly means to exist and whether there's more to life than the physical realm.

The movie also touches on the idea of guilt and redemption, as the characters grapple with the consequences of their past actions and the weight of their secrets. As they navigate the afterlife, they're forced to confront the darkness within themselves and the true nature of their relationships with one another.

Furthermore, Flatliners examines the concept of identity and how it's shaped by our experiences, memories, and connections with others. The film raises questions about whether our sense of self is tied to our physical bodies or if it can transcend beyond them.

Ultimately, Flatliners presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the mysteries of life, death, and the complexities of the human psyche.

original_title: Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole
overview: Soren, a young barn owl, is kidnapped by owls of St. Aggie's, ostensibly an orphanage, where owlets are brainwashed into becoming soldiers. He and his new friends escape to the island of Ga'Hoole, to assist its noble, wise owls who fight the army being created by the wicked rulers of St. Aggie's. The film is based on the first three books in the series.
tagline: On his way to finding a legend...he will become one.
title: Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole
plot:
In a world where owls are the dominant species, the story begins with a young owl named Soren, who lives on the island of Ga'Hoole. Soren is an outcast among his peers due to his unusual appearance and behavior. He is fascinated by the stories of the Great Tree, a sacred place where the ancient wisdom of the owls is stored.

Soren's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets a wise old owl named Ewan, who tells him about the prophecy of the Owls of Ga'Hoole. According to legend, five owls will gather at the Great Tree and choose a new leader to save their world from the evil Pure Ones. Soren is chosen by Ewan to embark on this perilous journey.

Soren sets out with his friends, Kludd, a skilled but arrogant owl, and Gylfie, a young and curious owl. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious predators, and rival owls who seek to claim the leadership of Ga'Hoole for themselves.

As Soren and his companions journey deeper into the unknown, they discover that the Pure Ones are led by a ruthless leader named Blind Eye, who seeks to destroy all non-Pure owls. The group soon realizes that their quest is not just about choosing a new leader but also about saving their world from destruction.

Throughout their journey, Soren and his friends face numerous challenges, including treacherous mountain passes, dark forests, and treacherous rivers. Along the way, they meet other owls who join their cause, including Gylfie's brother, Alaric, and a mysterious owl named Rook.

As the group nears the Great Tree, they are ambushed by Blind Eye's minions, leading to a fierce battle that tests Soren's leadership skills. In the heat of the battle, Soren discovers his true potential as a leader and proves himself worthy of the prophecy.

In the end, Soren and his companions reach the Great Tree, where they face off against Blind Eye in an epic showdown. With the help of his friends and allies, Soren defeats Blind Eye and claims the leadership of Ga'Hoole. The movie concludes with Soren standing atop a mountain, looking out over the land he has saved, surrounded by his fellow owls.

The Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of leadership, friendship, and self-discovery. With stunning animation and a richly detailed world, this movie is sure to captivate audiences of all ages.

original_title: Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
overview: Join the likes of Tatiana Maslany, Mark Ruffalo, Tim Roth, and Benedict Wong as they reveal how Marvel Studios’ She-Hulk: Attorney at Law was conceived and shaped. Discover what it took for She-Hulk’s creators to pull off the show’s tricky tone and deliver Marvel Studios’ first truly comedic series – one that boldly breaks the fourth wall to acknowledge its own audience, no less!
title: Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
plot:
Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law (2022) is a documentary series that delves into the creation and production of the popular Disney+ show She-Hulk: Attorney at Law. At its core, the series explores the themes of identity, empowerment, and self-discovery.

The documentary sheds light on how the show's protagonist, Jennifer Walters, navigates her journey from being a lawyer to becoming the superhero known as She-Hulk. The series highlights how the character's transformation is not just physical but also emotional, as she grapples with her newfound powers and the responsibilities that come with them.

Throughout the documentary, it becomes clear that the show's creators aimed to explore themes of female empowerment and self-acceptance. Jennifer Walters' journey serves as a metaphor for the struggles women face in patriarchal societies, where they are often expected to conform to societal norms and expectations. The series shows how She-Hulk's character defies these expectations, embracing her uniqueness and using her powers to challenge the status quo.

The documentary also touches on the theme of identity, particularly in the context of Jennifer Walters' complicated relationship with her father, Bruce Banner. Their dynamic serves as a microcosm for the complexities of family relationships and the struggles that come with navigating one's own identity.

Ultimately, Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law presents a powerful exploration of what it means to be a strong, empowered woman in a world that often seeks to constrain her. Through Jennifer Walters' journey, the series shows how embracing one's true self can lead to transformation and growth, both personally and professionally.

overview: Jim Hanson’s quiet life is suddenly disturbed by two people crossing the US/Mexico border – a woman and her young son – desperate to flee a Mexican cartel. After a shootout leaves the mother dead, Jim becomes the boy’s reluctant defender. He embraces his role as Miguel’s protector and will stop at nothing to get him to safety, as they go on the run from the relentless assassins.
tagline: Justice comes down to him.
title: The Marksman
plot:
The Marksman is a 2021 American action thriller directed by Robert Lorenz. It stars Liam Neeson as Jim Hanson, a widowed rancher and former Marine sniper living in Arizona, with Jacob Perez as Miguel, Katheryn Winnick as Hanson's stepdaughter Sarah, a Border Patrol agent, Juan Pablo Raba as the cartel enforcer Mauricio and Teresa Ruiz as Miguel's mother Rosa.

Jim Hanson, a widowed Vietnam War veteran, lives alone with his dog on a ranch along the Arizona-Mexico border that he is about to lose to the bank. He often reports illegal crossings to the Border Patrol. One day he encounters Rosa and her young son Miguel, who are fleeing from a Mexican drug cartel. When cartel gunmen led by Mauricio arrive, a shootout breaks out in which Hanson kills Mauricio's brother and Rosa is fatally wounded. Before dying, she begs Hanson to take Miguel to her relatives in Chicago and gives him a bag of money and an address.

Hanson initially hands the boy over to the authorities, but when he realizes that the cartel has corrupt contacts able to reach Miguel, he takes the boy himself and sets out on a road trip across the American heartland. Pursued by Mauricio and his men, who cross the border with the help of bribed officials, Hanson must rely on his old military skills and his wits while avoiding both the cartel and the authorities. When he uses his credit card to repair his truck, the gang picks up his trail, and a corrupt police officer on Route 66 in Oklahoma tries to hand the boy over to them. Along the way, the gruff old man and the grieving boy slowly develop a bond.

Neeson brings his familiar persona as a hardened protector to a more restrained, character-driven story that recalls classic western themes of honor and sacrifice.

The Marksman was released in the United States on January 15, 2021, by Open Road Films and Briarcliff Entertainment and topped the box office during the COVID-19 pandemic, grossing about 23.9 million dollars worldwide. Critics praised Neeson's performance but found the film formulaic, giving it 39 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44.

overview: A court-appointed legal guardian defrauds her older clients and traps them under her care. But her latest mark comes with some unexpected baggage.
title: I Care a Lot
plot:
I Care a Lot is a 2020 American black comedy film written and directed by Aneesh Chaganty and starring Rosamund Pike, Eiza González, Dianne Wiest, and Christopher Abbott. The movie was released on Netflix in 2021.

The story revolves around Marla Grayson (Rosamund Pike), a con artist who specializes in stealing wealth from wealthy elderly patients in nursing homes. She is hired by a wealthy client to steal the assets of her target, Margaret "Midge" Gardner (Dianne Wiest). Midge has been diagnosed with dementia and is being cared for at a nursing home.

Marla's plan involves befriending Midge, gaining her trust, and then exploiting her vulnerability. She enlists the help of her accomplice, Jennifer King (Eiza González), who poses as a social worker to gain access to Midge's medical records. As Marla gets closer to Midge, she begins to develop feelings for her, which complicates her mission.

However, things take a turn when Marla meets Midge's caregiver, Dr. Karmen "Kae" Thompson (Anna Deavere Smith), who is determined to protect Midge from exploitation. As Marla navigates the complex web of relationships between Midge, Jennifer, and Dr. Thompson, she begins to question her own motivations and morals.

Throughout the film, Pike delivers a nuanced performance as Marla, bringing depth and complexity to a character that could have been one-dimensional. The supporting cast also shines, particularly Wiest, who brings warmth and vulnerability to her portrayal of Midge.

The movie explores themes of loneliness, exploitation, and the complexities of human relationships. As Marla's feelings for Midge deepen, she is forced to confront the consequences of her actions and the harm she has caused to others. The film builds towards a tense and unexpected climax, as Marla's plans are threatened by Dr. Thompson and Jennifer.

Ultimately, I Care a Lot is a thought-provoking commentary on the ways in which we treat vulnerable individuals, particularly the elderly. The film raises important questions about exploitation, consent, and the complexities of human relationships. While it may not be an easy watch at times, Pike's performance and the film's thought-provoking themes make for a compelling and unforgettable viewing experience.

[No additional information available]

overview: A sailor prone to violent outbursts is sent to a naval psychiatrist for help. Refusing at first to open up, the young man eventually breaks down and reveals a horrific childhood. Through the guidance of his doctor, he confronts his painful past and begins a quest to find the family he never knew.
tagline: Antwone Fisher is at war... with himself.
title: Antwone Fisher
plot:
Antwone Fisher is a powerful and emotional drama that explores the complexities of identity, family, and redemption. The film delves into the life of its titular character, Antwone Fisher, who struggles to come to terms with his troubled past and find his place in the world.

At its core, the movie is a story about the long-lasting effects of childhood trauma and abandonment. Antwone's early life is marked by neglect and abuse, which leaves him feeling unloved and unworthy. As he navigates his way through adolescence and young adulthood, he grapples with feelings of anger, resentment, and self-doubt.

However, the film also suggests that it's never too late to seek redemption and forgiveness. Through a series of poignant and often humorous encounters with his estranged father, Antwone begins to confront the painful memories of his past and work towards healing and reconciliation.

One of the main themes of the movie is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Antwone's journey is a metaphor for the search for one's true self, which is often hindered by external factors such as family dynamics and societal expectations. The film ultimately suggests that it's up to each individual to take control of their own narrative and forge their own path in life.

The movie also explores the theme of forgiveness, both towards oneself and others. Antwone's journey is marked by a series of difficult choices and confrontations, which force him to re-evaluate his relationships with those around him. Through this process, he learns to let go of past hurts and resentments, and instead chooses to forgive himself and others.

Overall, Antwone Fisher is a powerful and moving drama that explores the complexities of human experience through its protagonist's journey towards healing, redemption, and self-discovery.

overview: A guy gets more than he bargained for after entering into an affair with the wife of an investment banker. Soon, a suspicious death and substantial life insurance policy embroil him in a scandal.
tagline: Wanting her was his first mistake
title: Careful What You Wish For
plot:
Careful What You Wish For is a 2015 American erotic thriller directed by Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum. It stars Nick Jonas as Doug Martin, Isabel Lucas as Lena Harper and Dermot Mulroney as her husband Elliot, with Graham Rogers, Kandyse McClure and Paul Sorvino. Its plot draws heavily on the 1981 neo-noir Body Heat, reworking the story of seduction, murder and betrayal around a teenage protagonist.

Doug Martin, a seventeen-year-old, is spending the summer with his parents at their lake house. When Elliot Harper, a wealthy investment banker, moves in next door with his much younger wife, Lena, Doug is instantly attracted to her. Elliot hires Doug to work on his sailboat, which gives him the opportunity to spend time near Lena, who is often left alone while her husband travels on business. Soon Lena and Doug begin a secret affair. She gives him a prepaid phone so they can communicate in secret and repeatedly warns him about Elliot's jealousy and violent temper, showing him bruises she says her husband inflicted.

One night Lena calls Doug to her house, where he finds Elliot dead on the floor. She claims that her husband attacked her and that she killed him accidentally while defending herself. Frightened, Doug agrees to help her cover up her role in the death. Soon afterward, an insurance investigator, Angie Alvarez, arrives to examine the circumstances surrounding the ten-million-dollar life insurance policy that Lena stands to collect, and the local sheriff also begins asking questions. As suspicion increasingly falls on him, Doug starts to realize that he may have been manipulated from the very beginning and that Lena's version of events may be designed to make him the perfect scapegoat.

The film borrows the femme fatale and murder-plot conventions of classic film noir while placing them in a sun-soaked summer setting with a young cast.

Careful What You Wish For was released by Starz Digital on June 10, 2016. It was poorly received, holding an approval rating of 17 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus criticized its stale plotting and curious lack of sensuality.

overview: Mr. Freeze turns Killer Croc and Bane into super-sized monsters, and they bash their way through downtown Gotham until the Caped Crusader and his team of heroes join the fight in their giant robot mechs.
title: Batman Unlimited: Mechs vs. Mutants
plot:
Batman Unlimited: Mechs vs. Mutants is an animated superhero film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie's narrative is driven by a sense of chaos and destruction, as two opposing forces - the Mechans and the Mutants - engage in an all-out war.

At its core, the film explores the theme of fear and how it can be exploited to manipulate people into doing the bidding of those who seek power. The Mechans, with their advanced technology and militaristic approach, represent a force that is driven by logic and reason, but also by a desire for control and domination. On the other hand, the Mutants embody a more primal and emotional response to fear, using their powers to lash out against those they perceive as threats.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and what it means to be human. The Mechans, with their advanced technology and artificial enhancements, raise questions about the nature of humanity and whether it is defined by our biology or our choices. Meanwhile, the Mutants, who are often seen as outcasts and misfits, challenge traditional notions of heroism and what it means to be a force for good.

Ultimately, Batman Unlimited: Mechs vs. Mutants presents a world that is both dark and complex, where the lines between good and evil are constantly blurred. The film's themes of fear, identity, and the nature of humanity serve as a backdrop for an action-packed narrative that explores the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

overview: In a social context deteriorated by a countrywide economic crisis, the life of several people will be turned upside down after they meet Cécile, a character who symbolizes desire.
tagline: Love, desire and complications...
title: Desire
plot:
Q, released in the United States as Desire, is a 2011 French erotic drama written and directed by Laurent Bouhnik. Set in Cherbourg, the film follows a loose group of young people whose lives are disrupted by a woman who embodies desire. The cast includes Déborah Révy, Hélène Zimmer, Gowan Didi, Johnny Amaro and Johan Libéreau. The film attracted attention for its unsimulated sex scenes, which members of its cast later discussed publicly.

Cécile is a 20-year-old woman whose father has recently died. Unable to confront her grief, she throws herself into sexual encounters with a succession of partners, friends and strangers alike. At the same time she appoints herself a guide to the people around her, sometimes seducing them and sometimes counseling patience, offering frank advice on how to give and receive pleasure. Her sometime boyfriend is Chance, a small-time criminal who loves her but cannot satisfy her. His friend Matt, who works as a mechanic, keeps pressuring his girlfriend Alice to sleep with him, but Alice does not feel ready. Meanwhile Chance and his friends scramble to earn money while trying to stay out of reach of rival criminals they have crossed.

On a ferry, Cécile eavesdrops on a married couple, flirts with the husband and slips him her number. It emerges that the wife has suffered a traumatic experience that makes intimacy difficult for her, and the couple's discussions about Cécile become a way of approaching their own problems. Alice, too, becomes involved in helping them, arranging a meeting in which the husband and wife come together blindfolded in an attempt to repair their relationship.

At a party organized by a group of women, Chance arrives carrying the urn holding the ashes of Cécile's father, which she has never been able to deal with. He tells her that he loves her and challenges her to take care of herself as she tries to care for everyone else. They leave together, and as they drive along the coast Cécile finally scatters her father's ashes. Having failed to find peace through her many encounters, including ones with Chance, Matt and Alice, she discovers another path toward healing and tells Chance that she loves him, though she knows it will not be easy.

The film's explicit content made it a subject of controversy. Hélène Zimmer, one of the lead actresses, said in 2015 that she had taken the role because of the challenge it represented, but admitted that she would happily remove the unsimulated sex scenes if she could.

overview: Rey develops her newly discovered abilities with the guidance of Luke Skywalker, who is unsettled by the strength of her powers. Meanwhile, the Resistance prepares to do battle with the First Order.
tagline: Darkness rises... and light to meet it
title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
plot:
Star Wars: The Last Jedi is a 2017 science fiction film directed by Rian Johnson, written by Johnson and Mark Hamill, and produced by Kathleen Kennedy, J.J. Abrams, and Dave Filoni.

The film takes place immediately after the events of The Force Awakens (2015). The Resistance, led by General Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher), is on the run from the First Order, a new evil force risen from the ashes of the Galactic Empire. Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), the legendary Jedi Master, has gone into exile on the planet Ahch-To, where he hopes to rebuild the Jedi Order.

The story begins with Rey (Daisy Ridley) searching for Luke, hoping to find a way to restore balance to the Force and defeat the First Order. She encounters Finn (John Boyega), a former Stormtrooper who has defected to the Resistance, and Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac), a skilled pilot. The trio embarks on a perilous journey to find Luke, facing numerous challenges along the way.

Meanwhile, Kylo Ren (Adam Driver), the conflicted leader of the First Order, is struggling with his own identity and loyalties. He is torn between his allegiance to the dark side and his lingering connection to Rey, who he believes may be strong in the Force.

As Rey searches for Luke, she encounters a series of cryptic clues and visions that lead her to Canto Bight, a luxurious casino planet where she meets DJ (Benicio del Toro), a skilled hacker. However, their encounter is short-lived, as they are pursued by Kylo Ren's forces.

Rey eventually finds Luke on Ahch-To, but he is reluctant to return to the Jedi Order, fearing that he will only lead to more suffering and conflict. Rey convinces him to train her in the ways of the Force, and they embark on a journey to confront their pasts and find redemption.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Resistance and the First Order, with Luke using his newfound connection to the Force to help turn the tide of the battle. However, Kylo Ren ultimately discovers Rey's true identity as strong in the Force, leading to a confrontation that leaves both characters severely injured.

In the aftermath, Rey sets out on her own journey, determined to find a new purpose and bring balance to the Force. Luke, meanwhile, is left to grapple with his own guilt and regret, realizing too late that he may have inadvertently contributed to the rise of the First Order.

The film concludes with a poignant moment between Leia and Rey, as they share a heartfelt goodbye before Leia's passing. The final shot is of Rey standing on the deck of the Resistance ship, looking out at the stars, ready to embark on her own journey into the unknown.

Overall, Star Wars: The Last Jedi is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores complex themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption in a galaxy far, far away.

overview: A Shaolin-trainer young woman returns to Japan to resuscitate her grandfather's defunct martial arts school.
title: Shaolin Girl
plot:
Shaolin Girl (Shōrin Shōjo) is a 2008 Japanese martial arts sports comedy directed by Katsuyuki Motohiro, best known for the Bayside Shakedown series, from a screenplay by Seishi Togawa and Rika Togawa. Inspired by Stephen Chow's Shaolin Soccer, which it transposes to women's lacrosse, the film stars Ko Shibasaki in her first solo leading role in four years, alongside Toru Nakamura, Kitty Zhang, Takashi Okamura and Yosuke Eguchi. Chow is credited as executive producer, and Tin Kai Man and Lam Chi Chung from Shaolin Soccer appear in similar roles. It was released in Japan on April 26, 2008.

Rin Sakurazawa returns to Japan after 3,000 days of training at a Shaolin martial arts school in China, hoping to spread kung fu at home as her late grandfather wished. She finds his dojo in ruins, and her former teacher Iwai, one of her grandfather's pupils, now runs a Chinese restaurant and urges her to give up her plan. Minmin, who works at the restaurant, persuades Rin to join the women's lacrosse team at Seikan International University, where her astonishing physical ability draws the attention of Tamura, the administrator who manages the team, and Iwai becomes its coach. Left out of the starting line-up for her first match, Rin comes on after a teammate is injured but plays only for herself, and the team falls apart. A game of football with local boys teaches her the meaning of teamwork, and as she wins back her teammates and teaches them the basics of kung fu, both the team and the dojo begin to revive. The university's president, Yuichiro Oba, himself a martial arts master, has been watching her and wants to draw out her hidden power. When his men abduct Minmin, Rin comes to understand Iwai's reluctance to fight and heads to the campus for a final battle to protect her friends.

The film was shot largely around Izunokuni and elsewhere in Shizuoka Prefecture. Its score is by Yugo Kanno, and mihimaru GT performed the theme song "Giri Giri Hero". Reported to have cost over one billion yen, it grossed about 1.51 billion yen in Japan. Critical reception was harsh: critic Kiichiro Yanashita derided it, and the magazine Eiga Hiho named it the worst film of 2008 by a wide margin in its annual poll of critics and writers. It was released in Germany as Kung Fu Girl.

overview: When Grouchy Smurf behaves badly to everyone and refuses to celebrate Christmas, the Smurfs of Christmas Past, Present and Future teach him to appreciate Christmas.
title: The Smurfs: A Christmas Carol
plot:
The Smurfs: A Christmas Carol is a 2011 American animated short film based on the Smurfs comics created by the Belgian artist Peyo and adapted from Charles Dickens's 1843 novella A Christmas Carol. Directed by Troy Quane from a script by Todd Berger, it was produced by Sony Pictures Animation, with animation by Sony Pictures Imageworks and Duck Studios. The voice cast includes George Lopez as Grouchy Smurf, Jack Angel as Papa Smurf, Melissa Sturm as Smurfette, and Fred Armisen, Gary Basaraba, Anton Yelchin and Hank Azaria.

On Christmas Eve, the Smurfs prepare for their holiday celebration. Grouchy refuses to take part and declares that he hates Christmas, to everyone's dismay. Papa Smurf brews a potion intended to restore Grouchy's festive spirit, and it ends up in Grouchy's mug of smurfberry nog. After drinking it he passes out, and when he wakes, the world around him, and he himself, has turned into hand-drawn animation.

Smurfette appears as the Smurf of Christmas Past and shows him earlier holidays, when Grouchy, longing for a hang glider, was disappointed year after year to receive yet another new hat from Papa Smurf, until a prank by Jokey made him lose his temper and turn against Christmas. Brainy, as the Smurf of Christmas Present, reveals how Grouchy's refusal to help has forced the others to take on extra work, leading Clumsy to set the tree on fire, and shows Papa lovingly crafting each Smurf's hat. Hefty, as the Smurf of Christmas Future, warns that if Grouchy does not change, the Smurfs will wander into the forest trying to cheer him up and fall into the clutches of Gargamel and his cat Azrael.

Grouchy wakes on Christmas morning transformed, admits he was wrong and realizes that the holiday is about a family that loves him. Papa gives him his gift first, a hat made especially for him, and after placing the star on the tree Grouchy uses it as a makeshift hang glider before crash-landing in the snow, joking that he hates that Christmas comes only once a year.

The short's hand-drawn sequence was based on Peyo's original designs. Melissa Sturm voiced Smurfette in place of Katy Perry, who was unavailable because of her concert tour. The short was released on DVD on December 2, 2011, as part of a holiday gift set with The Smurfs, and as a stand-alone DVD in 2013.

overview: In 1847, when Ireland is in the grip of the Great Famine that has ravaged the country for two long years, Feeney, a hardened Irish Ranger who has been fighting for the British Army abroad, returns home to reunite with his estranged family, only to discover the cruelest reality, a black land where death reigns.
tagline: In Ireland’s darkest hour vengeance shines a light
title: Black '47
plot:
Black '47 is a 2018 Irish historical drama film directed by Lance Daly. The movie is set during the Great Famine in Ireland and explores the harsh realities of poverty, starvation, and disease that ravaged the country at that time.

The main theme of Black '47 revolves around the struggle for survival in a desperate situation. The protagonist, Red Williams, played by Jack O'Connell, is forced to confront the brutal conditions faced by the Irish people during this period. As he navigates through the treacherous landscape, he must make impossible choices and confront his own morality in order to stay alive.

The film also delves into the theme of identity and how it is shaped by one's experiences. Red's journey is a metaphor for the struggles faced by many Irish people during this period, as they were forced to adapt to new circumstances and redefine their sense of self in the face of unimaginable hardship.

Furthermore, Black '47 touches on the theme of resistance and rebellion against oppressive systems. The film portrays the resilience and determination of the Irish people in the face of colonialism and economic exploitation, highlighting the ways in which they fought back against the forces that sought to control them.

Overall, Black '47 is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human survival, identity, and resistance in the face of unimaginable adversity.

overview: A mysterious global blackout yields countless populations to simply vanish, leaving only their clothes and possessions behind. A small handful of survivors band together in a dimly-lit tavern on 7th Street, struggling to combat the apocalyptic horror. Realizing they may in fact be the last people on earth, a dark shadow hones in on them alone.
tagline: Stay in the light.
title: Vanishing on 7th Street
plot:
Vanishing on 7th Street is a thought-provoking and haunting film that delves into the human condition in the face of catastrophic loss and transformation. The movie's narrative revolves around a mysterious phenomenon where people begin to vanish, leaving behind only their physical bodies.

At its core, Vanishing on 7th Street explores the themes of existential crisis, identity, and the search for meaning in a seemingly meaningless world. As the characters navigate this unexplained event, they are forced to confront their own mortality, the fragility of human existence, and the impermanence of everything around them.

The film also touches upon the idea of community and the bonds that tie people together. In the face of unimaginable loss, the remaining characters come together in a desperate attempt to find each other, form new connections, and create a sense of purpose. This serves as a poignant commentary on the human need for belonging and connection.

Furthermore, Vanishing on 7th Street raises questions about the nature of reality and the human perception of it. As the characters struggle to understand what is happening to them, they are forced to confront their own biases, assumptions, and limitations. The film's use of surreal and dreamlike sequences adds to the sense of disorientation and uncertainty, highlighting the fragility of our understanding of the world.

Ultimately, Vanishing on 7th Street is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the unknown, the unknowable, and the existential crises that we all face.

overview: The rough-hewn boss of a lumber crew courts trouble when he steps in to protect the youngest member of his team from an abusive father.
tagline: Who is he?
title: Joe
plot:
Joe is a 2013 American Southern Gothic crime drama directed by David Gordon Green and written by Gary Hawkins, adapted from Larry Brown's 1991 novel of the same name. Nicolas Cage stars as a volatile ex-convict who becomes a mentor and protector to a teenage boy, played by Tye Sheridan, with Ronnie Gene Blevins, Heather Kafka and Gary Poulter in supporting roles.

In rural Texas, the 15-year-old drifter Gary asks Joe Ransom, the tattooed, chain-smoking foreman of a crew that poisons trees to clear woodland, for work, and impresses him with his diligence. When Gary brings along his alcoholic father, Wade, the older man's laziness gets them both dismissed, and Joe witnesses Wade beating his son and taking his money. Gary returns alone to ask for his job back, and Joe rehires him, while the boy learns to hide his wages from his father.

Joe, who served time in prison for assaulting police officers, struggles to keep his violent temper in check. He is shot and wounded by Willie Russell, a local criminal with a long-standing grudge, and Willie's grudge extends to Gary after the boy beats him up for making crude remarks about his younger sister, Dorothy. When Willie demands to know where Gary lives, Joe refuses and thrashes him. Meanwhile Wade grows more dangerous, murdering a homeless man for his bottle of liquor and threatening Gary with a knife over his hidden earnings. Gary and Joe grow close; they spend a day searching for Joe's missing dog, Joe gives the boy his lighter, and later he helps Gary get a truck of his own.

The fragile peace collapses when Wade beats Gary, steals the truck and takes Dorothy to Willie, intending to sell her to him. Joe and Gary go after them. Joe rescues Dorothy, whom Gary takes to safety, and kills Willie and one of his men, but is mortally wounded in the gunfight. Cornered on a bridge, Wade throws himself to his death, and Gary returns with the sheriff to find Joe dying.

The film premiered in competition at the Venice Film Festival in August 2013, where Sheridan won the Marcello Mastroianni Award for best young actor, and was released by Lionsgate in April 2014. Critics praised it as a return to form for both Cage and Green; Metacritic gave it 74 out of 100. Poulter, a homeless man cast as Wade, died before the film's release, and his performance was widely acclaimed.

overview: The staff of an American magazine based in France puts out its last issue, with stories featuring an artist sentenced to life imprisonment, student riots, and a kidnapping resolved by a chef.
title: The French Dispatch
plot:
The French Dispatch is a 2021 American satirical comedy-drama film written and directed by Wes Anderson. The film is set in the fictional town of Ennui-sur-Sea, France, and pays homage to the classic pulp magazines of the 1940s and 1950s.

The story begins with an introduction to the world of The French Dispatch, a magazine that covers the lives of the people living in Ennui-sur-Sea. The film is presented as a collection of stories from the magazine's archives, each written by a different author. The first story is about Zeffirelli (Benicio del Toro), an Italian chef who has been hired to cook for the town's elite, but finds himself at odds with the town's aristocracy.

The second story follows Roebuck Wright (Timothée Chalamet), a young journalist who returns to Ennui-sur-Sea after being expelled from his previous school. Roebuck becomes infatuated with a local woman named Zazie (Léa Seydoux) and sets out to write the perfect article about her.

The third story centers around Arthur Howitzer Jr. (Owen Wilson), the editor of The French Dispatch, who is struggling to keep his magazine afloat in a world that no longer values pulp journalism. Arthur's life becomes complicated when he falls for a woman named Maybelle (Frances McDormand) and must navigate the complexities of small-town politics.

As the stories unfold, it becomes clear that Ennui-sur-Sea is not as idyllic as it seems. The town is plagued by corruption, inequality, and social unrest. Through Roebuck's story, we see the darker side of the town's aristocracy, who use their wealth and power to exploit the working class.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Arthur and the town's corrupt mayor (Adrien Brody), which ultimately leads to the downfall of the town's elite. The ending is bittersweet, with Roebuck finding love and success as a journalist, but also acknowledging the complexities and flaws of his own story.

Throughout the film, Wes Anderson's signature visual style and attention to detail are on full display. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty and charm of Ennui-sur-Sea in all its glory. The production design is equally impressive, with intricate sets and costumes that evoke the classic pulp magazines of the 1940s and 1950s.

Overall, The French Dispatch is a love letter to the art of storytelling and the power of journalism to shape our understanding of the world around us. With its unique blend of humor, satire, and drama, the film is a must-see for fans of Wes Anderson and anyone who loves a good story well-told.

overview: Near a gray and unnamed city is the Zone, a place guarded by barbed wire and soldiers, and where the normal laws of physics are victim to frequent anomalies. A stalker guides two men into the Zone, specifically to an area in which deep-seated desires are granted.
title: Stalker
plot:
Stalker is a 1979 Soviet science fiction film directed by Andrei Tarkovsky, based on the novel "Roadside Picnic" by Arkady and Boris Strugatsky. The movie follows three men who venture into a mysterious area known as the "Zone," where strange phenomena occur.

The story begins with Professor Zavodovskiy (Anatoli Solonitsyn), a scientist from Moscow, who is accompanied by his friends, Red Schuhart (Aleksandr Kaidansky) and Prof. Kirillov (Nikolai Grinko). The three men are drawn to the Zone, a restricted area surrounding a nuclear test site where strange occurrences have been reported.

The Zone is said to be a place of supernatural phenomena, where the laws of physics do not apply. Red, who has previously visited the Zone and returned with a mysterious artifact known as "the Stalker," becomes the guide for this expedition. The group's goal is to find the "Room," a mystical space within the Zone that is said to grant wishes.

As they journey into the Zone, the men encounter various surreal landscapes and strange creatures. They also experience a series of bizarre events, including hallucinations, unexplained noises, and visions. The atmosphere becomes increasingly unsettling, and the group begins to question their own sanity.

Throughout the film, Tarkovsky explores themes of existentialism, spirituality, and the human condition. The Zone is portrayed as a liminal space, where the boundaries between reality and fantasy are blurred. The characters' experiences within the Zone serve as a metaphor for the search for meaning and purpose in life.

As the journey progresses, the group's dynamics become increasingly strained. Red becomes obsessed with finding the Room, while Kirillov begins to question the true nature of their mission. Zavodovskiy, meanwhile, struggles to reconcile his scientific worldview with the supernatural events unfolding around him.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between the three men and a mysterious figure known as "the Stalker." The outcome is ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the meaning of the Room and the true nature of the Zone. Ultimately, the film concludes with Red, Kirillov, and Zavodovskiy emerging from the Zone, forever changed by their experiences.

Tarkovsky's masterful direction and the enigmatic Strugatsky novel have made Stalker a cult classic, widely regarded as one of the greatest films of all time. The movie's slow-burning pace, atmospheric sound design, and haunting visuals create a sense of unease and wonder, drawing the viewer into the mysterious world of the Zone.

In conclusion, Stalker is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores the human condition through the lens of science fiction. Tarkovsky's direction weaves together themes of existentialism, spirituality, and the search for meaning, creating a cinematic experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: John Matrix, the former leader of a special commando strike force that always got the toughest jobs done, is forced back into action when his young daughter is kidnapped. To find her, Matrix has to fight his way through an array of punks, killers, one of his former commandos, and a fully equipped private army. With the help of a feisty stewardess and an old friend, Matrix has only a few hours to overcome his greatest challenge: finding his daughter before she's killed.
tagline: Somewhere, somehow, someone's going to pay.
title: Commando
plot:
Commando is a classic action film directed by Mark L. Lester and starring Arnold Schwarzenegger as John Matrix, a retired special forces operative who must rescue his daughter from a group of mercenaries.

The movie begins with John Matrix (Schwarzenegger), a skilled and deadly operative, living a quiet life in the countryside with his 11-year-old daughter Jenny (Alyssa Milano). Unbeknownst to them, a group of ruthless mercenaries, led by the cunning and sadistic Arius (Daniel Bernhardt), have infiltrated their community. The mercenaries are searching for Matrix, who they believe has hidden a large sum of money somewhere in the area.

When the mercenaries attack Jenny's home, John is forced back into action to protect his daughter. He sets out on a perilous journey to rescue her and take down the enemy forces. Along the way, he encounters a range of colorful characters, including Gracie (Sharon Stone), a tough-as-nails mercenary who becomes an unlikely ally.

As Matrix navigates through the treacherous terrain, he faces off against Arius's henchmen in a series of intense and explosive battles. The action is relentless, with Matrix using his combat skills to take down enemy after enemy. Meanwhile, Gracie proves herself to be a valuable asset, providing comedic relief and helping Matrix stay one step ahead of the mercenaries.

As the stakes grow higher, Matrix discovers that Arius has a personal vendetta against him, having been defeated by Matrix in the past. The final showdown takes place at an abandoned warehouse, where Matrix faces off against Arius and his remaining henchmen. In a thrilling sequence of events, Matrix uses his wits and combat skills to take down the enemy, culminating in a dramatic confrontation with Arius.

In the end, John Matrix emerges victorious, having successfully rescued his daughter and avenged his past defeat. The movie concludes with Matrix and Gracie sharing a moment of tenderness, as they drive off into the sunset together.

Throughout the film, Schwarzenegger's signature blend of humor, charm, and machismo is on full display. His performance as John Matrix has become iconic in action cinema, cementing his status as one of the greatest action heroes of all time. The movie's success can be attributed to its well-crafted script, memorable characters, and, of course, Schwarzenegger's larger-than-life presence.

Overall, Commando is a classic action film that has stood the test of time. Its blend of humor, action, and adventure makes it a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: An aging thief hopes to retire and live off his ill-gotten wealth when a young kid convinces him into doing one last heist.
tagline: There are no partners in crime.
title: The Score
plot:
The Score is a 2001 crime drama film directed by Frank Oz. The movie revolves around a group of professional thieves who plan to steal $100 million from a wealthy businessman, but things take an unexpected turn when they discover that their target has a personal connection to one of the team members.

At its core, The Score explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and redemption. The film delves into the complexities of relationships between partners in crime, highlighting the tensions and conflicts that arise when individuals with different motivations and values work together towards a common goal. As the story unfolds, the characters are forced to confront their own personal demons and make difficult choices that challenge their sense of loyalty and identity.

The Score also touches on the idea of redemption, as one of the main characters seeks to atone for past mistakes and find a way to make amends with those he has wronged. This theme is woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and nuance to the film's exploration of the human condition.

Ultimately, The Score presents a thought-provoking portrayal of the gray areas between right and wrong, suggesting that even in the most morally ambiguous situations, individuals must find a way to navigate their own moral compasses and make choices that align with their values.

overview: A family migrates to the city after a tragic loss. When they reunite in their hometown 30 years later, buried emotions and painful secrets resurface.
title: Cici
plot:
Cici is a 2022 Turkish drama film written and directed by Berkun Oya and produced by Krek Film for Netflix. It stars Yılmaz Erdoğan as the patriarch Bekir, Nur Sürer and Funda Eryiğit as his wife Havva in later and earlier life, Okan Yalabık as their son Kadir, Ayça Bingöl as their daughter Saliha, Fatih Artman as the youngest son Yusuf, Olgun Şimşek as Cemil, İncinur Daşdemir as Yusuf's wife and Şevval Balkan as Saliha's daughter Naz. Yağız Yavru was the cinematographer, and the film, which uses no background score, runs 151 minutes.

Moving between several timelines, the film opens on a farm in the Turkish countryside decades earlier, where Bekir rules his family with an iron fist. His wife Havva resents his infidelity and the harshness with which he treats their children: he regularly slaps his eldest son Kadir, keeps the children out of school and records them with a video camera, while Saliha secretly meets Cemil, a boy with a remarkable singing voice who works on the farm, and young Yusuf is his father's favourite. After a particularly cruel punishment of Kadir, Bekir falls ill, and following the family's loss they move to the city. Some thirty years later Kadir, now a filmmaker, returns to the old house to shoot a film drawn from his childhood memories, recreating episodes such as the day his father punished him with a hosepipe. When the production stalls he stays on, and during the COVID-19 pandemic the family is reunited under the same roof: Havva, now suffering from dementia, has been released from her care home into Saliha's care, Saliha is divorced with a teenage daughter, and Yusuf, married with a son, is unhappy and frustrated that the farm has not been sold. As Kadir excavates their past, old tensions revive, Cemil and Saliha confront their unspoken romance, and painful family secrets come to light.

The film was released on Netflix on 27 October 2022. Marshall Shaffer of Decider recommended it as a modest meta-movie in the tradition of 8½, praising its exploration of the borders between reality and fiction and singling out Sürer's performance, while finding it overlong. Akash Deshpande of High on Films admired Yavru's photography and sound but found its shifts into comedy jarring, and Lori Meek of Ready Steady Cut praised the performances but called it a slow melodrama whose relationships remained underexplored.

keywords.name: based on magazine, newspaper or article

overview: A tenacious attorney uncovers a dark secret that connects a growing number of unexplained deaths to one of the world's largest corporations. In the process, he risks everything — his future, his family, and his own life — to expose the truth.
tagline: The truth has a man on the inside
title: Dark Waters
plot:
Dark Waters is a 2019 biographical drama film directed by Todd Robinson, based on the true story of Robert Bilott, an environmental lawyer who fought against DuPont's toxic water scandal in Parkersburg, West Virginia.

The main themes of Dark Waters include:

1. Environmental Justice: The film highlights the struggles of the local community in Parkersburg, who were exposed to toxic chemicals from DuPont's water supply, leading to severe health issues and even death.
2. Corporate Greed vs. Human Life: The movie portrays DuPont's relentless pursuit of profits over people's lives, as they knowingly released toxic substances into the environment, putting countless lives at risk.
3. Personal Courage: Robert Bilott's character is a symbol of courage in the face of overwhelming adversity. He risks his career and reputation to expose the truth about DuPont's actions, despite facing intense opposition from the corporation.
4. The Power of Whistleblowing: Dark Waters showcases the importance of whistleblowers like Robert Bilott, who bring attention to corporate malfeasance and hold those in power accountable for their actions.
5. Community Resilience: The film also explores the resilience of the local community, who come together to fight against DuPont's toxic legacy and demand justice.

The movie features an all-star cast, including Mark Ruffalo as Robert Bilott, Anne Hathaway as Sarah Buxton, Tim Robbins as Richard Bilott, and Bill Pullman as Rod Bilott.

overview: Max and Page are a brilliant mother/daughter con team who have their grift down to a fine science. Max targets wealthy, willing men and marries them. Page then seduces them, and Max catches her husband in the act. Then it's off to palimony city and the next easy mark.
tagline: Caution: Dangerous Curves Ahead
title: Heartbreakers
plot:
Heartbreakers is a 2001 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships, identity, and the blurred lines between truth and deception. The movie follows the story of two con artists, PAulette (played by a character who poses as a wealthy socialite) and her daughter Margie (played by a character who pretends to be a naive young woman), as they navigate their way through a series of romantic entanglements.

At its core, Heartbreakers is a film about the fragility of human relationships and the ways in which people present themselves to the world. The main characters are masters of manipulation, using their charm and wit to create elaborate personas that hide their true selves. As they navigate their way through love and heartbreak, they must confront the tension between their authentic desires and the masks they wear.

The film also explores themes of identity and self-discovery, particularly for Margie, who is struggling to find her place in the world and define herself outside of her mother's shadow. Through her relationships with various men, Margie begins to uncover fragments of her own true nature, forcing her to confront the complexities of growing up and finding one's own path.

Ultimately, Heartbreakers is a film about the power of vulnerability and authenticity in relationships. As the characters navigate their way through love and heartbreak, they must learn to be honest with themselves and others, embracing their imperfections and true selves in order to find genuine connection and intimacy.

overview: At the age of 10 years, young Rémi is snatched from his adoptive mother and entrusted to the signor Vitalis, a mysterious itinerant musician. Has its hard sides - he will learn the harsh life of acrobat and sing to win his bread. Accompanied by the faithful dog capi and of the small monkey Joli-Coeur, his long trip through France, made for meetings, friendships and mutual assistance, leads him to the secret of its origins.
title: Remi, Nobody's Boy
plot:
Remi, Nobody's Boy (French: Rémi sans famille) is a 2018 French historical adventure drama directed by Antoine Blossier and based on Hector Malot's 1878 novel Sans Famille, a classic of French children's literature. Maleaume Paquin stars as the young Rémi, with Daniel Auteuil as the street musician Vitalis, Virginie Ledoyen, Ludivine Sagnier and Jonathan Zaccaï in supporting roles. The film was released in French cinemas in December 2018.

The film is framed by a stormy night at an orphanage, where frightened children gather around an old man who tells them the story of his childhood. His name is Rémi. Abandoned as a baby and found outside a church, Rémi grew up happily in a French village in the 19th century with the woman he believed to be his mother, who loved him dearly. Their life changes when her husband, a stonemason working in Paris, is badly injured in an accident and returns home embittered and in debt. Revealing that Rémi is not their son, he decides to take the boy to an orphanage to be rid of another mouth to feed.

On the way they meet Vitalis, a former violinist who now travels the countryside as a street performer with a mischievous monkey named Joli-Cœur and a loyal dog named Capi. Discovering that Rémi has a beautiful singing voice, Vitalis offers to rent the boy from his foster father, sparing him the orphanage. Rémi reluctantly sets out on the road with Vitalis and his animals, and the old musician teaches him to read, to sing and to perform. Their wanderings across France bring hardship, danger and moments of joy, including a friendship with a sickly girl and her wealthy mother. Along the way Rémi learns more about the mystery of his birth and about Vitalis's own hidden past, while the bond between the boy and his gruff mentor grows into something like that of father and son.

The film was a popular success in France and received generally positive reviews, with praise for Auteuil's performance, its photography and its faithful but accessible treatment of the classic novel, which had previously been adapted many times for film, television and animation.

original_title: おおかみこどもの雨と雪
overview: After her werewolf lover unexpectedly dies in an accident, a woman must find a way to raise the son and daughter that she had with him. However, their inheritance of their father's traits prove to be a challenge for her.
tagline: Love wildly.
title: Wolf Children
plot:
Wolf Children is a 2012 Japanese fantasy drama film directed by Mamoru Hosoda, produced by Toho, and based on the manga series of the same name by Yuki Midorikawa.

The story revolves around Yūko Ichihara (voiced by Kana Ueda), a young woman who falls in love with a werewolf named Toshio Tanaka (voiced by Takuya Ishida) while working as an intern at a research facility. After their wedding, Yūko becomes pregnant and gives birth to twin children, Hana (a girl) and Shun (a boy). Unbeknownst to them, both of their parents are werewolves.

As the twins grow up, they begin to exhibit supernatural traits similar to those of their father. However, unlike Toshio, who is able to control his transformations, the children's powers are unpredictable and uncontrollable. Yūko struggles to balance her love for her family with the danger posed by her children's condition.

As Hana grows older, she becomes increasingly isolated from her peers due to her werewolf nature. She begins to develop a strong sense of independence and a desire to protect herself and those she cares about. Meanwhile, Shun is more open about his condition and forms close bonds with others who accept him for what he is.

The film's plot takes a dramatic turn when Hana discovers that she has the ability to transform into a wolf at will, much like her father. This newfound power allows her to protect herself and those around her from harm. However, it also puts her in danger of being discovered by humans who fear and hunt werewolves.

As tensions rise, Yūko must confront the reality of her children's condition and find a way to keep them safe while also teaching them how to control their powers. Along the way, she learns valuable lessons about motherhood, love, and acceptance.

The film's climax features an intense confrontation between Hana and a group of hunters who seek to capture and kill werewolves. With her newfound powers, Hana is able to defend herself and those she cares about, ultimately emerging victorious.

In the end, Yūko comes to terms with her children's condition and finds a way to live with it. The film concludes on a hopeful note, with Hana embracing her identity as a werewolf and finding a sense of belonging among others who accept her for what she is.

Overall, Wolf Children is a heartwarming and action-packed tale that explores themes of family, love, and acceptance in the face of adversity.

overview: Everyone knows that the stork delivers babies, but where do the storks get the babies from? The answer lies up in the stratosphere, where cloud people sculpt babies from clouds and bring them to life. Gus, a lonely and insecure grey cloud, is a master at creating "dangerous" babies. Crocodiles, porcupines, rams and more - Gus's beloved creations are works of art, but more than a handful for his loyal delivery stork partner, Peck. As Gus's creations become more and more rambunctious, Peck's job gets harder and harder. How will Peck manage to handle both his hazardous cargo and his friend's fiery temperament?
tagline: Charming and cute and clever
title: Partly Cloudy
plot:
Partly Cloudy is an animated film that tells the story of Polliwaugh, a young girl who lives on a small island in the middle of a stormy sea. The movie explores the theme of responsibility and growth as Polliwaugh learns to care for her younger sister, Polliwog, after their mother's departure.

The film also delves into the idea of letting go and embracing change. As Polliwaugh navigates her new role as a caregiver, she must confront the challenges of caring for another human being, which forces her to grow and mature beyond her years.

Furthermore, Partly Cloudy touches on the theme of isolation and loneliness. The island where Polliwaugh lives is surrounded by stormy weather, symbolizing the emotional turmoil that Polliwog experiences as a result of their mother's absence. Through Polliwaugh's journey, the film highlights the importance of human connection and community in overcoming feelings of loneliness.

The movie also explores the idea of identity and self-discovery. As Polliwaugh takes on new responsibilities, she begins to explore her own interests and passions, which helps her develop a sense of purpose and belonging.

Overall, Partly Cloudy is a heartwarming film that explores themes of growth, responsibility, letting go, isolation, loneliness, and identity, all set against the backdrop of a whimsical and imaginative world.

original_title: Jack et la mécanique du cœur
overview: In Scotland 1874, Jack is born on the coldest day ever. Because of the extreme cold, his heart stops beating. The responsible midwife in Edinburgh finds a way to save him by replacing his heart with a clock. So he lives and remains under the midwife's protective care. But he must not get angry or excited because that endangers his life by causing his clock to stop working. Worse than that, when he grows up, he has to face the fact he cannot fall in love because that too could stop his delicate heart.
title: Jack and the Cuckoo-Clock Heart
plot:
Jack and the Cuckoo-Clock Heart is a 2013 French-Belgian dark fantasy film directed by Mary Lambert, not in 2014. However, I can provide information on the movie.

The main themes of Jack and the Cuckoo-Clock Heart include:

1. **Coming of Age**: The story revolves around Jack's journey from childhood to adulthood, as he navigates the complexities of growing up and facing his fears.
2. **Identity**: Jack struggles with his identity, feeling like an outsider among his peers and trying to find his place in the world.
3. **Family Dynamics**: The film explores the complex relationships within Jack's family, particularly his relationship with his father, who is a clockmaker.
4. **Mental Health**: Jack's experiences with anxiety and depression are portrayed as a significant aspect of his character development.
5. **Fantasy and Reality**: The movie blends fantasy elements with realistic portrayals of childhood struggles, making it a thought-provoking exploration of the human experience.

The film received critical acclaim for its unique storytelling, atmospheric visuals, and nuanced performances.

original_title: The Death and Life of Bobby Z
overview: A DEA agent provides former Marine Tim Kearney with a way out of his prison sentence: impersonate Bobby Z, a recently deceased drug dealer, in a hostage switch with a crime lord. When the negotiations go awry, Kearney flees, with Z's son in tow.
tagline: To live a life of his own, he has to die first.
title: The Death and Life of Bobby Z
plot:
The Death and Life of Bobby Z is a crime drama film that delves into the complexities of loyalty, identity, and redemption. The movie follows Bobby Z, a former hitman who tries to leave his past life behind but finds himself drawn back in for one final job.

At its core, the film explores the theme of identity and how it's shaped by our experiences and choices. Bobby Z is a character torn between two personas: the person he was before his life of crime and the person he wants to become after trying to leave that life behind. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for his journey, as he struggles to reconcile his past and present selves.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty, particularly in the context of Bobby Z's relationships with those around him. His connections to his family, friends, and associates are put to the test as he navigates the moral gray areas of his profession. The film raises questions about the nature of loyalty and whether it can be genuine or if it's always tainted by self-interest.

Furthermore, The Death and Life of Bobby Z explores the theme of redemption, albeit in a nuanced and complex manner. Bobby Z's desire to leave his past life behind is rooted in a desire for redemption, but the film suggests that this may not be as straightforward as he hopes. Through Bobby Z's character, the movie raises questions about whether it's possible to truly change one's ways or if our past actions will always define us.

Overall, The Death and Life of Bobby Z is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature through its protagonist's journey.

overview: A family imprisoned by intruders is forced to play a terrifying game of "Kill, Or Be Killed". As the night unfolds, the game's mysterious rules become clear, and the family realizes their nightmare is being streamed live to riveted viewers all over the world, who are compelled to KEEP WATCHING... not knowing if what they're seeing is real, or staged.
tagline: Kill or Be Killed
title: Keep Watching
plot:
Keep Watching is a 2017 American found-footage psychological horror film directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett. The movie revolves around a family who receives a mysterious VHS tape that appears to show their daughter, but as the night progresses, it becomes clear that something sinister is at play.

The main theme of Keep Watching is the blurring of reality and illusion, as the family's perception of what is happening is constantly challenged. As the film progresses, it becomes increasingly difficult for the viewer to distinguish between what is real and what is just a product of the family's paranoia and fear.

Another dominant theme in the movie is the idea of surveillance and control. The VHS tape seems to be watching the family, manipulating their actions and emotions, and exerting a sense of control over them. This theme is particularly evident in the way the film uses long takes and point-of-view shots to create a sense of being watched.

The movie also explores the theme of motherhood and the lengths to which parents will go to protect their children. The mother's desperation to keep her daughter safe becomes an all-consuming force, driving her to make choices that are both desperate and terrifying.

Overall, Keep Watching is a tense and unsettling film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the ways in which technology can be used to manipulate and control us.

overview: A young drug dealer falls in love while facing disruption among the men in his gang, and being offered a career as a Reggaetón singer.
tagline: You can take the man out of the street... but you can't take the street out of the man.
title: Straight from the Barrio
plot:
Straight from the Barrio (Spanish: Talento de barrio) is a 2008 Puerto Rican crime drama directed by José Iván Santiago from a screenplay by George Rivera and Ángel M. Sanjurjo, and the first feature co-produced by the reggaeton star Daddy Yankee, who makes his screen acting debut in the lead. He plays Edgar "Dinero," a small-time gangster, with Katiria Soto as Soribel, Ángel "Maestro" Rodríguez as Jeico, César Farrait as Wichy, Angélica Alcaide as Natasha, Norma Colón as Edgar's mother and Eddie Dee as Jay. The story is loosely inspired by its star's own life.

Edgar, aptly nicknamed for his devotion to money, runs a drug operation in a housing project in Puerto Rico. His mother disapproves of his trade and refuses to leave the project for the comfortable middle-class house he has bought. Edgar has no musical ambitions of his own, but a record producer pushes him onto the stage of a seedy nightclub and secretly records his rapping, hoping to persuade him to change careers. At the same time he falls for Soribel, a well-off young woman from uptown, and must hide the depth of his feelings and the nature of his life from her.

Meanwhile, his crew begins to unravel. A vicious ex-convict, Jeico, destabilizes the gang from within and gets Edgar's younger sister hooked on drugs without Edgar noticing, while beatings and rivalries escalate into open conflict. A first recording session in New York goes badly because Edgar seems to lack energy, but when Soribel turns up there, his music becomes stronger and more passionate. As he tries to leave the street for the studio, violence follows him in both Puerto Rico and New York, and the film ends on an ambiguous note about whether he survives an attack.

Shot largely in the Barriada Morales community of Caguas, as well as in San Juan and New York, the film was released on 10 October 2008 by Maya Entertainment in a limited run in major U.S. cities, and in Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic, followed by DVD and Blu-ray in November. It made more than $1 million in Puerto Rico and was received well there, but American critics were harsh: reviewers found the script generic, the storytelling clumsy and the film derivative of 8 Mile and Carlito's Way, though some felt Daddy Yankee held his own on screen.

overview: Distraught, confused, and half-wild with fear, Sarah Carter emerges alone from the Appalachian cave system where she encountered unspeakable terrors. Unable to plausibly explain to the authorities what happened - or why she's covered in her friends' blood - Sarah is forced back to the subterranean depths to help locate her five missing companions.
tagline: Fear runs deeper
title: The Descent: Part 2
plot:
The Descent Part 2 is a 2009 British horror film directed by Jon Harris and a sequel to Neil Marshall's 2005 film The Descent. Written by James McCarthy, J Blakeson and James Watkins and produced by Christian Colson and Ivana MacKinnon, with Marshall as executive producer, it stars Shauna Macdonald, returning as Sarah, and Natalie Mendoza as Juno. Harris had served as the editor of the first film.

The film begins two days after the events of the original, in which six women ventured into an uncharted cave system and were attacked by blind, humanoid predators known as crawlers. Sarah emerges from the caves covered in blood and suffering from amnesia. When doctors discover that some of the blood belongs to one of her missing friends, Sheriff Vaines suspects that she may be responsible for the women's disappearance. He forces the traumatized Sarah to accompany him, his deputy Rios and a team of experienced cave rescuers back underground through an abandoned mine shaft to search for the others.

As the team descends, they find the body of one of the missing women and Sarah begins to recover fragments of her memory. A cave-in separates the group, and soon the crawlers begin hunting them in the dark tunnels. The rescuers discover a damaged video camera that reveals what happened to the women, and Sarah, now fully remembering, must use what she has learned about the creatures, which hunt by sound, to keep the survivors alive. Deep in the caves, the group discovers that Juno, whom Sarah left for dead after a bitter betrayal, is still alive, and the two women are forced into an uneasy alliance as they search for a way out of the crawlers' lair.

The sequel follows the American ending of the first film, in which Sarah escapes the caves, and expands the claustrophobic setting with more extensive gore and action.

The Descent Part 2 was released in British cinemas on 2 December 2009 and went directly to DVD in the United States on 27 April 2010. Reviews were mixed, with 48 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it lacked the unnerving power of its predecessor but offered enough nasty set pieces for gore fans.

overview: Thirteen year old Sam Cleary  suspects that his mysteriously reclusive neighbor Mr. Smith is actually the legendary vigilante Samaritan, who was reported dead 20 years ago. With crime on the rise and the city on the brink of chaos, Sam makes it his mission to coax his neighbor out of hiding to save the city from ruin.
tagline: 25 years ago the world's greatest hero vanished.
title: Samaritan
plot:
Samaritan is a 2022 American superhero film directed by Julius Avery and written by Bragi F. Schut, whose story was also adapted into a series of graphic novels. Produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pictures and Balboa Productions, it stars Sylvester Stallone as Joe Smith, Javon "Wanna" Walton as Sam Cleary, Pilou Asbæk as Cyrus, Dascha Polanco as Sam's mother Tiffany and Moisés Arias as Reza. The film offers a gritty, darker take on the superhero genre.

Decades earlier, Granite City was home to two superpowered twin brothers. After an angry mob burned their family's home, killing their parents, one brother became the heroic Samaritan, while the other became the villain Nemesis. To gain an advantage over his equally powerful sibling, Nemesis forged a sledgehammer capable of harming him. During a final battle at a power plant, both were believed to have been killed when the plant exploded, plunging the city into darkness.

Twenty-five years later, Granite City is impoverished and crime-ridden. Thirteen-year-old Sam Cleary, who is struggling to help his mother pay the rent, gets drawn into the world of a local gang and becomes obsessed with the theory that Samaritan is still alive. When a garbage collector named Joe Smith, a reclusive elderly man living across the street, fends off a group of gang members with apparently superhuman strength, Sam becomes convinced that he has found his hero. Joe denies everything, but after he heals from serious injuries in front of Sam's eyes, the two develop a friendship. Meanwhile, the ambitious criminal Cyrus recovers Nemesis's hammer and takes on his mantle, plotting to plunge the city into chaos, forcing Joe to confront the past he has tried to bury.

The film explores the legacy of heroes and villains and the moral gray areas between them, culminating in a twist that reframes the story of the two brothers.

Samaritan was released on August 26, 2022, by United Artists Releasing and Amazon Studios on the Prime Video streaming service. It received mixed reviews, with 38 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it creatively underpowered, and a Metacritic score of 45.

overview: Sherwood forest has a courageous new hero - Gwyn, the daughter of Robin Hood. Possessing the cunning skills of her legendary father and the beauty and intelligence of her mother Maid Marian, Gwyn is anxious to follow in her father's footsteps. King Richard nears death and Robin Hood and his Merry Men are summoned to help bring Richard's son Philip to his rightful place on the throne before the evil Prince John can assume power. Robin Hood's life and that of the future King of England soon lies in Gwyn's hands when Robin is captured and sentenced to death.
tagline: If you thought Robin Hood broke all the rules, wait until you meet his daughter!
title: Princess of Thieves
plot:
Princess of Thieves is a 2001 romantic adventure television film directed by Peter Hewitt and starring Keira Knightley as Gwyn, the daughter of Robin Hood and Maid Marian. Produced by Granada Entertainment USA and filmed in Romania, it co-stars Stuart Wilson as Robin Hood, Stephen Moyer as Prince Philip, Jonathan Hyde as Prince John, Malcolm McDowell as the Sheriff of Nottingham and Del Synnott as Froderick. The story imagines a new chapter in the Robin Hood legend, centered on the outlaw's spirited daughter.

Years after the famous adventures of Robin Hood, Maid Marian has died and Robin spends most of his time away fighting in the Crusades alongside King Richard the Lionheart. His daughter Gwyn has grown up largely without him, becoming an independent and strong-willed young woman with a remarkable talent for archery. Her only close companion is Froderick, a gentle young man studying for the church, who is quietly in love with her. When King Richard dies, Robin returns to England to ensure that the rightful heir takes the throne, but he is captured by his old enemies, the Sheriff of Nottingham and the scheming Prince John, who intends to seize the crown for himself.

Gwyn takes up her father's mission. She must find and protect Prince Philip, King Richard's illegitimate son, who has returned from exile in France to claim the throne but is traveling incognito under the name of his servant, who died protecting him. Gwyn crosses paths with the young man without knowing his true identity, and a romance begins to grow between them. Together they seek out the Merry Men and lead a daring attempt to rescue Robin from imprisonment in the Tower of London and stop Prince John's coronation before England falls into tyranny.

The film presents a family-friendly adventure with a heroine who proves herself the equal of her legendary father, and it was one of Knightley's first leading roles, made shortly before her international breakthrough.

Princess of Thieves premiered on ABC's The Wonderful World of Disney in 2001. Reviews were mixed: Scott Weinberg of eFilmCritic called it an entertaining little movie that bucks the odds, while BeyondHollywood found it aimed squarely at young girls and likely to bore other viewers.

overview: A former thief who is trying to go straight seeks vengeance on those who framed him.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG II
tagline: What Seagal does in Vegas, nearly destroys it.
title: Today You Die
plot:
Today You Die is a 2005 American action film directed and photographed by Don E. FauntLeRoy. Steven Seagal stars as Harlan Banks and also served as a producer alongside Randall Emmett, George Furla and Danny Lerner. The cast includes Anthony "Treach" Criss, Sarah Buxton, Mari Morrow, Nick Mancuso, Robert Miano and Kevin Tighe, with a brief early appearance by Chloë Grace Moretz. The film was released direct to DVD in the United States on 13 September 2005.

Harlan Banks is a professional thief with a personal code: he chooses his own jobs and prefers heists that leave him room to help people in need, in the manner of a modern Robin Hood. As the jobs grow riskier, his girlfriend Jada, worried about where his life is heading, urges him to quit. Banks agrees to pull one last job, joining a crew planning a $20 million robbery, but the heist goes wrong.
