He moves to Las Vegas with Jada, who wants him to go straight, and on the way into town they pass a children's hospital that is about to close for lack of funds.

In Las Vegas, Banks takes a job driving an armored car for a man named Max. The work turns out to be far from legitimate: during a run, his partner Bruno shoots a security guard, and Banks finds himself at the wheel of an armored van in a wild police chase down the Las Vegas Strip. He is caught, convicted and sent to prison, where he becomes friends with a fellow inmate known as Ice Cool. With Ice's help, Banks breaks out, determined to track down Max and the stolen money and to clear his name. His hunt brings him into contact with a federal agent pursuing the same case, and leads him into a violent confrontation with Max's organization and the corrupt figures behind the robbery, while the money offers him a last chance to do some good.

Like many of Seagal's films of the mid-2000s, Today You Die was produced on a modest budget for the home video market by the team of Emmett, Furla and Lerner, who made several of his direct-to-DVD action pictures. It received little critical attention on its release, and the few reviews it drew were mostly negative about its familiar plot.

overview: As Halloweentown prepares to celebrate its 1,000th anniversary, Marnie Piper and her brother Dylan return to Witch University, where trouble is in session from the Sinister Sisters and from someone who's plotting to use Marnie's powers for evil.
tagline: Unlock The Ultimate Secret This October!
title: Return to Halloweentown
plot:
Return to Halloweentown is a 2006 Disney Channel Original Movie that explores the complexities of family relationships, identity, and self-discovery. The story revolves around Marnie Piper, a teenager who returns to her magical heritage in Halloweentown, where she must navigate her dual identities as a mortal and a witch.

At its core, Return to Halloweentown is a film about embracing one's true nature and finding acceptance within oneself and others. Marnie's journey is marked by self-discovery, as she grapples with the expectations of her family, particularly her mother Gwen, who struggles to balance her own desires with the responsibilities of being a witch.

The movie also delves into themes of belonging and identity, as Marnie navigates her relationships with her family members, including her grandmother Aggie, who serves as a guiding figure in her life. The film's portrayal of Halloweentown as a vibrant, magical community highlights the importance of finding one's place within a supportive environment.

Furthermore, Return to Halloweentown touches on the theme of letting go and embracing change. Marnie must confront the challenges of growing up and moving away from her childhood, while also learning to appreciate the wisdom and experience that comes with age.

Overall, Return to Halloweentown is a heartwarming story about self-discovery, family, and finding one's place in the world.

overview: What happens when the undead return to life? In a world ravaged for years by a virus that turns the infected into zombie-like cannibals, a cure is at last found and the wrenching process of reintegrating the survivors back into society begins.
tagline: The cure is just the beginning
title: The Cured
plot:
The Cured is a 2017 Irish zombie musical horror film directed by David Freyne. The movie tells the story of a small town in Ireland that has been quarantined after a mysterious outbreak, where the infected are not the mindless undead, but rather people who have become violent and aggressive due to a mysterious illness.

The main theme of The Cured revolves around the struggle for humanity and empathy in a world that seems to have lost its way. As the story unfolds, we see how the characters grapple with their own emotions and relationships, often finding themselves torn between their desire to help others and their need to protect themselves from those who are infected.

The film also explores the idea of isolation and confinement, highlighting the psychological effects it has on individuals and communities. The quarantine serves as a metaphor for the ways in which society can become fragmented and divided, leading to a breakdown in human connection and understanding.

Furthermore, The Cured touches on themes of grief, loss, and redemption, as characters navigate their personal struggles and confront the consequences of their actions. Through its unique blend of horror and music, the film creates a sense of unease and tension, mirroring the emotional turmoil experienced by its characters.

Ultimately, The Cured presents a thought-provoking commentary on the human condition, encouraging viewers to reflect on the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding in a world that often seems to be torn apart by conflict and division.

overview: A group of friends on vacation in a seeming island paradise are stalked by an unrelenting great white after an accident leaves them stranded and left for dead.
tagline: 200 teeth. 0 chance.
title: Maneater
plot:
Maneater is a 2022 American horror thriller directed by Justin Lee and starring Nicky Whelan as Jessie, Shane West as Will, Trace Adkins as Harlan, Branscombe Richmond as Sheriff Kua and Jeff Fahey as Professor Hoffman, with Porscha Coleman, Zoe Cipres, Kelly Lynn Reiter, Alex Farnham and Ed Morrone. It belongs to the long tradition of killer-shark films, pitting a group of vacationers and a grieving father against a great white shark terrorizing a tropical island.

A huge great white shark has been attacking people in the waters around a group of islands. Among its victims is Jennifer, the adult daughter of Harlan, a widower, who is killed while surfing alone. Harlan is left with almost nothing of her to bury and becomes consumed by the desire for revenge. Soon afterward, the shark strikes again, snatching a young man in mid-air as he jumps from a popular cliff into a lagoon.

Meanwhile, Jessie joins her friends on a boat trip to the islands, guided by Captain Wally and his wife Beth. While the group spends the night camping on a small island, the shark kills Wally and Beth on their boat. The next morning Ty, who had cut his hand and been warned to stay out of the water, goes for a swim with Emma, and both are killed. When Will tries to row back to the boat to find out what has happened, the shark overturns his dinghy, and the attempt to save him costs more lives. Stranded and dwindling in number, the survivors call for help on the radio, and their plea reaches Harlan, who comes to find them. Jessie and Harlan must then face the shark, which has become trapped in a shallow bay at low tide.

The film draws on the conventions of Jaws and its many imitators, combining scenic island locations with a revenge story centered on Adkins's grieving father.

Maneater was released in August 2022. Critics were largely negative: Starburst gave it two stars out of five and called it one for shark completists only, IGN rated it 3 out of 10, and Common Sense Media described it as abysmally bad.

overview: Through a series of unfortunate events, three mummies end up in present-day London and embark on a wacky and hilarious journey in search of an old ring belonging to the Royal Family, that was stolen by the ambitious archaeologist Lord Carnaby.
tagline: Discover a new world
title: Mummies
plot:
Mummies (Spanish: Momias) is a 2023 English-language Spanish computer-animated comedy directed by Juan Jesús García Galocha in his feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Javier López Barreira and Jordi Gasull and a story by Gasull. It features the voices of Joe Thomas as Thut, Eleanor Tomlinson as Princess Nefer, Santiago Winder as Sekhem, Hugh Bonneville as Lord Sylvester Carnaby, Celia Imrie as his mother and Sean Bean as the Pharaoh, with Karina Pasian providing Nefer's singing voice.

Deep beneath the earth lies a hidden world where the mummies of ancient Egypt continue to live as they did thousands of years ago. Thut is a former chariot racer still haunted by the crash that ended his career, and Princess Nefer, the Pharaoh's daughter, is a free spirit who loves to sing and longs for a life beyond palace tradition. Thut's mischievous younger brother Sekhem is skilled with a boomerang.

Their underground world is disrupted when Lord Carnaby, an ambitious and unscrupulous British archaeologist, raids a tomb on the surface and steals an ancient ring belonging to the royal family. To recover it, Thut, Nefer and Sekhem must travel to the world of the living and end up in present-day London. There, the three mummies struggle to make sense of modern life, from traffic and technology to fame and social media, in a series of comic situations driven by the culture clash. Their task becomes even more urgent when Nefer's irrepressible singing goes viral, prompting Carnaby, aided by his bickering henchmen Danny and Dennys, to try to capture the princess and display her in an exhibition.

The film mixes slapstick, musical numbers and a romantic subplot, contrasting the rigid traditions of the mummies' world with the chaos of contemporary London.

Mummies was originally scheduled for release in 2021 under the title Moomios, as part of a partnership between Atresmedia Cine and Warner Bros. España, but was delayed by two years of extended production. It opened internationally beginning in Australia on January 5, 2023, and was released in Spain and in selected U.S. theaters by Warner Bros. Pictures on February 24, 2023. It received mixed reviews, with 53 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: The Empire of Izmer is a divided land: elite magicians called “mages” rule while lowly commoners are powerless. When Empress Savina vows to bring equality and prosperity to her land, the evil mage Profion plots to depose her.
tagline: This is no game
title: Dungeons & Dragons
plot:
Dungeons & Dragons (2000) is a fantasy adventure film that explores the complexities of male friendship and the struggle for identity. The movie delves into the world of Dungeons & Dragons, where four outcast teenagers find solace in their imaginary game, only to have it become all too real when they are transported into the fantasy realm.

At its core, the film is a coming-of-age story that examines the challenges of growing up and finding one's place in the world. The main characters, played by Jeremy Irons, Justin Whalin, Thomas Haden Church, and Ted Raimi, must navigate the complexities of adolescence, including peer pressure, self-doubt, and the quest for acceptance.

The movie also touches on themes of mental health, specifically depression and anxiety, as the characters struggle to cope with their own personal demons. The film's portrayal of these issues is nuanced and sensitive, avoiding simplistic solutions in favor of a more realistic exploration of the complexities of the human experience.

Furthermore, Dungeons & Dragons (2000) explores the idea of escapism and the power of imagination as a means of coping with the challenges of reality. The movie suggests that sometimes, it's necessary to temporarily leave behind the difficulties of everyday life and immerse oneself in a fantasy world in order to find solace and inspiration.

Overall, Dungeons & Dragons (2000) is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, friendship, mental health, and the power of imagination.

overview: When New Orleans Police Detective Danny Fisher stops a brilliant thief from getting away with a multimillion-dollar heist, the thief's girlfriend is accidentally killed. After escaping from prison, the criminal mastermind enacts his revenge, taunting Danny with 12 rounds of near-impossible puzzles and tasks that he must somehow complete to save the life of the woman he loves.
tagline: Can you survive 12 rounds for the one you love?
title: 12 Rounds
plot:
12 Rounds is a 2009 American action thriller directed by Renny Harlin and produced by WWE Studios. Professional wrestler John Cena stars as New Orleans police officer Danny Fisher, with Aidan Gillen as the villain Miles Jackson, Ashley Scott, Steve Harris, Gonzalo Menendez, Brian J. White and Taylor Cole. The film follows a detective forced to complete a series of twelve deadly challenges in exchange for his kidnapped girlfriend's life. It was released in theaters in the United States by 20th Century Fox on 27 March 2009.

Miles Jackson, an international arms dealer and terrorist, is hiding in New Orleans while being pursued by the FBI, led by agents George Aiken and Ray Santiago. Patrol officer Danny Fisher and his partner Hank Carver become caught up in the operation, and Fisher manages to track down Jackson and his girlfriend and accomplice, Erica. During the arrest, Erica is accidentally killed, and Jackson swears revenge.

A year later, Fisher has been promoted to detective. Jackson, having escaped from prison, calls him on his cellphone and reveals that he has kidnapped Fisher's girlfriend, Molly Porter, to avenge Erica's death. To save her, Fisher must complete twelve "rounds" of challenges across the city within strict time limits. The game begins with the destruction of Fisher's house and continues with increasingly dangerous tasks, including a runaway streetcar, a free-falling elevator and a bomb strapped to Molly's body. Working with Carver and with the FBI agents, who distrust him at first, Fisher races through New Orleans solving Jackson's clues, while gradually realizing that the elaborate game may be a cover for a much larger plan involving a massive theft.

The film received generally negative reviews, with critics finding its plot implausible and derivative of Die Hard with a Vengeance, while acknowledging the scale of its action set pieces filmed on location in New Orleans. It grossed about $17 million worldwide and later performed better on home video, leading WWE Studios to produce several direct-to-video sequels starring other wrestlers, beginning with 12 Rounds 2: Reloaded in 2013.

overview: Arthur Bishop is a 'mechanic' - an elite assassin with a strict code and unique talent for cleanly eliminating targets. It's a job that requires professional perfection and total detachment, and Bishop is the best in the business. But when he is ordered to take out his mentor and close friend Harry, Bishop is anything but detached.
tagline: Someone has to fix the problems.
title: The Mechanic
plot:
The Mechanic is a 2011 action thriller film directed by Dennis Gansel and starring Jason Statham and Ben Foster.

The movie begins with Arthur Bishop (Jason Statham), a skilled hitman who has retired from his profession. He lives a quiet life in the countryside, where he spends his days fixing cars and taking care of his garden. However, his peaceful existence is disrupted when he receives a visit from his old mentor, Jack (Tony Goldwyn), who informs him that his protégé, Steve Ford (Ben Foster), has been murdered.

Arthur is shocked by this news and feels responsible for Steve's death, as he had trained him in the art of killing. He decides to track down the man responsible for Steve's murder, who is revealed to be a ruthless hitman known as Mr. Jenkins (Dolph Lundgren).

As Arthur delves deeper into the world of high-stakes assassinations, he meets his new apprentice, Steve's brother, Ryan Ford (John Leguizamo). Arthur agrees to train Ryan in the ways of killing, but their relationship is complicated by Arthur's troubled past and his reluctance to pass on his skills.

Throughout the film, Arthur and Ryan engage in a series of intense battles with Mr. Jenkins and his team, who are determined to eliminate them. Along the way, Arthur also confronts his own demons and grapples with the moral implications of his profession.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Arthur's past is shrouded in mystery, and he has many secrets that he keeps hidden from Ryan. The film builds towards a thrilling climax as Arthur and Ryan face off against Mr. Jenkins in a final showdown.

Ultimately, Arthur emerges victorious, but not without scars. He finally finds some measure of redemption by passing on his skills to Ryan, who is determined to follow in his footsteps. The movie ends with Arthur riding away into the sunset, leaving behind his troubled past and embracing a new sense of purpose.

Overall, The Mechanic is a gripping action thriller that explores the darker side of human nature. Jason Statham delivers a standout performance as the complex and troubled Arthur Bishop, while Ben Foster brings a likable everyman quality to Ryan Ford.

overview: James Bond is sent to investigate the connection between a North Korean terrorist and a diamond mogul, who is funding the development of an international space weapon.
tagline: He's never been cooler.
title: Die Another Day
plot:
Die Another Day is a 2002 spy action film directed by Lee Tamahoni and produced by Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli, under the Eon Productions banner.

The movie begins with James Bond (played by Pierce Brosnan), who has been presumed dead after his last mission in Russia. However, he is actually being held captive by North Korean agents, led by the enigmatic and beautiful Gi (played by Kim Hye-ok). Gi is revealed to be a former lover of Bond's, who had faked her own death to escape from him.

Bond is eventually rescued by a British agent named Jinx Johnson (played by Halle Berry), who has been sent to extract him. However, their mission is compromised when they are ambushed by North Korean agents, and Bond is left for dead.

Meanwhile, in London, M (played by Judi Dench) informs Bond that he has been declared dead and that his replacement, a new 00 agent named Johnny English (played by Colin Farrell), will be taking over his duties. However, Bond soon discovers that this is not the case, as he receives a message from M, revealing that she has been kidnapped by North Korea.

Bond sets out on a mission to rescue M and uncover the truth behind Gi's betrayal. Along the way, he encounters a new villain, Zao (played by Rick Yune), who is revealed to be a skilled martial artist and assassin. Bond also meets a wealthy businessman named Gustav Graves (played by Toby Stephens), who is revealed to be working with North Korea.

As Bond delves deeper into the plot, he discovers that Gi has been working for Gustav, who plans to use a satellite-based laser system to hold the world hostage. The plan involves using the laser to destroy major cities around the world, and only Bond can stop it.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Bond and Zao, as well as a thrilling chase sequence through the streets of Seoul. In the end, Bond is able to defeat Gustav and Gi, and rescue M. The movie concludes with Bond reflecting on his past and his feelings for Gi, who has been revealed to be working against her own country.

Overall, Die Another Day was met with mixed reviews from critics, but it remains a popular entry in the James Bond franchise. The film's action sequences and visual effects were praised, while some critics felt that the plot was convoluted and the villainous characters underdeveloped.

overview: The untold story of Katherine G. Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson – brilliant African-American women working at NASA and serving as the brains behind one of the greatest operations in history – the launch of astronaut John Glenn into orbit. The visionary trio crossed all gender and race lines to inspire generations to dream big.
tagline: Meet the women you don't know, behind the mission you do.
title: Hidden Figures
plot:
Hidden Figures is a biographical drama film directed by Theodore Melfi, released in 2016 by Fox 2000 Pictures. The movie tells the story of three African-American women who worked as mathematicians and engineers at NASA during the early years of the space program.

The film begins with Katherine Johnson (played by Taraji P. Henson), a young girl from West Virginia who dreams of becoming an astronaut. Despite facing racism and sexism, she earns a scholarship to study mathematics at West Virginia State College. She later transfers to Howard University, where she meets her future colleagues, Dorothy Vaughan (Octavia Spencer) and Mary Jackson (Janelle Monáe).

The story takes off when Katherine is recruited by NASA's Langley Research Center in 1957. She works under the supervision of supervisor Al Harrison (Kevin Costner), who recognizes her exceptional mathematical skills. However, she faces racism and sexism from her colleagues, including the infamous "computer" segregation policy that restricts African-American employees to menial tasks.

As Katherine navigates this challenging environment, she also meets her future husband, Edgar (played by Winston Duke). The film showcases her remarkable work ethic, intelligence, and determination as she becomes an integral part of NASA's team. She works tirelessly to calculate trajectories for the Mercury Seven astronauts, including Alan Shepard and John Glenn.

Meanwhile, Dorothy Vaughan faces similar challenges as a supervisor at NASA. Despite being passed over for promotions, she perseveres and eventually earns the respect of her colleagues. Her story is intertwined with Katherine's, highlighting the struggles faced by women in STEM fields during that era.

Mary Jackson, an aspiring engineer, also faces obstacles due to her sex and skin color. She works as a "human computer" but dreams of becoming an actual engineer. With the help of her colleague, Katherine, she eventually earns the respect of her superiors and becomes the first African-American female engineer at NASA.

The film's climax revolves around the historic launch of John Glenn into space in 1962. Katherine's calculations are crucial to the success of this mission, which marks a significant milestone for the United States' space program.

Throughout the movie, the characters face numerous challenges, including racism, sexism, and personal struggles. However, they persevere, driven by their passion for mathematics, science, and engineering. The film ultimately celebrates the triumphs of these unsung heroes who paved the way for future generations of women in STEM fields.

The ending is a heartwarming tribute to the lives and achievements of Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan, and Mary Jackson. The movie concludes with a sense of hope and determination, as the characters look towards a brighter future for themselves and their communities.

Overall, Hidden Figures is an inspiring film that sheds light on the often-overlooked contributions of African-American women in NASA's early years. It is a testament to the power of perseverance, intelligence, and determination in the face of adversity.

overview: Henri “Papillon” Charrière, a safecracker from the Parisian underworld, is wrongfully convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment in the penal colony of French Guiana, where he forges a strong friendship with Louis Dega, a counterfeiter who needs his protection.
tagline: The greatest escape adventure ever told
title: Papillon
plot:
Papillon is a 2017 biographical prison drama directed by Michael Noer and written by Aaron Guzikowski. It tells the story of the French convict Henri Charrière, nicknamed Papillon ("butterfly") for the tattoo on his chest, who was wrongly convicted of murder in 1933 and sent to the penal colony of French Guiana, from which he eventually escaped with the help of the counterfeiter Louis Dega. Charlie Hunnam stars as Papillon and Rami Malek as Dega, with Eve Hewson, Roland Møller, Christopher Fairbank and Michael Socha in supporting roles. The screenplay is based on Charrière's memoirs Papillon and Banco and on the 1973 film adaptation starring Steve McQueen and Dustin Hoffman.

Papillon, a safecracker in the Paris underworld of the early 1930s, is framed for the murder of a pimp. Although his girlfriend Nenette can vouch for his innocence, he is convicted and sentenced to life in the penal colony of French Guiana, a brutal system of prisons from which escape is considered impossible. On the ship to South America he meets Louis Dega, a timid, wealthy counterfeiter from Marseille who is rumored to be hiding money on his person. After witnessing a prisoner murdered for the cash he had hidden, Papillon offers to protect Dega in return for financing an escape, and the two form an uneasy partnership that slowly turns into a deep friendship.

In the colony Papillon makes his first escape attempt after striking a guard to defend Dega, but he is captured and sentenced to a long term of solitary confinement in a dark cell, where he is starved and nearly loses his mind, yet refuses to betray his friend. After surviving further years of hardship and failed attempts, Papillon is finally sent to Devil's Island, a remote rocky outcrop surrounded by treacherous waters, where Dega also lives. Now older and worn down, Papillon studies the tides in search of a way to escape the island once and for all, while Dega must decide whether to join him.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017 and was released in the United States by Bleecker Street in August 2018. It received mixed reviews; critics praised the performances of Hunnam and Malek and the film's physical intensity but felt it added little to the celebrated 1973 version.

overview: Before he built a drug empire, Ferry Bouman returns to his hometown on a revenge mission that finds his loyalty tested — and a love that alters his life.
title: Ferry
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie called "Ferry" released in 2021 by De Mensen. The title and release date don't seem to match any well-known or widely released film.

However, I did find that there is a 2017 Dutch drama film called "Ferry" directed by Boudewijn de Groot, based on the novel of the same name by Herman Koch. If this is not the movie you are looking for, please provide more information or clarify which one you are interested in.

If it's the 2021 version by De Mensen, I couldn't find any details about the plot, characters, or themes.

overview: Thousands of activists arrive in Seattle, Washington in masses to protest the WTO Ministerial Conference of 1999 (World Trade Organization). Although it began as a peaceful protest with a goal of stopping the WTO talks, it escalated into a full-scale riot and eventually, a State of Emergency that pitted protesters against the Seattle Police Department and the National Guard.
tagline: Six lives, six battles, one city.
title: Battle in Seattle
plot:
Battle in Seattle is a political drama written and directed by the actor Stuart Townsend in his feature debut, a fictional ensemble story set against the real protests at the 1999 World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference. The cast includes Martin Henderson as the activist leader Jay, Michelle Rodriguez as Lou, André Benjamin as Django, Jennifer Carpenter as Sam, Woody Harrelson as the police officer Dale, Charlize Theron as his pregnant wife Ella, Connie Nielsen as the TV reporter Jean, Ray Liotta as Mayor Jim Tobin, Channing Tatum as a hard-line officer and Rade Šerbedžija as a delegate. Townsend drew on documentaries and films such as Medium Cool and mixed staged scenes with archival footage.

A prologue explains the WTO and why its critics accuse it of widening the gap between rich and poor nations. The activists are introduced dangling from a construction crane as they hang an anti-WTO banner. Jay, who has an extensive arrest record and a brother who died in an earlier protest, has spent months with Django planning a disruptive but strictly nonviolent action to shut the conference down. Lou is a guarded animal-rights activist drawn to Jay, Sam a law student wary of arrest, and Django a cheerful pacifist. Mayor Tobin, a former antiwar protester himself, wants to allow free speech while keeping anyone from getting hurt, but his police chief is skeptical. Inside the talks, a delegate campaigns for cheaper medicines for poor countries.

When the protesters refuse to clear the streets, police respond with tear gas and pepper spray, window-smashing anarchists seize the headlines, and pressure from the governor and the White House overrides the mayor, leading to curfews, a state of emergency and the National Guard. Jean, sent to cover the riot, becomes sympathetic to the demonstrators. Ella, a department-store clerk, is caught in the crowd and struck by a police baton, losing her baby. Denied leave, Dale turns his grief into rage and beats Jay in a church, later seeking him out to apologize. Hundreds are jailed, Sam works to free her friends, and the mayor is left with no way to save face.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2007 and opened in limited release a year later, earning less than $1 million. Reviews were mixed, with a 57% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 54; critics praised its passion but found the characters thinly drawn.

overview: Two hillbillies are suspected of being killers by a group of paranoid college kids camping near the duo's West Virginian cabin. As the body count climbs, so does the fear and confusion as the college kids try to seek revenge against the pair.
tagline: Evil just messed with the wrong hillbillies.
title: Tucker and Dale vs. Evil
plot:
Tucker & Dale vs Evil is a 2010 American horror-comedy film directed by Eli Craig, produced by Eden Rock Media, and written by Craig and Michael Davies.

The main themes of Tucker & Dale vs. Evil revolve around the misadventures of two well-meaning but dim-witted friends, Dale (Tyler Labine) and Tucker (Alan Tudyk), who are mistaken for murderers by a group of college students on a camping trip. The film cleverly subverts traditional horror movie tropes, using satire to poke fun at the genre's conventions.

Some of the key themes in the movie include:

1. **Misunderstanding and Miscommunication**: The film highlights how easily misunderstandings can lead to chaos and violence. Dale and Tucker are innocent, but their naivety is misinterpreted by others, leading to a series of hilarious and deadly consequences.
2. **Friendship and Loyalty**: Despite their differences, Dale and Tucker are loyal friends who would do anything for each other. Their friendship is the heart of the film, and their bond is tested throughout the movie.
3. **Social Satire**: The film uses humor to comment on social issues like racism, sexism, and classism. The characters' stereotypes and biases are exaggerated for comedic effect, but also serve as a commentary on how these attitudes can lead to misunderstandings and conflict.
4. **Horror Movie Tropes**: Tucker & Dale vs. Evil lovingly mocks traditional horror movie tropes, such as the "final girl" and the "creepy woods." The film's clever writing and direction turn these familiar conventions into comedic gold.

Overall, Tucker & Dale vs. Evil is a hilarious and entertaining film that uses satire to comment on social issues and poke fun at traditional horror movie tropes.

overview: When mysterious green slime monsters start popping out of soccer balls, all-star athletes Zlatan Ibrahimović and Megan Rapinoe must team up with their four biggest fans to stop evil scientist "Weird Al" Yankovic from stealing their talent.
title: The Soccer Football Movie
plot:
The Soccer Football Movie is a 2022 American animated family comedy film directed by Mitch Schauer and produced by Splash Entertainment for Netflix. The football stars Zlatan Ibrahimović and Megan Rapinoe voice animated versions of themselves, with "Weird Al" Yankovic as the villain, the sportscaster Rob Stone, and Kieran Walton, Madison Zamor, Tania Gunadi, Arnie Pantoja, Ian James Corlett, Tom Kenny, Grey DeLisle and Deeki Deke in the voice cast. The film runs 73 minutes and was released shortly before the 2022 FIFA World Cup.

A group of four young, avid soccer fans are desperate to meet their heroes, the "All-Stars" Ibrahimović and Rapinoe, and find themselves in the wrong place at the wrong time when an evil scientist played by Yankovic sets out to steal the talent and skills of the world's greatest players. He invents a green goo that turns into monstrous slugs, and mysterious slime creatures begin popping out of soccer balls; when Ibrahimović opens a gift box hoping to find a jetpack, a slug merges with him and drains away his abilities. Taken over by the slugs, the players, and eventually Yankovic himself, are transformed into huge green mutant versions of themselves. The two athletes must team up with their four biggest fans, who are honest, hardworking players in their own right, to stop the scientist, and the children's reliance on practice and fair play is set against his magic serum. Along the way they face a living monster ponytail, chases and fights, and a running joke about passing gas, before a final battle with a giant spider-like creature with a deadly stinger.

The film was released on Netflix on 9 November 2022 and received negative reviews. Scott Hines of Decider compared it to a present-day Space Jam and enjoyed Yankovic's villain and Rapinoe's turn, but found Ibrahimović's performance grating and the film aggressively goofy, with little character development or pacing, recommending that viewers skip it. John Sooja of Common Sense Media found Rapinoe and Ibrahimović excellent but judged its terrifying monsters too scary and violent for its intended young audience, and Ewan Gleadow of Cult Following called it a disaster, criticising animation in which models clipped through one another or failed to move.

overview: A young woman joins the military to be part of something bigger than herself and her small-town roots. Instead, she ends up as a new guard at Guantanamo Bay, where her mission is far from black and white. Surrounded by hostile jihadists and aggressive squadmates, she strikes up an unusual friendship with one of the detainees.
tagline: Connection takes courage
title: Camp X-Ray
plot:
Camp X-Ray is a 2014 American drama film directed by Peter Sattler. The movie follows the story of a female soldier, Lisa Torres (played by Kristen Stewart), who is stationed at Guantanamo Bay detention center in Cuba.

The main themes of Camp X-Ray include:

1. **Isolation and confinement**: The film explores the psychological effects of being trapped in a confined space with limited human interaction. Lisa's character is subjected to solitary confinement for 24 hours a day, which takes a toll on her mental health.
2. **Human connection and empathy**: Despite the physical barriers between them, Lisa forms an unlikely bond with one of the detainees, Abou Danan (played by Alexander Skarsgård). This connection humanizes both characters and challenges the viewer's perceptions of the detainees as "enemies."
3. **Power dynamics and control**: The film critiques the power imbalance between the US military personnel and the detainees. Lisa's character is forced to navigate this complex web of authority, where she must balance her duty with her growing sense of empathy for Abou.
4. **Identity and self-discovery**: Through Lisa's character, the film explores themes of identity and self-discovery. As she navigates her role as a soldier in a foreign land, Lisa is forced to confront her own values and motivations.

The movie received critical acclaim for its nuanced portrayal of the Guantanamo Bay detention center and the complex relationships between soldiers and detainees.

overview: In the town of Dillford, humans, vampires and zombies were all living in peace - until the alien apocalypse arrived. Now three teenagers-one human, one vampire, and one zombie-have to team up to figure out how to get rid of the visitors.
tagline: Get out undead or alive.
title: Freaks of Nature
plot:
Freaks of Nature is a 2015 American comedy horror film directed by Robbie Pickering and written by Oren Uziel. It stars Nicholas Braun as Dag, Mackenzie Davis as Petra and Josh Fadem as Ned, with Joan Cusack, Bob Odenkirk, Keegan-Michael Key, Ed Westwick, Patton Oswalt, Vanessa Hudgens and Denis Leary. The story follows three high-school outcasts in a town where humans, vampires and zombies live side by side until an alien invasion turns the species against one another.

The small town of Dillford, Ohio, is home to three groups that barely tolerate each other. Vampires sit at the top of the social ladder and are the coolest kids at school; zombies are kept in a ghetto and allowed out only with special collars that keep them docile; and humans are somewhere in between. Dag, a nerdy human teenager, is desperate to lose his virginity to Lorelei, the most popular girl in school, and is humiliated by Rick Wilson, the baseball coach who also runs the local meat factory and has replaced its human workers, including Dag's mother, with cheap zombie labor.

Meanwhile, Petra, a social outcast, is seduced and bitten by Milan, the school's playboy vampire, who then abandons her to cope alone with her new condition. Ned, Dag's former best friend and one of the smartest people in town, is so tired of being ostracized by his family and teachers that he lets a zombie bite him so that he will no longer have to think. Just as Dag finally seems about to win over Lorelei, aliens invade Dillford, and the residents, believing they are being attacked by the other species, plunge into an all-out war. Dag, Petra and Ned, now a human, a vampire and a zombie, must put aside their differences, uncover the aliens' plans and unite the town against the real enemy.

The film uses its supernatural premise to satirize high-school cliques, prejudice and social hierarchies.

Freaks of Nature was given a limited release by Columbia Pictures on October 30, 2015. It received negative reviews, with none of the five critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes giving it a positive review; The SciFi Movie Page suggested watching it only for the scenes featuring Key, Leary, Odenkirk and Oswalt.

original_title: Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore
overview: Professor Albus Dumbledore knows the powerful, dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald is moving to seize control of the wizarding world. Unable to stop him alone, he entrusts magizoologist Newt Scamander to lead an intrepid team of wizards and witches. They soon encounter an array of old and new beasts as they clash with Grindelwald's growing legion of followers.
tagline: Return to the magic.
title: Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore
plot:
Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore is a 2022 American fantasy adventure film directed by David Yates, and it is the third installment in the Fantastic Beasts series, which is set in the Harry Potter universe.

The story takes place five years after the events of Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald (2018). Albus Dumbledore (Jude Law) has been appointed as the Headmaster of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, while Gellert Grindelwald (Johnny Depp) is on the run from the authorities. Meanwhile, Newt Scamander (Eddie Redmayne), a magizoologist, is tasked with capturing a group of magical creatures that have escaped from Grindelwald's control.

As Newt delves deeper into the world of magic, he discovers that Grindelwald has been secretly manipulating events in Europe to spark a global war between wizards and non-magical people. The story also explores the backstory of Albus Dumbledore and his relationship with Gellert Grindelwald, which is revealed through a series of flashbacks.

Throughout the film, Newt teams up with Albus Dumbledore's brother, Aberforth (Richard Coyle), and Leta Lestrange (Zoe Kravitz), who has her own complicated history with Newt. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Grindelwald and prevent a catastrophic war.

The film features stunning visual effects, impressive action sequences, and a richly detailed world of magic. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Jude Law as the enigmatic Albus Dumbledore. The story is engaging, with plenty of twists and turns that keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore is an exciting addition to the Fantastic Beasts series, offering a thrilling adventure filled with magic, mystery, and memorable characters.

overview: Isaac Netero is the chairman of the Hunter Association. Decades ago he sealed away Jed, a Hunter who had mastered the use of On, the dark "shadow" of Nen. Now On users have reappeared at the Heaven's Arena "Battle Olympia" tournament. For Netero, this is the last mission: to protect the Association and the world from a threat driven by hatred and the thirst for revenge. And he's going to need all the help he can get in order to succeed.
title: Hunter x Hunter: The Last Mission
plot:
Hunter × Hunter: The Last Mission is a 2013 Japanese animated feature directed by Keiichiro Kawaguchi and released on December 27, 2013. The second film based on Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter × Hunter manga, it features the voices of Megumi Han as Gon, Mariya Ise as Killua, Miyuki Sawashiro as Kurapika, Keiji Fujiwara as Leorio and Ichirō Nagai as Isaac Netero.

Decades before the main story, Netero, chairman of the Hunter Association, defeats a formidable enemy named Jed. In the present, hooded figures storm a prison and recruit its inmates. Gon and Killua, on a break from their expeditions, travel to Heaven's Arena with Wing and Biscuit to cheer on their friend Zushi in the Battle Olympia tournament, while Leorio is ambushed on his way to meet them. The intruders seize the tower: Gaki takes the place of Zushi's opponent and defeats him, Shura hijacks the security system, and Rengoku places a curse on Netero that seals his Nen and immobilizes him. Their leader hurls Gon and Killua from the tower, but they survive and fight their way back.

Netero identifies the leader as Jed, his former friend and head of Shadow, the Hunter Association's covert unit, which Netero destroyed after its members began using On, a forbidden power that is the opposite of Nen and is fueled by hatred. The descendants of Shadow, persecuted by the government after the group's fall, revived Jed through their hatred, and he trained them in On. Their aim is to force the Association to reveal the Black Report, a record of the crimes committed against them. As the battle spreads through the building, Gon and Killua defeat Gaki, who dies under the terms of his vow, and Kurapika, present as a bodyguard for his employer Neon, defeats Shura with Leorio's help, but is infected with Jed's blood, which seals his Nen. Hisoka is also present in the tower.

On the roof, Gon is infected too and embraces On to fight Jed, while Killua persuades Rengoku to let go of her hatred, freeing Netero from her curse. Netero chooses to absorb Jed's attacks rather than strike back, and Gon finally purifies the On within Jed with his own Nen, allowing his old enemy to die in peace. With Shadow defeated, the tournament goes ahead.

The film grossed about ¥850 million at the Japanese box office. It had its US premiere at the Japan Film Festival of San Francisco in July 2014, and Viz Media screened an English dub in US theaters in January 2019 before releasing it on home video that March.

overview: A family takes refuge in a fallout shelter to avoid a dangerous outbreak.
tagline: Fear will find you.
title: Hidden
plot:
Hidden is a 2015 American psychological thriller written and directed by Matt and Ross Duffer, known as the Duffer Brothers, in their feature film debut. It stars Alexander Skarsgård as Ray, Andrea Riseborough as Claire and Emily Alyn Lind as their daughter Zoe. The film follows a family struggling to survive in hiding after a mysterious outbreak, and it was the last film of producer Richard D. Zanuck, who died before filming began.

An unknown outbreak has devastated the United States. Ray, Claire and their young daughter Zoe have taken refuge in an abandoned fallout shelter after the military began bombing the civilian population of their town. They have lived underground for many months, surviving on dwindling supplies and following strict rules: stay calm, stay quiet and never go outside. Above them roam creatures Zoe calls the Breathers, who have been hunting the family and have nearly found them several times. Ray and Claire's single priority is keeping Zoe alive, whatever happens to them.

The family's fragile routine is disturbed when they discover that a rat has been eating their food and has found a way into the shelter through a small air duct. While trying to catch it, Ray accidentally knocks over a lamp and starts a fire. Although they put it out, the smoke drifts up the duct and leaves ash on the hatch, potentially revealing their hiding place. When Claire and Ray go to the surface to conceal the shelter, Zoe spots a figure through her homemade periscope and breaks the rules to warn them. A Breather follows them back, and the family must find a way to survive the siege. Flashbacks to the beginning of the outbreak gradually reveal how the family came to be in the shelter and the truth about the Breathers.

The film relies on a single claustrophobic location and slowly building tension, ending with a twist that recontextualizes the story.

Hidden was written shortly after the Duffers graduated from Chapman University and acquired by Warner Bros. in 2011, but it received only a limited release in September 2015, shortly before the brothers created the series Stranger Things. It received generally positive reviews from the few critics who saw it, with 83 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Bo Peep explains what happened to herself and her sheep between the events of Toy Story 2 and Toy Story 4.
title: Lamp Life
plot:
Lamp Life is a 2020 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for the streaming service Disney+. Written and directed by Valerie LaPointe, head of story on Toy Story 4, in her directorial debut, and produced by Mark Sondheimer, it is a spin-off of that feature, running about seven minutes. Annie Potts reprises her role as the porcelain shepherdess Bo Peep, with Ally Maki as Giggle McDimples and Emily Davis as Bo's three sheep, while Woody is voiced by Jim Hanks, Tom Hanks's younger brother. The score was composed by Jake Monaco.

The short fills in what happened to Bo Peep between Toy Story 2 and Toy Story 4. After reuniting with Woody, Bo, joined by her friend Giggle, tells him in a series of flashbacks how she became a lost toy. Once part of a nursery lamp in the bedroom of Andy's younger sister Molly, Bo and her sheep were given away when Molly outgrew them. In her next home, a child's bedroom, she is bored because the mother will not let the children play with the lamp, and as the years pass she moves through a montage of temporary homes, including a white elephant party where teenagers treat her roughly, at one point setting her on fire. She eventually lands in the Second Chance Antiques store, where she is safe but bored once again, and where Gabby Gabby and her ventriloquist dummies make a brief appearance. Wanting adventure and the chance to be played with, Bo devises a plan with Giggle, outwits the shop's surprisingly elaborate security system and breaks out with her sheep, beginning a free life as a lost toy.

LaPointe built the short partly from flashback material cut from Toy Story 4, which had been sad in tone, reworking the gags into comedy as Bo looks back on her hard life with humor. She received guidance from Pete Docter and producer Jonas Rivera, and kept the lamp at the center of the frame while cutting through time, seasons and settings. Lamp Life premiered on Disney+ on 31 January 2020. Reviewers found it charming and packed with quick gags and Pixar Easter eggs, though Laughing Place considered it a tame series of vignettes that added little to the character.

overview: A goofy stork mistakenly delivers a baby panda to the wrong door. A bear, a moose, a tiger and a rabbit set on an arduous but fun-filled adventure through the wilderness to return the panda to its rightful home.
tagline: Big dreams. Big travel. Big trouble!
title: The Big Trip
plot:
The Big Trip (Russian: Bolshoye puteshestviye), also released as The Big Trip 3D and Mission: Panda, is a 2019 Russian animated adventure comedy directed by Vasily Rovensky, who also co-wrote and produced it, and Natalya Nilova. The Russian voice cast is led by Dmitry Nazarov and Maxim Galkin, with Philip Kirkorov, Alexey Vorobyov and the figure skater Tatiana Navka in supporting roles.

The story begins with a delivery gone wrong. A stork entrusted with bringing a newborn baby panda to its parents makes a mistake and drops the cub off at the wrong address: the forest home of Mic-Mic, a grumpy, solitary Asiatic black bear who wants nothing more than to be left in peace. Unable to simply abandon the infant, Mic-Mic reluctantly sets out to return the panda to its rightful mother and father, accompanied by Oscar, a chatty and excitable hare whose constant talking tests the bear's patience.

The mismatched pair, with the baby in tow, embark on a long and perilous journey toward the panda's distant home. Along the way they encounter a gallery of eccentric animals who alternately help and hinder them. Among them are Duke, a clumsy pelican; Janus, a cowardly wolf; Amur, a Siberian tiger with a poetic bent; an unhinged moose named Houston; and Python, a villainous reticulated python. Through the adventure, the gruff bear gradually warms to his tiny charge, and the unlikely companions learn the value of friendship and responsibility.

The film had its world premiere in Turkey on April 12, 2019, and opened in Russian cinemas on April 27. It was a commercial success, earning around $2.2 million in Russia and about $7.1 million worldwide, with the Netherlands its strongest European market, though it received negative reviews. Lionsgate released it on DVD in the United States in January 2020 with an English dub led by Pauly Shore as Mic-Mic and Drake Bell as Oscar. A sequel, Big Trip 2: Special Delivery, was released in Russia in October 2021, again distributed in the United States by Lionsgate.

overview: Zia, distraught over breaking up with his girlfriend, decides to end it all. Unfortunately, he discovers that there is no real ending, only a run-down afterlife that is strikingly similar to his old one, just a bit worse. Discovering that his ex-girlfriend has also "offed" herself, he sets out on a road trip to find her.
tagline: Life is a trip, but the afterlife is one hell of a ride
title: Wristcutters: A Love Story
plot:
Wristcutters: A Love Story is a dark comedy film that delves into the complexities of human existence, mortality, and the afterlife. The movie follows two dead friends, Craig and Jane, who find themselves in a purgatory-like state, stuck in a desolate landscape with no apparent purpose or direction.

The main theme of Wristcutters is the exploration of existential crises and the search for meaning in life. The film's protagonist, Craig, struggles to come to terms with his own mortality and the fact that he has been dead for over 20 years. His journey is a metaphor for the human experience, where individuals often find themselves lost and uncertain about their place in the world.

The movie also touches on the idea of loneliness and isolation, as both Craig and Jane are stuck in this limbo with no one to turn to. Their interactions with other characters, including a group of fellow dead souls, serve as a commentary on the human need for connection and community.

Furthermore, Wristcutters critiques societal norms and expectations surrounding death and mourning. The film's portrayal of a bureaucratic afterlife, where the deceased are forced to navigate a soulless system, serves as a commentary on the ways in which we often try to control or manipulate death rather than accepting it as a natural part of life.

Ultimately, Wristcutters: A Love Story is a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own mortality and the complexities of existence.

overview: After Silvia Broome, an interpreter at United Nations headquarters, overhears plans of an assassination, an American Secret Service agent is sent to investigate.
tagline: The truth needs no translation.
title: The Interpreter
plot:
The Interpreter is a 2005 psychological thriller film directed by Roger Donaldson and starring Nicole Kidman, Sean Penn, and Catherine Keener.

At its core, The Interpreter explores the complex web of emotions and motivations that drive individuals to make life-altering decisions. The story delves into the themes of deception, loyalty, and the blurred lines between truth and fiction. As the protagonist Alice Bowman (Nicole Kidman) becomes embroiled in a deadly game of cat and mouse with a mysterious assassin, she finds herself torn between her duty as an interpreter for the United Nations and her growing feelings for her colleague Silvio (Sean Penn).

The film masterfully weaves together elements of suspense, intrigue, and romance, creating a narrative that is both thrilling and emotionally resonant. Through Alice's character, the movie sheds light on the fragility of human relationships and the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions.

One of the primary themes of The Interpreter is the destructive power of secrets and lies. As Alice navigates the treacherous landscape of international politics and espionage, she must confront the dark truth about her own past and the motivations that drive those around her. This theme is expertly intertwined with the film's exploration of loyalty, trust, and the complexities of human relationships.

Ultimately, The Interpreter is a gripping tale of psychological tension and emotional depth, one that probes the darkest recesses of the human heart and emerges with a profound understanding of the devastating consequences of our choices.

original_title: LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape
overview: The scientists of Jurassic World create a captivating and terrifying new creature that loves hot dogs. But what happens when the hot dogs run out?
title: LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape
plot:
LEGO Jurassic World: The Indominus Escape is a 2016 American animated comedy short produced by Universal and the LEGO Group as part of the toy line tied to the Jurassic World franchise. It first appeared in October 2016 as a five-part online series and was then released on DVD later that month as a single 24-minute film, packaged with the short LEGO Jurassic World: Employee Safety Video. Set before the events of Jurassic World (2015), it reimagines most of that film's characters as minifigures and is regarded as the first animated spin-off of the Jurassic Park franchise. The voice cast includes Bryce Dallas Howard, A.J. LoCascio, Jake Johnson, Lauren Lapkus, Zachary Levi, BD Wong, Fred Tatasciore and Sendhil Ramamurthy.

The story opens with park owner Simon Masrani flying Claire Dearing to the island and showing off with aerial stunts, until he crashes into the aviary and tumbles out of his helicopter. Owen Grady rescues him with the help of a trained Pteranodon. Before he is driven away in an ambulance, Masrani tells Claire that Jurassic World will need a new attraction. Meanwhile, the security chief Vic Hoskins goes hunting in the woods and mistakes a park employee in a dinosaur costume for the real thing, chasing him through the jungle for much of the film.

Claire resolves to create a brand-new dinosaur. Owen doubts it can be done, but Dr. Henry Wu proves otherwise by combining Velociraptor and Carnotaurus DNA, and Owen later discovers a whole collection of earlier hybrids kept in an old section of the island. Wu's newest creation, the Indominus rex, turns out to have an insatiable appetite for hot dogs. When it spots the same costumed employee, now dressed as a hot dog mascot, it breaks out of its enclosure and pursues him. Claire calls in the containment unit, rams the beast with a truck and uses a trail of hot dogs to lure it, while Owen's raptors briefly turn against the soldiers because the Indominus shares their DNA. Eventually Owen arrives with the old Tyrannosaurus and the hybrids, and together they drive the Indominus into a pit. The next day visitors enjoy the new attraction, dinosaurs kicking a gyrosphere like a ball with Hoskins still trapped inside, while in a closing scene Wu feeds a second Indominus.

overview: Mike discovers that being the top-ranking laugh collector at Monsters, Inc. has its benefits – in particular, earning enough money to buy a six-wheel-drive car that's loaded with gadgets. That new-car smell doesn't last long enough, however, as Sulley jump-starts an ill-fated road test that teaches Mike the true meaning of buyer's remorse.
title: Mike's New Car
plot:
Mike's New Car is a 2002 American animated comedy short produced by Pixar Animation Studios and directed by Pete Docter and Roger L. Gould. It reunites Mike Wazowski and James P. "Sulley" Sullivan, the monster heroes of Monsters, Inc., voiced again by Billy Crystal and John Goodman. It was the first Pixar short to feature dialogue and the first to be built around characters and situations from an existing Pixar film.

Some time after the events of Monsters, Inc., Mike proudly shows off his brand-new six-wheel-drive car to Sulley, who is puzzled about what happened to Mike's old one. Inside, Sulley amuses himself by fiddling with the adjustable power seat until an irritated Mike tells him to stop. As soon as the engine starts, the seatbelt warning begins to chime; Sulley buckles up without difficulty, but Mike's belt is stuck, and in trying to free it he accidentally locks himself out of the car.

Mike asks Sulley to press the unlock button, but faced with a dashboard covered in controls, Sulley opens the hood instead. The hood is too tall for Mike to reach, and when Sulley tries to help he slams it on Mike's fingers; attempting to free him, he catapults Mike onto the engine and shuts him inside the compartment. Mike has to phone Sulley from under the hood to be let out. Back in the driver's seat, Mike finally fastens his seatbelt, but the windshield wipers switch on by themselves. Ordering Sulley not to touch anything, Mike presses a button that blasts loud Latin music, and further button-pushing throws the car into total chaos.

Mike stops the madness by pulling out the key, but when Sulley tries to adjust the rearview mirror and breaks it, the exasperated Mike throws him out and speeds off, wrecking the car. Sulley notes that the airbag never deployed, at which point it bursts open and launches Mike into the air. Sulley catches him, and Mike admits that he misses his old car. Over the end credits, Mike fondly recalls his old vehicle before the two friends agree to walk to work.

The short premiered on September 17, 2002, as a bonus feature on the DVD and VHS releases of Monsters, Inc., and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film. The DVD includes a mock commentary credited to "Docter and Gould" that is actually delivered by the directors' young sons.

overview: Six friends hire a medium to hold a séance via Zoom during lockdown — but they get far more than they bargained for as things quickly go wrong. When an evil spirit starts invading their homes, they begin to realize they might not survive the night.
tagline: Someone new has joined the meeting.
title: Host
plot:
Host is a 2020 British independent supernatural horror film directed by Rob Savage, who co-wrote it with Gemma Hurley and Jed Shepherd. A screenlife film that takes place entirely on a Zoom video call, it stars Haley Bishop, Jemma Moore, Emma Louise Webb, Radina Drandova, Caroline Ward and Edward Linard as a group of friends, with Seylan Baxter as a medium. It was conceived and shot during the COVID-19 pandemic, with the cast filming themselves at home while Savage directed them remotely.

During a lockdown in London in July 2020, Haley, Jemma, Radina, Emma, Caroline and Teddy join the weekly Zoom call they use to keep in touch. For fun, Haley has arranged an online séance led by a medium named Seylan, who warns them to treat the spirits with respect, although only Haley and Caroline take the ritual seriously. Teddy soon drops out of the call, and Jemma, bored, claims to feel the presence of a school friend who killed himself. When Seylan's connection drops, Jemma admits that she made the story up as a joke.

Moments later, strange things begin to happen. Haley's chair is yanked across the room, Caroline sees the legs of a hanging body in her attic, a photograph reveals a figure hanging in Haley's home and a glass shatters on its own. When Seylan reconnects, she explains that Jemma's invented story may have allowed a malevolent spirit to wear the guise of the fictional friend and cross into the world of the living. She tells them to close the séance properly, but the entity keeps interrupting. As the presence moves from house to house and their connections fail one by one, the isolated friends can only watch on their screens as each of them is targeted.

Running just under an hour, the film exploits the familiar features of video calls, from frozen screens and dropped connections to face filters, to generate scares, capturing the anxiety of pandemic isolation.

Host debuted on the streaming service Shudder on 30 July 2020 and was released in cinemas and on digital platforms by Vertigo Releasing on 4 December 2020. It received widespread acclaim, with 99 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed about 444,000 dollars against a budget of around 100,000 dollars.

overview: Police commissioner Funes and three researchers of supernatural phenomena investigate inexplicable events that are occurring in the suburbs of Buenos Aires.
tagline: They are in your house… Watching you…
title: Terrified
plot:
Terrified (Spanish: Aterrados) is a 2017 Argentine supernatural horror film written and directed by Demián Rugna. Told through a series of interlocking stories, it concerns a wave of terrifying paranormal events in a quiet neighborhood of Buenos Aires and the team of investigators who try to understand them. The cast includes Maxi Ghione, Norberto Gonzalo, Elvira Onetto, George Lewis and Julieta Vallina.

The film opens with Clara, who hears voices coming from the drain of her kitchen sink, apparently discussing a plan to kill her. Her husband Juan dismisses her fears and blames their noisy neighbor, Walter. That night, awakened by loud thumping, Juan finds Clara's lifeless body suspended in the air in their bathroom, being slammed repeatedly against the wall by an invisible force. Suspected of her murder, Juan is taken into custody.

The story then jumps back in time to show that Walter has been suffering his own supernatural torment. Every night invisible forces shake and move the furniture in his house, and when he sets up a video camera, it records a tall, gaunt figure emerging from under his bed and hiding in his wardrobe. Across the street, Alicia's young son is killed in a road accident, and days later his decomposing corpse is found sitting at the family's kitchen table. Funes, a police commissioner who has been called to these cases, enlists the help of three paranormal investigators: Jano, an expert in such phenomena; Mora Albreck, a researcher; and Rosentock, a former coroner. As each investigator spends the night in one of the affected houses, they confront entities that seem to exist in another dimension and to be using the neighborhood as a doorway into ours, and the officer struggles to hold onto his sanity as the horror escalates.

Terrified was well received by genre audiences and critics, holding an 83 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It won the award for best horror feature at Fantastic Fest, and Vulture included it among the best horror films of 2018, praising its excellent deaths and creature effects and recommending it to fans of Insidious and The Conjuring. Its international success led to plans for an American remake and helped establish Rugna as a leading figure in Latin American horror.

overview: Risking his life, Luke ventures to Rome to visit Paul -- the apostle who's bound in chains and held captive in Nero's darkest and bleakest prison cell. Haunted by the shadows of his past misdeeds, Paul wonders if he's been forgotten as he awaits his grisly execution. Before Paul's death, Luke resolves to write another book that details the birth of what will come to be known as the church.
tagline: Where sin abounds... grace abounds more
title: Paul, Apostle of Christ
plot:
Paul, Apostle of Christ is a 2018 American drama film directed by Chris Downey and written by Mike Bernardo and Jonathan Bernardo. The movie stars James Egan as Saul, also known as Paul the Apostle, and Bruce Dern as Saint Peter.

The film begins with Saul, a young Pharisee who is deeply devoted to his faith and is part of the Jewish community in Jerusalem. He is particularly close to Saint Peter, who becomes like a mentor to him. However, after a dramatic encounter on the road to Damascus, Saul's life takes a drastic turn. He experiences a profound conversion experience where he encounters Jesus Christ, which leads him to become one of the most influential figures in Christianity.

As Saul begins his new journey as an apostle, he faces opposition from within and outside the Jewish community. Many of his former friends and family members reject him due to his radical change in faith. Meanwhile, Saint Peter is struggling with his own doubts about Jesus' divinity and the implications of his teachings on the Jewish people.

The plot thickens when Saul meets Saint Paul (played by Jim Caviezel), a Roman soldier who has also had a transformative experience with Jesus. The two men form an unlikely bond as they discuss their shared faith and the challenges they face in spreading Christianity to the Gentiles. However, their conversation is interrupted by the arrival of King Agrippa II, who is determined to silence them.

As tensions rise, Saul and Saint Paul are put on trial before King Agrippa, where they defend their faith against accusations of blasphemy. The trial becomes a pivotal moment in the film, as it highlights the risks and challenges faced by early Christians in spreading their message.

Throughout the movie, the relationship between Saul and Saint Peter is also explored in depth. Despite their differences, they remain close friends and confidants, with Saint Peter serving as a source of guidance and support for Saul. The dynamic between the two characters adds an emotional depth to the film, highlighting the complexities of faith and friendship.

The movie concludes with Saul's execution by beheading, which marks a tragic end to his journey as an apostle. Despite facing persecution and adversity, Saul remains committed to his faith, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of Christianity for centuries to come.

Overall, Paul, Apostle of Christ is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of faith, friendship, and the challenges faced by early Christians. The movie features strong performances from its cast, particularly Bruce Dern as Saint Peter, who brings gravity and depth to his portrayal of the iconic biblical figure.

overview: Best friends, Neil and Gilbert start their senior year of high school with high hopes and aspirations. Neil has always fantasized about being cool enough to date his long time crush and Gilbert has always dreamed of being a social media super star. After what is, by all accounts, a very disappointing and embarrassing first day in school, Neil makes a magical wish to be cool just at the magical moment when the clock strikes 11:11. The next morning, Neil wakes up to a reality that is straight from the comics of his dreams.
title: Supercool
plot:
Supercool is a 2021 American teen comedy directed by the Finnish filmmaker Teppo Airaksinen and written by Olli Haikka. Set in the world of an American high school, it follows a boy whose wish to become cool enough to win over his crush comes true overnight, with unexpected consequences. Jake Short and Miles J. Harvey star as the two best friends, with Madison Davenport, Damon Wayans Jr. and Iliza Shlesinger in supporting roles. The film premiered at the San Francisco International Film Festival in April 2021 and received a wider release in February 2022.

Neil and Gilbert are best friends beginning their senior year of high school with big hopes. Neil has long dreamed of being cool enough to go out with Summer, the girl he has had a crush on for years, while Gilbert dreams of becoming a social media celebrity. Their first day of the school year turns out to be a disappointing and embarrassing disaster, confirming their status as unpopular outsiders.

That night, at the magical moment when the clock reads 11:11, Neil makes a wish to be cool. The next morning he wakes up to find that his life has been transformed into something resembling the comic books he has always fantasized about, and that the wish has changed both him and the way the world responds to him. Suddenly he has a chance to attract Summer's attention and to become the person he always wanted to be. With the help of Jimmy, Neil's charismatic and unpredictable neighbor, and Gilbert's wild schemes for online fame, the boys embark on one epic night of parties, misadventures and escalating chaos. As the night goes on, Neil begins to discover that being cool is not quite what he imagined, and the friends must face what really matters to them, including their friendship with each other.

The film was made by a Finnish director and writer working within the conventions of the American high school comedy, a genre built around wish fulfilment, unrequited crushes and the search for popularity. Reviews were limited and mostly lukewarm; on Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 40 percent approval rating based on 10 reviews, with an average score of 4.9 out of 10.

overview: A new member has joined Eli and the Shane Gang! Junjie, once the protector of the Eastern Caverns, is a master of the slugslinging art of Slug Fu! But even with the power of five slingers, the Shane Gang find themselves in over their heads as they race across The 99 Caverns in search of the Legendary Elemental Slugs. The five Elementals are ancient slugs of great power, and the forbearers of all slugs found in SlugTerra today. In the wrong hands, they could bring Slugterra to the brink of destruction. So when an evil alliance starts hunting down the Elementals, Eli and his friends — old and new — take off in pursuit of the greatest threat their world has ever faced!
title: SlugTerra: Return of the Elementals
plot:
SlugTerra: Return of the Elementals is an animated science fiction film that delves into the complexities of identity, belonging, and self-discovery. The story revolves around Dax, a young boy who discovers he has the ability to transform into various creatures known as "Elementals." As Dax navigates his newfound powers, he must confront the challenges of being different and finding his place in the world.

The film explores the theme of identity through Dax's journey, as he struggles to balance his human life with his Elemental persona. This internal conflict serves as a metaphor for the difficulties many people face when trying to reconcile their true selves with societal expectations. The movie also touches on the idea of belonging, as Dax searches for a sense of community and acceptance among others who possess similar abilities.

Furthermore, SlugTerra: Return of the Elementals examines the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The Elemental powers are depicted as both a blessing and a curse, highlighting the importance of responsible behavior and self-awareness when dealing with extraordinary abilities.

Ultimately, the film presents a narrative that encourages viewers to embrace their individuality and find strength in their differences. Through Dax's story, SlugTerra: Return of the Elementals conveys a message about self-acceptance, perseverance, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

overview: A true-life drama in the 1920s, centering on British explorer Col. Percy Fawcett, who discovered evidence of a previously unknown, advanced civilization in the Amazon and disappeared whilst searching for it.
tagline: A man's reach should exceed his grasp... or what's a heaven for?
title: The Lost City of Z
plot:
The Lost City of Z is a 2016 American biographical drama film directed by James Gray, not 2017, but I'll provide you with the details.

The film is based on the life of British explorer Percy Fawcett (played by Charlie Hunnam), who disappeared in the Amazon jungle in 1925. The story begins in 1906, where we see a young Fawcett (played by Tom Holland) as a soldier during World War I. After the war, he becomes fascinated with cartography and geography, which leads him to join the Royal Geographical Society.

Fawcett's obsession with finding the Lost City of Z, a mythical city deep in the Amazon jungle that he believes was once inhabited by an advanced civilization, drives him to embark on several expeditions. He is joined by his friends and fellow explorers, Henry Costin (played by Robert Pattinson) and Ralph Costen (played by Sienna Miller).

As Fawcett's expeditions become more frequent, we see his relationships with his wife, Nina (played by Sienna Miller), and his friend, Henry, begin to fray. The tension between the three men is palpable, and their differing opinions on how to proceed with the expedition create conflict.

The film follows Fawcett's journey as he becomes more and more obsessed with finding the Lost City of Z. He becomes convinced that it holds the key to unlocking the secrets of the Amazon jungle and its ancient civilization. As the years go by, Fawcett's expeditions become more frequent, but they also become more perilous.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Fawcett disappears in 1925, leaving behind only his journal and a cryptic message that reads: "I have found it." The film ends with a sense of mystery and tragedy, as we are left wondering what happened to Fawcett and whether he ever truly found the Lost City of Z.

Throughout the film, Gray uses stunning cinematography to bring the Amazon jungle to life. The film's score, composed by David Julyan, adds to the sense of tension and adventure that permeates the story.

Overall, The Lost City of Z is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores the themes of obsession, exploration, and the human condition. Charlie Hunnam delivers a powerful performance as Percy Fawcett, bringing depth and nuance to the character.

overview: A luxury condo manager leads a staff of workers to seek payback on the Wall Street swindler who defrauded them. With only days until the billionaire gets away with the perfect crime, the unlikely crew of amateur thieves enlists the help of petty crook Slide to steal the $20 million they’re sure is hidden in the penthouse.
tagline: Ordinary guys. An extraordinary robbery.
title: Tower Heist
plot:
Tower Heist is a 2011 American action comedy film directed by Brett Ratner and written by Ted Griffin, Jeff Nathanson, and Seth Gordon. The movie stars Ben Affleck, Eddie Murphy, and Casey Affleck.

The story begins with Josh Kovaks (Ben Affleck), the manager of the prestigious Tower One, a luxury high-rise building in New York City. Josh is responsible for ensuring that the wealthy residents of the tower are well taken care of, but he's also deeply unhappy with his life. He feels underappreciated and overworked, and longs for excitement and adventure.

One day, Josh discovers that Foreclosures Inc., a company owned by the ruthless and cunning Arthur Shaw (Alan Tudyk), has been foreclosing on many of the tower's residents, leaving them homeless and destitute. Josh decides to take matters into his own hands and gathers a team of disgruntled tenants, including Eddie Murphy's character, Slide, a charming and skilled thief; Casey Affleck's character, Nate, a young and ambitious stockbroker; and Charles Grodin's character, Ben, a retired accountant.

The team devises a plan to break into Shaw's penthouse apartment and steal $20 million from his safe. However, things don't go according to plan, and the team soon finds themselves in a series of hilarious and action-packed misadventures as they try to outsmart Shaw's security system and escape with their loot.

As the team navigates the complexities of Shaw's penthouse, they also begin to uncover his dark secrets and motives. They learn that Shaw has been embezzling money from his investors and using it to fund his own lavish lifestyle. The team decides to take revenge on Shaw by stealing the money and leaving him with nothing.

The movie builds towards a thrilling climax as Josh and his team face off against Shaw in an epic battle of wits and cunning. In the end, they successfully steal the money and escape with their lives, but not before Shaw is forced to confront the consequences of his actions.

Throughout the movie, the characters are well-developed and relatable, with each one bringing their own unique personality and skills to the table. The chemistry between the cast members is undeniable, and their banter and interactions add a lot of humor and heart to the film.

Overall, Tower Heist is a fun and entertaining movie that combines action, comedy, and drama in a way that's both exciting and engaging. With its talented cast, witty script, and clever plot twists, it's no wonder that this movie has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

overview: A DEA agent and an undercover Naval Intelligence officer who have been tasked with investigating one another find they have been set up by the mob -- the very organization the two men believe they have been stealing money from.
tagline: 2 Guns, 1 Bank.
title: 2 Guns
plot: [No information found]

overview: Wake in Fright is the story of John Grant, a bonded teacher who arrives in the rough outback mining town of Bundanyabba planning to stay overnight before catching the plane to Sydney, but as one night stretches into several he plunges headlong into his own destruction.
tagline: Have a drink, mate? Have a fight, mate? Have some dust and sweat, mate? There's nothing else out here.
title: Wake in Fright
plot:
Wake in Fright is a 1971 Australian psychological drama film directed by Ted Kotcheff. The movie follows the story of John Birkin, a schoolteacher from Sydney who travels to a remote town in rural Australia for a staff meeting. However, things take a dark turn when he finds himself stranded and isolated with a group of rough-riding cowboys.

The main theme of Wake in Fright is the clash between civilization and savagery, as embodied by Birkin's character, who represents the constraints of urban life, and the cowboys, who embody the raw, untamed spirit of the Australian outback. As Birkin becomes increasingly isolated and desperate, he begins to lose his grip on reality, and the lines between good and evil become blurred.

The film also explores themes of masculinity, power dynamics, and the dangers of unchecked male aggression. The cowboys in the film are portrayed as a group of rough-riding, hard-drinking men who are driven by their own desires and impulses, with little regard for authority or social norms. Birkin, on the other hand, is a symbol of the repressed, middle-class values that are seen as weak and effeminate by the cowboys.
