From Bodi's quirky bandmates to his wise-cracking manager, each character brings their own unique personality to the table, making for a rich and engaging narrative that explores the complexities of friendship and community.

Overall, Rock Dog is a heartwarming film that celebrates individuality, cultural heritage, and the power of music to bring people together.

overview: Inspired by the classic tale of Peter Pan, The Lost Girls chronicles four generations of Darling women as they struggle in the aftermath of their adventures with Peter Pan in Neverland. Like her grandmother and her mother Jane before her, Wendy must escape Pan’s hold on her and the promise he desperately wants her to keep. As her daughter Berry comes into Peter’s orbit, Wendy must fight to save her relationship with her daughter while reconciling her legacy.
tagline: A family legend. A neverending fantasy.
title: The Lost Girls
plot:
The Lost Girls is a 2022 British fantasy drama written and directed by Livia De Paolis, who also plays the adult Wendy. Based on Laurie Fox's 2003 novel of the same name, it is inspired by J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan and is set several generations after the original story, exploring the consequences of Peter's promise to keep returning to the women of the Darling family. Vanessa Redgrave, Joely Richardson, Iain Glen, Louis Partridge and Julian Ovenden co-star. The film was released in cinemas and on streaming platforms on 17 June 2022.

Wendy Braverman is the granddaughter of the original Wendy Darling. As a little girl, she listens to her grandmother, Nana Wendy, tell stories of Neverland and promise that Peter Pan will one day come for her too and that she will be enchanted by him. Wendy is homeschooled by her protective father, who fears losing her as he lost his wife Jane, Wendy's mother, who disappeared years before.

When Wendy is a teenager, Peter appears at her window one night, and she falls in love with him. He flies her to Neverland and makes her promise never to grow up. There she has a disturbing encounter with Captain Hook and a vision of her missing mother. Back home, Wendy waits for Peter to return, but the years pass without him. Nana Wendy warns her that she will love another man, but that it will never be enough. As an adult, Wendy marries a kind man named Adam and starts a family, yet she remains haunted by memories of Peter and visions of Hook, and her longing for the boy who never grew up strains her marriage. When Peter reappears and she asks him about her mother, Wendy begins to understand a painful pattern that has shaped generations of women in her family, each enchanted by Peter and left unable to fully live their adult lives. She must decide how to protect her own daughter from the same fate.

The film reinterprets the Peter Pan story from the perspective of the girls Peter leaves behind, treating his visits less as a magical gift than as a source of lasting loss and emotional damage. It drew attention for its cast, which brought together Vanessa Redgrave and her daughter Joely Richardson, with Louis Partridge as an ageless, charming and ultimately unsettling Peter Pan. Reviews were generally negative, with critics finding its ideas intriguing but its execution uneven.

overview: Foreign Legion officer Galoup recalls his once glorious life, training troops in the Gulf of Djibouti. His existence there was happy, strict and regimented, until the arrival of a promising young recruit, Sentain, plants the seeds of jealousy in Galoup's mind.
tagline: Maybe freedom begins with remorse
title: Beau Travail
plot:
Beau Travail is a 1999 film directed by Claire Denis, not La Sept-Arte. The movie is set in French Polynesia and explores the complexities of colonialism, power dynamics, and the human condition.

The main theme of Beau Travail revolves around the tension between discipline and freedom, as embodied by the character of Captain Galoup (played by Denzel Washington). On the surface, he appears to be a strict and authoritative figure, but beneath this façade lies a complex web of emotions and desires. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Galoup's rigid exterior is a coping mechanism for his own vulnerabilities and sense of disconnection.

The film also delves into the theme of identity, particularly in the context of colonialism and cultural exchange. The characters are caught between their French identities and their Polynesian surroundings, leading to a blurring of boundaries and a search for meaning. This is reflected in the character of Gilbert (played by Denzel Washington's on-screen doppelganger), who struggles to reconcile his own identity with the expectations placed upon him.

Furthermore, Beau Travail touches on the theme of masculinity and its performance. The film critiques traditional notions of masculinity, highlighting the performative nature of male identity and the ways in which it can be both a source of strength and weakness.

Overall, Beau Travail is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, power dynamics, and the search for meaning in a complex and often fraught world.

overview: Cecilie and Joachim are about to get married when a freak car accident leaves Joachim disabled, throwing their lives into a spin. The driver of the other car, Marie, and her family don’t get off lightly, either. Her husband Niels works in the hospital where he meets Cecilie and falls madly in love with her.
title: Open Hearts
plot:
Open Hearts is a 2002 drama film directed by Susanne Bier. The movie revolves around the lives of two couples, both in their mid-30s, who meet at a funeral and form an unlikely bond over their shared grief.

At its core, Open Hearts explores the complexities of human relationships, love, and loss. It delves into the intricacies of marriage, friendship, and the fragility of life. The film masterfully weaves together themes of mortality, identity, and the search for meaning in a seemingly indifferent world.

Through the characters' struggles to come to terms with their own vulnerabilities and the impermanence of human connections, Open Hearts poses profound questions about the nature of love, loyalty, and the human condition. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the characters are not just navigating their individual crises but also grappling with the fragility of relationships and the search for authenticity in a world where appearances can be deceiving.

Ultimately, Open Hearts is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on the complexities of love, loss, and connection.

overview: With new friends in a new kingdom, Barbie learns what it means to be herself when she trades places with a royal lookalike in this musical adventure.
title: Barbie: Princess Adventure
plot:
Barbie: Princess Adventure is a 2020 computer-animated musical adventure comedy television film directed by Conrad Helten and written by Ann Austen. Released on Netflix in the United States on September 1, 2020, it is the 37th entry in the Barbie film series and the first feature adaptation of the series Barbie: Dreamhouse Adventures. America Young voices Barbie, with Erica Lindbeck as Princess Amelia, Ritesh Rajan as Ken, Dave Fennoy as the royal adviser Alfonso and Angelo Restaino as Prince Johan.

Barbie is an American teenager who hopes to inspire others through her vlog but has only a small audience. She and her friends receive an all-expenses-paid invitation to the European kingdom of Floravia, not realizing that the trip has been arranged with a hidden agenda by Floravia's Princess Amelia. By watching Barbie's videos, Amelia has noticed that the two look almost identical. Her life and her picture-perfect public image are rigidly controlled by Alfonso, and she has never been allowed to find her own identity or voice. She proposes that the two switch places for a week before her coronation, so that she can finally experience life outside the palace gates.

Barbie agrees, and while Amelia enjoys her week of freedom, Barbie takes on the role of princess, sharing dances with Prince Johan, Amelia's fiancé from a neighboring kingdom. Barbie also faces a dilemma of her own when an unscrupulous content aggregator offers her a major platform, forcing her to decide what changes she is willing to accept. Johan uncovers the ruse and kidnaps the princess, hoping to force Amelia to marry him so that he can rule both his country and Floravia, and Barbie too is captured. With help from Ken, their friends and Barbie's puppies, Barbie and Amelia escape and foil Johan's plot. Amelia is crowned, Alfonso learns to trust her to make her own decisions, and both girls resolve to stay true to themselves.

Produced by Mattel Television and Mainframe Studios, the film was the first Barbie production from Mattel Television after its 2019 rebrand. Its soundtrack album was released digitally on August 28, 2020. Jennifer Green of Common Sense Media praised its diverse cast, snappy music, contemporary dancing and messages of self-affirmation and living offline, writing that these animated adventures offer upbeat fun, while Screen Rant noted its similarities to the Princess Switch films.

overview: After returning from a wedding reception, a couple staying in an isolated vacation house receive a knock on the door in the mid-hours of the night. What ensues is a violent invasion by three strangers, their faces hidden behind masks. The couple find themselves in a violent struggle, in which they go beyond what either of them thought capable in order to survive.
tagline: Lock the door. Pretend you're safe.
title: The Strangers
plot:
The Strangers is a 2008 American psychological horror film directed by Bryan Bertino and written by Bertino and Adam Wingard. The movie follows a young couple, James Hoyt (Scott Speedman) and Kristen McKay (Liv Tyler), who are on a romantic getaway to a secluded lake house in upstate New York.

The beginning of the film sets the tone for the rest of the story, showcasing the idyllic relationship between James and Kristen. They arrive at their destination, a beautiful lake house with breathtaking views, eager to spend some quality time together. As they settle into their new surroundings, it becomes clear that they are trying to escape the stress and mundanity of their daily lives.

However, their tranquility is short-lived. On the first night of their stay, three masked strangers - Man in the Mask (Bryan Greenberg), Pin-Up Girl (Gemma Ward), and Man with the Scars (Tom Budge) - appear at the house uninvited. The couple is shocked and terrified as the strangers begin to terrorize them, making it clear that they are not there by chance.

As the night wears on, James and Kristen try to defend themselves against the masked intruders. However, their attempts at self-defense are met with brutal force, leaving them battered and bruised. The Strangers' motives for attacking the couple remain unclear throughout the film, adding to the sense of unease and tension.

The plot development is slow-burning, building up to a climax that is both shocking and disturbing. As the night wears on, James and Kristen are subjected to physical and emotional abuse by the strangers. The film's use of long takes and close-ups creates a sense of claustrophobia, making the audience feel trapped alongside the characters.

The ending of the film is both haunting and unsettling. Without giving away too many spoilers, it becomes clear that the Strangers' true intentions are far more sinister than initially thought. The final act of the film is a masterclass in building tension, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats as they try to piece together the mystery.

One of the standout aspects of The Strangers is its use of atmosphere and suspense. The film's score, composed by Bobby Koeger, adds to the sense of unease, while the cinematography captures the isolation and vulnerability of the characters. The performances from Scott Speedman and Liv Tyler are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, The Strangers is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of isolation, vulnerability, and the breakdown of relationships. With its slow-burning tension and shocking climax, it's a must-see for fans of psychological horror.

overview: After a botched assassination attempt, the mismatched duo finds themselves in Paris, struggling to retrieve a precious list of names, as the murderous crime syndicate's henchmen try their best to stop them. Once more, Lee and Carter must fight their way through dangerous gangsters; however, this time, the past has come back to haunt Lee. Will the boys get the job done once and for all?
tagline: The Rush Is On!
title: Rush Hour 3
plot:
Rush Hour 3 is a 2007 action comedy film directed by Brett Ratner and starring Jackie Chan and Chris Tucker as the main characters, Inspector Lee and Detective James Carter. The movie takes place three years after the events of Rush Hour 2.

The story begins with Inspector Lee (Jackie Chan) being summoned to Paris by his friend, Inspector Soo-Yong (Ken Leung), who is now working for Interpol. Soo-Yong informs Lee that a valuable artifact, the "Dragon's Blood" diamond, has been stolen from a museum in Paris. The thief plans to sell it on the black market, and Soo-Yong needs Lee's help to track him down.

Upon arrival in Paris, Lee meets up with his old friend, Detective James Carter (Chris Tucker), who is now working for Interpol as well. Carter is initially reluctant to work with Lee again, but eventually agrees to help him solve the case.

As they begin their investigation, Lee and Carter discover that the thief is a wealthy businessman named Yuen (Yuen Wah), who has connections to the Triads. They also learn that Yuen plans to sell the diamond to a mysterious buyer in Dubai.

Lee and Carter's investigation takes them from Paris to Hong Kong, where they encounter various obstacles and challenges along the way. Along the way, Lee must confront his own personal demons and learn to trust Carter again.

As the story unfolds, Lee and Carter discover that Yuen is working with a group of Triad members who are seeking revenge against the Chinese government for their treatment of them in Hong Kong. The group plans to use the diamond to fund their operations and exact revenge on China.

In the climactic final act, Lee and Carter track down Yuen and his accomplices to Dubai, where they engage in a high-stakes battle to recover the stolen diamond. In the end, Lee and Carter successfully foil the plot, but not before Yuen is killed by one of his own accomplices.

The movie ends with Lee and Carter returning to Hong Kong as heroes, where they are greeted with parades and celebrations. The film concludes on a positive note, with Lee and Carter's friendship stronger than ever.

Overall, Rush Hour 3 received mixed reviews from critics, but was still a commercial success, grossing over $250 million worldwide. While it did not live up to the expectations of some fans, the movie still delivered plenty of action, humor, and excitement, making it a satisfying conclusion to the Rush Hour trilogy.

overview: A group of friends stranded near a desolate cornfield find shelter in an old farmhouse, though they soon discover the dwelling is the center of a supernatural ritual.
tagline: Join the harvest.
title: Husk
plot:
Husk is a 2011 American anthology horror film directed by Joe Swanberg and Adam Wingard, among others. The story revolves around a group of friends who reunite at a remote cabin in Wisconsin for a weekend getaway.

The main theme of Husk is the exploration of relationships, intimacy, and the complexities of human connections. As the characters navigate their personal struggles and insecurities, they are forced to confront the imperfections and vulnerabilities that exist within themselves and those around them. The film delves into the tension between desire and repression, as well as the blurred lines between friendship and romance.

Throughout the narrative, Husk also touches on themes of isolation, loneliness, and the disconnection that can occur when individuals retreat from their responsibilities and relationships. The remote cabin setting serves as a metaphor for the characters' inner worlds, where they are forced to confront their deepest fears and desires.

Ultimately, Husk presents a nuanced portrayal of human relationships, highlighting the complexities and nuances that exist within even the most seemingly ordinary interactions.

overview: Metal drummer Ruben begins to lose his hearing. When a doctor tells him his condition will worsen, he thinks his career and life is over. His girlfriend Lou checks the former addict into a rehab for the deaf hoping it will prevent a relapse and help him adapt to his new life. After being welcomed and accepted just as he is, Ruben must choose between his new normal and the life he once knew.
tagline: Music was his world. Then silence revealed a new one.
title: Sound of Metal
plot:
Sound of Metal is a 2019 American drama film directed by Darius Marder, written by Darius Marder, Abraham Marder, and Derek Mulligan, and starring Riz Ahmed, Paul Raci, and Olivia Cooke.

The movie follows the story of Ruben Stone (Riz Ahmed), a heavy metal drummer who suffers from tinnitus, a condition that causes ringing in his ears. The constant noise is unbearable for him, and he begins to lose his hearing gradually. As his hearing deteriorates, Ruben's life starts to unravel. He becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to connect with his girlfriend, Leah (Olivia Cooke), and his friends.

Ruben decides to take drastic measures to preserve his remaining hearing by undergoing a cochlear implant surgery. However, the procedure is not without risks, and Ruben must confront the possibility that he may lose his sense of sound forever. As he prepares for the surgery, Ruben's relationships with those around him begin to fray.

One day, while out on a walk, Ruben meets Joe (Paul Raci), a deaf man who becomes his friend and confidant. Despite their vastly different experiences, the two men form a deep bond, and Joe teaches Ruben about the world of sign language and Deaf culture. Through Joe's eyes, Ruben begins to see the world in a new light, and he starts to question his own identity and purpose.

As Ruben navigates his relationships with Leah and Joe, he must also confront the harsh realities of his condition. The cochlear implant surgery is a turning point for him, as it forces him to reevaluate what it means to be human and to experience the world around him. Through his journey, Ruben comes to realize that sound is not just something we hear, but also something we feel and connect with.

The film's title, Sound of Metal, refers to the heavy metal music that Ruben loves, as well as the physical sensation of hearing. It's a metaphor for the way that sound can both destroy and create us. As Ruben's hearing fades away, he begins to find new ways to experience the world, and in doing so, he discovers a new sense of purpose and meaning.

Ultimately, Sound of Metal is a powerful exploration of identity, community, and the human condition. Through its nuanced portrayal of a complex character, the film raises important questions about what it means to be alive and to connect with others. The movie's climax is both heartbreaking and hopeful, as Ruben comes to terms with his new reality and finds a way to move forward.

Overall, Sound of Metal is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of human experience. With its powerful performances, nuanced direction, and thought-provoking themes, it's a movie that will stay with you long after the credits roll.

overview: Kingdom of Hungary, 17th century. As she gets older, powerful Countess Erzsébet Báthory (1560-1614), blinded by the passion that she feels for a younger man, succumbs to the mad delusion that blood will keep her young and beautiful forever.
tagline: She sacrificed all for love and others for beauty
title: The Countess
plot:
The Countess is a 2009 French-German historical drama written and directed by Julie Delpy, who also composed its score and stars in the title role. Based on the life of the notorious Hungarian noblewoman Elizabeth Báthory, it co-stars Daniel Brühl as István Thurzó and William Hurt as his father, Count György Thurzó. It was Delpy's third feature as a director, and she described it as less a gothic tale than a drama about the psychology of people who are given power.

Elizabeth Báthory is born in 1560 into one of the most powerful noble families of Hungary and is raised from childhood to accept harshness and cruelty as part of her station. As a teenager she becomes pregnant by a young peasant, whom she is forced to watch being tortured and killed, and her child is taken from her immediately after birth. She is later married to Count Ferenc Nádasdy and has children with him. When Nádasdy dies of an illness contracted during the wars against the Ottomans, Elizabeth inherits his vast estates and becomes one of the wealthiest and most powerful people in the kingdom, to the point that the Habsburg ruler Matthias is deeply in debt to her.

At a ball, Elizabeth meets István, the twenty-one-year-old son of Count Thurzó, and the two fall passionately in love. György Thurzó, however, forces his son to break off the relationship and marry the daughter of a wealthy merchant. Devastated, the aging Elizabeth becomes convinced that their age difference destroyed the affair. When she is splashed with blood after striking a servant girl and is told by her flattering attendants that her skin looks younger, she begins to believe that bathing in the blood of virgins can preserve her youth and beauty. Her servants start abducting and killing young peasant women to obtain their blood, until the disappearances can no longer be ignored and Thurzó, who has political and financial reasons to bring her down, leads an investigation into her crimes.

Delpy approaches the legend as a psychological drama about power, vanity and the fear of aging. Found guilty, Elizabeth is spared execution because of her noble birth and is instead walled into her room at Čachtice Castle for the rest of her life.

The Countess premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival on 9 February 2009. It received largely negative reviews; Variety's Boyd van Hoeij wrote that although some individual moments work, the screenplay lacks psychological connective tissue.

overview: A fatal plane crash changes the lives of Roman and Jake forever. Roman loses his wife and daughter in the accident, while Jake loses his mind—as he happens to be the air traffic controller who failed to avert the nightmare. Rage and revenge engulfs Roman and Jake finds himself swamped with guilt and regret.
tagline: All he had left was revenge
title: Aftermath
plot:
Aftermath is a 2017 American thriller film directed by Eshom Nelms and Christopher Renz. The movie follows a former Army Ranger, Ronin (played by Aaron Eckhart), who returns home to find his family brutally murdered in their home. Consumed by grief and anger, Ronin sets out on a quest for revenge against the perpetrators.

The main themes of Aftermath include:

1. **Grief and Trauma**: The film explores the devastating effects of trauma and loss on individuals and families. Ronin's journey is driven by his need to cope with the unbearable pain of losing his loved ones.
2. **Revenge vs. Redemption**: As Ronin navigates the dark world of revenge, he begins to question whether his actions will bring him closure or perpetuate a cycle of violence. This internal conflict serves as a commentary on the destructive nature of revenge and the importance of seeking redemption.
3. **The Blurred Lines between Good and Evil**: The film raises questions about morality and the nature of evil. Ronin's perception of right and wrong becomes increasingly distorted as he seeks justice, highlighting the complexities of human behavior in the face of trauma.
4. **The Dangers of Unchecked Emotions**: Aftermath portrays the dangers of allowing emotions like anger and grief to consume us. Ronin's inability to control his emotions leads him down a path of destruction, serving as a cautionary tale about the importance of emotional regulation.

Throughout the film, these themes are expertly woven together to create a gripping narrative that explores the human condition in the face of unimaginable tragedy.

overview: An unexpected pregnancy takes a terrifying turn for newlyweds Zach and Samantha McCall.
tagline: The Devil Always Gets His Due
title: Devil's Due
plot:
Devil's Due is a 2014 American found-footage supernatural horror film directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett in their feature directorial debut and written by Lindsay Devlin. It stars Allison Miller as Samantha McCall and Zach Gilford as her husband Zach, with Sam Anderson as Father Thomas. Produced for 20th Century Fox, the film was developed after the directors' segment 10/31/98 in the 2012 horror anthology V/H/S attracted studio attention.

Zach McCall begins recording a video diary on the eve of his wedding to Sam, so that their future children will have a record of the family's history. The newlyweds spend their honeymoon in the Dominican Republic, where a fortune teller unsettles Sam by telling her that she was born from death and that they have been waiting for her. Later that night, lost in an unfamiliar part of the city, the couple accepts a ride from a taxi driver who takes them to an underground nightclub. After drinking heavily, they black out, and Sam is taken to a hidden chamber where she is subjected to a satanic ritual. The next morning they wake up in their hotel remembering nothing.

A few weeks after returning home, Sam discovers that she is pregnant despite having taken birth control pills. The couple is delighted at first, but Zach continues filming everything, and the footage gradually reveals that something is wrong. During the first ultrasound the monitor briefly turns to static, and as the pregnancy progresses, Sam develops nosebleeds, bruising, a craving for raw meat despite being a vegetarian, sudden bursts of violent rage and frightening displays of strength and telekinesis. Strangers seem to be watching the house, and hidden cameras are secretly installed to monitor her. As Zach investigates, he uncovers evidence that a cult has chosen Sam to carry a child for a sinister purpose and that their lives are in grave danger.

The film combines the found-footage format with the themes of Rosemary's Baby, using home video, security cameras and other recording devices to tell its story.

Devil's Due was released on January 17, 2014. It received negative reviews, with 21 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it derivative and mostly uninspired, and a Metacritic score of 34.

overview: Diagnosed with a mental illness halfway through his senior year of high school, a witty, introspective teen struggles to keep it a secret while falling in love with a brilliant classmate who inspires him to open his heart and not be defined by his condition.
tagline: If you can't trust your mind, trust your heart.
title: Words on Bathroom Walls
plot:
Words on Bathroom Walls is a poignant and thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of mental health, identity, and the struggles of growing up. The movie follows the story of Jamie Sullivan, a charismatic and creative teenager who navigates his way through high school while living with schizophrenia.

At its core, Words on Bathroom Walls explores the theme of finding one's voice in the face of adversity. Jamie's experiences with mental illness serve as a catalyst for self-discovery, forcing him to confront his emotions, challenge societal expectations, and forge his own path. The film beautifully captures the tension between conformity and individuality, highlighting the importance of embracing one's uniqueness.

The movie also touches on the theme of social isolation and the struggle to form meaningful connections with others. Jamie's relationships with his family and peers are fraught with challenges, as he grapples with feelings of loneliness and disconnection. Through Jamie's journey, the film sheds light on the devastating consequences of neglecting mental health and the importance of empathy and understanding in building strong relationships.

Furthermore, Words on Bathroom Walls tackles the theme of identity and self-acceptance. As Jamie navigates his way through adolescence, he must confront the expectations placed upon him by others and forge a sense of self that is authentic and true to who he is. The film's portrayal of Jamie's inner world is both haunting and beautiful, offering a powerful exploration of the human experience.

Ultimately, Words on Bathroom Walls is a heart-wrenching and ultimately uplifting film that celebrates the resilience of the human spirit. Through its thoughtful and nuanced portrayal of mental health, identity, and relationships, the movie offers a powerful message of hope and acceptance.

overview: Anna Fritz is a beautiful and famous actress. Suddenly her body is found in a hotel and the news of her death goes around the planet. The young, shy caretaker Pau works at the hospital where they carried the body of Anna Fritz. He and his friends  decide to take pictures of the body of Anna Fritz.  They decide they could make love to her and nobody would know. They are in front of Anna Fritz ... and can do with it what  they want.
title: The Corpse of Anna Fritz
plot:
The Corpse of Anna Fritz (Spanish: El cadáver de Anna Fritz) is a 2015 Spanish thriller co-written and directed by Hèctor Hernández Vicens. It stars Alba Ribas as Anna Fritz, Albert Carbó as Pau, Cristian Valencia as Ivan and Bernat Saumell as Javi, with Nico Avila as a doctor. Set almost entirely within a hospital morgue during a single night, it is a claustrophobic and disturbing story about guilt, complicity and survival.

Pau works as an orderly in a hospital, a job that gives him access to the bodies brought to the morgue. One night the body of Anna Fritz, a famous and much-admired young actress who has died suddenly, is brought in. Unable to resist, Pau takes a photograph and sends it to his friends Ivan and Javi, who come to the hospital to see the body for themselves. Egged on by the domineering Ivan, Pau and Ivan commit a horrific crime against the corpse, while Javi, disgusted, refuses to take part.

In the middle of the assault, the men realize to their horror that Anna has opened her eyes: she is alive, but paralyzed and unable to speak. The three are now faced with a terrible choice: to seek medical help and face the consequences of what they have done, or to kill her to cover up their crime. Javi insists that they must save her and take responsibility, while Ivan is determined to silence her and persuades the weak-willed Pau that they have no choice. Their argument turns violent, with fatal consequences. As the men debate her fate, Anna gradually regains control of her body, and the night turns into a desperate struggle in which she must find a way to escape from the morgue alive.

With few characters and a single location, the film builds tension from the moral collapse of its characters and from the perspective of a victim who cannot move or call for help.

The Corpse of Anna Fritz premiered at the South by Southwest festival in Austin, Texas, on 15 March 2015. Reviews were mixed to positive, with about 67 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. IGN's Cliff Wheatley praised Alba Ribas's performance and the tense subject matter, though he felt that even its 76-minute running time was too long, while the International Business Times thought it might have worked better as a short film.

overview: Desperate to pay the bills and come through for their loved ones, three lifelong pals risk it all by embarking on a daring bid to knock off the very bank that absconded with their money.
tagline: You're never too old to get even.
title: Going in Style
plot:
Going in Style is a 2017 American comedy-drama film directed by David Dobkin, starring Michael Caine, Zooey Deschanel, and Tommy Lee Jones.

The main themes of Going in Style revolve around friendship, loyalty, and the power of older adults to challenge societal norms. The movie follows two retired men, William "Billy" Baldwin (Michael Caine) and Henry "Hank" senior (Tommy Lee Jones), who are forced by their bank to rob a bank as part of a scheme to avoid foreclosure on their homes.

As they embark on this adventure, they meet Doris Miller (Zooey Deschanel), a feisty and charming widow who joins them on the heist. Through their shared experiences, the three form an unlikely bond, which becomes a source of strength and inspiration for each other.

The film explores themes such as:

1. Friendship: The movie highlights the importance of male friendships, particularly among older adults, who often find themselves marginalized or overlooked in society.
2. Loyalty: Billy, Hank, and Doris demonstrate unwavering loyalty to one another, which becomes a driving force behind their actions throughout the film.
3. Challenging societal norms: The characters refuse to accept their perceived limitations as they age, instead choosing to take control of their lives and challenge the status quo.
4. Empowerment: Through their experiences, the three main characters find a sense of empowerment and self-discovery, which is particularly evident in Doris's character development.

Overall, Going in Style offers a heartwarming and entertaining exploration of themes that are both timely and timeless.

original_title: 劇場版総集編【後編】メイドインアビス 放浪する黄昏
overview: Second compilation movie of the TV series which covers episodes 9-13. Riko and Reg descend to the third and fourth layer where Riko has her first experience of the Curse.
title: Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight
plot:
Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight is an anime film that delves into the complexities of human existence, particularly in the context of exploration and discovery. The story follows Riko, a young girl who embarks on a perilous journey to the bottom of a mysterious abyss, accompanied by her companion Reg.

At its core, Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight explores the theme of existentialism, where the protagonist's quest for answers about the nature of existence and the meaning of life becomes an all-consuming force. Riko's journey is not just about uncovering secrets but also about confronting the darkness within herself and the world around her.

The film also touches on the idea of loneliness and isolation, as Riko navigates the desolate landscape of the abyss, often finding herself disconnected from others and forced to rely solely on her own wits and determination. This sense of solitude serves as a catalyst for introspection, allowing Riko to grapple with her own emotions and the weight of her responsibilities.

Furthermore, Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight examines the concept of sacrifice and the true cost of ambition. Reg's unwavering dedication to Riko and their shared quest raises questions about the nature of love, loyalty, and the sacrifices one is willing to make for others.

Throughout the film, the director weaves together these themes with a sense of wonder and awe, capturing the beauty and mystery of the abyss as a metaphor for the unknown and the unexplored aspects of human experience. Ultimately, Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight presents a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be human, to search for meaning, and to confront the darkness that lies within ourselves and the world around us.

overview: Demon hunter, Jebediah Huntley teams up with an FBI agent to battle a supernatural force in the southern state of Mississippi.
title: Don't Kill It
plot:
Don't Kill It is a 2016 American comedy horror film directed and edited by Mike Mendez from a screenplay by Dan Berk and Robert Olsen. Dolph Lundgren stars as Jebediah Woodley, an eccentric demon hunter who travels to a small Mississippi town to destroy an ancient, murderous demon. Kristina Klebe, Tony Bentley, James Chalke, Billy Slaughter and Miles Doleac appear in supporting roles. The script was originally set in Alaska, but filming was moved to Mississippi for financial reasons, and the film was made for less than $1 million, part of it raised through crowdfunding on Indiegogo.

While hunting deer in southern Mississippi, a man named Gabriel follows his dog to a small golden box, which the dog opens. The animal begins to act strangely and attacks Gabriel, who is forced to shoot it. Gabriel returns home with the same black eyes and erratic behavior, murders his family and then begins killing his neighbors until he is shot dead by a neighbor named Marcus, who immediately develops black eyes himself and carries on the slaughter. The demon, it turns out, passes into whoever kills its current host.

Days later, Jebediah Woodley, a weathered demon hunter who has spent decades tracking this particular entity, hears about the killings on the radio and comes to town. At the same time, FBI agent Evelyn Pierce, who grew up in the area, has been sent to investigate the massacres as a possible case of domestic terrorism. Pierce and the local police chief dismiss Woodley's talk of demons and have him detained, but when the killings continue, Pierce is forced to accept that he is right. Woodley explains that the demon cannot simply be killed, since its killer becomes the next host, and that it must be trapped instead. As panic spreads and the townspeople start to turn on one another, Woodley and Pierce try to stop the demon without letting anyone kill it, a task that becomes increasingly difficult as it jumps from body to body.

The film played on the genre festival circuit before its release and was generally well received by horror critics, who enjoyed its sense of humor, its gory effects and Lundgren's relaxed, self-mocking turn as the gruff hunter.

overview: Johnny Knoxville and his band of maniacs perform a variety of stunts and gross-out gags on the big screen for the first time. They wander around Japan in panda outfits, wreak havoc on a once civilized golf course, they even do stunts involving LIVE alligators, and so on.
tagline: Do not attempt this at home.
title: Jackass: The Movie
plot:
Jackass: The Movie is a 2002 American reality slapstick comedy directed by Jeff Tremaine and produced by Tremaine, Spike Jonze and Johnny Knoxville. A continuation of the MTV television series Jackass, which had ended its run, it was produced by Lynch Siderow Productions and Dickhouse Productions and features most of the original cast, including Knoxville, Bam Margera, Chris Pontius, Steve-O, Dave England, Ryan Dunn, Wee Man, Preston Lacy and Ehren McGhehey.

Like the series, the film has no conventional plot. It is a compilation of dangerous stunts, crude skits and elaborate pranks on unsuspecting members of the public, intercut with comments from the cast. It opens with a mock Hollywood action sequence set to "O Fortuna", in which the entire cast rides a giant shopping cart downhill amid explosions while each member is introduced, before Knoxville delivers his signature greeting and the group crashes into a fruit stand.

Among the many stunts and pranks that follow, Knoxville is flipped over and knocked out in a golf cart, Steve-O snorts wasabi, Bam Margera plants a live alligator in his mother April's kitchen, Chris Pontius dances in public in a thong as his character Party Boy, and Ryan Dunn takes on a female Japanese kickboxing champion. Wee Man causes chaos in the streets of Tokyo inside a giant traffic cone, and the cast endure painful encounters with animals, paper cuts, fireworks and bodily functions. Throughout, the cast's willingness to injure and humiliate themselves for the camera is the central source of humor, along with their obvious camaraderie.

Like the series, the film relies on the cast's apparent fearlessness and on the reactions of bystanders, and it is widely regarded as a cult phenomenon of the 2000s.

MTV Films and Paramount Pictures released the film on October 25, 2002. Made for about 5 million dollars, it opened at number one at the U.S. box office with 22.8 million dollars and grossed 79.5 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 49 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 42, and it was followed by Jackass Number Two in 2006.

overview: To take down South Boston's Irish Mafia, the police send in one of their own to infiltrate the underworld, not realizing the syndicate has done likewise. While an undercover cop curries favor with the mob kingpin, a career criminal rises through the police ranks. But both sides soon discover there's a mole among them.
tagline: Lies. Betrayal. Sacrifice. How far will you take it?
title: The Departed
plot:
The Departed is a crime drama film directed by Martin Scorsese, released in 2006 by Warner Bros. Pictures and Plan B Entertainment. The movie is an adaptation of Hong Kong cinema's "Infernal Affairs," which was itself based on the 1998 Hong Kong film "An Insult to Injury."

The story takes place in Boston, where undercover cop Billy Costigan (Leonardo DiCaprio) infiltrates a powerful Irish mob led by Frank Costello (Jack Nicholson). Meanwhile, Costello hires Colin Sullivan (Matt Damon), an ambitious and loyal mole who is secretly working for the police.

As both men navigate their respective worlds, they begin to form close relationships with those around them. Billy becomes friends with Queenan (Martin Sheen) and Dignam (Mark Wahlberg), two seasoned detectives who are initially unaware of his true identity. Colin, on the other hand, gains the trust of Costello's inner circle, including his right-hand man, Madolyn (Vera Farmiga).

As the story unfolds, both Billy and Colin become deeply entrenched in their respective roles, with each trying to outmaneuver the other. However, as they gather intelligence and build relationships, they begin to realize that they are playing a deadly game of cat and mouse.

The plot thickens when Billy is forced to go undercover at Costello's headquarters, where he witnesses Colin's treachery firsthand. Meanwhile, Colin becomes increasingly paranoid, suspecting that someone within the police department is working against him.

In a stunning twist, it is revealed that Dignam has been secretly working with Costello all along, and that Billy had unknowingly infiltrated the wrong organization. The film builds towards a tense showdown between Billy and Colin, as they both try to outsmart each other in a desperate bid for survival.

Ultimately, Billy manages to expose Colin's betrayal, but not before he is mortally wounded by his own hand. In a poignant twist, it is revealed that Queenan had been working with Costello all along, having been compromised by the mole within the police department.

The Departed received widespread critical acclaim, earning eight Academy Award nominations and winning four, including Best Picture, Best Director, Best Film Editing, and Best Adapted Screenplay. The film's complex web of characters and plot twists was widely praised for its originality and tension, cementing its place as one of the greatest crime dramas of all time.

Overall, The Departed is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the dark underbelly of organized crime in Boston. With outstanding performances from its cast, including DiCaprio, Damon, and Nicholson, the film is a masterclass in storytelling and character development.

overview: Isi and Ossi couldn't be any more different: She's a billionaire's daughter from Heidelberg, he's a struggling boxer from the nearby town of Mannheim. But when Isi meets Ossi, the two quickly realize that they can take advantage of one another: She dates the broke boxer to provoke her parents and get them to fund a long-desired chef training in New York. He tries to rip off the rich daughter to finance his first professional boxing match. Their plans soon develop into emotional chaos that challenges everything the two believe to know about money, career and love.
title: Isi & Ossi
plot:
Isi & Ossi is a 2020 German comedy film directed by Gernot Rollne and Felix von Gunten. The movie follows the story of two friends, Isa and Ossi, who are struggling to find their place in the world after completing their military service.

The main theme of Isi & Ossi revolves around the challenges of transitioning from a structured environment like the military to civilian life. The film explores how these young men navigate the complexities of adulthood, including finding employment, building relationships, and defining their identities.

One of the central themes is the struggle for identity and belonging. Isa and Ossi are both trying to figure out who they are outside of their military roles, which often defined them during their service. The film delves into their insecurities, fears, and desires as they try to find their place in the world.

The movie also touches on themes of masculinity, friendship, and the difficulties of growing up. Isa and Ossi's relationship is a key aspect of the film, as they support each other through the ups and downs of life. However, their friendship is also put to the test as they face different challenges and make choices that affect their bond.

Overall, Isi & Ossi is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the challenges faced by young adults transitioning from military service to civilian life. The film offers a relatable portrayal of the struggles and triumphs of growing up, making it a endearing and entertaining watch.

overview: Galo and the Burning Rescue Fire Department face off against BURNISH, a group of mutants who are able to control and wield flames, and the fire disaster they have unleashed on Earth.
tagline: The world ablaze.
title: Promare
plot:
Promare is a 2019 Japanese animated science fiction action film directed by Hiroyuki Imaishi and written by Kazuki Nakashima, co-produced by Studio Trigger and XFLAG. It features character and mecha designs by Shigeto Koyama, 3D computer animation by Sanzigen and music by Hiroyuki Sawano. The film was the first feature produced by Trigger, a studio founded by former staff of Gainax, and reunites Imaishi and Nakashima, the director and writer of Gurren Lagann and Kill la Kill.

Thirty years before the story begins, a catastrophe known as the Great World Blaze saw outbreaks of spontaneous human combustion kill half of the world's population. Some survivors developed the ability to create and control flames and became known as the Burnish, a minority feared and persecuted by the rest of society. In the city of Promepolis, Galo Thymos, a hot-headed young member of the firefighting team Burning Rescue, battles fires caused by the Mad Burnish, a radical Burnish group branded as terrorists, and defeats their leader, Lio Fotia, who is then arrested by the Freeze Force, the police force serving the city's governor, Kray Foresight.

Lio and the other prisoners escape, and Galo follows them to a hideout where he sees Lio trying to save a dying Burnish and learns that Kray has been capturing Burnish people for human experiments. Galo, who idolizes Kray for having saved his life as a child, confronts the governor, who reveals that the Earth will soon be destroyed by a surge of magma from its core and that he plans to use the Burnish's power to fuel a warp drive and escape the planet with a select few. Arrested for opposing the plan, Galo must join forces with his former enemy Lio to uncover the true nature of the Burnish flames and save both peoples.

The film is known for its bold, neon-colored, geometric visual style and over-the-top action, while its story deals with themes of discrimination and prejudice.

Promare was released in Japan by Toho Animation on May 24, 2019, and in North America by GKIDS. It received widespread critical acclaim, with 97 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, was selected for the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, and was nominated for the Annie Award for Best Animated Feature – Independent.

overview: Years after the original Backdraft, Sean, son of the late Steve "Bull" McCaffrey, is assigned to investigate a deadly fire only to realize it is something much more sinister.
title: Backdraft 2
plot:
Backdraft 2 is a 2019 American action film directed by Jon Turteltaub and written by Michael Brandt and Derek Haas. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1991 film Backdraft, which was based on the novel of the same name by Robert Crais.

The main themes of Backdraft 2 revolve around family, loyalty, and redemption. The story follows Brian McCaffrey (played by Josh McConaughey), the son of the late firefighter Stephen "Bull" McCaffrey (played by William Baldwin) from the original film. Brian is a young firefighter who struggles to live up to his father's legacy while navigating his own personal demons.

As Brian delves deeper into the world of firefighting, he must confront his troubled past and learn to balance his desire for recognition with the need to protect those around him. The movie explores themes of family loyalty, as Brian tries to prove himself as a firefighter in his own right, while also honoring his father's memory.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption, as Brian seeks to make amends for past mistakes and find forgiveness from those he has hurt. Throughout the story, Brian must confront his own personal struggles and learn to trust himself and others in order to become a true firefighter.

Overall, Backdraft 2 is an action-packed drama that explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption, while also delivering high-octane firefighting sequences and intense action scenes.

original_title: 劇場版 ポケットモンスター　キミにきめた！
overview: Ash Ketchum wakes up late one morning after having broken his alarm clock in his sleep. He eventually makes it to Professor Oak's lab, but is told that the three starter List of Pokémon (Bulbasaur, Squirtle, and Charmander) have already been taken by Trainers who were on time. However, Oak reveals that he has one more Pokémon, an Electric-type named Pikachu. Despite its volatile and feisty personality, as well as its refusal to get inside a Poké Ball, Ash happily takes Pikachu for his journey.
title: Pokémon the Movie: I Choose You!
plot:
Pokémon the Movie: I Choose You! is a 2017 animated adventure film based on the popular media franchise Pokémon, produced by OLM, Inc. and TV Tokyo.

The movie begins with Ash Ketchum, a young boy from Pallet Town, who has just received his very first Pokémon, Pikachu, from Professor Oak. Ash's dream is to become a Pokémon Master, and he sets out on an epic journey to catch more Pokémon and battle Gym Leaders to earn Badges.

As Ash and Pikachu travel through various regions, they meet new friends, including Misty, a skilled Pokémon Trainer from Cerulean City, and Brock, a Pokémon Breeder from Pewter City. The trio embarks on a thrilling adventure to challenge the eight Gym Leaders in their respective cities.

However, Team Rocket, led by Giovanni, is also on the hunt for rare and powerful Pokémon. They plan to steal the legendary Pokémon Mewtwo, which has been hidden away for years. Ash and his friends soon find themselves caught up in Team Rocket's sinister plans.

As they journey through different regions, Ash and Pikachu face numerous challenges and obstacles, including battling fierce wild Pokémon and overcoming treacherous terrain. Along the way, Ash learns valuable lessons about friendship, perseverance, and believing in himself.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Ash and Giovanni at the Indigo Plateau, where the eight Gym Leaders gather to compete for the title of Pokémon Master. With Pikachu by his side, Ash faces off against Team Rocket's powerful Pokémon, including Meowth and Arbok.

In a thrilling finale, Ash and Pikachu use their combined strength and teamwork to defeat Team Rocket and Giovanni, saving Mewtwo from falling into the wrong hands. The movie concludes with Ash and his friends celebrating their victory and looking forward to their next adventure together.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and engaging, bringing the beloved Pokémon characters to life in a way that will delight both old and new fans of the franchise. The story is full of action, humor, and heart, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Pokémon the Movie: I Choose You! is a fun and exciting adventure that celebrates the spirit of friendship, teamwork, and believing in oneself. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, this movie is sure to delight fans of the Pokémon franchise and newcomers alike.

overview: Rattled by sudden unemployment, a Manhattan couple surveys alternative living options, ultimately deciding to experiment with living on a rural commune where free love rules.
tagline: Leave your baggage behind
title: Wanderlust
plot:
Wanderlust is a 2012 American romantic comedy film directed by David Wain. The movie follows the story of George and Molly, a couple who are struggling with their mundane lives in suburban America. They embark on a journey to find meaning and connection, leading them to join a hippie commune.

The main theme of Wanderlust revolves around the search for authenticity and freedom. The film critiques societal expectations and the monotony of modern life, as embodied by George's corporate job and Molly's stay-at-home mom role. As they immerse themselves in the commune, they begin to question their own identities and desires, leading to a journey of self-discovery.

The movie also explores themes of love, relationships, and community. The characters' experiences at the commune serve as a catalyst for them to re-evaluate their connections with each other and with others. Through their interactions with the commune's eccentric residents, George and Molly learn to let go of their inhibitions and find new ways of expressing themselves.

Furthermore, Wanderlust touches on the idea of escapism and the human desire to break free from societal norms. The film pokes fun at the excesses of the hippie movement while also celebrating its ideals of freedom and nonconformity. Ultimately, the movie suggests that true fulfillment can be found by embracing one's individuality and finding a sense of belonging in a community that values authenticity and connection.

Overall, Wanderlust is a lighthearted and humorous exploration of themes that are both universally relatable and uniquely quirky.

original_title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery
overview: World-famous detective Benoit Blanc heads to Greece to peel back the layers of a mystery surrounding a tech billionaire and his eclectic crew of friends.
title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery
plot:
Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is a 2022 American mystery film written and directed by Rian Johnson and produced by Johnson and Ram Bergman. A standalone sequel to Knives Out (2019), it stars Daniel Craig as the detective Benoit Blanc, who takes on a new case involving the tech billionaire Miles Bron and his circle of friends. Edward Norton plays Bron, and the ensemble cast includes Janelle Monáe, Kathryn Hahn, Leslie Odom Jr., Jessica Henwick, Madelyn Cline, Kate Hudson and Dave Bautista. Netflix acquired the rights to two Knives Out sequels in 2021 for a reported $469 million.

In May 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, Miles Bron, co-founder of the technology company Alpha, invites his old friends, who call themselves the "Disruptors," to a murder mystery weekend at his estate on a private Greek island, sending each an elaborate puzzle box. The guests are Alpha's head scientist Lionel Toussaint; Connecticut governor Claire Debella; the tactless model turned fashion designer Birdie Jay; the men's rights streamer Duke Cody; and Cassandra "Andi" Brand, Alpha's ousted co-founder, who is estranged from the others after a bitter lawsuit. They are joined by Birdie's assistant Peg, Duke's girlfriend Whiskey and, unexpectedly, Benoit Blanc, who says he received an invitation that Miles insists he never sent.

At the island's centerpiece, a giant glass dome called the Glass Onion, Miles shows off his art collection, including the Mona Lisa on loan from the Louvre, and reveals that the estate runs on Klear, a new hydrogen-based fuel he plans to launch despite warnings from Lionel and Claire that it is dangerous. Blanc quickly realizes that every guest owes Miles something and that each has a motive to harm him, and that Andi, in particular, believes her friends lied under oath to help Miles take control of the company. When the weekend's playful murder game is interrupted by a real death, Blanc must untangle a web of secrets in which nothing is quite what it seems, and the film revisits earlier events from a new perspective.

Glass Onion premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2022, played in cinemas for a limited one-week run in November and was released on Netflix in December. It received widespread acclaim for its screenplay, humor and performances, especially Monáe's, and earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay.

overview: When Lou, who has become the "father of the Internet," is shot by an unknown assailant, Jacob and Nick fire up the time machine again to save their friend.
tagline: The Laws of Space and Time are About to be Violated.
title: Hot Tub Time Machine 2
plot:
Hot Tub Time Machine 2 is a comedy film that explores the consequences of playing with time and the importance of friendship. The movie delves into the theme of nostalgia, as the characters struggle to come to terms with the passing of time and the loss of their youth.

The film also touches on the idea of regret and the what-ifs of life. As the characters are transported back in time again, they are forced to confront their past mistakes and the choices they made that led them down a certain path. This theme is woven throughout the story, as the characters grapple with the consequences of their actions and try to make amends.

Furthermore, Hot Tub Time Machine 2 examines the concept of identity and how it changes over time. As the characters navigate different eras, they are forced to confront their own identities and the people they have become. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Adam, who struggles to reconcile his past and present selves.

Ultimately, the movie suggests that true friendship and camaraderie can help us navigate the complexities of life and find our way back to ourselves. Through its lighthearted and humorous tone, Hot Tub Time Machine 2 offers a heartwarming exploration of the human experience.

overview: Pro quarter-back, Paul Crewe and former college champion and coach, Nate Scarboro are doing time in the same prison. Asked to put together a team of inmates to take on the guards, Crewe enlists the help of Scarboro to coach the inmates to victory in a football game 'fixed' to turn out quite another way.
tagline: If you can't get out, get even.
title: The Longest Yard
plot:
The Longest Yard is a sports comedy film directed by Peter Segal, released in 2005. The movie stars Adam Sandler as Paul Crewe, a former NFL quarterback who becomes a coach at a minimum-security prison.

Paul Crewe (Adam Sandler) was once a successful NFL quarterback but lost his job and reputation after being involved in a scandal that led to the death of an opponent on the field. He is sentenced to 3 years in prison for manslaughter. While serving his time, he becomes the coach of the prison's football team, which has not won a game in over 40 years.

Crewe's goal is to lead the team to victory and prove that even in a place like this, there can be redemption and hope. However, he faces opposition from the corrupt warden, George "The King" Weathers (Burt Reynolds), who wants to keep the prison's football team losing so that the inmates will stay docile and obedient.

As Crewe tries to whip his team into shape, he also has to deal with the harsh realities of prison life. He befriends a fellow inmate, Caretaker (Chris Rock), who becomes his assistant coach. Together, they try to motivate their teammates and overcome the obstacles that stand in their way.

Throughout the movie, Crewe's character undergoes significant development as he learns to balance his desire for revenge against Weathers with his newfound sense of purpose and responsibility as a coach. He also starts to form connections with some of the inmates, including Caretaker, who becomes like a protégé to him.

As the team begins to win games, Crewe's reputation grows, and he becomes a symbol of hope for the inmates. However, Weathers will stop at nothing to crush their spirits and maintain his own power over the prison.

In the climactic final game, Crewe's team faces off against Weathers' favorite team, led by the ruthless and arrogant quarterback, Shane Falco (David Spade). The game is intense, with both teams fighting for victory. In the end, Crewe's team emerges victorious, and he finally gets his revenge against Weathers.

The movie ends on a high note, with Crewe's team celebrating their win and Crewe himself finding redemption and a new sense of purpose. He has proven that even in the darkest of places, there is always hope for change and redemption.

Overall, The Longest Yard is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and heart. It features strong performances from Adam Sandler and Burt Reynolds, as well as a talented supporting cast.

overview: When the White House (Secret Service Code: "Olympus") is captured by a terrorist mastermind and the President is kidnapped, disgraced former Presidential guard Mike Banning finds himself trapped within the building. As the national security team scrambles to respond, they are forced to rely on Banning's inside knowledge to help retake the White House, save the President and avert an even bigger disaster.
tagline: When our flag falls our nation will rise.
title: Olympus Has Fallen
plot:
Olympus Has Fallen is a 2013 American political action thriller directed and co-produced by Antoine Fuqua from a screenplay by Creighton Rothenberger and Katrin Benedikt, the first installment of the Has Fallen series. Gerard Butler, who also co-produced, stars as a disgraced Secret Service agent, with Aaron Eckhart as the President and Morgan Freeman as the Speaker of the House, alongside Angela Bassett, Ashley Judd, Melissa Leo, Dylan McDermott and Rick Yune.

Mike Banning, a former Army Ranger on the presidential detail, has grown close to President Benjamin Asher, First Lady Margaret and their young son, Connor. When the presidential limousine skids off an icy bridge during a winter drive, Banning pulls the President to safety but cannot save Margaret. Eighteen months later, he has been moved off the detail to a desk job at the Treasury Department.

During a visit by the South Korean prime minister, a commando unit led by the North Korean terrorist Kang Yeonsak launches a coordinated air and ground assault on Washington and seizes the White House, aided by Dave Forbes, a former Secret Service agent working in private security. Asher and members of his cabinet are taken hostage in the underground bunker, and the prime minister is executed on camera. Banning fights his way into the building and makes contact with Speaker Allan Trumbull, now acting president, and Secret Service director Lynne Jacobs at the Pentagon. Kang demands the withdrawal of American forces from the Korean peninsula, but his real goal is Cerberus, a system for destroying nuclear missiles in flight, which he plans to use to detonate America's arsenal in its silos. It can be activated only with codes held by Asher and two senior officials.

Operating alone inside the White House, Banning rescues Connor, kills Forbes and many of the attackers, and destroys the anti-aircraft weapons that annihilated a military helicopter assault. Kang executes hostages in reprisal, then fakes his own and Asher's deaths in a helicopter explosion to cover an escape. Banning sees through the ruse, kills Kang in the bunker, and with Trumbull's guidance shuts down Cerberus with seconds to spare before escorting Asher out.

Released by FilmDistrict on March 22, 2013, it grossed about $170 million worldwide against a $70 million budget. Reviews were mixed, praising the action and Butler but faulting the violence and script. It was followed by London Has Fallen (2016) and Angel Has Fallen (2019).

overview: At an elite boarding school for girls, six friends jokingly engage in a late night ritual, calling forth the spirit of a dead former student who reportedly haunts their halls. Before morning, one of the girls is dead, leaving the others wondering what they may have awakened.
title: Seance
plot:
Seance is a 2021 supernatural horror slasher film written and directed by Simon Barrett, known as the screenwriter of You're Next and The Guest, in his feature directorial debut. It stars Suki Waterhouse as Camille Meadows, with Madisen Beaty, Inanna Sarkis, Ella-Rae Smith, Stephanie Sy, Djouliet Amara, Jade Michael, Seamus Patterson and Marina Stephenson Kerr. Set in an exclusive boarding school, the film blends ghost story and murder mystery.

One night at the Edelvine Academy for Girls, a clique led by the cruel and popular Alice plays a prank on their classmate Kerrie by staging an appearance of the Edelvine Ghost, the legend of a student who once took her own life at the school. Shaken, Kerrie returns to her room, where she glimpses a figure watching her; moments later the girls hear her scream and find that she has fallen to her death from her window.

Soon afterward, a new student, Camille Meadows, arrives to take Kerrie's place and is assigned her old room, where strange things begin to happen. After a fight with Alice and her friends, Bethany, Yvonne, Rosalind and Lenora, Camille and her roommate Helina are given detention with the group in the library, where Alice persuades them to hold a séance to contact Kerrie. To everyone's surprise, a spirit answers and warns them that they will be murdered. That same night Lenora vanishes, and the school assumes she has run away, but a blood-drawn symbol in her room suggests otherwise. As more girls die in apparent accidents, Camille, Helina and the remaining members of the clique must determine whether they are being hunted by a vengeful ghost or by a very human killer, while Camille hides secrets of her own.

Barrett plays with the conventions of the boarding-school ghost story before turning the film into a slasher mystery with an unexpected climax.

Seance was released by RLJE Films on May 21, 2021. Reviews were mixed: it holds 47 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said Barrett has filmmaking flair but not enough to lift a somewhat pedestrian story, while IndieWire's Kate Erbland noted that it grows more convoluted as it goes on.

overview: Jack Torrance accepts a caretaker job at the Overlook Hotel, where he, along with his wife Wendy and their son Danny, must live isolated from the rest of the world for the winter. But they aren't prepared for the madness that lurks within.
tagline: He came as the caretaker, but this hotel had its own guardians - who'd been there a long time
title: The Shining
plot:
The Shining is a psychological horror film directed by Stanley Kubrick, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The movie was released in 1980 and produced by Hawk Films.

The story begins with Jack Torrance (played by Jack Nicholson), a struggling writer and former teacher who takes a job as the winter caretaker of the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado. Jack, along with his wife Wendy (Shelley Duvall) and their son Danny (Danny Lloyd), moves to the hotel, hoping that the isolation will help him overcome his personal demons and focus on his writing.

Upon arrival, they are greeted by the hotel's manager, Stuart Ullman (Barry Nelson), who warns them about the hotel's dark past and the supernatural forces that reside within its walls. However, Jack is skeptical of these warnings and sees the job as an opportunity to escape his troubles and find inspiration for his writing.

As the winter weather sets in, Jack becomes increasingly unhinged due to the isolation and the hotel's eerie atmosphere. He begins to experience strange visions and hears voices, which he initially attributes to the stress of his new role. However, it soon becomes clear that something more sinister is at play.

Danny, who possesses a unique psychic ability known as "the shine," begins to experience terrifying visions and premonitions, including a recurring nightmare about a grizzly bear attacking him. As Jack's behavior becomes more erratic, Wendy starts to suspect that he has become possessed by the hotel's dark forces.

As the winter weather intensifies, Jack's sanity unravels completely, and he becomes violent towards his family. In a shocking turn of events, Jack freezes to death in the hedge maze outside the hotel, while Wendy and Danny are forced to flee for their lives.

The film's climax features an iconic scene where Wendy and Danny escape from the hotel by driving away in a snowcat, leaving behind the possessed Jack. The final shot of the film shows a photograph on the hotel's door, which appears to be a picture of Jack standing in front of the hotel, with his eyes black as coal.

Throughout the film, Kubrick masterfully builds tension and suspense, using long takes, eerie sound design, and an unsettling score to create a sense of unease. The Shining is widely regarded as one of the greatest horror films of all time, and its influence can still be felt in popular culture today.

It's worth noting that Stanley Kubrick was known for his meticulous attention to detail and his desire to control every aspect of his films. He worked closely with Stephen King to adapt the novel into a screenplay, but ultimately decided to deviate from the original story, which led to some controversy among fans of the book. Despite this, The Shining remains a masterpiece of horror cinema that continues to captivate audiences to this day.

overview: Sarah Nolan is a newly divorced woman cautiously rediscovering romance with the enthusiastic but often misguided help of her well-meaning family. As she braves a series of hilarious disastrous mismatches and first dates, Sarah begins to trust her own instincts again and learns that, no matter what, it's never a good idea to give up on love.
tagline: The hardest trick is making them stay.
title: Must Love Dogs
plot:
Must Love Dogs is a romantic comedy that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and personal growth. The film delves into the theme of finding one's true self and embracing vulnerability in order to form meaningful connections with others.

The movie follows the story of Sarah (played by Diane Lane), a successful businesswoman who has given up on love after a string of failed relationships. She makes a pact with her friends to remain single for a year, but things take an unexpected turn when she meets Jake (played by John Cusack), a charming and handsome dog trainer.

As Sarah navigates her feelings for Jake, the film explores the idea that true love requires embracing one's flaws and imperfections. The movie shows how Sarah learns to let go of her defenses and open herself up to the possibility of love, ultimately discovering that it's okay to be vulnerable and take risks in relationships.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Sarah is forced to re-evaluate her priorities and values in life. Through her journey, she learns to balance her career ambitions with her desire for personal fulfillment and happiness.

Overall, Must Love Dogs is a heartwarming romantic comedy that celebrates the beauty of love, relationships, and personal growth.

overview: Tragedy, betrayal and a mysterious discovery fuel a woman's vengeance for the loss of her tribe and family.
tagline: And so it begins.
title: Kingdom: Ashin of the North
plot:
Kingdom: Ashin of the North (Korean: Kingdom: Ashinjeon) is a 2021 South Korean historical horror thriller, a feature-length special of the Netflix zombie series Kingdom, written by series creator Kim Eun-hee and directed by Kim Seong-hun. Running about 93 minutes, it serves as a sidequel to the second season and explores the backstory of Ashin, the mysterious woman glimpsed in that season's finale, as well as the origin of the resurrection plant behind the plague. Jun Ji-hyun stars as Ashin, with Kim Si-a as the young Ashin, Park Byung-eun as Min Chi-rok, Kim Roi-ha as her father Ta Hab, Koo Kyo-hwan as the Jurchen leader Ai Da Gan, and Jung Suk-won and Kwon Bum-taek reprising their series roles.

Decades before the events of Kingdom, young Ashin lives with her father and ailing mother in a village on the northern border of Joseon. Her people, the Seongjeoyain, are Jurchen by origin, but because they have lived on Joseon land for so long they are shunned as traitors by the Jurchen and treated as second-class citizens in Joseon. With the kingdom weakened by the Japanese invasion in the south, the border becomes a flashpoint as Jurchen warriors sense that Joseon forces are stretched thin, and a dispute over hunting territory threatens all-out war. While Ashin searches for the legendary resurrection flower to save her mother, her family and neighbors are slaughtered, caught in the crossfire. Orphaned and alone, she discovers an abandoned shrine deep in the forest whose ancient murals reveal the plant's power to raise the dead. Consumed by grief, she grows into a cold, formidable warrior and archer, works her way in among those she needs, and patiently plots a terrible revenge to avenge the Seongjeoyain and wipe out both Joseon and the Jurchen, setting in motion the zombie outbreak that will later sweep the country.

Kingdom: Ashin of the North was released on Netflix on 23 July 2021. Reviews were very positive. NME's Hidzir Junaini called it an epic, tragic and enthralling antihero story that deepens the franchise's mythology, praising Kim Eun-hee's writing, which makes viewers root for Ashin's vengeance before being horrified by its scale, and the striking northern landscapes. Decider's Jade Budowski recommended it as a cinematic marvel that works even for newcomers to the series, likening its scale to Game of Thrones and singling out Kim Si-a's gutting performance as the young Ashin. Some critics felt it thinner than the main series.

overview: Set on an island off the coast of New England in the summer of 1965, Moonrise Kingdom tells the story of two twelve-year-olds who fall in love, make a secret pact, and run away together into the wilderness. As various authorities try to hunt them down, a violent storm is brewing off-shore – and the peaceful island community is turned upside down in more ways than anyone can handle.
tagline: A tormenting and surprising story of children and adults during the stormy days of the summer of 1965.
title: Moonrise Kingdom
plot:
Moonrise Kingdom is a 2012 American romantic fantasy film written and directed by Wes Anderson. It was produced by Scott Rudin Productions, in association with Fox Searchlight Pictures.

The main themes of Moonrise Kingdom revolve around the complexities of human relationships, isolation, and the power of love to transcend societal norms. Here's a breakdown of the plot development and ending:

Beginning:
The film takes place in 1965 on an isolated island off the coast of New England. We meet two outsiders: Sam (Jared Gilman), a shy and introverted 12-year-old boy, and Suzy (Kara Hayward), a free-spirited and independent 12-year-old girl who live on opposite sides of the island. They fall in love, but their relationship is forbidden by society.

Plot Development:
As the story unfolds, we see Sam and Suzy's romance blossom despite the disapproval of their families and the community. The two embark on a journey to escape their circumstances, accompanied by a group of misfit outsiders who become their allies. Along the way, they face various challenges, including encounters with the island's strict authorities and the harsh realities of adulthood.

Ending:
Ultimately, Sam and Suzy's love prevails, but not without some sacrifices. The film concludes with a poignant and bittersweet ending, as the two lovers part ways to start new lives, leaving behind their childhood dreams and the freedom they once knew. However, the ending also suggests that their love will endure, even if it's in a more subtle and mature form.

Themes:
Throughout the film, Anderson explores several themes, including:

1. The power of love: Moonrise Kingdom celebrates the transformative power of love to bring people together and transcend societal norms.
2. Isolation and belonging: The film highlights the tension between feeling isolated and finding one's place in the world.
3. Coming-of-age: Sam and Suzy's journey is a classic coming-of-age story, as they navigate the complexities of adolescence and learn to let go of their childhood dreams.
4. Nonconformity: The film celebrates individuality and nonconformity, encouraging viewers to challenge societal norms and forge their own paths.

Overall, Moonrise Kingdom is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, and identity in a way that's both poignant and entertaining.

overview: The world is falling into chaos. As he roams a crumbling city, Duncan MacLeod, the Highlander, remembers happier times before the love of his life left... Hopeless and alone, MacLeod finds his way to a band of immortal companions, including his mysterious friend Methos, and a mortal, Watcher Joe Dawson. Together this small group sets out on a quest to find the origin of the first Immortal.
tagline: In a world without end, their will is eternal. But a quest for the source of immortality will awaken the Guardian.
title: Highlander: The Source
plot:
Highlander: The Source, released in some countries as Highlander 5: The Source, is a 2007 American science fantasy action film directed by Brett Leonard and the fifth installment of the Highlander film series. Like its predecessor, Highlander: Endgame, it follows the continuity of Highlander: The Series, with Adrian Paul reprising his role as the immortal swordsman Duncan MacLeod, alongside Peter Wingfield as Methos, Jim Byrnes as Joe Dawson, Thekla Reuten as Anna Teshemka and Cristian Solimeno as the Guardian. It is the only film in the series not to feature the original protagonist, Connor MacLeod.

In a possible future, society has partly collapsed into violence and chaos, with gangs fighting over territory and many people reduced to scavenging. A group of immortals who still possess resources and advanced technology, including the ancient Methos, a computer hacker named Reggie, the warrior Zai Jie and Cardinal Giovanni, a representative of the Vatican, is searching for the Source of Immortality. When Zai Jie finds a lead to its location, he is killed by the Guardian of the Source, a monstrous immortal of unnatural speed.

Methos asks his old friend Joe Dawson to find Duncan MacLeod, who has been wandering alone since separating from his mortal wife Anna, who left him because he cannot father children. After surviving an attack by the Guardian, Duncan joins the group, and they travel to a monastery to consult the Elder, an ancient being who can help them find the Source.
