As Satan, in the banker's body, leaves a trail of destruction across the city, Jericho takes it upon himself to protect Christine from the cult, from Satan and from a faction within the Vatican that believes the only way to prevent the apocalypse is to kill her. His battle against overwhelming supernatural power becomes a test of his lost faith as the countdown to the millennium approaches.

End of Days received mostly negative reviews, with critics criticizing its script and tone, although Byrne's performance as Satan drew praise. It grossed about $212 million worldwide. It was Schwarzenegger's first starring role after undergoing heart surgery in 1997, and it was noted as one of his rare roles playing a vulnerable, emotionally broken hero.

overview: Since the moment they met at age 5, Rosie and Alex have been best friends, facing the highs and lows of growing up side by side. A fleeting shared moment, one missed opportunity, and the decisions that follow send their lives in completely different directions. As each navigates the complexities of life, love, and everything in between, they always find their way back to each other - but is it just friendship, or something more?
tagline: Right Love. Wrong Time.
title: Love, Rosie
plot:
Love, Rosie is a 2014 romantic comedy-drama directed by Christian Ditter from a screenplay by Juliette Towhidi, adapted from Cecelia Ahern's 2004 novel Where Rainbows End. Lily Collins and Sam Claflin star as two lifelong friends in Dublin whose romance is repeatedly thwarted, with Christian Cooke, Tamsin Egerton, Suki Waterhouse, Jamie Beamish and Jaime Winstone in supporting roles.

Rosie and Alex have been inseparable since childhood. On Rosie's eighteenth birthday they share a drunken kiss, and Alex realizes he loves her, but the next morning a hungover Rosie, who remembers nothing, says she wishes the night had never happened, and Alex takes this as rejection. Rosie goes to the school dance with Greg, the most attractive boy in their year, while Alex pairs off with the popular Bethany. Rosie and Alex both win places to study in Boston, Alex at Harvard and Rosie in hotel management, but Rosie becomes pregnant after her night with Greg. Unwilling to hold Alex back, she conceals the pregnancy and stays home, giving birth to a daughter, Katie, while Alex leaves for America; when he learns the truth, he becomes Katie's godfather.

Over the following years their lives keep pulling them apart. A visit to Boston ends badly when Rosie learns that Alex's girlfriend Sally is pregnant. Rosie marries Greg, who returns after having fled to Ibiza when he heard of her pregnancy, but he proves unfaithful and unreliable. When Rosie's father dies, Alex writes her a letter declaring that she deserves a better man and that he could be him, but Greg hides it. By the time Rosie leaves her husband and finds the letter, Alex is engaged to Bethany, and Rosie is asked to be his "best man."

At the wedding reception Rosie gives a speech celebrating their friendship, and Alex finally learns that she never remembered their first kiss. Rosie uses her inheritance to open her own small hotel, and Alex eventually turns up as a guest, where the two at last acknowledge their feelings and kiss.

The film premiered in London on October 6, 2014, and was shot in Toronto and Dublin. It received largely negative reviews, though audiences responded more warmly, and grossed about $25.5 million worldwide. Rotten Tomatoes reports 32% approval, its consensus calling the leads appealing but undone by a clichéd story. Collins's performance was widely singled out for praise.

original_title: 劇場版 BLEACH MEMORIES OF NOBODY
overview: In Karakura Town, unidentifiable spirits begin appearing en mases. While attempting to deal with these strange souls, Ichigo Kurosaki and Rukia Kuchiki meet Senna, a mysterious shinigami who wipes out most of them. Senna refuses to answer any questions, so Ichigo is forced to follow her while Rukia tries to find out what's going on.
title: Bleach the Movie: Memories of Nobody
plot:
Bleach: Memories of Nobody is a 2006 Japanese animated supernatural action film, the first feature adapted from Tite Kubo's Bleach manga and anime. It was directed by Noriyuki Abe and written by Masashi Sogo, with Masakazu Morita voicing Ichigo Kurosaki and Fumiko Orikasa voicing Rukia Kuchiki. It opened in Japanese cinemas on December 16, 2006.

Ichigo and Rukia are Soul Reapers, who guide the souls of the dead to the afterlife realm of the Soul Society and fight Hollows, monstrous lost souls. After they slay a Hollow in a Karakura Town park, strange ghostly white figures begin to appear, and a mysterious female Soul Reaper named Senna arrives to destroy them. She refuses to answer their questions, and while Rukia returns to the Soul Society for information, Ichigo follows the cheerful, headstrong girl around town. Investigators from the Soul Society reveal that the figures are Blanks, amnesiac souls lost in the space between worlds, whose combined memories form an entity called the Shinenju. Their realm, the Valley of Screams, is being pushed toward a collision with both the human world and the Soul Society, apparently by someone seeking the Shinenju.

Ichigo protects Senna from an attack by a mysterious group, and the two spend time together reuniting lost souls. When Soul Society forces declare that Senna herself is the Shinenju, and order Ichigo to surrender her, he refuses, insisting that she is a person in her own right. The attackers, revealed as the Dark Ones, a band of exiles seeking revenge on the Soul Society, abduct Senna and bind her to a device in the Valley of Screams that will cause the worlds to collide. The Soul Society's head captain prepares to destroy the Valley, but Ichigo's Soul Reaper allies join him in a desperate rescue, defeating the Dark Ones while Ichigo overcomes their leader, Ganryu.

The collapse continues until Senna sacrifices herself to push the worlds apart. Weakened and fading, she asks Ichigo to show her a gravestone bearing the name she believes is hers; he kindly lets her believe it, and she fades away content, as the memories of her begin to vanish from everyone but him.

The film was released in a limited run in the United States in June 2008, followed by a DVD that October. Reviewers generally judged it a fan-pleasing spin-off, praising its production values and the character of Senna while noting its confusing moments and lack of impact on the series.

overview: A getaway driver for a bank robbery realizes he has been double crossed and races to find out who betrayed him.
tagline: Drive fast. Think faster.
title: Wheelman
plot:
Wheelman is a 2017 action thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The movie follows the story of Ben, a former getaway driver who is forced back into his old life after being double-crossed by his associates.

At its core, Wheelman explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal. Ben's world is turned upside down when he discovers that those he trusted have abandoned him, leaving him to pick up the pieces of his shattered life. This sense of betrayal serves as a catalyst for Ben's downward spiral, as he becomes increasingly consumed by anger and a desire for revenge.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and redemption. As Ben navigates the treacherous underworld of organized crime, he is forced to confront the choices he made in the past and the person he has become. Through his journey, Ben grapples with the idea of finding redemption and making amends for past mistakes.

Furthermore, Wheelman critiques the notion of toxic masculinity and the dangers of unchecked aggression. Ben's character embodies a toxic form of masculinity that is rooted in violence and control, but as the story progresses, it becomes clear that this persona is both a product of his environment and a destructive force that threatens to consume him.

Ultimately, Wheelman presents a complex and thought-provoking exploration of human nature, one that raises questions about the consequences of our actions and the fragility of the human psyche.

overview: A dad moves into a new house with his son and girlfriend. When he's out of town working, the son makes a new "friend" next doors.
title: The Other Side
plot:
The Other Side (Swedish: Andra sidan), released internationally as The Evil Next Door, is a 2020 Swedish supernatural horror film and the first feature from writer-directors Oskar Mellander and Tord Danielsson. Dilan Gwyn stars as Shirin, with Linus Wahlgren as her boyfriend Fredrik, Eddie Eriksson Dominguez as his young son Lukas, Henrik Norlén as Peter Lindvall, Karin Holmberg as the teacher Katja and Janna Granström as the neighbour Julia; the contortionist Troy James plays the monster.

After his wife dies of cancer, Fredrik tries to start over by buying one half of a semi-detached house and moving in with Lukas, aged five, and Shirin. Lukas senses that another child once lived in his new room and becomes agitated when Shirin opens a nailed-shut hatch to the attic. Fredrik then takes a job that keeps him away except at weekends, leaving Shirin alone with a boy who still grieves for his mother and who asks whether dead people can come back. When a ball rolls through a gap in the hedge from next door, Lukas decides he has a new friend and begins talking to him through the wall, even though the other half of the house has been empty for years.

The strangeness grows. Lukas is terrified by a creature in the attic, and Shirin hears knocking at night, though police find nothing next door. A neighbour tells her that the previous owners' child vanished without warning, a baby monitor shows a ghostly boy in Lukas's room, and in the empty house she finds a door opening onto a large hole in the floor. Fredrik blames her, but she traces the missing child, Kim, and visits the former owner, Peter Lindvall, whose wife broke down after the loss. Lukas says his friend is kind and wants to stop an old man from taking him too. One night the creature tries to drag Lukas into the attic; after he is treated in hospital, Fredrik throws Shirin out. Visiting Mrs. Lindvall, she learns from a photograph that Kim was a girl and so cannot be Lukas's friend. Returning as the monster carries Lukas off, she follows him down into the hole, faces the creature and claims the boy as hers, and it disappears. Holding Lukas, she sings his mother's lullaby for the first time.

The film opened in Swedish cinemas on 23 October 2020 and was released abroad by Magnet Releasing in 2021. Reviews were mixed: critics credited its moody Scandinavian atmosphere and some effective scares but found it derivative, with thinly drawn characters.

overview: As sadomasochistic yakuza enforcer Kakihara searches for his missing boss he comes across Ichi, a repressed and psychotic killer who may be able to inflict levels of pain that Kakihara has only dreamed of.
tagline: Love really hurts.
title: Ichi the Killer
plot:
Ichi the Killer is a 2001 Japanese psychological horror film directed by Takashi Miike, produced by Kadokawa Shoten Publishing Co., Ltd., and distributed by Toho. The movie is based on the manga of the same name by Hideo Yokoyama.

The main themes of Ichi the Killer revolve around the exploration of human nature, particularly the duality of good and evil, as well as the consequences of violence and trauma. Here's a brief overview of the plot development and ending:

The story follows Kakihara, a young yakuza member who is tasked with bringing a notorious hitman named Ichi to his boss. However, upon meeting Ichi, Kakihara discovers that he is not what he seems, and their relationship becomes complex and twisted.

As the narrative unfolds, it delves into themes of:

1. **The blurred lines between good and evil**: Ichi's character serves as a catalyst for exploring the nature of humanity, highlighting the gray areas between right and wrong.
2. **Trauma and its effects**: The film portrays the devastating consequences of violence, abuse, and trauma on individuals, particularly Kakihara, who becomes increasingly entangled in Ichi's world.
3. **The cyclical nature of violence**: The movie critiques the self-perpetuating cycle of violence within yakuza culture, where members are conditioned to perpetuate harm as a means of survival.
4. **Identity and duality**: Through Kakihara's character, the film explores the tension between his own identity and his association with Ichi, highlighting the complexities of human relationships.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving audiences to ponder the true nature of Ichi and Kakihara's relationship. Ultimately, the movie concludes with a sense of unease, as the audience is left questioning what is real and what is just a product of the characters' twisted perceptions.

Overall, Ichi the Killer is a thought-provoking film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes that are both haunting and unsettling.

overview: A young woman fights the spirit that is slowly taking possession of her.
tagline: Evil will do anything to live.
title: The Unborn
plot:
The Unborn is a 2009 supernatural horror film directed by David S. Goyer and starring Aaron Eckhart, Cam Gigandet, and Gerard Butler.

The story begins with a young woman named Sam (played by Odette Yustman), who has been institutionalized since childhood due to her severe mental illness. She suffers from hallucinations and is unable to distinguish reality from fantasy. As the film progresses, it becomes clear that Sam's condition is not just a product of her imagination, but rather a manifestation of an ancient evil that has taken hold of her.

The plot centers around a mysterious figure known as "The Unborn," who is revealed to be a vengeful spirit born from the fetus of a woman who was brutally murdered by her husband. The Unborn is a malevolent entity with supernatural powers, and it feeds on fear and terror.

As Sam's condition worsens, she begins to experience terrifying hallucinations and visions, which are later revealed to be connected to an ancient ritual that took place in the 17th century. The ritual was performed by a group of women who were seeking revenge against their husbands for their mistreatment.

Gerard Butler plays the role of Father Patrick, a priest who is tasked with performing an exorcism on Sam. However, as the ritual progresses, it becomes clear that Father Patrick's own faith is being tested, and he begins to question whether he can truly save Sam from The Unborn.

Meanwhile, Aaron Eckhart plays the role of Dr. Lawrence Gordon, a psychiatrist who is trying to help Sam overcome her mental illness. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Dr. Gordon has his own secrets and motivations, which are slowly revealed throughout the film.

The climax of the film takes place in an abandoned church, where Father Patrick performs the exorcism ritual on Sam. However, as the ritual reaches its peak, it becomes clear that The Unborn is not just a simple entity - it's a manifestation of the collective guilt and trauma of the women who were involved in the 17th-century ritual.

In the end, Father Patrick manages to perform an exorcism on Sam, but not before she is forced to confront her own dark past and the evil that has taken hold of her. The film ends with Sam seemingly freed from The Unborn's grasp, but the audience is left wondering whether she will ever be truly cured.

Overall, The Unborn is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of trauma, guilt, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it has developed a loyal fan base over the years, and its unique blend of supernatural horror and psychological thriller elements makes it a compelling watch for fans of the genre.

overview: A rag tag unit of misfits known as the War Pigs must go behind enemy lines to exterminate Nazis by any means necessary.
tagline: Victory is the only option
title: War Pigs
plot:
War Pigs is a 2015 American war drama film directed by Richard Rowley. The movie follows a group of young men who join the US Army in order to escape their mundane lives and find meaning, only to be sent to Iraq as part of the invasion.

The main theme of War Pigs revolves around the disillusionment and frustration felt by these young soldiers as they are thrust into a senseless and brutal conflict. The film explores the emotional toll that war takes on individuals, particularly those who are far from home and have no clear understanding of why they are fighting.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the motivations behind the invasion are complex and multifaceted, driven by a mix of politics, economics, and ideology. However, for the soldiers themselves, the reality of war is often starkly different from the idealized notion of patriotism and heroism that they were sold before enlisting.

The film also touches on themes of identity, belonging, and the search for purpose in life. The characters are all struggling to find their place in the world, and the experience of war serves as a catalyst for them to confront their own insecurities and fears.

Ultimately, War Pigs is a powerful anti-war statement that challenges the notion of patriotism and heroism in the face of senseless violence and destruction.

overview: A motorcycle stunt rider considers committing a crime in order to provide for his wife and child, an act that puts him on a collision course with a cop-turned-politician.
tagline: One moment can change your life.
title: The Place Beyond the Pines
plot:
The Place Beyond the Pines is a 2013 American drama film written and directed by Damien Chazelle, produced by Sidney Kimmel Entertainment. The movie follows three interconnected storylines that explore themes of family, loyalty, and redemption.

The film begins with Jason Brody (Ryan Gosling), a former motorcycle stunt performer who has retired to live a quiet life in a small town with his wife, Linda (Carey Mulligan). However, their happiness is short-lived as Jason's estranged son, Tyler (Harrison Ford Jr.), arrives on the scene, seeking financial support. Unbeknownst to Jason, Tyler is involved in a life of crime and has gotten himself into debt.

As the story unfolds, we are introduced to Luke Glanton (Ethan Hawke), a former rodeo rider who has become a mechanic at a local garage. Luke's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Ava (Olivia Wilde), a single mother with a troubled past. The two form a connection, and Luke becomes embroiled in her world.

The third storyline revolves around Robin (Ansel Elgort), a young and ambitious motorcycle stunt performer who idolizes Jason Brody. After a tragic accident leaves him with a serious injury, Robin sets out to find his estranged father, who has abandoned him. Along the way, he meets a local woman named Maya (Dakota Johnson) and becomes entangled in her life.

As the storylines converge, we see how each character's actions have consequences that ripple throughout their lives. Jason Brody is forced to confront his past and take responsibility for his son's actions. Luke Glanton must navigate his complicated feelings for Ava and find a way to redeem himself. Robin, meanwhile, discovers the truth about his father's disappearance and sets out on a journey of self-discovery.

Throughout the film, Chazelle explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption. The title "The Place Beyond the Pines" refers to a mythical place where one can escape their troubles and find solace. However, as the characters navigate their complex lives, they realize that this place is often an illusion, and true redemption requires confronting one's past and taking responsibility for one's actions.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a tragic confrontation between Jason Brody and Tyler, which has devastating consequences for all involved. The ending is both heartbreaking and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of human relationships and the nature of redemption.

Overall, The Place Beyond the Pines is a powerful and emotionally charged drama that explores the complexities of human relationships and the search for redemption. With outstanding performances from its cast and Chazelle's masterful direction, the film is a must-see for fans of drama and thriller genres.

overview: After India's father dies, her Uncle Charlie, who she never knew existed, comes to live with her and her unstable mother. She comes to suspect this mysterious, charming man has ulterior motives and becomes increasingly infatuated with him.
tagline: Innocence Ends.
title: Stoker
plot:
Stoker is a 2013 psychological horror-thriller film directed by Park Chan-wook, starring Mia Wasikowska, Matthew Goode, and Nicole Kidman. The movie follows the story of a young woman named Charlotte Stoker (Mia Wasikowska), who returns home from college to care for her terminally ill mother.

The main themes of Stoker include:

1. **Grief and Mourning**: The film explores the complex emotions that arise when dealing with loss, particularly in the context of grief and mourning. Charlotte's return home is a catalyst for her to confront her feelings about her mother's illness and eventual death.
2. **Female Empowerment**: Stoker features a strong female protagonist who takes control of her life and asserts her independence. Charlotte's journey is one of self-discovery, as she navigates the complexities of adulthood and learns to assert herself in a world dominated by men.
3. **Family Dynamics**: The film examines the intricate web of relationships within the Stoker family, particularly between Charlotte and her mother. The complex dynamics between these characters are revealed through subtle hints and suggestions, adding to the overall sense of unease and tension.
4. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Charlotte navigates her new reality, she begins to question her own identity and sense of self. This theme is closely tied to the film's exploration of grief, mourning, and female empowerment.
5. **The Dark Side of Human Nature**: Stoker features a sinister figure in the character of Uncle Charlie (Matthew Goode), who represents the darker aspects of human nature. His presence serves as a catalyst for Charlotte's journey, forcing her to confront the shadows within herself.

Throughout the film, Park Chan-wook masterfully weaves these themes together, creating a complex and thought-provoking narrative that explores the complexities of human emotions and relationships.

overview: When her idyllic vacation takes an unthinkable turn, Ellen Martin begins investigating a fake insurance policy, only to find herself down a rabbit hole of questionable dealings that can be linked to a Panama City law firm and its vested interest in helping the world's wealthiest citizens amass larger fortunes.
tagline: Panama Papers
title: The Laundromat
plot:
The Laundromat is a 2019 film that delves into the world of international finance and corruption, focusing on the Panama Papers scandal. At its core, the movie explores the theme of power and greed, as embodied by the wealthy and influential individuals who use offshore accounts to hide their ill-gotten gains.

Through the story of Ruth Kramer (played by Julia Roberts), a determined and resourceful woman, the film sheds light on the darker aspects of global finance and the corrupt systems that allow these crimes to thrive. The movie also touches on the theme of accountability, as Ruth's quest for justice puts her at odds with powerful forces that seek to silence her.

Furthermore, The Laundromat critiques the notion of "clean money" and the ways in which wealth can be laundered and hidden from public scrutiny. The film highlights the consequences of this corruption, not only for individuals but also for entire communities and societies as a whole.

Ultimately, the movie serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked power and greed, and the importance of holding those in positions of authority accountable for their actions.

overview: Two top CIA operatives wage an epic battle against one another after they discover they are dating the same woman.
tagline: It's SPY Against SPY
title: This Means War
plot:
This Means War is a 2012 American action comedy film directed by J.P. Beasley and written by Hayley Mills and Michael Markowitz. The movie stars Chris Pine, Tom Hardy, Reese Witherspoon, and Tilda Swinton.

The story revolves around two CIA agents, FDR (Chris Pine) and Tinker (Tom Hardy), who are both assigned to the same female agent, Lauren Scott (Reese Witherspoon). Both men fall in love with Lauren, but they keep their feelings hidden from each other. As they work together to take down a terrorist organization, they engage in an escalating game of one-upmanship, trying to outdo each other and win Lauren's affection.

As the story unfolds, we see FDR and Tinker's contrasting personalities and approaches to their job. FDR is more laid-back and easy-going, while Tinker is intense and aggressive. Despite their differences, they both share a deep commitment to their work and a strong sense of loyalty to each other.

The plot thickens when Lauren becomes the target of a terrorist organization led by a mysterious figure known as "The General" (Tilda Swinton). As FDR and Tinker try to protect Lauren, they must also navigate their complicated feelings for her. The tension between them builds, leading to a series of escalating pranks and one-upmanship.

As the story reaches its climax, FDR and Tinker are forced to work together to take down The General and save Lauren. In the process, they must confront their own emotions and learn to put aside their rivalry for the sake of their mission.

The movie ends with a dramatic showdown between FDR and Tinker, as they face off against The General in a tense battle. In the end, FDR emerges victorious, but not before Tinker reveals that he has fallen deeply in love with Lauren. The movie concludes on a bittersweet note, leaving the audience wondering what will happen next for these two characters.

Overall, This Means War is a fun and action-packed romantic comedy that explores the complexities of male friendship and rivalry. With its witty dialogue and strong performances from the cast, it's a great watch for fans of the genre.

overview: A young girl named June with a big imagination makes an incredible discovery -- the amusement park of her dreams has come to life. Filled with the world's wildest rides operated by fun-loving animals, the excitement never ends. But when trouble hits, June and her misfit team of furry friends begin an unforgettable journey to save the park.
tagline: Dream Bigger
title: Wonder Park
plot:
Wonder Park is a 2019 American animated fantasy adventure comedy produced by Paramount Animation and Nickelodeon Movies, with animation by Ilion Animation Studios, from a screenplay by Josh Appelbaum and André Nemec. Brianna Denski voices the young heroine June Bailey, with Jennifer Garner and Matthew Broderick as her parents and Mila Kunis, John Oliver, Kenan Thompson, Ken Jeong, Norbert Leo Butz and Ken Hudson Campbell as the park's animals. Director Dylan Brown was dismissed by Paramount in early 2018, and the film was released without a credited director on March 15, 2019.

June is an imaginative girl who, with her mother, invents Wonderland, a magical amusement park run by talking animals: Boomer the blue bear, Greta the wild boar, the beaver brothers Gus and Cooper, the porcupine Steve, who secretly loves Greta, and the chimpanzee Peanut, who builds new rides from the ideas whispered to him by June's mother. When her mother falls ill and leaves for treatment, June abandons the game and burns her park plans. Sent off to maths camp, she fears her father cannot cope without her and escapes from the bus to head home.

Lost in the woods, she discovers a real Wonderland, now run-down and engulfed by a menacing cloud called the Darkness that is devouring the park. With the animals she tries to restart the Clockwork Swings, the machine at the heart of the park, but they are attacked by the Chimpanzombies, former plush toys that serve the Darkness. Separated from the others, June finds Peanut hiding in Zero-G Land, where he admits he is lost without the voice in his head. June realises that the Darkness grew out of her own despair over her mother's illness.

When she confesses this, the hurt animals turn their backs on her, and the Chimpanzombies seize Peanut. Discovering that she has been the source of the park's ideas all along, June repairs a ride, catches up with her friends and convinces them she wants to help. She plunges into the Darkness to rescue Peanut, promising to be his imaginative voice, and he conjures an escape slide. Realising that the Clockwork Swings are keyed to her own handwritten name, they restart the machine and clear the Darkness. June returns home to her recovered mother, and together they build a backyard Wonderland.

Wonder Park grossed about 124 million dollars worldwide against a budget estimated at 80 to 100 million dollars, and received generally negative reviews.

overview: In London for the Prime Minister's funeral, Mike Banning discovers a plot to assassinate all the attending world leaders.
tagline: The world's leaders have assembled. So have their enemies.
title: London Has Fallen
plot:
London Has Fallen is a 2016 American action thriller film directed by Babak Anvari and written by David Coggeshall, Art Linson, and John Pogue. The movie stars Gerard Butler, Morgan Freeman, and Angela Bassett.

The film begins with President Benjamin Asher (Morgan Freeman) attending the annual NATO summit in London, where he is greeted as a hero for his efforts to strengthen international relations. However, during the ceremony, a terrorist attack occurs, and the President's motorcade is ambushed by a group of heavily armed assailants.

The attackers, led by the enigmatic and ruthless Abigail Asher (Jordana Brewster), are revealed to be members of a shadowy organization known as "The Syndicate." The group seeks revenge against the United States for its perceived wrongdoings, particularly in regards to the death of their leader, who was killed during a previous operation.

As the President's security detail scrambles to respond to the attack, Mike Banning (Gerard Butler), the former head of the Secret Service, is pulled out of retirement to lead the rescue mission. Banning, who has been struggling with PTSD and personal demons since his last mission went awry, must now confront his past and face off against The Syndicate.

As Banning navigates the treacherous streets of London, he teams up with a local police officer, Detective Sean McPherson (Omar Sy), to track down Abigail Asher and prevent further attacks. Along the way, they encounter a series of deadly obstacles, including a high-speed car chase through the city's streets.

As the stakes escalate, Banning discovers that The Syndicate is planning to assassinate world leaders at various international events, including the G20 summit in China. With time running out, Banning must use his skills and experience to stop Abigail Asher and prevent a global catastrophe.

The film culminates in an intense showdown between Banning and Abigail Asher at the G20 summit. In a tense and action-packed confrontation, Banning manages to defeat Abigail's henchmen and ultimately faces off against her. However, just as he thinks he has won, it is revealed that Abigail was merely a pawn in a larger game.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that the true mastermind behind The Syndicate is none other than President Asher himself. Banning must now confront his own doubts and fears to stop the real enemy and save the world from destruction.

The film ends with Banning emerging victorious, but not without scars. He has finally found redemption and a new purpose in life, and he is ready to face whatever challenges come his way next.

Overall, London Has Fallen is an action-packed thrill ride that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and sacrifice. With its breakneck pace and pulse-pounding action sequences, the film is sure to keep viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish.

overview: In Oklahoma, Agnes, a lonely waitress living in an isolated and dilapidated roadside motel, meets Peter, a quiet and mysterious man with whom she establishes a peculiar relationship.
tagline: Paranoia is contagious
title: Bug
plot:
Bug is a 2006 psychological horror film directed by William Friedkin and written by Tracy Letts, who adapted his own 1996 stage play. Ashley Judd stars as Agnes White, with Michael Shannon, who originated his role on stage, as Peter Evans, and Lynn Collins, Brían F. O'Byrne and Harry Connick Jr. in supporting roles. The film follows a lonely woman in a rural Oklahoma motel who descends into shared paranoia after taking in a mysterious drifter. It debuted at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival and was released by Lionsgate in May 2007.

Agnes is a waitress at a lesbian bar who lives in a run-down motel room on the outskirts of an Oklahoma town. She has never recovered from the disappearance of her young son, Lloyd, nearly ten years earlier, and she numbs herself with drugs and alcohol alongside her friend R.C. She is troubled by silent phone calls that she believes come from her violent ex-husband, Jerry Goss, who has just been released from prison. One night R.C. introduces her to Peter, a quiet, polite drifter, and Agnes, lonely and drawn to his gentleness, lets him stay with her.

Jerry soon shows up, threatening and beating Agnes, and Peter comforts her afterward; the two become lovers. In the middle of the night, Peter claims to have found an aphid in the bed. He reveals that he is a Gulf War veteran who believes he was the subject of secret army experiments and that tiny insects were implanted in his body. Agnes begins to see the bugs too. As Peter's fears of government conspiracy, surveillance and infestation intensify, the couple seal themselves inside the motel room, covering it in insecticide, flypaper and aluminum foil. A man claiming to be Peter's doctor arrives to bring him back, but by then Agnes has fully embraced Peter's delusions, connecting them to her own grief and guilt over her lost son, and the pair spiral toward a terrifying and violent climax.

Bug received generally positive reviews. Critics praised its claustrophobic intensity, Friedkin's direction, its treatment of paranoia and especially the performances of Judd and Shannon, the latter often cited as a breakthrough. Its writing divided critics, and the film was a box-office disappointment, in part because it was marketed as a conventional horror film. It has since gained a cult following as one of Friedkin's notable late works.

overview: The Sorcerer and the White Snake is an ancient Chinese fable about a woman demon who falls in love with a mortal is brought to life through the latest advances in CGI and action techniques.
title: The Sorcerer and the White Snake
plot:
The Sorcerer and the White Snake, previously known as It's Love and Madame White Snake, is a 2011 Chinese-Hong Kong action fantasy film directed by Ching Siu-tung and starring Jet Li as the Buddhist abbot Fahai. Based on the Chinese folk tale Legend of the White Snake, it co-stars Raymond Lam as the herbalist Xu Xian, Eva Huang as the White Snake Susu, Charlene Choi as the Green Snake Qingqing and Wen Zhang as Fahai's apprentice Neng Ren, with Vivian Hsu, Miriam Yeung and Chapman To in supporting roles.

Abbot Fahai and his young apprentice Neng Ren travel the land subduing demons and imprisoning them in the Lei Feng Pagoda, as they do after capturing an ice harpy on a mountaintop. On another mountain, two snake spirits, Susu and her sister Qingqing, watch a young herbalist, Xu Xian, gathering herbs. When Qingqing frightens him into a lake, Susu takes human form and saves him by breathing her own life essence into him with a kiss. Enchanted by the encounter, Susu follows Xu Xian to the city, where the two fall in love and marry, while he remains unaware that his bride is a snake demon.

Meanwhile, during a fight with bat demons, Neng Ren is bitten and begins turning into a bat demon himself. Fleeing his master, he is befriended by the playful Qingqing and discovers that he has kept his human feelings despite his transformation. Fahai, who believes that humans and demons cannot coexist, becomes suspicious of Susu and gives Xu Xian a dagger capable of killing demons. When Fahai sets out to expose Susu's true nature, she risks everything to protect Xu Xian and their love, defying the abbot in a spectacular confrontation between demon magic and Buddhist power.

The film reinterprets the classic legend as a romantic fantasy about love between humans and spirits, using extensive computer-generated effects and wire-work martial arts.

The film was shot in 3-D and was screened out of competition at the 68th Venice International Film Festival on 3 September 2011. It was released in mainland China on 28 September 2011 and in Hong Kong the following day.

original_title: Rock Dog 2: Rock Around the Park
overview: When Bodi and his band 'True Blue' leave Snow Mountain, to tour with pop sensation, Lil' Foxy, they learn that fame comes at a price.
title: Rock Dog 2: Rock Around the Park
plot:
Rock Dog 2: Rock Around the Park is a 2021 Chinese-American computer-animated musical comedy film directed by Mark Baldo and produced by Huayi Brothers Pictures, Splash Entertainment and HB Wink Animation. A sequel to Rock Dog (2016), one of the most expensive Chinese animated productions, which had flopped at the box office, it replaces the original's celebrity voice cast with a new voice cast led by Graham Hamilton as Bodi, with Ashleigh Ball, Andrew Francis, Kathleen Barr as Lil' Foxy, Brian Drummond, Brian Dobson and Jason Simpson as Lang. Lionsgate released it in the United States on digital platforms in June 2021, followed by DVD and Blu-ray days later; it opened in Russia, Ukraine, Peru and other countries later in 2021 and premiered on Sky Cinema in the United Kingdom in January 2022.

Set a year after the first film, the story follows Bodi, the guitar-playing dog from the village of Snow Mountain, whose power-pop trio True Blue has become the hottest new act in the city, its music radiating waves of blue energy over its fans. The band attracts the attention of Lang, a music-impresario sheep with a fluffy pompadour and a British Invasion accent, who invites them on tour with the pop sensation Lil' Foxy. Lang has hidden agendas: he wants to separate Bodi from his bandmates, to shut down Rock'n'Roll Park, where the city's diehard rockers keep the flame burning, and to harness Bodi's musical energy with a special machine so that he can hypnotise crowds of musicians into his zombie-like followers. Meanwhile, back in Snow Mountain, Bodi's family fret about his sudden fame while profiting from True Blue merchandise, and an avalanche strikes the village. Bodi has to learn the price of fame and how to stay true to himself, his roots and his friends.

Phil Hoad of The Guardian called it a hectic sequel with an all-over-the-place plot, mixing celebrity satire and a nostalgic Asian rural fable with a Zootopia-style city and references from Bill & Ted to the Rolling Stones; he found the animation cheaper and stiffer than the original's and the satire generic, but thought it worldly enough to intrigue pre-teens and credited its finale with a demented energy. Common Sense Media recommended it from age six, praising its messages about self-worth, family, teamwork and humility.

overview: To regain her sense of smell and get back her lover, a detective joins forces with a perfume maker who uses deadly methods to create the perfect scent.
title: The Perfumier
plot:
The Perfumier (German: Der Parfumeur) is a 2022 German crime thriller film written and directed by Nils Willbrandt and produced by Moovie and Constantin Television for Netflix. Very loosely inspired by Patrick Süskind's novel Perfume, it stars Emilia Schüle as Sunny, a police detective who has lost her sense of smell, and Ludwig Simon as Dorian, a perfume maker obsessed with creating the scent of love. The supporting cast includes Sólveig Arnarsdóttir, Anne Müller, Robert Finster and August Diehl.

Sunny is investigating the murders of two women whose bodies were dismembered to remove their sweat glands. At the same time she is consumed by her affair with the married Juro and desperate to keep her sensual hold on him, a struggle made harder by her inability to smell. In the course of the investigation she encounters Dorian, a suspect who is trying to distill the essence of love even if it means drawing on gruesome sources, and she suspects that he may hold the key to restoring her lost sense. When she discovers that one of his compounds has an irresistible effect on Juro, she cannot resist using it. The detective and the suspected killer enter an uneasy partnership in which Dorian tries to help Sunny regain her sense of smell through both physical and psychological methods, seeking to unlock something buried inside her. Dorian, who admits he has never known love, wonders whether he can still create it, and the film explores the links between scent, desire and obsession through surreal, neon-lit imagery, with Sunny narrating the story in voice-over throughout.

The Perfumier was released on Netflix on 21 September 2022. Critics were largely negative, and the film holds a low Rotten Tomatoes score. Marshall Shaffer of Decider called it a confusing, frustrating mix of crime drama, erotic thriller and character study that never makes smell feel real or urgent, though he credited Schüle with a committed performance that makes the most absurd elements plausible. Lori Meek of Ready Steady Cut found it boring and nonsensical, criticizing the relentless narration, one-dimensional characters and pretentious visual style, and noted that the plot shares little with Süskind's book beyond a killer obsessed with scents, recommending the 2006 film Perfume: The Story of a Murderer as a better adaptation.

overview: Continuing his "legendary adventures of awesomeness", Po must face two hugely epic, but different threats: one supernatural and the other a little closer to his home.
tagline: Grab destiny by the rice dumplings.
title: Kung Fu Panda 3
plot:
Kung Fu Panda 3 is a 2016 American computer-animated action comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie is directed by Jennifer Yuh Nelson and Alessandro Carloni, and it marks the third installment in the Kung Fu Panda franchise.

The story begins with Po (voiced by Jack Black), the Dragon Warrior who has been training to become a kung fu master under Master Shifu (voiced by Dustin Hoffman). However, Po's life is disrupted when he discovers that his long-lost father, Li Shan (voiced by Randall Duk Kim), is alive. Li Shan is the emperor of the Valley of Peace and has been searching for Po to fulfill an ancient prophecy.

As Po travels to the Valley of Peace with Master Oogway's (voiced by Randall Duk Kim) spirit, he meets his long-lost father and learns about his heritage as a panda warrior. However, their reunion is short-lived, as they are ambushed by the evil snow leopard, Tai Lung's (voiced by Ian McShane) brother, Kai (voiced by J.K. Simmons).

Kai is a powerful and malevolent spirit who seeks to destroy all the chi in the Valley of Peace, plunging the world into chaos. Po, Li Shan, and their allies must band together to stop Kai and his minions.

Along the way, Po discovers that he has a twin brother, Ping (voiced by Jack Black), who was separated from him at birth. Ping is also a kung fu master, but he lacks the heart and spirit of his brother. Together, the brothers embark on a journey to defeat Kai and save their home.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and memorable characters. The voice cast delivers outstanding performances, with Jack Black bringing his signature energy and charm to Po's character. The film's action sequences are thrilling and well-choreographed, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

As the story unfolds, Po and Ping learn valuable lessons about family, friendship, and finding one's true purpose. In the end, they successfully defeat Kai and restore balance to the Valley of Peace. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of Po and his father reconciling, and Po finally embracing his heritage as a panda warrior.

Overall, Kung Fu Panda 3 is a delightful and action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, family, and self-discovery. With its lovable characters, stunning animation, and engaging storyline, it's a must-watch for fans of the franchise and animation enthusiasts alike.

overview: The lives of two Danish families cross each other, and an extraordinary but risky friendship comes into bud. But loneliness, frailty and sorrow lie in wait.
title: In a Better World
plot:
In a Better World is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of our actions. The film tells the story of a young doctor, Anton Fischer, who becomes embroiled in a complicated web of family dynamics and moral dilemmas.

At its core, In a Better World explores the theme of redemption and personal growth. Through Anton's journey, the film shows how individuals can confront their past mistakes and work towards making amends, not just with others, but also with themselves. This is reflected in the character of Martin, who struggles to come to terms with his own guilt and responsibility for a tragic event.

The movie also examines the complexities of human relationships, particularly those between parents and children, and how these relationships can be both loving and toxic. The character of Susanne, Martin's daughter, serves as a catalyst for exploring these themes, highlighting the difficulties of navigating complex family dynamics and the need for forgiveness and understanding.

Furthermore, In a Better World touches on the theme of social responsibility and the consequences of our actions. Through Anton's work in a Danish hospital, the film sheds light on the complexities of healthcare and the moral dilemmas that come with it. The character of Martin, who is struggling to cope with his past, serves as a reminder of the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and making amends.

Overall, In a Better World is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, personal growth, and social responsibility, inviting viewers to reflect on their own values and moral compass.

overview: Mariachi plunges headfirst into the dark border underworld when he follows a trail of blood to the last of the infamous Mexican drug lords, Bucho, for an action-packed, bullet-riddled showdown. With the help of his best friend and a beautiful bookstore owner, the Mariachi tracks Bucho, takes on his army of desperados, and leaves a trail of blood of his own.
tagline: When the smoke clears, it just means he's reloading.
title: Desperado
plot:
Desperado is a 1995 American action film written and directed by Robert Rodriguez. The movie stars Antonio Banderas as El Mariachi, a Mexican musician who becomes embroiled in a complex web of crime and revenge.

The main themes of Desperado include:

1. **Revenge and Retribution**: The film's central plot revolves around El Mariachi's quest for revenge against the ruthless bandit, Jack (played by Steve Buscemi). As El Mariachi navigates the treacherous landscape of the Mexican underworld, he becomes increasingly consumed by his desire for revenge.
2. **Identity and Belonging**: El Mariachi is a complex character who struggles to find his place in the world. He is a musician, but also a gunslinger, and this dual identity creates tension and conflict within him. Throughout the film, El Mariachi grapples with his sense of self and where he belongs.
3. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: The relationships between characters in Desperado are marked by loyalty and betrayal. El Mariachi's quest for revenge is motivated by a desire to protect his friends and loved ones from harm. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that some characters are willing to betray others for personal gain.
4. **Redemption and Sacrifice**: Ultimately, Desperado is a film about redemption and sacrifice. El Mariachi's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as he learns to confront his demons and make difficult choices in order to achieve his goals.

Overall, Desperado is a gripping and intense action film that explores themes of revenge, identity, loyalty, and redemption. The movie features stunning stunts, memorable characters, and a gripping plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Two estranged brothers reunite at their childhood home in the Alaskan wild. They set out on a two-day hike and are stalked by an unrelenting grizzly bear.
tagline: Hunt or be hunted.
title: Into the Grizzly Maze
plot:
Into the Grizzly Maze, originally titled Red Machine and later Endangered and Grizzly, is a 2015 American action horror film directed by David Hackl from a screenplay by Guy Moshe and Jack Reher. It stars James Marsden as Rowan Moore, Thomas Jane as his brother Beckett, Piper Perabo as Beckett's wife Michelle, Scott Glenn and Billy Bob Thornton as the hunter Douglas. The film follows two estranged brothers stalked by a massive, relentless grizzly bear in the Alaskan wilderness.

As boys, Beckett and Rowan Moore had a terrifying encounter with a grizzly bear in a remote area of the Alaskan wilderness known as the Grizzly Maze. Years later, the brothers have grown apart: Beckett has become a local deputy, while Rowan has just been released from prison. Rowan returns home, and an old friend, Mary Cadillac, asks him to look for her missing husband Johnny. Meanwhile, an enormous grizzly begins killing people in the area, beginning with a group of hunters and then two loggers.

Rowan reunites with Beckett, who has married Michelle, a deaf wildlife photographer and conservationist. Rowan says he has come back to visit the Maze and pay his respects to their late father. When the killings are reported, Douglas, a hunter and butcher, warns that the animal is larger and more cunning than any ordinary bear and offers to track it. As Rowan and Michelle go missing in the Maze, Beckett sets out to find them with Rowan's former girlfriend Kaley. The brothers and their companions are soon trapped in the wilderness with the bear, which is hunting them one by one, and they must put aside their old resentments if they are to survive.

The film combines a creature-feature premise with a family drama about brothers reconciling, set against rugged forest landscapes.

The film's original distributor dropped the project, and Vertical Entertainment and Destination Films released it on video on demand on May 19, 2015, followed by a limited theatrical release on June 26, 2015. It received mixed to negative reviews, with 36 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43.

original_title: 夜明け告げるルーのうた
overview: In a small fishing village, a gloomy middle school student named Kai meets a mermaid named Lu.
title: Lu Over the Wall
plot:
Lu Over the Wall is a 2017 Japanese animated musical fantasy film written and directed by Masaaki Yuasa. The movie follows the story of Riki Nishimura, an 11-year-old boy who moves to a seaside town with his mother, where he discovers that the town's residents are being terrorized by a giant sea monster known as Lu.

The main themes of Lu Over the Wall include:

1. **Isolation and Loneliness**: The movie explores the theme of isolation and loneliness through Riki's character. He is a shy and introverted boy who struggles to make friends in his new town, and his experiences with Lu serve as a catalyst for him to connect with others.
2. **Music as a Form of Expression**: Music plays a central role in the movie, serving as a means of expression and communication between characters. The film's soundtrack features a range of genres, from jazz to rock, which adds to the overall sense of energy and excitement.
3. **The Power of Friendship**: Through Riki's relationships with his friends, including Hana and Shun, the movie highlights the importance of friendship and camaraderie in overcoming adversity.
4. **Embracing One's True Self**: Lu Over the Wall encourages viewers to embrace their true selves and not be afraid to express themselves. The film's protagonist, Riki, learns to accept his own quirks and flaws, which ultimately helps him connect with others.

The movie's unique blend of music, animation, and storytelling creates a captivating narrative that explores these themes in a way that is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

overview: When strange, supernatural murders suddenly become the talk a peaceful town, two detectives must solve a deadly game, but will the myth of this game reveal secrets too close to home.
title: The Darker the Lake
plot:
The Darker the Lake is a 2022 supernatural crime thriller film directed by Lok Kwan Woo, whose earlier films include White Terror and Angels Never Cry, from a screenplay by Z Zoccolante based on Woo's story. Produced by companies including Sky Films, Slater Brothers Entertainment, Seven Look Productions, Error 404 Productions and Udum Media, it stars Elyse Levesque and Veronica Ferres, with Gina Stiebitz, Vladimir Burlakov, Tiffany Hsu, Tsao Yu-ning, Lü Yulai and Ludger Bökelmann in supporting roles. Set in the Austrian town of St. Michael im Lungau, the film was released in the United Kingdom on digital platforms on 21 March 2022 by (Yet) Another Distribution Company and 101 Films, with a 15 certificate.

The story unfolds in two timelines. In 1987, five teenagers in the town play Painkiller, a supernatural game using chess pieces, cards, a lighter and a timekeeper with a watch, in which each player describes a revenge fantasy and the one whose rage is purest is chosen to have their wish granted by an entity that feeds on pain, at a terrible cost. All of them die except Lea (Stiebitz), who is recorded on video saying that her friends are dead and that she may have killed them. In 2021, the peaceful town is shaken by a series of murders and suicides, the latest an old man shooting his best friend dead beside the lake, with chess pieces left at the scenes. Detective Tamara (Levesque) is assigned to investigate, to her annoyance, with a new partner, Lukas (Burlakov), who connects the case to the thirty-year-old footage. The inquiry strikes close to home: the grown-up Lea (Ferres), now blind and still haunted by the entity, is Tamara's mother, and she refuses to talk about the past. As the detectives try to understand the game's deadly myth before anyone else dies, the fraught relationship between mother and daughter comes to the fore.

Reviews were mixed. Road Rash gave it three stars, calling it an enjoyable, creepy film with Nordic noir undertones, attractive yet sinister Austrian scenery, good acting and a neat twist, though its flashbacks could be confusing and several plot points were left unexplained. Mihail Baltateanu of Grimoire of Horror praised it as one of the best-looking independent horror films of the year, with gorgeous wintry photography, but criticised its occasionally stilted dialogue and its reliance on on-screen pages of text as information dumps.

belongs_to_collection.name: Ghost In The Shell: Arise Collection

original_title: 攻殻機動隊 新劇場版
overview: When a ghost-infecting virus known as Fire-Starter begins spreading through the system resulting in the assassination of the Japanese Prime Minister, Major Motoko Kusanagi and her elite team of special operatives are called in to track down its source.
title: Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie
plot:
Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie is a thought-provoking anime film that explores several complex themes. Here are some of the main themes present in the movie:

1. **Existentialism and Identity**: The film delves into the nature of existence, consciousness, and identity. The protagonist, Major Motoko Kusanagi, grapples with her own existence as a cyborg, questioning what it means to be human. This theme is further explored through the character of Batou, who struggles with his own sense of self.

2. **Artificial Intelligence and Humanity**: The movie raises questions about the ethics of creating artificial intelligence that surpasses human capabilities. The cyberpunk world of Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie highlights the blurred lines between humans and machines, making it difficult to distinguish between the two.

3. **Power and Corruption**: The film explores the corrupting influence of power, particularly in the context of government agencies and corporations. The villainous character, Aramaki, represents a powerful figure who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals, highlighting the dangers of unchecked power.

4. **Free Will and Determinism**: The movie touches on the theme of free will versus determinism, as Major Kusanagi navigates her own destiny and confronts the possibility that her actions may be predetermined by external forces.

5. **Social Commentary**: Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie offers a commentary on contemporary societal issues, such as government surveillance, corporate control, and the impact of technology on human relationships.

6. **Self-Discovery and Personal Growth**: Throughout the film, Major Kusanagi undergoes a journey of self-discovery, confronting her own limitations and biases to become a more effective and compassionate leader.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story. The movie's exploration of these ideas makes it a thought-provoking and engaging watch for audiences interested in science fiction and philosophical inquiry.

overview: Calvin is a young novelist who achieved phenomenal success early in his career but is now struggling with his writing – as well as his romantic life. Finally, he makes a breakthrough and creates a character named Ruby who inspires him. When Calvin finds Ruby, in the flesh, sitting on his couch about a week later, he is completely flabbergasted that his words have turned into a living, breathing person.
tagline: She's Out Of His Mind
title: Ruby Sparks
plot:
Ruby Sparks is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Jonathan Dayton and Valerie Faris. The movie stars Paul Dano as Calvin Weir-Field, a writer who creates a fictional character named Ruby Sparks, played by Zoe Kazan.

The main themes of Ruby Sparks revolve around the complexities of love, relationships, and free will. At its core, the film explores the idea that our choices and actions are influenced by our past experiences, emotions, and desires.

Calvin's creation of Ruby Sparks is a metaphor for his own longing for connection and companionship. As he writes her into existence, he becomes increasingly invested in their relationship, but also struggles with the moral implications of controlling someone's life.

Throughout the film, Calvin grapples with the consequences of his actions, as Ruby begins to develop her own agency and desires. The movie raises questions about the nature of love, whether it can be truly selfless or if it's always motivated by personal gain.

The film also touches on themes of identity, creativity, and the power of storytelling. Calvin's writing becomes a form of escapism for him, but also serves as a means to understand himself and his place in the world.

Ultimately, Ruby Sparks is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, love, and the complexities of creating something that can think and feel for itself. The film's ending, which I won't spoil here, leaves the audience pondering the consequences of Calvin's actions and the true nature of love and connection.

overview: Laura and Harrison have the picture-perfect romance built on the foundation of a shared love of music. After a deadly accident, Laura gets the chance to save the love of her life when she discovers that their mixtape can transport her back in time.
tagline: Rewind and love again.
title: Press Play
plot:
Press Play is a 2022 science fiction romantic drama directed by Greg Björkman in his feature debut, from a screenplay he wrote with James Bachelor based on a story by Josh Boone. Clara Rugaard and Lewis Pullman star, with Lyrica Okano, Christina Chang, Matt Walsh and Danny Glover in supporting roles. The film was shot in Hawaii.

Laura, an aspiring artist, is introduced by her friend Chloe to Chloe's stepbrother Harrison, who works at the record store Lost & Found, owned by the kindly Cooper. The two hit it off immediately, going to a Japanese Breakfast concert on their first date, and Harrison gives Laura a blank cassette so they can make a mixtape together. As their romance deepens, Laura is accepted into an art mentorship, and Harrison, who has been accepted to medical school across the country, decides to stay with her. The day after they finish painting a mural together on his birthday, Harrison is hit and killed by a car. Grief-stricken, Laura leaves the unfinished mixtape behind at the store.

Four years later, at Chloe's wedding, Cooper returns the tape. When Laura plays it, she discovers that each song transports her briefly back to the moment in her past when it was recorded. Using these short visits, she warns Harrison of his death, but each time she returns to the present, he has died in a different way, while her interventions have also altered other lives, such as Chloe's marriage. In one timeline the store burns down with Harrison inside, and Laura confides in a heartbroken Cooper, who suggests she may not be meant to save him. Desperate, she even tells Harrison to break up with her and go to medical school, but he refuses, saying he would rather stay with her and risk dying anyway.

Finally accepting that she cannot keep him, Laura discovers a hidden extra song on the tape's B-side, which takes her back to the moment before she first met Harrison. She chooses not to walk into the store, sacrificing their relationship to spare his life. Back in the present, the timeline has been restored, Chloe is happily married to her true partner, and Laura is invited to a family Christmas dinner, where Harrison arrives and introduces himself to her as a stranger.

The Avenue acquired the film and released it in US theaters and on digital platforms on June 24, 2022. Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes reported that 67% of 18 critics gave it a positive review.

overview: In 1950s Ireland and New York, young Eilis Lacey has to choose between two men and two countries.
tagline: Two countries, two loves, one heart
title: Brooklyn
plot:
Brooklyn is a 2015 romantic period drama directed by John Crowley and written by Nick Hornby, adapted from Colm Tóibín's 2009 novel. Saoirse Ronan stars as a young Irish immigrant in 1950s New York, with Emory Cohen, Domhnall Gleeson, Jim Broadbent and Julie Walters in supporting roles. Filmed in Ireland and Montreal with only brief shooting in Brooklyn itself, it premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2015, where Fox Searchlight bought it after a bidding war.

In 1951 Eilis Lacey lives in the small town of Enniscorthy in south-east Ireland with her mother and her older sister Rose. Unable to find steady work, she serves part-time in the shop of the spiteful Miss Kelly. Rose arranges through Father Flood, an Irish priest in Brooklyn, for Eilis to emigrate to the United States. On the crossing, her worldly cabin-mate Georgina helps her through seasickness and tells her how to pass immigration.

In Brooklyn Eilis lodges in a boarding house for young Irishwomen run by the strict but kindly Mrs Kehoe and works at a department store, but she is crippled by homesickness. Father Flood enrols her in night classes in bookkeeping at Brooklyn College. At an Irish dance she meets Tony Fiorello, a warm Italian-American plumber, and as their romance grows and her studies go well, she begins to feel at home. Then Rose dies suddenly. Before Eilis leaves to comfort her mother, Tony shows her the land on Long Island where he hopes to build them a house, and they marry quietly at City Hall.

Back in Enniscorthy, Eilis finds herself welcomed into a life that now seems full of possibility. She fills in at Rose's old bookkeeping job, which may become permanent, and her friend Nancy introduces her to Jim Farrell, a well-off and gentle young man who clearly hopes to marry her. Eilis delays her return, neglects Tony's letters and keeps her marriage secret. Then Miss Kelly, having heard the news from gossip, summons her and hints that she knows the truth. Recognising the narrowness of the town, Eilis declares her married name, tells her mother she is returning to her husband, and leaves Jim a letter. On the voyage back she advises a nervous young emigrant just as Georgina once advised her, and is reunited with Tony in Brooklyn.

Brooklyn was acclaimed, with 97% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and earned three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Actress for Ronan.

overview: Abby Russell, a beautiful, dedicated nurse with a sinister side, has a secret life in which she targets and punishes dishonest men.
tagline: Your pain is her pleasure.
title: Nurse 3-D
plot:
Nurse 3D is a horror-comedy film that delves into the darker side of human nature, particularly in the context of relationships and intimacy. The movie follows Amy (played by Katie Cassidy) as she navigates her way through a series of gruesome encounters with patients at a hospital, where she works as a nurse.

At its core, Nurse 3D is a film that explores the theme of toxic masculinity, where men are portrayed as violent, aggressive, and emotionally immature. The movie highlights how these traits can lead to destructive behavior, particularly in relationships where women are objectified and exploited.

The film also touches on the theme of female empowerment, as Amy begins to assert her own boundaries and take control of her life. Through her experiences, she learns to stand up for herself and reclaim her agency, ultimately becoming a stronger and more confident individual.

Furthermore, Nurse 3D critiques societal norms around sex and intimacy, particularly in the context of women's bodies being objectified and commodified. The movie presents a commentary on how these norms can lead to a culture of violence and exploitation, where women are seen as mere objects rather than human beings with agency and autonomy.

Overall, Nurse 3D is a film that uses horror elements to explore deeper themes about relationships, power dynamics, and the objectification of women.

original_title: Marvel One-Shot: All Hail the King
overview: A documentary filmmaker interviews the now-famous Trevor Slattery from behind bars.
tagline: The Toast of Croydon is back.
title: Marvel One-Shot: All Hail the King
plot:
Marvel One-Shot: All Hail the King is a 2014 superhero short film that explores the theme of power, corruption, and the blurred lines between heroism and villainy. The story delves into the complexities of Tony Stark's character, particularly his struggles with ego, pride, and the weight of responsibility.

The film takes place after the events of Iron Man 3, where Tony Stark has become increasingly isolated and withdrawn, feeling like a vigilante rather than a hero. This sense of disillusionment is exacerbated by the fact that he is no longer being recognized as a legitimate superhero, but rather as a self-appointed avenger.

As the story unfolds, we see Tony's obsession with power and control grow, leading him to take matters into his own hands and create a new identity for himself: the Mandarin. This transformation serves as a metaphor for the corrupting influence of power and the dangers of unchecked ego.

Throughout the film, the line between heroism and villainy becomes increasingly blurred, leaving the audience questioning what it means to be a true hero. The character of Aldrich Killian, aka the Mandarin, serves as a foil to Tony Stark, highlighting the differences between those who seek to use power for the greater good and those who are driven by personal ambition.

Ultimately, Marvel One-Shot: All Hail the King is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges our assumptions about heroism, power, and the nature of evil.

overview: Alien pods come to Earth and, naturally, start taking over Human Hosts. One such pod only manages to take over one human's, Shin Izumi, right arm. Together they grow and co-exist, all the while the other aliens are making meals of other humans; Shin feels he must put a stop to it all, but his alien, Migi, doesn't see why.
tagline: A constant battle of resistance.
title: Parasyte: Part 2
plot:
Parasyte: Part 2 (Japanese: 寄生獣 完結編, Hepburn: Kiseijū: Kanketsu-hen) is a 2015 Japanese science fiction action horror film directed by Takashi Yamazaki and the second of two live-action films adapted from Hitoshi Iwaaki's manga Parasyte. Shota Sometani stars as the high school student Shinichi Izumi, with Ai Hashimoto, Sadawo Abe as the voice of Migi, Eri Fukatsu as Ryoko Tamiya and Masahiro Higashide. It concludes the story begun in Parasyte: Part 1, released the previous year.

Months after the events of the first film, mysterious parasitic organisms that take over human hosts by replacing their heads continue to prey on people. The police have begun using Uragami, a captured serial killer who can recognize parasites, to identify them among the population, but he fails to pick out Shinichi, who has a parasite living in his right hand. Shinichi and the parasite, Migi, which failed to reach his brain, continue to track down and kill the creatures. Shinichi learns that he is being followed by Kuramori, an investigator hired by the parasite Ryoko Tamiya, who is studying the relationship between parasites and humans.

Tamiya has given birth to a human baby and is gradually learning what it means to be a mother, becoming fiercely protective of the child even against her own kind. Kuramori, ignoring Shinichi's warnings, records a conversation with the city's mayor, Takeshi Hirokawa, who secretly leads an organized group of parasites, a decision with deadly consequences. As the authorities prepare a large-scale operation to exterminate the parasites in city hall, Shinichi faces Gotō, a powerful parasite made up of several organisms within one body. The final battle forces Shinichi to rely on his bond with Migi and his own humanity, while Tamiya's choices shed new light on what separates humans from the creatures that hunt them.

The film was a box-office success in Japan, although reviews were mixed. Edmund Lee of the South China Morning Post gave it two and a half stars out of five, and Elizabeth Kerr of The Hollywood Reporter saw it as an example of producers trying to squeeze another hit out of material that did not demand it. James Marsh of Twitch Film was more positive about the story's science fiction, horror and adventure elements.

overview: Construction company owner John Matthews learns that his estranged son, Jason, has been arrested for drug trafficking. Facing an unjust prison sentence for a first time offender courtesy of mandatory minimum sentence laws, Jason has nothing to offer for leniency in good conscience. Desperately, John convinces the DEA and the opportunistic DA Joanne Keeghan to let him go undercover to help make arrests big enough to free his son in return. With the unwitting help of an ex-con employee, John enters the narcotics underworld where every move could be his last in an operation that will demand all his resources, wits and courage to survive.
tagline: How Far Would You Go To Save Your Son?
title: Snitch
plot:
Snitch is a 2013 American action thriller directed by Ric Roman Waugh, inspired by the case of a DEA informant. Dwayne Johnson stars as a father who goes undercover to win leniency for his son, with Barry Pepper, Susan Sarandon, Jon Bernthal, Benjamin Bratt and Michael Kenneth Williams in supporting roles. It was released in the United States on February 22, 2013.

In Missouri, the college student Jason Collins agrees, at the urging of his friend Craig, to receive a package at his home. It contains pills and a tracking device, and DEA agents arrest him within minutes. Jason's estranged father, John Matthews, the owner of a construction company, learns that Craig set Jason up to reduce his own sentence, and that under mandatory minimum laws Jason faces at least ten years in prison unless he informs on someone else, something he cannot or will not do. John appeals to the ambitious federal prosecutor Joanne Keeghan and she agrees to reduce Jason's sentence if John himself helps bring down a dealer, with DEA agent Cooper monitoring his activities.

Searching his employee files, John finds Daniel James, an employee with two prior drug convictions who is trying to stay straight. With a large cash offer, John persuades the reluctant Daniel to introduce him to the local dealer Malik, without revealing that he is working for the government. Posing as a struggling businessman, John offers to move drugs in his company's trucks, and Malik insists that he and Daniel drive the first shipment from near the Mexican border themselves. They survive an ambush by rivals, impressing the cartel leader Pintera.

When Cooper declines to arrest Malik in hopes of reaching higher targets, Keeghan reneges on the deal unless John continues. Daniel discovers the truth, and fearing cartel reprisals, both men send their families into hiding. Pintera hires John to carry cash into Mexico, and Keeghan promises Jason's release if Pintera is caught. John devises his own plan: he evades DEA surveillance, Daniel obtains Pintera's phone number from Malik, and John guides Cooper to both the money and the kingpin. After a violent highway chase, Pintera is caught, John passes his reward to Daniel, and Jason is freed as the family enters witness protection.

Snitch grossed about $58 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes noted one of Johnson's more thoughtful performances but found its message muddled by lackluster storytelling, and Metacritic gave it 51 out of 100.

overview: Upon learning that he has to come out of retirement to steal 50 cars in one night to save his brother Kip's life, former car thief Randall "Memphis" Raines enlists help from a few "boost happy" pals to accomplish a seemingly impossible feat. From countless car chases to relentless cops, the high-octane excitement builds as Randall swerves around more than a few roadblocks to keep Kip alive.
tagline: Ice Cold, Hot Wired.
title: Gone in Sixty Seconds
plot:
Gone in Sixty Seconds is a 2000 American action heist film directed by Dominic Sena and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films. The movie stars Nicolas Cage, Angelina Jolie, and Robert Duvall.

The story begins with Randall "Memphis" Raines (Nicolas Cage), a former car thief who has retired from the business after a stint in prison. Memphis is haunted by his past and struggles to connect with his estranged daughter, Sara (Amber Valletta). He's also being pursued by a ruthless crime lord named Earl (Christopher Eccleston).

One day, Memphis receives an offer from a wealthy collector, Julian (Robert Duvall), who wants him to steal 50 high-performance cars within 60 days. The catch is that the cars are all highly valuable and extremely difficult to steal. Memphis agrees to take on the challenge, but only if he can do it with his old crew.

Memphis reunites with his former partner, Bobby (Angus Macfadyen), and together they assemble a team of skilled thieves, including Sara's boyfriend, Ben (Benjamin Bratt). The team includes a mechanic, a safe-cracker, and an expert in car customization. As the deadline approaches, tensions rise within the group, and Memphis must navigate his complicated relationships with his crew members.

As the heist unfolds, Memphis and his team face numerous obstacles, including rival thieves, corrupt police officers, and treacherous terrain. The stakes are raised when Memphis discovers that one of the cars is a rare 1967 Shelby Cobra, which holds sentimental value for him.

Throughout the film, Nicolas Cage delivers an energetic performance as the charismatic but troubled Memphis. His character's backstory is gradually revealed through flashbacks, showcasing his rise to fame as a car thief and his subsequent fall from grace.

The movie's climax features an intense car chase sequence, where Memphis and his team must outrun their pursuers while navigating the streets of Los Angeles. The film concludes with a dramatic showdown between Memphis and Earl, which ultimately leads to the redemption of Memphis' character.

Overall, Gone in Sixty Seconds is an action-packed thrill ride with a talented cast and impressive car stunts. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has developed a cult following over the years, thanks to its memorable characters, witty dialogue, and high-octane action sequences.

original_title: The Santa Clause 3: The Escape Clause
overview: Now that Santa and Mrs. Claus have the North Pole running smoothly, the Counsel of Legendary Figures has called an emergency meeting on Christmas Eve! The evil Jack Frost has been making trouble, looking to take over the holiday! So he launches a plan to sabotage the toy factory and compel Scott to invoke the little-known Escape Clause and wish he'd never become Santa.
tagline: 'Twas the Fight Before Christmas...
title: The Santa Clause 3: The Escape Clause
plot:
The Santa Clause 3: The Escape Clause is a Christmas comedy film released in 2006 by Walt Disney Pictures, directed by Michael Lembeck and written by Leo Benvenuti, Steve Rudnick, and Jerry Bresler. The movie serves as the third installment in the Santa Clause trilogy.

Beginning:
The story begins with Scott Calvin (Tim Allen), also known as Santa Claus, who is struggling to balance his duties as Santa with his family life. His son Charlie (Eric Lloyd) has grown up and moved away, and Scott's wife Carol (Wanda Sykes) is feeling neglected. Meanwhile, a new villain emerges in the form of Jack Frost (Martin Short), an immortal winter spirit who seeks to take over Christmas.

Plot Development:
Jack Frost, tired of being forgotten by humans, decides to take matters into his own hands and steal Christmas. He kidnaps Santa Claus and plans to use his powers to become the new ruler of Christmas. Scott Calvin must find a way to stop Jack Frost and save Christmas. Along the way, he teams up with his son Charlie, who has grown up and is now a teenager.

As the story unfolds, Scott discovers that Jack Frost's plan involves using an ancient book known as the "Escape Clause," which would allow him to escape the cycle of winter and become human forever. The Escape Clause is a powerful magical artifact that can be used to break free from one's predetermined fate.

Ending:
In the climactic final battle, Scott Calvin faces off against Jack Frost in an epic showdown. With the help of his son Charlie and some unexpected allies, Scott manages to defeat Jack Frost and shatter the Escape Clause. In doing so, he ensures that Christmas is saved and that the cycle of winter continues.
