overview: A matchmaker connects Molly and Jacob, but their new romance is put to the test when they realize that they are competing deli owners. Will a Hanukkah miracle keep them together?
tagline: Two rival delis serving a whole latke of love.
title: Hanukkah on Rye
plot:
Hanukkah on Rye is a 2022 American Hanukkah romantic comedy television film directed by Peter DeLuise from a screenplay by Julie Sherman Wolfe. Produced for Hallmark Media with Just To Be Clear Productions, it stars Yael Grobglas and Jeremy Jordan, with Linda Darlow, Paula Shaw, David Eisner, Lisa Horner and Harry Nelken, and features the singer-songwriter Lisa Loeb, who contributed a new Hanukkah song. The film premiered on the Hallmark Channel on 18 December 2022 and runs 84 minutes.

Molly (Grobglas) hopes to take over Gilbert's, her family's struggling, staunchly traditional deli on New York's Lower East Side, from her parents, if it does not go out of business first. Jacob (Jordan) is the heir to Zimmer's, a Los Angeles deli that has thrived by embracing modernity, serving fajitas and decorating with light-up menorahs, and his parents send him to New York to scout locations for a new franchise. The building he settles on turns out to be just down the street from Gilbert's. Meanwhile the two singletons' meddling grandmothers have signed them up with an elite Jewish matchmaker whose supposedly foolproof method requires clients to write longhand letters to an anonymous match. As Molly and Jacob spar in person over their rival businesses, they are also falling in love through their letters. Bonding over the scarcity of good Hanukkah songs and their families' stories of immigrant ancestors pursuing the American dream, the pair must discover whether their romance can survive their families' competing business interests, in a story that takes in a latke competition and climaxes with an old immigration tale.

The film was well received. TheWrap ranked it fourth of Hallmark's 43 new holiday films of 2022, describing it as a big bowl of The Shop Around the Corner with a dollop of Crossing Delancey and praising the lovely lead performances, Wolfe's sprightly screenplay and Loeb's new song. Talia Lakritz of Business Insider called it an authentic, delightful rom-com that finally got Hallmark's Hanukkah films right after earlier efforts that felt like Christmas movies with Jewish characters added as an afterthought. Irene Katz Connelly of the Forward found it schlocky but an indisputable improvement, with jokes that felt written by and for Jews, though she considered it essentially a knockoff of Nora Ephron's You've Got Mail.

overview: Weeks after the deadly assault on Fortress Camp, Robert makes a daring rescue to save Sasha, the widow of his old nemesis Balzary. But back in the camp's command bunker, it appears Sasha may have devious plans of her own. As a new attack breaks out, Robert is confronted with a familiar face he thought he'd never see again…
tagline: The war isn't over. It's just starting.
title: Fortress: Sniper's Eye
plot:
Fortress: Sniper's Eye, also known as Fortress 2, is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Josh Sternfeld and a sequel to Fortress (2021). Jesse Metcalfe and Bruce Willis return as Paul Michaels and his father Robert, a retired CIA agent, with Chad Michael Murray as the villain Frederick Balzary. The supporting cast includes Natali Yura as Sasha, Kelly Greyson, Ser'Darius Blain, Natalie Burn and Michael Sirow. Lionsgate released the film on 29 April 2022.

The first film was set at Fortress, a secret resort for retired American intelligence officers built around a high-tech underground command bunker, which came under attack by Balzary and his mercenaries. A few weeks after that assault, the survivors are trying to recover and reassess their lives. Robert, who believes he killed Balzary, undertakes a risky mission to rescue Sasha, the woman presented as his old enemy's widow, and brings her back to the camp. He is wounded in the operation and spends much of his recovery in the infirmary.

Back at the Fortress, it soon becomes clear that Sasha is not the helpless victim she appeared to be and has plans of her own inside the camp's command center. When a new attack breaks out, the residents are taken hostage, and Robert is confronted with a face he thought he would never see again: Balzary is alive and determined to finish what he started. Robert and Paul, whose relationship has long been strained, must put their differences aside and work together with the other survivors to retake the bunker, protect their friends and stop Balzary and Sasha before their scheme succeeds.

The film was received very poorly. On Rotten Tomatoes, none of the seven critics' reviews collected were positive, with an average rating of 2 out of 10. Jeannette Catsoulis of The New York Times called it a sequel so dumb that no effort by Willis could reasonably be expected to save it, and noted that his character spends most of the film confined to a hospital bed. Leslie Felperin of The Guardian gave it two stars out of five. The film was released shortly after Willis's family announced in March 2022 that he was retiring from acting because of a diagnosis of aphasia, and several critics viewed his final low-budget films, released in the months that followed, with discomfort in light of his condition.

overview: A medieval English knight is magically transported to present day where he ends up falling for a high school science teacher.
tagline: A modern day romance with a medieval twist
title: The Knight Before Christmas
plot:
The Knight Before Christmas is a 2019 Christmas fantasy romantic comedy directed by Monika Mitchell and written by Cara J. Russell. Vanessa Hudgens stars as a small-town science teacher and Josh Whitehouse as a medieval knight transported to the present day, with Emmanuelle Chriqui, Harry Jarvis and Ella Kenion in supporting roles. It was filmed in Ontario, with Charleville Castle in Ireland standing in for the knight's home, and released on Netflix on November 21, 2019.

In 1334, near Norwich, England, the knight Sir Cole Lyons takes part in a Christmas hawking contest with his brother, Geoffrey. In the woods, Cole meets an old woman and kindly offers to escort her to shelter. Revealing herself to be a sorceress, she gives him a glowing medallion and announces that she will send him on a quest to a distant land of "flying steel dragons" and "magic boxes," warning that unless he completes it by midnight on Christmas Eve he will never become a true knight. She does not tell him what the quest is.

In present-day Bracebridge, Brooke Winters, a science teacher disillusioned with love after being left by her boyfriend, takes her niece Claire to the opening of a Christmas castle attraction, the very spot where Cole appears. Bewildered by the modern world, he is struck by Brooke's car. When doctors and a police officer assume he has amnesia, since he has no identification and insists that he is a medieval knight, Brooke lets him stay in her guest house while he recovers.

Cole gradually adapts to modern life, marveling at television, diners and voice assistants, and charms Brooke's family and friends with his chivalry. Brooke opens up about her late parents and her past heartbreak, while Cole searches for his quest, rescuing children from a frozen lake and stopping a pickpocket, yet still feeling unfulfilled. On Christmas Eve he helps Brooke host a festive dinner, and when they kiss under the mistletoe, his medallion glows: his quest is complete. They part tearfully at the castle, and Cole returns to the 14th century in time for his knighting ceremony. Seeing his unhappiness, Geoffrey urges him to go back, and the sorceress returns him to 2019, where on Christmas Day he rides up on horseback to declare his love for Brooke.

Rotten Tomatoes reports a 71% approval rating, its consensus calling the film endearing and charming despite a plot that borders on the absurd.

overview: In the fall of 1987, a group of small-town friends must survive the night in the home of a sinister couple after a tragic accident occurs. Needing only to make a single phone call, the request seems horribly ordinary until they realize that this call could change their life…or end it.
title: The Call
plot:
The Call is a 2020 American supernatural horror film directed by Timothy Woodward Jr. and written by Patrick Stibbs. It stars Lin Shaye and Tobin Bell, appearing on screen together for the first time, alongside Chester Rushing, Erin Sanders, Mike C. Manning, Sloane Morgan Siegel and Judd Lormand. It was Woodward's second collaboration with Shaye after The Final Wish (2018). The film opened in select US theatres and drive-ins on 2 October 2020, reached video on demand on 30 October and was released on Blu-ray in December 2020.

In the autumn of 1987, Chris (Rushing) moves with his mother to the small town of Willow Falls after his parents' divorce. On his first day at school he meets Tonya (Sanders), who introduces him to brothers Zack (Manning) and Brett (Siegel). They tell him that Tonya's younger sister Laura disappeared from the daycare run by Edith Cranston (Shaye), a former schoolteacher whom the town suspects of the crime and rumours call a witch, and that they have long tormented Edith and her husband Edward (Bell) by vandalising their home. Chris refuses to join in when the others throw bricks through the Cranstons' windows. Worn down by years of abuse, Edith hangs herself. Days later Edward summons the four teenagers to his house and reveals that Edith has left them her fortune: each will receive $100,000 if they go upstairs, dial a number on an old telephone and stay on the line for one minute. The call connects to a phone placed in Edith's casket at her request. One by one they are pulled into a personal hell in which Edith's spirit forces them to relive their worst memories: for Zack and Brett, the beatings from their abusive father; for Chris, the car crash that killed his pregnant girlfriend Sarah. Chris escapes but returns to help Tonya, whose own nightmare reveals that she killed Laura out of jealousy and blamed Edith. After Chris shoots Edward, Tonya vanishes into the room with the phone, and Chris, realising no one can escape the house, steps back into his own hell.

The film received generally negative reviews, with a 44% Rotten Tomatoes rating from 25 reviews and a consensus citing a lack of genuine scares and an overload of genre tropes. Leslie Felperin of The Guardian called it a shonky assemblage of tired tropes redeemed mainly by Shaye's game performance, while Drew Tinnin of Dread Central gave it three out of five, praising Shaye and the dark revenge story despite tonal problems.

overview: The Crawley family goes on a grand journey to the south of France to uncover the mystery of the dowager countess's newly inherited villa.
tagline: A cinematic return.
title: Downton Abbey: A New Era
plot:
Downton Abbey: A New Era is a 2022 British comedy-drama film directed by Simon Curtis, written by Julian Fellowes, and produced by Carnival Films. The movie serves as the sequel to the 2019 film Downton Abbey and follows the Crawley family on a new adventure.

The story begins with the Crawleys preparing for their annual summer ball at Downton Abbey. However, the festivities are disrupted when Lady Mary's cousin, Patrick Crawley (played by Luke Thompson), arrives unexpectedly. Patrick is revealed to be the long-lost son of Robert Crawley, Earl of Grantham, and his late wife, Cora.

As it turns out, Patrick has been living in France with his wife, Lucy Smith (played by Emma Corrin), a cousin of Lady Mary's. The couple has been struggling financially due to a series of unfortunate events, including the loss of their home and business. They are forced to sell their belongings and move back to England.

The Crawleys take Patrick and Lucy in, offering them a place at Downton Abbey. However, things become complicated when it is revealed that Patrick's presence could potentially disrupt the family's inheritance plans. The family must navigate this new development while also dealing with their own personal struggles and relationships.

Meanwhile, Daisy Mason (played by Sophie McShera), who has been working as a travel agent, convinces the Crawleys to join her on a trip to the south of France. They embark on a journey to the village of Saint-Agnès-sur-Mer, where they hope to find inspiration for their own lives and perhaps even discover some long-lost family secrets.

Upon arrival in Saint-Agnès-sur-Mer, the group becomes embroiled in a mystery surrounding a local artist who has been accused of theft. As they delve deeper into the mystery, they uncover a web of deceit and betrayal that threatens to upend their own lives.

Throughout the film, the characters must navigate their relationships with each other while also confronting their personal demons. Lady Mary struggles with her feelings for Patrick, while Lady Edith (played by Laura Carmichael) grapples with her own sense of identity. Meanwhile, Mr. Carson (played by Jim Carter) and Mrs. Hughes (played by Phyllis Logan) must contend with the challenges of managing a large estate.

As the story unfolds, the Crawleys discover that the local artist is not who they seem to be. In fact, he is an imposter who has been using his charm and wit to swindle the villagers out of their money. The group must work together to expose the truth and bring the imposter to justice.

In the end, the Crawleys emerge victorious, but not without some unexpected twists and turns. Patrick and Lucy's relationship is put to the test as they navigate their feelings for each other amidst the chaos. Meanwhile, the rest of the family comes to terms with their own personal growth and development.

Overall, Downton Abbey: A New Era is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of love, identity, and community. With its talented cast and witty dialogue, it is sure to delight fans of the original series and newcomers alike.

overview: Former childhood pals Leo and Nikki are attracted to each other as adults—but will their feuding parents' rival pizzerias put a chill on their sizzling romance?
tagline: Love is an acquired taste.
title: Little Italy
plot:
Little Italy is a 2018 Canadian romantic comedy-drama film directed by Donald Petrie. The movie follows the story of Max, a young man who returns to his hometown of Toronto's Little Italy after being away for several years.

The main theme of Little Italy revolves around the idea of identity and belonging. Max struggles to find his place in the world outside of his family's expectations, but ultimately discovers that home is where the heart is. The film explores the complexities of cultural heritage and the importance of embracing one's roots.

Throughout the movie, themes of love, family, and community are also woven together, highlighting the significance of human connections in our lives. Max's relationships with those around him, particularly his mother and a local business owner, help shape his understanding of himself and where he belongs.

The film also touches on the idea of nostalgia and the passing of time, as Max navigates his way through adulthood while still holding onto memories of his childhood. Overall, Little Italy is a heartwarming story about finding one's place in the world and embracing the people and places that make life meaningful.

overview: A bachelor party becomes a savage fight for survival when the groomsmen unwittingly unleash a fabled predator upon the festivities.
tagline: No Man Can Resist Her. All Men Should.
title: Siren
plot:
Siren (stylized as SiREN) is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by Gregg Bishop and written by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski. The first spin-off of the V/H/S anthology franchise, it is a feature-length expansion of "Amateur Night," David Bruckner's segment from V/H/S (2012), with Hannah Fierman reprising her role as the creature Lily. Chase Williamson stars as Jonah, with Justin Welborn, Michael Aaron Milligan and Hayes Mercure. Unlike its predecessor, the film is told in a conventional narrative style rather than as found footage. It received a limited theatrical release on 2 December 2016.

The film opens years in the past, as a mystic and a sheriff investigate a séance in a church that has ended in the deaths of everyone present. The creature summoned during the ritual, which takes the form of a young girl, kills the sheriff, and the mystic places a shackle around her ankle to control her.

In the present, Jonah is about to get married, and his brother Mac and friends Rand and Elliot take him out for his bachelor party. Disappointed by a seedy strip club, they are approached by a stranger who leads them to a secret underground club in the countryside. Its owner, the charismatic Mr. Nyx, turns out to be the mystic from the prologue. When Jonah asks for an experience that will not compromise his loyalty to his fiancée, Nyx sends him to a private room where a captive young woman, Lily, sings to him from behind glass. Her song puts him into a trance in which he relives every sexual experience of his life. Believing she is a trafficking victim, Jonah and his friends help her escape, only to discover that she is the monstrous creature from the opening scene. Lily, who has formed a dangerous fixation on Jonah, follows him through the night, killing anyone who stands in her way, while Nyx and his men pursue the group to reclaim his prized possession.

Siren received mixed reviews, with a 65 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 54. Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times called it, for the most part, a clever and confident expansion of a terrific short that stings less but still packs plenty of poison, while other critics found it less effective than Bruckner's original segment.

overview: Sentenced to six years in prison, Malik El Djebena is alone in the world and can neither read nor write. On his arrival at the prison, he seems younger and more brittle than the others detained there. At once he falls under the sway of a group of Corsicans who enforce their rule in the prison. As the 'missions' go by, he toughens himself and wins the confidence of the Corsican group.
production_companies: Conseil Régional de Provence-Alpes Côte d'Azur
tagline: Escaping the prison of life.
title: A Prophet
plot:
A Prophet is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of the human condition, particularly in the context of the French prison system. The movie delves into the struggles of its protagonist, Abel, as he navigates the harsh realities of life behind bars.

At its core, A Prophet is a story about redemption, forgiveness, and the cyclical nature of violence. Abel's journey is marked by his transformation from an innocent young man to a hardened convict, driven by a desire for survival and revenge against those who have wronged him. As he rises through the ranks of the prison hierarchy, Abel must confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of his own actions.

One of the primary themes of A Prophet is the exploration of masculinity and its relationship to violence. The film portrays a world where traditional notions of masculinity are often distorted or corrupted by the harsh realities of life in prison. Abel's character embodies this tension, as he struggles to reconcile his desire for power and respect with his own sense of vulnerability and humanity.

The movie also examines the theme of loyalty and friendship, highlighting the complex web of relationships that exists within the prison system. Abel's bond with his fellow inmates, particularly his mentor and friend, Le Fabre, serves as a source of comfort and support in an otherwise brutal environment.

Furthermore, A Prophet touches on issues of social inequality and the systemic failures that lead to the marginalization of certain groups. The film critiques the French prison system, revealing its flaws and injustices, and highlighting the need for reform and rehabilitation rather than simply punishment.

Ultimately, A Prophet is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of violence, redemption, and forgiveness in a world marked by inequality and social injustice.

overview: The story of the Battle of Midway, and the leaders and soldiers who used their instincts, fortitude and bravery to overcome massive odds.
tagline: One battle turned the tide of war.
title: Midway
plot:
Midway is a 2019 war film directed by Roland Emmerich, who produced it with Harald Kloser, from a screenplay by Wes Tooke. Covering the first six months of the Pacific War, from the attack on Pearl Harbor to the Battle of Midway in June 1942, it is a new take on the events depicted in the 1976 film of the same name. The cast includes Ed Skrein as the dive bomber pilot Dick Best, Patrick Wilson as the intelligence officer Edwin Layton, Woody Harrelson as Admiral Chester Nimitz, Luke Evans, Aaron Eckhart, Nick Jonas, Mandy Moore, Dennis Quaid, Tadanobu Asano and Darren Criss. A long-held passion project for Emmerich, the film was largely financed independently with significant Chinese investment.

In 1937, Edwin Layton, an American naval attaché in Tokyo, is warned by Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto that American threats to Japan's oil supply could drive the country to war. Four years later, on 7 December 1941, Japan launches its surprise attack on Pearl Harbor, devastating the US Pacific Fleet. Yamamoto and Rear Admiral Tamon Yamaguchi argue for a bold follow-up strike against Midway Atoll, but are overruled until the Doolittle Raid on Tokyo in April 1942 shocks the Japanese high command into approving their plan.

Meanwhile, the newly appointed commander of the Pacific Fleet, Admiral Nimitz, relies on Layton and the codebreaker Joseph Rochefort, whose team is intercepting Japanese messages about an operation against a target identified only as "AF." Officials in Washington believe the target lies in the South Pacific, but Layton and Rochefort become convinced it is Midway and devise a ruse to prove it. The film follows the war through the eyes of the aviators and sailors of the carrier USS Enterprise, including the reckless but brilliant Best and his family, as well as the Japanese commanders, and culminates in the Battle of Midway, where American dive bombers turn the tide of the war in the Pacific by sinking four Japanese aircraft carriers.

Midway received mixed reviews. Critics praised its spectacular aerial combat sequences and its respectful, relatively balanced depiction of both sides, but criticized its dialogue, crowded storytelling and thin characterizations. It grossed about $127 million worldwide.

overview: A writer stumbles upon a long-hidden secret when he agrees to help former British Prime Minister Adam Lang complete his memoirs on a remote island after the politician's assistant drowns in a mysterious accident.
tagline: Read between the lies.
title: The Ghost Writer
plot:
The Ghost Writer, released in the United Kingdom and Ireland as The Ghost, is a 2010 neo-noir political thriller directed by Roman Polanski, who adapted it with Robert Harris from Harris's 2007 novel The Ghost. Ewan McGregor plays the unnamed title character, with Pierce Brosnan, Olivia Williams, Kim Cattrall and Tom Wilkinson.

A British ghostwriter is hired to finish the memoirs of the former prime minister Adam Lang after the previous writer, Lang's longtime aide Mike McAra, drowns in what appears to be an accident. The Ghost travels to a beach house on Martha's Vineyard, where Lang is staying with his sharp, unhappy wife Ruth and his assistant and lover Amelia Bly. Soon after he arrives, Lang's former foreign secretary, Richard Rycart, accuses him of authorizing the illegal seizure of terrorism suspects for torture, and Lang faces possible prosecution by the International Criminal Court.

Left behind, the Ghost finds a hidden envelope among McAra's belongings, with photographs that contradict Lang's account of his past. A local resident tells him that the tides could never have carried McAra's body to where it was found, and Ruth reveals that Lang and McAra had argued the night before he died. Driving McAra's car, the Ghost follows the destination programmed into its navigation system to the home of Paul Emmett, a Harvard professor with links to the CIA, who is evasive about his ties to McAra and Lang. Realizing he is being followed, the Ghost contacts Rycart, who tells him McAra had discovered evidence of Lang's role in rendition flights. When the Ghost confronts Lang, the former prime minister angrily rejects the suggestion that he was recruited by the CIA, but soon afterward he is assassinated by a grieving anti-war protester.

The Ghost is asked to finish the book for posthumous publication. At its London launch, he learns that Emmett once taught Ruth at Harvard, and realizes that McAra hid a message in the manuscript, spelled out by the first words of each chapter, revealing that Ruth was recruited by the CIA. He slips Ruth a note with his discovery and leaves; moments later, a car speeds toward him offscreen, and the pages of the manuscript scatter in the wind.

The film won Polanski the Silver Bear for Best Director at the Berlin Film Festival and six European Film Awards, including Best Film. Critics widely praised it as an expertly crafted thriller.

overview: A successful woman in New York City finds her life upended when she is forced to confront a dark truth that threatens to unravel her meticulously crafted life.
title: Luckiest Girl Alive
plot:
I don't have information on a movie titled "Luckiest Girl Alive" released in 2022 by Made Up Stories. 

However, I do know that there is a novel with the same title written by Jessica Knoll, published in 2015. The story revolves around Annie Fitzpatrick, a successful and charismatic woman who appears to have it all - a beautiful appearance, a loving family, and a thriving career as a photographer.

The narrative takes a dark turn when Annie's high school best friend, Raina, is murdered, and the police investigation reveals that Raina was not the innocent victim everyone thought she was. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Annie had a complex and troubled relationship with Raina, and that their friendship was built on secrets and lies.

Throughout the novel, Knoll expertly weaves together multiple timelines, revealing the events leading up to Raina's murder and the aftermath of the crime. The author also delves into themes of trauma, mental health, and the complexities of female relationships.

As the story progresses, Annie's seemingly perfect life begins to unravel, exposing her own dark secrets and the true nature of her relationship with Raina. Ultimately, the novel builds towards a shocking revelation that changes everything Annie thought she knew about herself and her past.

The 2022 film adaptation of "Luckiest Girl Alive" stars Milly Alcock as Annie Fitzpatrick, and it appears to follow the same basic plot as the novel. However, I do not have information on the specific details of the movie's storyline or its production.

overview: Chema has a mission: to date Claudia, the attractive new girl at his school, and lose his virginity. Can he fulfill his dream before graduating?
title: Who's a Good Boy?
plot:
Who's a Good Boy? (Spanish: El Guau) is a 2022 Mexican teen sex comedy written and directed by Ihtzi Hurtado. Sebastian Dante stars as a high school senior desperate to lose his virginity, with Sirena Ortiz, Harold Azuara, Diego Meléndez, Luisa Guzmán Quintero, Adrián Vázquez and Grettell Valdez in supporting roles. The title refers to a slang term for a boy who devotedly serves a girl he loves while being kept in the friend zone. The film was released worldwide on Netflix on November 23, 2022.

Chema is in his final year of high school and is mortified that all his friends have already had sex while he cannot even manage a conversation with a girl. His fun-loving uncle Jaime arrives for a visit, offering plenty of advice about women and lending him his truck. When the principal assigns Chema to show the glamorous new student Claudia around, she quickly seems interested in him, but he is too nervous to respond. He begins driving her to school and accompanying her to dance classes. Meanwhile, his longtime friend Eli, who wants him to play in a band with her for the school's Christmas posada, is hurt to see him spending all his time with Claudia.

At a party at Claudia's house, she tries to seduce Chema, but fear paralyzes him again. When his family hears what happened, his sister warns him that he is in danger of becoming Claudia's "guau," a loyal pet who does everything for a popular girl without ever being considered as a boyfriend. Claudia asks him to the posada, but then secretly invites another boy, Sebas, to her house, and when Chema sneaks in on them, a humiliating mishap leaves his clothes behind. Claudia insists they are best friends and announces she is going to the dance with Sebas, offering to help him ask Eli instead.

At the posada, Chema and Eli are having a wonderful time until Claudia and Sebas goad him into admitting that he really wanted Claudia, and Eli, overhearing, walks out. Eli rejects his apologies for weeks, and Jaime abruptly leaves town. As graduation approaches, Chema publicly declares that nobody should have to be a "guau," winning applause and even Sebas's respect. At graduation he turns Claudia down when she finally makes a move, wins Eli back, and decides to give up his planned engineering degree to pursue his true passion, music. The film ends on the class trip to Cancún, where the new couple are caught together in an airplane bathroom.

original_title: A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love
overview: After 15 years, Pat moves home from Hawaii with his two sons and through a series of coincidences, or Godwinks, ends up stuck in traffic next to his high school sweetheart, Margie, at Christmas.
title: A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love
plot:
A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love is a heartwarming holiday romance film that explores the complexities of love, loss, and second chances. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of finding redemption and forgiveness in the face of past mistakes.

The story follows a woman who returns to her hometown for Christmas, only to reconnect with an old flame who has been carrying around emotional scars from their past. As they rekindle their romance, they must confront the pain and heartache that drove them apart in the first place.

Through the lens of this second chance at love, the movie sheds light on the power of forgiveness and the importance of facing one's mistakes head-on. The film suggests that it's never too late to make amends and start anew, and that sometimes, all it takes is a little bit of courage and vulnerability to heal old wounds.

The movie also touches on the theme of nostalgia and the bittersweet nature of revisiting past loves. As the protagonist navigates her feelings for her old flame, she must confront the memories and emotions that have been holding her back from moving forward. This introspection serves as a poignant reminder that love can be both a source of joy and pain, and that sometimes, it's necessary to let go of the past in order to move towards a brighter future.

Ultimately, A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love is a film about the transformative power of love and forgiveness, and the idea that even in the most unexpected ways, we can find redemption and happiness.

original_title: โปรแกรมหน้า วิญญาณอาฆาต
overview: What kind of scenes in a horror film scares you the most? When a ghost appears totally unexpectedly? When the main character does not see the ghost sneaking up behind him? When at the very end you find out that the main character was actually a ghost all along? But none of this compares to the feeling of arriving home alone and suddenly being stuck by a feeling of deja-vu.
tagline: When the movie ends it's not really the end.
title: Coming Soon
plot:
Coming Soon (Thai: Programme Na Winyarn Arkhad) is a 2008 Thai horror film directed by Sophon Sakdaphisit, in his directorial debut, from a script he co-wrote with Kongkiat Komesiri and Chanajai Tonsaithong. Sakdaphisit had previously co-written the hit Thai horror films Shutter (2004) and Alone (2007). The film stars Chantavit Dhanasevi as a cinema projectionist, with Worrakarn Rotjanawatchra, Oraphan Arjsamat and Sakulrath Thomas,, and builds its scares around a cursed film.

Shane, a projectionist at a Bangkok multiplex who is pressured into helping copy an unreleased print for pirate DVDs, and his ex-girlfriend Som, an usher there, watch the new horror film about Chaba, a village woman who abducts and murders two children. As she is about to kill a third, villagers catch her and hang her. Unsettled but intrigued, the pair look into the story behind the film and discover that it was based on a real case from thirty years earlier. Visiting the house where the crimes are said to have happened, Shane falls down the stairs and is injured.

At the hospital, when they explain that they were researching Chaba, a doctor tells them that the real Chaba is not dead at all but is still alive in a psychiatric institution. Shane digs deeper and finds a behind-the-scenes clip from the production. It shows that the actress who played Chaba, Ingchan, was forced to repeat the hanging scene again and again because the director felt it was not convincing enough. Although she wore a safety harness beneath the noose, it broke during the final take and she was genuinely hanged. That take was the one used in the finished film shown in cinemas.

Realising the danger, Shane warns Som and races to the cinema to find her. Inside the auditorium the vengeful ghost of Ingchan haunts him, and he is supernaturally pulled into the hanging scene of the film itself, where he finds the bodies of colleagues and friends who had also watched it. Som arrives and can only watch the screen in horror as the ghost gouges out Shane's eyes and kills him. Som meets the same fate and is drawn into the film as well.

Later, as the film plays in a crowded cinema and reaches the hanging scene, the dead woman suddenly comes to life and screams at the audience, asking whether they really want to see her die. Reviewers found the film delivered some effective scares and a sound script, while noting the rookie flaws of a first-time director and a lack of real innovation.

overview: The police force of a remote Midwestern town search for a killer Santa Claus who is picking off citizens on Christmas Eve.
tagline: He knows who's been naughty.
title: Silent Night
plot:
Silent Night is a 2012 American slasher film directed by Steven C. Miller, a loose remake of the 1984 film Silent Night, Deadly Night and the sixth entry in that series. Jaime King stars as a small-town deputy hunting a killer in a Santa suit, with Malcolm McDowell, Donal Logue, Ellen Wong and Brendan Fehr in supporting roles. It received a limited theatrical release on November 30, 2012, followed by a DVD and Blu-ray release in December.

In the small town of Cryer, Wisconsin, a masked man in a Santa Claus costume electrocutes a deputy who has been having an affair with a married woman, whom he also kills. On Christmas Eve, Deputy Aubrey Bradimore, a young widow still grieving her husband and struggling to live up to the reputation of her father, a retired lawman, is called in on her day off by the gruff Sheriff Cooper and discovers the bodies. Cooper decides to keep the investigation quiet from the mayor.

The killer, who punishes those he judges to be "naughty," embarks on a gruesome spree, murdering a spoiled teenager, a pair of pornographers at a local motel, a woman at a Christmas tree farm and a corrupt reverend who has been stealing from the collection plate. Aubrey suspects a drug dealer, Karsson, who flees, and later Jim, a local man who plays Santa, as the killer goes on to murder the mayor, his daughter and her boyfriend. During the town's Christmas parade, Aubrey searches a crowd full of men in Santa suits, arrests Jim when he runs, and is forced to shoot Karsson when he pulls a gun.

Noticing a gift box containing a lump of coal, like ones received at the station and by her father, Aubrey rushes to her parents' home and finds her father murdered. Meanwhile the killer storms the police station, slaughtering Cooper, another deputy and Jim. Aubrey and the station secretary are trapped inside as he tries to burn the building with a homemade flamethrower, but Aubrey overpowers him and sets him ablaze. He survives and escapes. The killer is revealed to be Ronald Jones Jr., a local chimney sweep who as a boy witnessed his father burn his ex-wife alive at a Christmas party before being killed by Aubrey's father, then a deputy. The film ends with Ronald driving out of town.

Silent Night received mixed reviews, with some horror critics praising its balance of gore and dark comedy and judging it superior to many remakes, and others dismissing it as a routine slasher. Kevin Riepl composed the score.

overview: In custody in New York, Detective James Knight finds himself in the middle of a jailbreak led by The Christmas Bomber, a brutal fanatic whose Santa Claus disciples are terrorizing the city. With the promised return of his badge in exchange for taking out the terrorists, the steely-eyed Knight doles out mercy for the just...and merciless justice for all the rest.
title: Detective Knight: Redemption
plot:
Detective Knight: Redemption, also known as Christmas Knight, is an American Christmas-set action thriller from 2022. Edward John Drake directed and co-wrote it with Corey Large, who also produced alongside Randall Emmett and George Furla for Emmett/Furla Oasis, BondIt Media Capital and Buffalo 8 Productions. The second installment of the Detective Knight trilogy and a sequel to Detective Knight: Rogue, it stars Bruce Willis as Detective James Knight and Paul Johansson as the villain Ricky Conlan, with Lochlyn Munro, Miranda Edwards, Beau Mirchoff, Corey Large, Jimmy Jean-Louis, Michael Eklund and John Cassini as Mayor Vassetti. The music is by Scott Currie.

Following the events of the first film, Knight is in custody in New York for the killings of the criminals Winna and Brigga. During the Christmas season, a riot breaks out in the prison, led by Ricky Conlan, a brutal fanatic known as "The Christmas Bomber", whose followers, the "Real Saints of Christmas", dress as Santa Claus and terrorize the city. With the police stretched thin outside the walls, the authorities need a man on the inside to crush the uprising, and Knight is caught in the middle of the jailbreak. He strikes a deal: in exchange for taking out the terrorists, he will be reinstated and get his badge back. As the bomber's disciples spread chaos across the city, Knight sets out to stop them, showing mercy to the innocent and merciless justice to the rest, with the help of colleagues including Fitzgerald (Munro) and Anna Shea (Edwards).

The film was shot back to back with the third installment in Vancouver from November to December 2021 under the working title Christmas Knight, and was retitled in September 2022. Several actors reprised their roles from the first film, while Johansson, Cassini and Jerry Yu joined the cast. It is among the final films of Willis, who retired from acting after being diagnosed with aphasia, a condition later identified as frontotemporal dementia. Lionsgate released it in limited theaters and on demand on 9 December 2022, followed by DVD and Blu-ray on 17 January 2023. Critics were largely negative: Movie Nation and Blu-ray.com dismissed it as dull, and Common Sense Media noted that Willis appears even less than in the first film, with tricks to film around him that often fail. Film Threat and Midwest Film Journal were more positive, calling it an entertaining crime caper for fans who know what to expect.

overview: Set in 1951, a blacklisted Hollywood writer gets into a car accident, loses his memory and settles down in a small town where he is mistaken for a long-lost son.
tagline: Sometimes your life comes into focus one frame at a time.
title: The Majestic
plot:
The Majestic is a 2001 American drama film directed by Randall Wallace. The story revolves around Peter Appleton, a successful screenwriter who suffers from amnesia and finds himself in the midst of World War II.

At its core, The Majestic explores themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the power of storytelling. Peter's journey is one of self-discovery as he navigates his way through the complexities of war-torn Hollywood and grapples with his own dark past. As he becomes embroiled in the lives of those around him, particularly a young woman named Elizabeth, he begins to confront the mistakes of his past and seek redemption.

The film also delves into the idea that stories have the power to heal and transform us. Peter's experiences as a screenwriter serve as a metaphor for the way stories can shape our perceptions of reality and help us make sense of ourselves. Through his writing, he finds a way to process his emotions and come to terms with his past.

Furthermore, The Majestic touches on the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and relationships. Peter's amnesia serves as a catalyst for him to re-examine his life and confront the choices that have led him to where he is today. As he forms connections with those around him, he begins to rediscover himself and find a sense of purpose.

Overall, The Majestic is a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that highlights the transformative power of storytelling, forgiveness, and redemption.

overview: A television reporter and her cameraman are trapped inside a building quarantined by the CDC after the outbreak of a mysterious virus which turns humans into bloodthirsty killers.
tagline: Contain The Truth.
title: Quarantine
plot:
Quarantine is a 2008 American found-footage horror film directed by John Erick Dowdle and written by Drew Dowdle. The movie follows a group of television news reporters who are sent to cover a mysterious outbreak in an apartment building, only to find themselves trapped and fighting for survival.

The main theme of Quarantine revolves around the concept of isolation and how it can amplify fear and paranoia. As the characters become increasingly isolated from the outside world, they begin to turn on each other, revealing their darker selves. This theme is expertly woven throughout the film, as the characters' initial sense of camaraderie and professionalism slowly gives way to desperation, mistrust, and ultimately, chaos.

The movie also explores the idea of the "other," highlighting how fear and misunderstanding can lead to violence and aggression towards those who are perceived as different or threatening. The infected individuals in the film serve as a metaphor for the unknown, representing a force that is beyond human control and understanding.

Furthermore, Quarantine touches on the theme of media representation and the responsibility that comes with it. The news reporters' initial enthusiasm to cover the story gradually gives way to a sense of unease and discomfort, highlighting the blurred lines between observer and participant in the midst of chaos.

Overall, Quarantine is a tense, suspenseful thriller that masterfully crafts an atmosphere of fear and uncertainty, exploring themes that are both timely and timeless.

overview: Haunted by terrible acts the Nazis forced him to participate in, the disenchanted Father Lankester Merrin focuses his energies on helping with an archaeological dig in the northern part of Kenya. There, the crew uncovers a church that predates Christian missions into the area, but the discovery also causes strange events to start occurring -- including physical changes to a young, disabled boy, whom Merrin grows to suspect has been possessed by a demon.
tagline: Go back before the beginning, to the place where evil was born.
title: Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist
plot:
Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist is a 2005 supernatural horror film directed by Paul Schrader, not Morgan Creek Productions. However, I can provide information on the movie.

The main themes of Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist revolve around the origins of the demonic entity Pazuzu and its connection to the Catholic Church's rituals and practices. The story explores the dark history of the Church's attempts to harness supernatural power for their own purposes.

The film delves into the theme of corruption and the dangers of unchecked ambition, as embodied by the character of Father Merrin (played by Stellan Skarsgård). As he becomes increasingly consumed by his desire for knowledge and power, he begins to lose sight of his faith and moral principles.

Another significant theme is the exploration of demonic possession and the nature of evil. The film suggests that demonic entities are not just malevolent beings but also complex, multifaceted creatures with their own motivations and desires.

The movie also touches on the idea of the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. As Father Merrin delves deeper into the mysteries of Pazuzu, he becomes increasingly entangled in a web of supernatural events that threaten to destroy him and those around him.

Overall, Dominion: Prequel to The Exorcist is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores themes of corruption, ambition, demonic possession, and the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human control.

overview: A woman’s body disappears mysteriously from the morgue without a trace. Police inspector Jaime Peña investigates the strange occurrence with the help of Álex Ulloa, the widower of the missing woman.
tagline: Death is not always the end
title: The Body
plot:
The Body (Spanish: El cuerpo) is a 2012 Spanish psychological thriller directed by Oriol Paulo, from a screenplay he co-wrote with Lara Sendim. José Coronado stars as a police inspector, Hugo Silva as a widower under suspicion, Belén Rueda as his wealthy wife and Aura Garrido as his young mistress. It was released in Spain in December 2012.

One night, the night watchman at a forensic institute flees in panic and is struck by a car, leaving him in a coma. Inspector Jaime Peña, called to investigate, learns that a body has vanished from the morgue: that of Mayka Villaverde, a powerful pharmaceutical executive who died of an apparent heart attack hours earlier. Her much younger husband, Álex Ulloa, is summoned from a rendezvous with his lover, Carla, whom he has assured that Mayka is dead. Peña, who still speaks of his own wife, killed years earlier in a car accident, in the present tense, notices that Álex refers to Mayka in the past tense far too easily and suspects that someone stole the body to prevent an autopsy.

Álex is in fact guilty: he poisoned Mayka's wine with TH-16, an experimental toxin from her company that induces a heart attack after several hours and leaves no trace. As the night wears on, strange incidents at the morgue convince Álex that Mayka faked her death and is alive and seeking revenge, having discovered his affair and his plans. Under pressure he confesses to Peña, but evidence against him accumulates, the watchman wakes to describe a masked gunman, and Peña tells him that there is no record of a woman named Carla at the address he provided.

While Álex is being transported, Mayka's body is found in the woods. Álex flees and collapses, and Peña finally reveals the truth. Years earlier, Mayka and Álex caused the crash that killed Peña's wife and fled without calling for help, leaving her to die in front of Peña and his young daughter. Carla is that daughter, who seduced Álex as part of a plan devised with her father to expose him, and the disappearance of the body was staged by them. As Álex struggles to breathe, he learns that Carla dosed him with TH-16 hours earlier, so that his death will look like a stress-induced heart attack.

The film was well received for its twisting plot, one reviewer calling it lean, moody and superior. Its success led to numerous remakes, including a Tamil-Kannada version, the South Korean film The Vanished (2018), the Hindi film The Body (2019), and Italian and Indonesian versions.

original_title: The Art of Racing in the Rain
overview: A family dog - with a near-human soul and a philosopher's mind - evaluates his life through the lessons learned by his human owner, a race-car driver.
tagline: Meet the dog who will show the world how to be human
title: The Art of Racing in the Rain
plot:
The Art of Racing in the Rain is a 2019 American drama directed by Simon Curtis and written by Mark Bomback, based on the 2008 novel by Garth Stein. It stars Milo Ventimiglia as race car driver Denny Swift and Amanda Seyfried as his wife Eve, with Kevin Costner as the voice of Enzo, Denny's golden retriever, who narrates the story. Kathy Baker and Martin Donovan play Eve's parents.

In Seattle, the elderly and failing Enzo reflects on his life, recalling a Mongolian belief that a dog who is ready will be reincarnated as a human, and hoping that he will find Denny again in another life. Years earlier, Denny, an aspiring racing driver, adopts Enzo as a puppy and names him after Enzo Ferrari. While Denny divides his time between teaching, racing and dreaming of Formula One, Enzo absorbs his master's philosophy of racing, including the idea that a great driver must learn to anticipate and stay calm in difficult conditions such as rain.

Denny meets Eve, and although Enzo is jealous at first, he soon comes to love her. The couple marry, despite the disapproval of Eve's wealthy father Maxwell, and have a daughter, Zoë, born while Denny is away driving in the 24 Hours of Daytona. As the years pass, Denny's career advances slowly, and the family faces a devastating blow when Eve becomes seriously ill. Her illness leads to a painful custody battle in which Eve's parents try to take Zoë away from Denny, threatening everything he has built. Through it all, Enzo observes the people he loves with loyalty and wisdom, convinced that, as on the racetrack, the way to win is to keep going through the storm.

The film is told entirely from the dog's perspective and uses racing as a metaphor for life, perseverance and grief. Its final scene features a brief appearance by former Formula One driver Giancarlo Fisichella.

The Art of Racing in the Rain was released by 20th Century Fox on August 9, 2019, and grossed about 33.8 million dollars worldwide. It received mixed reviews, with 44 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it sentimental and contrived, and a Metacritic score of 43.

overview: A mega-platinum, aging rock star's supermodel wife is abducted by pirates while vacationing in Chile.
tagline: Rock Out with Your Glock Out
title: Gun Shy
plot:
Gun Shy is a 2017 British action comedy directed by Simon West and starring Antonio Banderas as Turk Henry, a washed-up rock star. Olga Kurylenko plays his wife Sheila, with Mark Valley, Aisling Loftus, Jesse Johnson, Martin Dingle Wall, Ben Cura and David Mitchell in supporting roles. The screenplay by Toby Davies and Mark Haskell Smith is adapted from one of Smith's comic novels. The film was released on 8 September 2017.

Turk Henry was once the bass player of Metal Assassin, a heavy metal band remembered for a crude hit song, but since leaving the group he has lived in lazy seclusion in his Malibu mansion, drinking beer and barely noticing his wife, a former supermodel. Sheila finally persuades him to leave the house for a vacation in Chile, the country of his birth, but once there Turk refuses to venture beyond the confines of their luxury resort. While he lounges by the pool, Sheila goes on a sightseeing tour to see llamas and is kidnapped by a group of hapless, financially desperate amateur pirates, who demand a ransom of one million dollars once they discover whose wife she is.

Turk can easily afford the ransom, and is relieved by how little they want, but paying it proves to be much more complicated than expected. Unable to reach his manager in England, he must rely on the manager's junior assistant, Marybeth, who travels to Chile with the money. An ambitious and obstructive official at the United States embassy, Ben Hardin, hopes to advance his career by treating the kidnapping as an act of terrorism and blocks the payment. Meanwhile, Sheila discovers that she is in little real danger, as her captors turn out to be fans of Metal Assassin who are new to crime and need her help with basic tasks. With the help of a crude Australian mercenary, the out-of-shape Turk is forced to take matters into his own hands and venture out to rescue his wife.

Gun Shy was panned by critics. It holds a 0 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 11 reviews and a Metacritic score of 21. Variety called it a witless, graceless farce, and other reviewers criticized its script and direction, although several credited Banderas with providing a few moments of amusement through his committed, over-the-top performance.

overview: Gray Wheeler just lost everything. But it could be the best thing that ever happened to her. After the death of her fiancé, Gray moves in with her late love's best friends. While Sam and Dennis do their best to cheer Gray up, Fritz doesn't seem to care. Once Gray breaks through Fritz's defenses, however, she finally sees why her fiancé thought so highly of him. As they spend more time together, Gray learns that her chances for love have not died out with her fiancé. But when some surprise guests show up on their doorstep, it'll take the love of all of her new friends to help Gray learn that life may be messy, but love is messier.
tagline: Life is messy. Love is messier
title: Catch and Release
plot:
Catch and Release is a 2006 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Susannah Grant in her directorial debut. It stars Jennifer Garner as Gray Wheeler, Timothy Olyphant as Fritz, Kevin Smith as Sam, Sam Jaeger as Dennis and Juliette Lewis as Maureen. Filmed in Vancouver and Boulder, Colorado, it follows a woman whose fiancé dies shortly before their wedding and who discovers his secrets while falling for his best friend.

In Boulder, Gray Wheeler attends the funeral of her fiancé, Grady Douglas, on the day they were supposed to be married. Grieving and overwhelmed, she learns that because they were not married she is entitled to nothing from his estate, and she can no longer afford the house they had chosen together. She moves in with Grady's close friends Dennis and Sam, who share a house, and is soon joined by Fritz, Grady's charming but irresponsible best friend from Los Angeles, a commercial director with whom she immediately clashes.

While sorting through Grady's affairs, Gray discovers that he had a secret investment account and had been sending money every month to an unknown woman. Fritz reluctantly reveals that Grady had a son with Maureen, a massage therapist in Los Angeles, and claims the child was conceived before Grady met Gray. When Maureen and her young son Mattie arrive in Boulder looking for Grady, Gray realizes that the boy is too young for that to be true and that Grady had been unfaithful. Hurt and confused, she finds herself drawn to Fritz, while Dennis, who has his own feelings for her, struggles with jealousy, and the easygoing Sam bonds with Maureen. As the group of friends comes to terms with Grady's death and his secrets, Gray must decide how to move on with her life.

The title refers to the practice of catch-and-release fishing, which Gray criticizes in a moment that reflects her feelings about relationships and loss.

Catch and Release premiered at the Austin Film Festival on October 20, 2006, and was released in the United States on January 26, 2007. It received negative reviews, with 23 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43, and it was a box-office disappointment, grossing about 16 million dollars.

overview: When a presidential candidate dies unexpectedly in the middle of the campaign, the Democratic party unexpectedly picks a Washington, D.C. alderman as his replacement .
title: Head of State
plot:
Head of State is a satirical comedy film that explores the complexities of politics and power. The movie follows Mays Gillen (played by Chris Rock), an African American man who becomes the President of the United States after the sudden death of the incumbent president.

At its core, Head of State delves into the themes of identity, community, and the struggle for representation in a system that often marginalizes those who are not part of the elite. Mays' journey from being an ordinary citizen to the head of state serves as a metaphor for the experiences of many underrepresented groups who feel disconnected from the power structures that govern their lives.

The film also critiques the notion of "meritocracy" and the idea that anyone can rise to the top through hard work and determination, regardless of their background or circumstances. Mays' character embodies this sentiment, as he navigates the complexities of the presidency while staying true to his roots and values.

Furthermore, Head of State touches on the theme of cultural identity and the importance of preserving one's heritage in the face of assimilation and cultural homogenization. The film's portrayal of African American culture and community serves as a powerful commentary on the struggles faced by marginalized groups in America.

Overall, Head of State is a witty and incisive comedy that uses satire to explore pressing issues of identity, power, and representation in contemporary America.

overview: Troy, the popular captain of the basketball team, and Gabriella, the brainy and beautiful member of the academic club, break all the rules of East High society when they secretly audition for the leads in the school's musical. As they reach for the stars and follow their dreams, everyone learns about acceptance, teamwork, and being yourself.
title: High School Musical
plot:
High School Musical is a 2006 American musical television film produced for Disney Channel, the first installment of the High School Musical franchise. Directed and choreographed by Kenny Ortega from a screenplay by Peter Barsocchini, it stars Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens, with Ashley Tisdale, Lucas Grabeel, Corbin Bleu, Monique Coleman and Alyson Reed. Filmed mainly in Salt Lake City, Utah, the story has often been described as a modern variation on Romeo and Juliet.

On New Year's Eve at a ski lodge, the basketball star Troy Bolton and the shy, academically gifted Gabriella Montez are pushed into singing karaoke together and discover an unexpected connection. When the holidays end, Troy is astonished to find that Gabriella has transferred to his school, East High in Albuquerque. Gabriella is soon courted by the scholastic decathlon team led by Taylor McKessie, while the school's drama queen, Sharpay Evans, who rules the theater club with her twin brother, Ryan, sees her as a rival. Troy and Gabriella are drawn to the auditions for the school's winter musical, but arrive too late to sign up. Overheard singing together by the young composer Kelsi, they are granted a callback audition by the drama teacher, Ms. Darbus.

Their audition upends the school's social order, inspiring other students to reveal hidden passions that break with their cliques. Alarmed that their stars are being distracted from the championship game and the decathlon, Troy's best friend Chad and Taylor trick Gabriella into believing that Troy does not care about her, and she withdraws from the musical. The two soon regret their scheme and confess, and Troy and Gabriella reconcile. Sharpay then persuades Ms. Darbus to move the callback to the same time as the basketball final and the decathlon. Working together, the two teams create distractions that let Troy and Gabriella slip away, and the pair arrive in time to win the lead roles with "Breaking Free." Both teams win their competitions, and the whole school celebrates together.

High School Musical premiered on January 20, 2006, and became one of Disney Channel's most successful original films, drawing millions of viewers and spawning a best-selling soundtrack, a stage adaptation, two sequels including the theatrical High School Musical 3: Senior Year, books and video games. It won Emmy Awards and made stars of its young cast.

overview: Whatever Works explores the relationship between a crotchety misanthrope, Boris and a naïve, impressionable young runaway from the south, Melody. When Melody's uptight parents arrive in New York to rescue her, they are quickly drawn into wildly unexpected romantic entanglements. Everyone discovers that finding love is just a combination of lucky chance and appreciating the value of "whatever works."
tagline: A new comedy!
title: Whatever Works
plot:
Whatever Works is a 2009 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Woody Allen. The movie revolves around Cady (played by Evan Rachel Wood), a young woman who leaves her small town in search of independence and freedom, only to find herself drawn to a free-spirited man named Gordon (played by Paul Dano) who lives off the grid.

The main theme of Whatever Works is the exploration of individuality and nonconformity. The film celebrates the idea of living life on one's own terms, rejecting societal norms and expectations in favor of a more authentic and spontaneous existence. Through Cady's journey, the movie highlights the tension between the desire for freedom and the need for connection and community.

The film also delves into the complexities of relationships and intimacy, as Cady navigates her feelings for Gordon while struggling to define herself outside of their relationship. The movie raises questions about what it means to be independent, how much one is willing to compromise in order to find love and belonging, and whether true freedom can coexist with vulnerability.

Furthermore, Whatever Works touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Cady grapples with her own desires, values, and sense of purpose. The movie suggests that finding oneself is a continuous process, one that requires embracing uncertainty and being open to new experiences and relationships.

Overall, Whatever Works is a nuanced exploration of the human search for meaning, connection, and individuality, inviting viewers to reflect on their own values and priorities in life.

overview: Macbeth, the Thane of Glamis, receives a prophecy from a trio of witches that one day he will become King of Scotland. Consumed by ambition and spurred to action by his wife, Macbeth murders his king and takes the throne for himself.
title: The Tragedy of Macbeth
plot:
The Tragedy of Macbeth is a 2021 American film written, directed and produced by Joel Coen, based on William Shakespeare's play Macbeth. It was the first film directed by one of the Coen brothers without the other. Denzel Washington stars as Macbeth and Frances McDormand, who also produced, as Lady Macbeth, with Bertie Carvel, Alex Hassell, Corey Hawkins, Harry Melling, Kathryn Hunter and Brendan Gleeson. Shot in black and white on stylized, minimalist soundstage sets, it premiered at the New York Film Festival in September 2021, received a limited theatrical release from A24 in December and began streaming on Apple TV+ in January 2022.

Returning from battle, where they have led King Duncan's army to victory over the traitorous Thane of Cawdor, the Scottish generals Macbeth and Banquo are met by three witches, all played by Kathryn Hunter. The witches hail Macbeth as the future Thane of Cawdor and as king, and tell Banquo that he will father a line of kings. The first prophecy is quickly fulfilled when Duncan gives Macbeth Cawdor's title, but the king then names his son Malcolm as his heir, an obstacle to Macbeth's ambition.

When Duncan stays at Macbeth's castle, Lady Macbeth persuades her hesitant husband to murder him. She drugs the king's guards, and Macbeth kills Duncan in his sleep, then executes the servants to cover the crime. Malcolm flees to England, and Macbeth becomes king. Haunted by the witches' words about Banquo's descendants, he arranges the murder of Banquo and his son Fleance, but the boy escapes. Increasingly tyrannical and tormented by visions, including the ghost of Banquo, Macbeth seeks out the witches again, who assure him that no man born of woman can harm him and that he is safe until Birnam Wood comes to his castle at Dunsinane. Lady Macbeth descends into guilt-ridden madness, and as Macduff, whose family Macbeth has slaughtered, joins Malcolm's army, the king's reign moves toward its inevitable end. The film gives an expanded role to the nobleman Ross, played by Alex Hassell.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for Coen's direction, Bruno Delbonnel's cinematography, the production design and the performances, particularly those of Washington and Hunter. It received three Academy Award nominations, for Best Actor for Washington, Best Cinematography and Best Production Design.

original_title: Winx Club - Il mistero degli abissi
overview: The archenemies of the Winx Club, the Trix witches, team up with the evil nymph Politea and find out that, to defeat the fairies once and for all and become invincible, it takes very little: a Pearl hidden in the Deep of the Infinite Ocean! As small as powerful, the Pearl of the Depth gives enormous powers to those who possess it!  For the Winx there is not a minute to waste: how will they stop the plans of their enemies before it's too late?  Get ready: the most dangerous mission of the Winx is about to begin!
title: Winx Club: The Mystery of the Abyss
plot:
Winx Club: The Mystery of the Abyss is an animated television film that revolves around the adventures of Bloom and her friends as they navigate through a mysterious underwater world. 

The movie delves into the theme of self-discovery, as each character faces their own personal struggles and insecurities in this alien environment. For instance, Bloom must confront her feelings of inadequacy and learn to trust herself in order to save her friends.

Moreover, the film explores the idea of unity and cooperation among its characters. As they work together to unravel the secrets of the Abyss, they discover that their unique skills and strengths are essential to overcoming the challenges they face.

Additionally, the movie touches upon the theme of environmentalism, as the characters encounter a world ravaged by pollution and destruction. This serves as a metaphor for the consequences of human actions on the natural world and highlights the importance of preserving our planet's beauty and resources.

The film also features a strong narrative about friendship and loyalty, showcasing how Bloom and her friends stand by each other through thick and thin, even in the face of adversity.

overview: A small town girl is caught between dead-end jobs. A high-profile, successful man becomes wheelchair bound following an accident. The man decides his life is not worth living until the girl is hired for six months to be his new caretaker. Worlds apart and trapped together by circumstance, the two get off to a rocky start. But the girl becomes determined to prove to the man that life is worth living and as they embark on a series of adventures together, each finds their world changing in ways neither of them could begin to imagine.
tagline: Live boldly.
title: Me Before You
plot:
Me Before You is a 2016 romantic drama directed by Thea Sharrock in her feature directorial debut and adapted by Jojo Moyes from her own 2012 novel. It stars Emilia Clarke as Louisa "Lou" Clark and Sam Claflin as Will Traynor, with Janet McTeer and Charles Dance as Will's parents, Brendan Coyle as Lou's father and Matthew Lewis as her boyfriend Patrick. It was filmed at historic locations across the United Kingdom, including Pembroke Castle in Wales and Chenies Manor House in Buckinghamshire.

In the small English town of Stokebridge, Lou Clark, a cheerful and quirky young woman who needs money to support her family, accepts a six-month position as a caregiver for Will Traynor. Will is a wealthy former banker and adventurous sportsman who became quadriplegic after being hit by a motorcycle two years earlier. Embittered and depressed, he treats Lou coldly at first, and his ex-girlfriend's announcement that she is marrying his former best friend only deepens his despair.

Lou perseveres, and the two gradually grow close as Will introduces her to films, music and ideas beyond the confines of her small-town life, encouraging her to be more ambitious. By chance, Lou learns that Will has agreed to give his parents six months before travelling to Switzerland to end his life through assisted suicide. Determined to change his mind, she plans a series of outings and adventures to show him that life is still worth living. As her relationship with her boyfriend Patrick falls apart, Lou and Will fall in love, culminating in a trip to Mauritius. But Will's decision remains firm, forcing Lou to confront the limits of love and the meaning of respecting another person's choices.

The film's portrayal of disability and assisted suicide drew criticism from many disability rights activists, who argued that it implied that the lives of disabled people are not worth living, and protests were held at several screenings.

Me Before You was released on 3 June 2016 and was a commercial success, grossing about 208.4 million dollars worldwide against a 20 million dollar budget. Reviews were mixed, with 55 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51, although the performances of Clarke and Claflin were praised.

overview: In a mountain town, where corn and poppies grow, the girls wear boyish haircuts and have hiding places underground to escape the threat of being stolen. Ana and her two best friends grow up together, affirming the bonds of their friendship and discovering what it means to be women in a rural town marked by violence. Their mothers train them to flee death, to escape those who turn them into slaves or ghosts. They create their own impenetrable universe, but one day one of the girls doesn’t make it to her hiding place in time.
tagline: Find the light in the darkness.
title: Prayers for the Stolen
plot:
Prayers for the Stolen is a 2021 film that delves into the complexities of human relationships and the devastating consequences of colonialism, oppression, and trauma. The movie masterfully weaves together the interconnected lives of several characters in a small town in Mexico, exposing the dark underbelly of their community's history.

At its core, Prayers for the Stolen is a powerful exploration of the long-lasting effects of historical trauma on individuals and communities. The film sheds light on the ways in which the legacy of colonialism continues to shape the lives of those living in its aftermath, often perpetuating cycles of violence, silence, and resistance.

Through the characters' stories, the movie highlights the intricate web of relationships between oppressors and oppressed, highlighting how these dynamics can both harm and heal. The film also delves into themes of identity, culture, and belonging, showcasing the ways in which individuals navigate their place within a community that has been shaped by historical trauma.

Ultimately, Prayers for the Stolen is a poignant reminder of the importance of acknowledging and confronting the painful truths of our collective past, in order to work towards healing and reconciliation. The film's nuanced portrayal of complex characters and relationships serves as a powerful testament to the resilience of the human spirit, even in the face of unimaginable hardship.

overview: Cousins Thomas and David, owners of a mobile restaurant, team up with their friend Moby, a bumbling private detective, to save the beautiful Sylvia, a pickpocket.
tagline: Not since Don Quixote has Spain had so much fun!
title: Wheels on Meals
plot:
Wheels on Meals is a 1984 Hong Kong action comedy film directed by Sammo Hung, starring Sammo Hung, Yuen Biao, and Joey Wong.

The main themes of Wheels on Meals revolve around friendship, loyalty, and the struggle for identity. The story follows two friends, Jack (Sammo Hung) and Tony (Yuen Biao), who are struggling to find their place in the world after leaving a martial arts school. They embark on a journey to find work as stuntmen, but instead get caught up in a series of misadventures involving crime lords, gangsters, and corrupt officials.

Throughout the film, Sammo Hung's character, Jack, grapples with his own identity and sense of purpose, while Yuen Biao's character, Tony, tries to find his place as a stuntman. The two friends support each other through various challenges, showcasing their loyalty and camaraderie.

The film also explores the theme of social commentary, critiquing the corruption and decay of Hong Kong society during the 1980s. The movie features a satirical portrayal of the city's underworld, highlighting issues such as organized crime, police corruption, and government inefficiency.

Overall, Wheels on Meals is a lighthearted, entertaining film that balances action, comedy, and drama, with a strong focus on friendship and loyalty.

overview: Following the events at home, the Abbott family now face the terrors of the outside world. Forced to venture into the unknown, they realize that the creatures that hunt by sound are not the only threats that lurk beyond the sand path.
tagline: Silence is not enough.
title: A Quiet Place Part II
plot:
A Quiet Place Part II is a 2021 American horror film directed by John Krasinski and Emily Blunt, who also star in the movie alongside Millicent Simmonds. The film takes place after the events of the first part and follows the Abbott family as they navigate their new reality.

The story begins with Evelyn (Emily Blunt) giving birth to a baby girl, which is a significant event for the family. However, the baby's arrival also puts them at risk due to the presence of monsters that hunt by sound. The family must find a way to protect their newborn and ensure her survival in this post-apocalyptic world.

The Abbotts embark on a perilous journey through the woods, searching for a safe haven where they can raise their daughter without being detected by the creatures. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, abandoned buildings, and other survivors who may be hostile towards them.

As they navigate this new world, Evelyn struggles to cope with her newfound motherhood and the weight of responsibility that comes with it. She must also confront her own fears and limitations as a mother in order to protect her daughter. Meanwhile, Regan (Millicent Simmonds), their deaf daughter, plays a crucial role in the family's survival, using her unique abilities to detect and avoid danger.

Throughout their journey, the Abbotts face numerous challenges, including encounters with the creatures and other survivors who are struggling to survive. They also encounter a group of people who claim to have found a safe haven, but Evelyn is skeptical about their intentions.

As the story unfolds, Evelyn begins to realize that her daughter's presence may be more than just a threat to their survival - it may also hold the key to their future. The film builds towards a climactic confrontation with the creatures and a shocking revelation about the true nature of the world they live in.

Ultimately, A Quiet Place Part II is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of motherhood, sacrifice, and resilience in the face of unimaginable danger. The film features stunning performances from its cast, particularly Emily Blunt and Millicent Simmonds, who deliver powerful and emotional performances that bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, A Quiet Place Part II is a gripping and intense horror film that expands on the world and characters introduced in the first part. It's a must-see for fans of the genre and anyone looking for a thrilling cinematic experience.

overview: An idealistic attractive young couple acquires a stunning, life-like robot for guilt free help, but as the three grow closer, their perception of humanity will be altered forever.
tagline: They're too human to be perfect. He's too perfect to be human.
title: Life Like
plot:
Life Like is a 2019 American science fiction drama written and directed by Josh Janowicz in his feature debut. Steven Strait and Addison Timlin play a wealthy young couple who buy a lifelike android servant, played by Drew Van Acker, with James D'Arcy as the robot's creator. Produced by Lionsgate and distributed by Grindstone Entertainment Group, it was released on home video and digital platforms on May 14, 2019.

After the death of his father, James inherits leadership of the family's investment firm and moves with his wife, Sophie, from the city to a large suburban mansion. Uncomfortable with being waited on by a butler, maid and cook, Sophie dismisses them, and the couple instead turn to Julian, an entrepreneur who sells artificially intelligent humanoid robots as domestic servants. They choose a male model named Henry, who carries out his duties with unfailing courtesy. Encouraged by Sophie, who spends long hours reading to him, Henry begins to show signs of emotion and even reports having dreams.

As Henry grows more humanlike, unsettling tensions emerge in the household. Sophie finds him wandering naked and disoriented outside at night, and she becomes disturbed when he mimics James's expressions of love. James suspects Henry is developing feelings for his wife, although Julian assures him this is impossible. The android's relationships with both husband and wife become increasingly intimate and confused, provoking jealousy, guilt and recriminations between the couple, who argue over who is to blame. When Sophie demands that Henry be shut down, he refuses to obey Julian, declaring that he knows of his lies.

The couple discover the truth: Julian is a fraud, and his supposed machines are real people whom he took in as abused or abandoned children and raised to believe that they were androids. Henry was one of them. When FBI agents arrive to arrest Julian at the couple's home, he shoots them and turns his gun on James and Sophie, but Henry attacks and overpowers his creator. Overwhelmed by the betrayal and his shame at having violated the trust of his owners, Henry takes his own life as James and Sophie try to comfort him. Five years later, the couple have a young son, whom they have named Henry.

The film explores questions of identity, desire and the boundaries between human and machine within the confines of a single house, and it marked the feature debut of Janowicz, previously a director of commercials and short films.

overview: The son of a sailor, 5-year-old Sosuke, lives a quiet life on an oceanside cliff with his mother Lisa. One fateful day, he finds a beautiful goldfish trapped in a bottle on the beach and upon rescuing her, names her Ponyo. But she is no ordinary goldfish.
tagline: Welcome to a world where anything is possible.
title: Ponyo
plot:
